bill_summary: This bill adds zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies to the list of live nondomesticated animals that are prohibited from being imported, sold, traded, possessed, or bred in Maryland. It also reduces the time a nonresident can travel through the state with prohibited animals from 10 days to 48 hours and repeals a specific exception for nondomesticated animals used as assistance animals by persons with severe mobility-limiting disabilities.
responsible_party: State and local law enforcement officers and local animal control authorities
stakeholders: Current and potential owners of zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies; nonresidents traveling through Maryland with prohibited animals; individuals with mobility-limiting disabilities; and local animal control agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. While individuals who violate the law are subject to misdemeanor fines of up to $1,000 and entities up to $10,000, specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly references permits and licenses issued by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) as exceptions to the prohibition on possessing or trading certain nondomesticated animals, and DNR is responsible for managing wildlife regulations in the state.

The Maryland State Police, as the state's primary law enforcement agency, is responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including the new prohibitions and misdemeanor offenses related to the possession and trade of zebras, kangaroos, and other nondomesticated animals.

The bill repeals an existing exception that allows individuals with mobility-limiting disabilities to possess nondomesticated animals as assistance animals, which directly impacts the department's mission to coordinate services and advocate for Marylanders with disabilities.
The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the judicial branch, which will be responsible for adjudicating the misdemeanor charges and penalties established or modified by this legislation.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to state agencies like DNR and the Maryland State Police regarding the enforcement of the Criminal Law Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for providing legal representation to indigent individuals charged with the misdemeanor crimes created or expanded by this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry to study and make recommendations on restructuring the State's electric utility industry; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly on or before November 1, 2027.
Title: Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland’s Electric Utility Industry to evaluate and make recommendations on alternative utility and governance models, such as publicly owned utilities and cooperatives. The task force is required to study electricity rates, infrastructure investment, legal implications of asset transfers, and the potential costs and benefits of transitioning to different market participation models.
stakeholders: Maryland electric ratepayers, investor-owned and municipal electric utilities, electric cooperatives, and PJM Interconnection, LLC.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by approximately $667,000 in FY 2027 and $333,000 in FY 2028 to hire a consultant to support the task force's duties. These costs are offset by a corresponding increase in special fund revenues from assessments imposed by the PSC on regulated public service companies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Public Service Commission (PSC) provide staff for the Task Force. Furthermore, the PSC Chair designates the Task Force Chair, and a member of the Commission is a required member of the Task Force. The fiscal note indicates a significant impact of approximately $1 million on the PSC for consultant services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary body, the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry, which falls directly under this collective designation for state-authorized task forces conducting special studies.

The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is a mandated member of the Task Force and is responsible for designating a representative from an independent electricity generation company to serve as a member.

The People's Counsel is a mandated member of the Task Force. The Task Force's focus on restructuring the utility industry and evaluating electricity rates aligns directly with the agency's mission to represent the interests of residential utility consumers.

The Secretary of the Environment is a mandated member of the Task Force. Restructuring the electric utility industry has significant implications for environmental quality and the state's climate commitments.

The Secretary of Transportation is a mandated member of the Task Force, as utility restructuring and grid management significantly impact the state's transportation infrastructure and electrification efforts.

The Task Force is required to analyze the legal implications of transferring privately owned electric company assets to public ownership, specifically through eminent domain. As the chief legal officer for the state and counsel to its agencies, the OAG will likely provide necessary legal guidance on these constitutional and statutory matters.

The Governor is responsible for appointing a public representative with expertise in the electric utility industry to the Task Force. Additionally, the Governor oversees the executive agencies participating in the study.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and personnel. The bill carries a fiscal impact involving special fund expenditures and assessment revenues that DBM must monitor, as well as provisions for travel reimbursements provided in the state budget.
The Office of Appointments within the Executive Department would likely assist the Governor in recruiting and vetting the required appointee with utility industry expertise.

Synopsis: Applying statewide certain provisions of law authorizing the use of speed monitoring systems in certain residential districts.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Speed Monitoring Systems - Residential Districts
Status: In the House - Second Reading Passed

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: This bill authorizes all local jurisdictions in Maryland to install and use speed monitoring systems (speed cameras) on highways in residential districts with a maximum speed limit of 35 miles per hour. This expands the existing authority which was previously restricted to Anne Arundel, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties. Use of these systems is subject to local law enactment, notice, and public hearing requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) and the Maryland District Court
stakeholders: Motorists traveling through residential districts and local government authorities in Maryland jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues from contested District Court cases may increase minimally starting in fiscal 2027. Local jurisdictions (excluding those already authorized) will see an increase in revenues from civil penalties and an increase in expenditures for the installation, administration, and operation of speed monitoring programs, which may be significant depending on the scale of implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note explicitly states that individuals receiving speed monitoring citations may elect to stand trial in the District Court. The Judiciary (supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts) is responsible for handling these contested cases and collecting associated fine revenues.

As the parent agency for the State Highway Administration and Maryland Transportation Authority, MDOT is responsible for the state's transportation network and highway safety initiatives, which are directly impacted by speed monitoring policy.

The bill explicitly mentions the State Highway Administration's authority to use speed monitoring systems and references traffic engineering practices, which the SHA is responsible for implementing to establish speed limits.
The Maryland Transportation Authority is explicitly named in the bill as an agency authorized to use speed monitoring systems on specific routes like the Intercounty Connector (MD Route 200).

The Comptroller is the state's principal revenue collector. The fiscal note indicates that fine revenues from contested speed camera cases are paid into the State's general fund, which falls under the Comptroller's oversight.

The State Treasurer's Office manages and protects state funds. Because the bill is projected to increase general fund revenues from contested citations, the Treasurer is responsible for the receipt and management of these funds.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning. The bill's impact on general fund revenues from court-contested citations requires DBM to account for these fiscal changes in state budgeting.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police are involved in enforcing motor vehicle and traffic safety laws, and they provide support to local agencies regarding public safety and traffic enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice and safety policy. Speed monitoring systems are a key tool in the state's public safety and traffic enforcement strategy.

Synopsis: Requiring that each legislative district established for the purpose of electing members of the House of Delegates consist of three single-member delegate districts; requiring the General Assembly to enact a law establishing and governing a Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention to establish legislative and congressional districts and establishing certain requirements regarding the Redistricting Convention; establishing the Redistricting Convention; etc.
Title: Districting - Single-Member Districts and Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention
Status: In the House - First Reading House Rules and Executive Nominations

General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to require that each legislative district for the House of Delegates be divided into three single-member delegate districts. It also establishes an elected 188-member Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention to draw legislative and congressional boundary lines every ten years following the decennial census, a duty previously handled by the Governor and General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections, Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention, Supreme Court of Maryland, Office of the Attorney General, and Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for the General Assembly and Congress, and residents of Maryland legislative and congressional districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will increase state expenditures every ten years beginning in fiscal 2031 to conduct elections for the 188 members of the Redistricting Convention. The state will also incur costs for convention operations, including travel reimbursements for members and administrative support from the Office of the Attorney General and Department of Legislative Services. There may be additional costs related to the Supreme Court of Maryland's expanded original jurisdiction over redistricting challenges. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly impacts the Governor's Office by proposing a constitutional amendment that removes the Governor's current authority to prepare and present legislative redistricting plans to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Office of the Attorney General, alongside the Department of Legislative Services, shall jointly staff the newly created Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention.
DBM is relevant as it oversees the state budget, and the bill requires that members of the 188-person Redistricting Convention be reimbursed for expenses as provided in the state budget.
The bill requires that all meetings of the Redistricting Convention be livestreamed for public observation, which falls under the telecommunications and digital services strategy managed by DoIT.

The Department of Planning typically manages the state's census data and GIS mapping infrastructure, which are essential technical resources for the Redistricting Convention's task of drawing boundary lines.

The bill grants the Supreme Court of Maryland exclusive original jurisdiction to hear challenges to redistricting plans or to establish plans if the Convention fails to do so; the AOC provides the operational and legal support for the judiciary to execute these duties.
SBE is a primary implementing agency responsible for determining the election date for the 188 convention members and apportioning seats among the counties based on decennial census data.

As the custodian of state laws and official records, the Secretary of State is relevant because redistricting plans certified by the Convention become law and are treated like bills for the purposes of publication and codification.

The bill establishes strict eligibility requirements for convention members, including prohibitions on current or former registered lobbyists; the State Ethics Commission regulates lobbying and would be involved in verifying such qualifications.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Civic Excellence Program in the State Department of Education; authorizing a local school system to participate in the Program to recognize students who meet criteria related to student proficiency in civics and civic literacy; and requiring the Department, no later than the 2027-2028 school year, to develop guidelines to assist participating local school systems.
Title: Public Schools - Maryland Civic Excellence Program - Established
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). The voluntary program allows participating local school systems to recognize students and public schools that promote civic readiness and engagement. MSDE is required to develop guidelines for determining student proficiency in civics and civic literacy by the 2027-2028 school year, and participating local school systems may award students a 'Seal of Civic Excellence' along with cords, medals, or other diploma insignia.
stakeholders: Public school students, local school systems, the Maryland State Department of Education, and potential collaborating nonprofit or civic organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can develop the required guidelines for the program using existing resources. Local school systems that choose to participate may experience an increase in discretionary expenditures and operational impacts related to administering the program and providing awards (such as medals or diploma insignia). No impact on state or local revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program within the Department of Education (MSDE) and mandates that the Department administer the program, develop guidelines for student proficiency in civics, and receive reports from participating local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program's purpose is to recognize civic readiness and engagement among students, which directly aligns with this department's mission to promote service, volunteerism, and civic engagement across the state.

The bill allows local school systems to collaborate with institutions of higher education to support the program; as the regulatory and coordinating body for postsecondary education, the Commission oversees these institutions.
As a state-operated higher education system, its member institutions are potential collaborators for local school systems to support the implementation of the Maryland Civic Excellence Program.
As a public university, Morgan State is a potential collaborator for local school systems in the implementation and support of the program's civic engagement goals.
As an independent public honors college, it may serve as a collaborating institution of higher education to support local school systems in the program.
This office is responsible for community affairs and engagement, including promoting civic participation, which overlaps with the program's goal of fostering civic readiness and engagement.

The agency collects student performance data; if the Seal of Civic Excellence becomes a tracked student outcome or proficiency metric, it would likely be integrated into their repository for analysis of student performance.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Education and would be responsible for advising on the development of guidelines and implementation of the program.

Synopsis: Requiring a county that submits an application to the Secretary of Transportation for funding for certain transportation services for elderly and disabled persons to identify interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers in the application; requiring the Secretary to adopt procedures to ensure counties cooperate in establishing interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers; etc.
Title: Transportation - Paratransit Services - Interjurisdictional Routes
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires counties that apply for State funding for elderly and handicapped transportation services to identify and establish interjurisdictional paratransit routes connecting to facilities within specific healthcare networks, including Adventist Healthcare, Johns Hopkins Medicine, LifeBridge Health, Luminis Health Maryland, MedStar Health, and the University of Maryland Medical System.
stakeholders: Elderly and handicapped residents, Maryland county governments, Baltimore City, and major healthcare provider networks.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be managed within existing budgeted resources. Total State funding for the Statewide Special Transportation Assistance Program (at least 4305908 adjusted for inflation) remains unchanged, but the bill may shift the distribution of these funds among local jurisdictions. Local governments are expected to see an indeterminate increase in expenditures to provide the mandated interjurisdictional paratransit routes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The Secretary of Transportation manages the Statewide Special Transportation Assistance Program (SSTAP), identifies funding for elderly and handicapped transportation in the budget, and is tasked with adopting procedures to ensure counties cooperate on interjurisdictional paratransit routes.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Transportation to consult with the Department of Aging in distributing funds and developing enforcement procedures. Furthermore, local area agencies on aging, which fall under this department's network, must certify approval of the projects for which counties seek funding.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Transportation consult with the Department of Disabilities regarding the distribution of funds and the creation of enforcement procedures for the paratransit program, which specifically serves handicapped individuals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and would be responsible for advising on the development of new procedures and enforcement mechanisms related to interjurisdictional paratransit requirements and county cooperation.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and long-term planning. The bill requires MDOT to identify specific amounts within its budget for these services, which DBM monitors to ensure efficiency and alignment with state resources.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and appoints the Secretary of Transportation. The bill modifies the administrative responsibilities and budget execution of a cabinet-level agency reporting to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring certain expedited proceedings in a wrongful detainer action if the property that is the subject of the action is, at the time of the complaint, advertised or listed for sale or lease by the complainant and requiring that notice of a hearing or appeal be served in person or, under certain circumstances, posted conspicuously on the property; requiring the District Court or the circuit court to issue a warrant within 24 hours if the court rules in favor of the complainant in an expedited wrongful detainer action; etc.
Title: Real Property - Expedited Wrongful Detainer Proceedings - Property for Sale or Lease
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m. (Economic Matters)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill establishes an expedited legal process for wrongful detainer actions when the real property in question is advertised or listed for sale or lease. It mandates specific shortened timelines for court summons, hearings, and judicial rulings, requiring the District Court to hold a hearing within five days of a complaint and issue a ruling within two business days. Additionally, it requires that warrants for possession be issued within 24 hours of a favorable ruling and executed immediately by the sheriff.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District Court and Circuit Courts) and local Sheriffs' Offices
stakeholders: Property owners listing real estate for sale or lease, individuals in actual possession of property without a legal right, the Maryland court system, and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While the Maryland Judiciary and local sheriffs' offices may experience operational impacts to meet the expedited schedules for hearings, appeals, and warrant executions, the fiscal note states that no significant expenditure or revenue changes are expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates specific, expedited timelines for processing wrongful detainer cases in both District and Circuit Courts, including requirements for immediate summons, hearings within five days, rulings within two business days, and warrant issuance within 24 hours. The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for providing the operational, legal, and technological support needed to implement these procedural changes within the Maryland Judicial Branch.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the State, providing legal counsel to the Judiciary and all state agencies. The agency would be responsible for interpreting the new legal requirements for expedited proceedings and representing the state's interests or advising the courts on the implementation of these procedural changes to the Real Property Article.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development is tasked with ensuring safe and secure housing and overseeing community vitality. While the bill is procedural, it modifies the process for recovering possession of real property that is listed for sale or lease, which has implications for property owners and the broader real estate market within the department's policy scope.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an institution of higher education from denying access or services to a student based on the student's diagnosis of sickle cell disease; requiring an institution of higher education to provide reasonable accommodations for students with sickle cell disease; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop an education and awareness campaign for institutions of higher education in the State regarding students with sickle cell disease; etc.
Title: Sickle Cell Disease - Institutions of Higher Education - Policies, Procedures, and Educational Campaigns (Kaitlyn's Law)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment and Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Known as Kaitlyn's Law, this bill prohibits Maryland institutions of higher education from denying access or services to students based on a sickle cell disease diagnosis and requires these institutions to provide reasonable accommodations. It mandates the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with other state entities to develop an education and awareness campaign, clinical procedures, and a framework for assessing and supporting students with sickle cell disease.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students with sickle cell disease and the faculty, health personnel, and administrative staff at Maryland institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $139,400 in FY 2027 and $157,900 in FY 2028. These funds will cover the costs of hiring contractual personnel at the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission to develop educational materials, clinical procedures, and monitoring frameworks. Public institutions of higher education and local community colleges are expected to implement the bill's requirements using existing resources, although some minor costs for student accommodations may be incurred.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency tasked with developing the education and awareness campaign, creating the framework and procedures for institutions of higher education, and providing technical assistance and monitoring. The fiscal note also identifies a significant expenditure increase for MDH to hire a nurse program administrator.

The Commission is explicitly required to consult with the Department of Health to develop the sickle cell framework and procedures, jointly provide technical assistance to institutions, and develop a process to monitor compliance. The fiscal note identifies a fiscal impact for MHEC to hire a contractual program manager.

As the governing body for 12 public institutions of higher education, USM is directly impacted by the bill's requirements to provide reasonable accommodations, establish reporting procedures, and ensure non-discrimination based on sickle cell disease diagnosis.

As a public institution of higher education and a state agency, Morgan State University must comply with the bill's mandates regarding student accommodations, access, and reporting procedures for sickle cell disease.
As a public honors college and independent state agency, the college is required to implement the bill's policies, procedures, and accommodation requirements for students with sickle cell disease.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Statewide Steering Committee on Sickle Cell Disease be consulted in the development of the framework, procedures, and educational materials, and that it helps provide technical assistance and monitoring.

DBM is responsible for the state's personnel and budget. The bill requires the creation of new contractual positions at MDH and MHEC, which has a fiscal impact that DBM must oversee in the state budget.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies and institutions. It would likely be involved in advising MDH, MHEC, and public universities on the legal requirements for 'reasonable accommodations' and the anti-discrimination protections mandated by the bill.

The department is responsible for ensuring programs and services are inclusive and integrated for residents with disabilities. Since sickle cell disease can be a disabling condition requiring reasonable accommodations in educational settings, this bill aligns with their core mission of advancing accessible housing and community living.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "student financing company" to exclude an institution of postsecondary education for purposes of certain registration and reporting requirements.
Title: Financial Institutions – Definition of Student Financing Companies – Alteration
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of a 'student financing company' to exclude institutions of postsecondary education. This change exempts these institutions from specific registration and annual reporting requirements mandated for entities providing student financing in Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Institutions of postsecondary education, student financing companies, and students who utilize student financing products
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. Specific revenue or expenditure estimates are unavailable because the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the definition of a 'student financing company' within the Financial Institutions Article, which falls under the regulatory oversight of the Department's Office of Financial Regulation. This office is responsible for the registration and reporting requirements that institutions of postsecondary education will be exempt from under this legislation.

MHEC is the state's central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education. Since the bill exempts institutions of postsecondary education from certain financial registration and reporting requirements, it directly affects the operational and regulatory environment of the institutions under MHEC's purview.

As the state's public higher education system comprising 12 institutions, USM is an 'institution of postsecondary education' that would be exempted by this bill from the registration and reporting requirements typically applied to student financing companies.

As a public, state-governed postsecondary institution, Morgan State University is directly impacted by the bill's alteration of the definition of student financing companies, which removes the university from certain regulatory requirements if it provides student financing products.

As an independent public honors college and an institution of postsecondary education, Saint Mary's is directly impacted by this legislation, which exempts it from registering as a student financing company with the Department of Labor.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor and the Maryland Higher Education Commission. It would likely be responsible for advising on the implementation of these definition changes and interpreting the extent of the exemption.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases and regulatory enforcement actions for various state agencies, including the Department of Labor. Changes to registration and reporting mandates for student financing entities could affect the scope or volume of administrative cases brought by or against the Office of Financial Regulation.

Synopsis: Requiring the District Court for Anne Arundel County to issue its summons for a trial to repossess for failure to pay rent to any constable or sheriff's designee; providing that a sheriff's designee in Anne Arundel County has the same authority and responsibility as a constable or sheriff in an action to repossess for a failure to pay rent; requiring a sheriff's designee to post a notice of a trial at a certain property or address; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Summons for Actions to Repossess for Failure to Pay Rent - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal procedures for summonses and trials in failure to pay rent cases specifically in Anne Arundel County. It requires the District Court to issue summonses to constables or sheriff's designees, changes the trial date from the 5th day to the 30th day after a complaint is filed, requires trial notices to be posted at the property at least 7 days before the trial, and limits the court to 100 such cases on any given day.
responsible_party: District Court for Anne Arundel County and the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Landlords and tenants in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State finances, although the Judiciary anticipates operational impacts regarding case scheduling and high volumes in Anne Arundel County. Local expenditures may decrease if the bill leads to operational efficiencies and reduced overtime within the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's office. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations of the District Court in Anne Arundel County, which is supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts. It alters procedural requirements for issuing summonses, increases the timeline for trial from 5 to 30 days, and imposes a cap on the number of cases scheduled per day. The fiscal note explicitly identifies a moderate operational impact on the Judiciary.

Synopsis: Requiring certain interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports sponsored by certain schools and certain locker rooms to be expressly designated based on biological sex; prohibiting certain entities from taking certain adverse actions against a school for maintaining separate interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports or locker rooms for students of the female sex; etc.
Title: Education - Interscholastic and Intramural Junior Varsity and Varsity Teams and Locker Rooms - Designation Based on Sex (Fairness in Girls' Sports Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: The Fairness in Girls' Sports Act requires that interscholastic and intramural athletic teams and locker rooms in Maryland public high schools and certain nonpublic high schools be expressly designated based on biological sex. The bill prohibits students of the male sex from participating on teams or using locker rooms designated for females, protects schools from adverse actions for maintaining these sex-based designations, and establishes a right for students or schools to bring civil actions for damages and legal fees in the event of violations or retaliation.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems
stakeholders: Public and nonpublic high school students, local school systems, and athletic associations or organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local school systems may incur additional costs related to potential civil litigation and locker room modifications; however, a reliable estimate of these costs is not feasible at this time according to the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office coordinates high-profile policy initiatives. This bill involves significant social and educational policy that aligns with executive oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

While the fiscal note indicates no direct State fiscal impact, DBM is the principal fiscal agency and supervises budget execution and personnel policies that may be tangentially affected by changes in school system administrative requirements.

MSDE is the primary agency for the bill's implementation. It oversees public education policies and regulations, specifically those governing the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA) which manages the athletic programs mentioned in the bill.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to MSDE regarding the bill's compliance with federal laws like Title IX and constitutional Equal Protection clauses, and would represent the State in any resulting litigation.
The bill creates a new cause of action allowing students and schools to bring civil suits for damages, which will be adjudicated within the State's judicial system managed by the AOC.

The MCCR enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws. The bill's requirements for sex-based designation and its protections against 'adverse actions' may conflict with or impact the Commission's enforcement scope regarding sex and gender identity discrimination.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze the challenges related to the delay in student enrollment counts and its effect on school funding and the connection between growing student populations and the provision of school funding; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 15, 2026.
Title: Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze challenges related to student enrollment counts and population growth as they relate to school funding. The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local boards of education, the Maryland State Department of Education, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) assumes that the task force can be staffed using existing resources, resulting in no net fiscal impact. However, the Office of the Governor estimates a fiscal 2027 requirement of $254,000 for contractual support and an executive assistant. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Office of the Governor to provide staffing for the Task Force and mandates that the Governor appoint nine members and the chair. The Governor's Office also noted a potential fiscal impact of $254,000 for contractual staff to fulfill this mandate.

As the agency overseeing public education funding and enrollment, MSDE is a primary stakeholder. A representative from the department is a named member of the Task Force, and the study directly concerns MSDE's core operations and funding formulas.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary task force to address specific government issues (education funding and student population growth), falling under the regulatory and administrative scope of this entity.
The Office of the Comptroller is a named member of the Task Force, reflecting its role as the state's chief financial officer in analyzing fiscal data related to education funding.

The fiscal note identifies the Maryland Department of Planning as the agency responsible for school enrollment projections, which are a central component of the Task Force's required analysis of student population growth.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting the nine members and chair to be appointed to the newly created Task Force.

As the agency responsible for state budget development and long-term fiscal planning, DBM would be impacted by Task Force recommendations regarding changes to education funding formulas and state expenditures.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a communication between an attorney and a client that acts as a fiduciary is subject to the attorney-client privilege even if fiduciary funds are used to compensate the attorney for services rendered to the client.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Fiduciaries - Attorney-Client Privilege
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/28 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill clarifies that the attorney-client privilege applies to communications between an attorney and a client acting as a fiduciary, even if the attorney is paid using fiduciary funds. It also specifies that a fiduciary relationship between a fiduciary and a beneficiary does not waive this privilege.
stakeholders: Fiduciaries (including trustees, executors, and agents under power of attorney), attorneys, and beneficiaries of estates and trusts
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. The fiscal impact on small businesses is reported as minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a rule regarding the attorney-client privilege in fiduciary relationships, which is a rule of evidence directly applicable to judicial proceedings and the legal support infrastructure managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Register of Wills is responsible for administrative probate and overseeing decedents' estates. This bill directly clarifies the legal protections for communications between attorneys and fiduciaries, such as personal representatives, who are central to the agency's core functions.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to the Judiciary and all state agencies. This bill's clarification of attorney-client privilege for fiduciaries impacts the legal standards the OAG must apply when representing state entities acting in fiduciary capacities.

The agency acts as a fiduciary for the State Retirement and Pension System. The bill's provisions regarding the use of fiduciary funds to compensate attorneys and the subsequent impact on attorney-client privilege are relevant to the agency's management of its legal relationships.

The department frequently acts in fiduciary roles, such as serving as a guardian for foster children or vulnerable adults. The bill's clarification of legal privilege for fiduciaries directly affects the agency's legal interactions in these protective service roles.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to withdraw Maryland from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI), a cooperative effort among Eastern states to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It repeals the statutory requirement for the State to participate in the initiative and eliminates the mandate that proceeds from the sale of carbon dioxide allowances be deposited into the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund to support energy assistance, efficiency, and renewable energy programs.
stakeholders: Maryland electricity ratepayers, low-income households receiving energy assistance, energy efficiency program participants, renewable energy developers, and state agencies including the Maryland Energy Administration and the Department of the Environment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a significant loss of special fund revenue for the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) by ending Maryland's participation in RGGI carbon allowance auctions. These proceeds currently fund low-income energy assistance (at least 50% of revenue), energy efficiency (20%), and renewable energy initiatives (20%). While the bill includes a provision allowing up to 100,000,000 dollars of existing compliance fees to be used for solar development in fiscal year 2026, the overall fiscal impact is an indeterminate but substantial decrease in ongoing revenue for climate and energy programs. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note were not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Governor to immediately begin the process of withdrawing Maryland from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) and requires the Governor to report the details and reasons for the withdrawal to the General Assembly.

As the primary agency for environmental protection and air quality, MDE currently implements the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and greenhouse gas reduction plans. The bill repeals sections of the Environment Article governing RGGI and removes a funding source for MDE's Air and Radiation Administration.

The Maryland Energy Administration (referred to as the 'Administration' in the bill) administers the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). This bill eliminates the fund's primary revenue source—RGGI auction proceeds—which will significantly impact the agency's ability to fund energy efficiency, renewable energy, and climate programs.

The bill impacts the funding for the Electric Universal Service Program and other low-income energy assistance programs within the Department of Human Services, which are currently supported by at least 50% of the State's RGGI auction proceeds.

The withdrawal from RGGI represents a significant fiscal shift, removing hundreds of millions of dollars in annual revenue from the state's special funds. DBM is responsible for the overall state budget and long-term fiscal planning impacted by this loss of revenue.

The bill amends Article - Natural Resources to remove the requirement that the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund be used to help achieve implementation of Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative offset opportunities in urban areas.

The PSC is involved in the transfer of funds to the Strategic Energy Investment Fund and oversees the administration of ratepayer credits and refunds (legislative energy relief refunds) mentioned in the bill's modifications to the fund's use.

The bill explicitly mentions the Maryland Clean Energy Center as a recipient of mandated funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. The removal of RGGI proceeds from the fund directly threatens this statutory funding stream.

The bill amends findings in the Economic Development Article regarding the state's reliance on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas policy. It also affects the funding for the Maryland Energy Innovation Fund, which supports economic development in the energy sector.
The bill impacts the funding for the Climate Technology Founder’s Fund, which is established under the Economic Development Article and managed by TEDCO to support early-stage technology businesses.

As the advocate for residential utility consumers, the People's Counsel is relevant due to the bill's impact on energy assistance funding and the distribution of rate relief credits to Maryland residents.

The bill specifies funding levels for the Maryland Energy Innovation Institute, which is housed within the University of Maryland (a USM institution), and relies on the Strategic Energy Investment Fund for its operations.

The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Governor and state agencies regarding the withdrawal from an interstate memorandum of understanding and the subsequent repeal of state regulations.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which the bill modifies by removing RGGI proceeds as a source of revenue.

The Treasurer's Office is responsible for holding the Strategic Energy Investment Fund separately and managing the investment of its funds, both of which are affected by the structural changes in the bill.
This multi-agency initiative focuses on climate resilience and environmental preservation; the withdrawal from RGGI represents a major shift in the state strategies this initiative coordinates.

The bill mandates that the Division of Historical and Cultural Programs within the Department of Planning provide staffing for the newly created Commission on the Ten Commandments Monument.

bill_summary: The Old Line Plate Program Act of 2026 requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to develop and auction numeric-only registration plates that resemble Maryland's 1911 license plates, featuring white characters on a black background. The bill establishes a program for the auction, issuance, and transfer of 'registration number rights' for numeric-only sequences of one to five digits, with collected fees used to recover administrative costs and the remainder credited to the Transportation Trust Fund.
stakeholders: Owners of passenger vehicles, light trucks, and multipurpose vehicles in Maryland; vehicle registration number collectors; and the Maryland Department of Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues will increase from auction proceeds and transfer fees, with the first auction required by December 1, 2026. TTF expenditures will also increase for plate production and auction administration. While the exact impact depends on participation, an illustrative estimate from the Fiscal Note suggests $275,000 in annual revenue based on the auction of 1,000 plates at an average price of $275, with production costs estimated at $10 per set and auction costs at $27,500 per event.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including developing the Old Line Plate, managing the inventory of numeric-only registration numbers, operating the public auction program, and adopting regulations.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a modal administration under the Department of Transportation, and the bill directs that all fees collected from the program be credited to the Transportation Trust Fund, which the Department manages.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services oversees Maryland Correctional Enterprises, which is the entity responsible for the actual manufacturing and production of Maryland state vehicle registration plates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Motor Vehicle Administration and will be involved in drafting the necessary regulations and reviewing the legal framework for the auction and transfer of registration number rights.

The Maryland State Police enforce motor vehicle laws and traffic safety; the introduction of a new registration plate design (numeric-only with a unique color scheme) impacts law enforcement identification and automated reader systems.

The Office of Administrative Hearings will adjudicate any contested cases resulting from the Motor Vehicle Administration's authority to deny, suspend, or revoke registration number rights or transfers.

The Office of Legislative Audits will be responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of the Motor Vehicle Administration's management of the auction program and the collection of associated revenues.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state's budget and personnel; the bill creates a new revenue stream and requires state expenditures for the administration of the auction and plate production.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state procurement and contracts, which may include approving any major service contracts required for the plate production or the operation of the public auction program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals may be called upon to adjudicate bid protests or contract disputes if the state procures external services for the auction platform or plate manufacturing.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for overseeing the fiscal integrity and revenue collection processes established by the bill.
The State Treasurer manages state funds, including the Transportation Trust Fund, and sits on the Board of Public Works to approve procurements related to the implementation of this new program.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the criteria for overtime pay exemptions for employees working in administrative, executive, or professional capacities. It establishes a specific schedule of minimum weekly salary thresholds that must be met for the exemption to apply, starting at $769.23 in July 2027 and increasing annually to $961.54 by July 2031. It also codifies specific duty-based requirements related to management, office work, or specialized intellectual instruction.
stakeholders: Employees in administrative, executive, and professional roles; private and public sector employers in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, so specific dollar estimates for state and local government impacts are unavailable. The bill establishes new salary thresholds for overtime exemptions which will likely increase labor costs for employers, including the State and local jurisdictions, as they may be required to pay overtime to previously exempt employees or increase salaries to meet the new minimum thresholds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary regulatory agency responsible for enforcing workplace safety and labor laws, including the wage and hour regulations that this bill directly amends.

As the state's central personnel and fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for managing state employee classifications and the state budget, both of which will be significantly impacted by changes to overtime eligibility and salary thresholds.
USM is one of the state's largest employers of professional and administrative staff; many employees in these categories may have their exempt status affected by the new salary thresholds.

PERB oversees collective bargaining for state and higher education employees. Changes to overtime exemptions directly intersect with labor contracts and the terms of employment for represented workers.
The Comptroller's office manages the payroll for state employees and will be responsible for implementing technical payroll changes to reflect new overtime eligibility and compensation rules.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the interpretation and implementation of new labor laws and would represent the state in disputes involving wage and hour claims.
The Judiciary employs a substantial number of administrative and professional staff through the AOC whose overtime exempt status will be governed by these new statutory definitions.
MSDE oversees local school systems and employs professional staff. The bill codifies duties tests and salary thresholds that affect the classification of educational administrators and professionals.
MDOT is a major state employer with a large workforce including many professional and administrative roles that may transition from exempt to non-exempt under the proposed salary escalations.
The Commission coordinates policy for postsecondary institutions that employ thousands of administrative and professional workers affected by these new overtime standards.

Traffic calming devices, such as raised crosswalks and narrowed roads, directly impact pedestrian safety and accessibility for residents with disabilities, which is a core focus of this department's advocacy and policy coordination.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, MDOT oversees the state's multi-modal transportation network and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which will fund the required study.

The bill requires a consistent statewide policy for traffic calming on highways in the State. As the agency responsible for operating and maintaining Maryland's toll highways, the MDTA would be affected by the implementation of such a policy.

The State Highway Administration is the primary agency tasked with conducting the study, researching best practices, developing guidelines, and reporting recommendations for a statewide traffic calming policy.

Federal fund revenues are expected to increase by $44,800,000 accordingly. Local governments providing PRP services may experience increased expenditures to adjust delivery processes and increased revenues from Medicaid billing. Small business PRP providers will receive higher reimbursement but are required to provide more services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and oversee the reimbursement of psychiatric rehabilitation program (PRP) services.
The bill has a significant fiscal impact, increasing state Medicaid expenditures by an estimated $74.7 million annually starting in FY 2027, requiring budget planning and oversight by DBM.
The bill focuses on youth psychiatric rehabilitation services, directly aligning with this office's mission to improve access to health services and well-being for Maryland's children.
Psychiatric Rehabilitation Programs serve individuals with serious emotional disturbances or mental disorders, which are categories of disability coordinated by this department.
The bill targets youth with severe functional impairments living with guardians; this population often receives preventative services and aid through DHS and local departments of social services.

Youth involved in the juvenile justice system frequently require psychiatric rehabilitation services; the bill's changes to reimbursement and service frequency directly impact treatment options for DJS youth.
The Commission is responsible for planning the state's health system needs and improving access to care, which includes community-based psychiatric support services.

The OAG will likely provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of regulations, especially concerning potential conflicts with federal laws like EPSDT and the Mental Health Parity Act mentioned in the fiscal note.

OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies; changes to Medicaid reimbursement rules and service caps may lead to hearings regarding medical necessity or benefit denials.
The target population for these psychiatric services includes school-aged youth, and PRPs often coordinate with educational systems to support students with serious emotional disturbances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Edible Forests and Foraging Program within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to manage and regulate the harvesting of mushrooms and plant materials on State-owned land. It requires the department to designate foraging areas where individuals must obtain a permit to forage and allows for the establishment of 'edible forests' where no permit is required for noncommercial personal consumption. A special fund is created to collect permit fees and support the program's administrative and maintenance costs.
stakeholders: Individuals who forage for mushrooms or plant materials for personal consumption and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures increase starting in fiscal 2027. The Department of Natural Resources estimates that establishing an edible forest plot costs approximately $10,000 per acre for site preparation and planting. Additional staff costs, such as a technician, may be required at approximately $75,223 annually. Special fund revenues will increase from foraging permit application fees, though the total amount is indeterminate. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Natural Resources as the primary agency responsible for establishing, administering, and regulating the Edible Forests and Foraging Program, including designating foraging areas and issuing permits.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Edible Forests and Foraging Fund separately and to invest the money within the fund.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the Edible Forests and Foraging Fund, which is a special, nonlapsing fund created to support the program.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM will oversee the budget for the new program and fund. The fiscal note also suggests that additional personnel may eventually be needed to manage the program.

The bill mandates the establishment of edible forests on 'State-owned land,' not just land owned by DNR. As the agency responsible for the maintenance and management of state facilities and real estate, DGS may be impacted by these land-use designations.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources as it develops the regulations, permit requirements, and fee waiver processes mandated by the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Natural Resources and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which must include appropriations for the new Edible Forests and Foraging Fund.
The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and the use or transfer of state property, which may be relevant as areas of state-owned land are designated for the program.
The program's focus on cultivating noninvasive plants for consumption aligns with the Department of Agriculture's mission regarding plant resource protection and environmental stewardship.
The establishment of edible forests and foraging areas impacts land use and quality of life in rural counties, areas of primary focus for the Rural Maryland Council.
The Department of Planning provides policy guidance on sustainable growth and resource management, which overlaps with the creation of new land-use categories like edible forests.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and procurement policy initiatives. The bill mandates new procurement standards that affect executive agencies and places final approval authority in the hands of the Chief Procurement Officer, an executive branch official.

Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the existing state prohibition that prevents applicants for video lottery operation licenses, current license holders, and individuals or entities with at least a 5% ownership interest in video lottery facilities from making campaign contributions to candidates for nonfederal public office in Maryland.
stakeholders: Applicants for video lottery operation licenses, video lottery operation license holders, owners of interests in video lottery facilities, and candidates for nonfederal public office in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals Section 13-237 of the Election Law Article, which is the primary body of law overseen and administered by the State Board of Elections. The agency is responsible for regulating campaign finance reporting and ensuring compliance with election laws affected by this repeal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts applicants and holders of video lottery operation licenses, which are regulated by this agency. The bill specifically references the State Government Article sections governing the agency's oversight of video lottery facilities and operations.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes criminal offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process and campaign finance laws. Repealing a prohibition on specific types of campaign contributions directly affects the scope of their investigative and prosecutorial oversight.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies, including the State Board of Elections and the Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal implications of repealing these contribution restrictions.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the agencies impacted by this legislation. The Governor also has the authority to sign or veto the legislation, which represents a policy shift regarding the interaction between gaming interests and political campaigns.

The State Ethics Commission is charged with maintaining public confidence in the integrity of state government. Changes to campaign finance laws involving highly regulated industries like gaming have implications for government transparency and public ethics standards.

bill_summary: This bill allows for the reallocation of school safety grants to local school systems that have fully expended their initial allocations and demonstrate further unmet needs for school resource officers or law enforcement coverage within the same fiscal year.
stakeholders: Local school systems, local law enforcement agencies, and public school students and staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill authorizes the redistribution of an existing $10,000,000 mandated annual appropriation for school safety grants. While the total State expenditure remains unchanged at $10,000,000, the bill allows funds to be reallocated to jurisdictions with greater need, potentially affecting the distribution of revenue and expenditures among local school systems. Specific dollar estimates for administrative reallocation costs are unavailable as no formal Fiscal Note was included with the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As an independent unit within MSDE specifically responsible for school safety grants and coordinating the requirements of the Safe Schools Act (of which Section 7-1508 is a core component), this agency is the primary body that would manage the reallocation process for these funds.

MSDE is the parent agency for the Maryland Center for School Safety and oversees the 24 local school systems mentioned in the bill. The agency's leadership will be responsible for policy changes regarding how these school safety grants are administered and reallocated.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution. The authority to reallocate appropriated grant funds within a fiscal year typically requires oversight or coordination with DBM to ensure fiscal compliance and accurate revenue/expenditure tracking.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and manages law enforcement and youth program funds. Because the grants in question serve both local school systems and local law enforcement agencies for school resource officers, GOCPP may be involved in the coordination or evaluation of 'need' for reallocation.

The bill mandates that the Governor continue to include a specific $10 million appropriation in the annual budget bill. Changes to how these funds are distributed or reallocated affect the Governor's budget proposals and policy priorities regarding school safety.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a regulatory framework for the sale and resale of event tickets in Maryland. It requires ticket resellers who sell 50 or more tickets annually to register with the Office of the Attorney General, obtain a surety bond, and submit biannual reports. The bill caps resale prices at 110% of the initial ticket price, limits secondary marketplace fees, requires refunds for counterfeit or cancelled events within 10 days, and mandates the use of technology to prevent ticket-buying bots.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Division of Consumer Protection
stakeholders: Ticket resellers, secondary ticket exchanges, ticket issuers (including venues, sports teams, and performers), and event ticket consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $258,600 in FY 2027 to hire one program administrator, one administrative aide, and one assistant Attorney General to implement and enforce the registration program. Annual costs are projected to increase to $346,900 by FY 2031. No material impact on State or local revenues is expected, though civil and criminal penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act could lead to increased special fund recoveries.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the OAG's Division of Consumer Protection with administering the new ticket reseller registration program, maintaining a public list of registrants, receiving sales reports, and enforcing the Act through the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

As the manager of major sports and entertainment venues like Camden Yards and M&T Bank Stadium, the Authority acts as a 'Ticket Issuer' and 'Venue Operator,' making it subject to the bill's requirements for refunds, transferability disclosures, and anti-bot technology implementation.

Member institutions within the system operate athletic departments, theaters, and performance venues that issue tickets for public events, subjecting them to the bill's regulatory standards for ticket issuers.

The university acts as a ticket issuer for its athletic events and cultural performances, requiring compliance with the bill's provisions regarding refund timelines, transferability, and technological safeguards against automated purchases.

The fiscal note identifies a need for three new positions (Program Administrator, Administrative Aide, and Assistant Attorney General) and significant general fund expenditures to implement the bill, which falls under DBM's personnel and budgetary oversight.

Because violations of the bill are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices, enforcement actions and consumer lawsuits would be adjudicated within the state court system managed by the AOC.
The bill regulates the ticket market for entertainment, arts, and sports, which are vital components of the state's tourism and economic development sectors overseen by the Department of Commerce.
As a ticket-issuing state institution for collegiate events and cultural programming, the college must comply with the bill's mandates for ticket issuers.
The commission operates an archaeological park and museum that issues tickets for public entry and events, making it subject to the bill's requirements for ticket issuers.
The corporation manages the Reginald F. Lewis Museum and issues tickets for entry and programs, requiring adherence to the bill's consumer protection and refund standards.

The bill mandates that ticket issuers implement technology to prevent automated bot purchases; state agencies acting as ticket issuers may require guidance or strategy from DoIT to meet these technical requirements.
Maryland Public Television (MPT) may act as a ticket issuer for cultural events or member-focused programming, necessitating compliance with the bill's regulations.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies tasked with implementing the bill and is responsible for proposing the budget allocations necessary for the new regulatory program.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county to establish subclasses of real property consisting of land and improvements to land and set separate real property tax rates for each subclass.
Title: Property Taxes - Authority of Counties to Establish Subclasses and Set Separate Rates for Land and Improvements to Land
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Baltimore City and Maryland county governments to establish separate subclasses for real property consisting of land and improvements to land, allowing them to set different tax rates for each subclass.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City, and county governing bodies
stakeholders: Maryland property owners, Baltimore City and county governments, and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are estimated to increase by $39,125,030 in FY 2027 for SDAT to implement computer system modifications, data storage, and additional personnel. Local government expenditures are projected to increase by $14,800,000 in FY 2027 to reimburse SDAT for 90% of these implementation costs. Local property tax revenues may increase or decrease depending on the specific tax rates adopted by individual jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes counties to create separate tax subclasses for land and improvements, which will lead to a significant increase in the complexity of property assessments and a likely surge in appeals requiring adjudication by this agency.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, this agency will experience an increased caseload for factual determinations and appeals concerning real property valuations and the application of separate tax rates.

The bill is projected to increase State general fund expenditures by tens of millions of dollars for IT system modifications and personnel, directly impacting the state's budget development and fiscal planning overseen by DBM.

The fiscal note identifies a requirement for massive IT system modifications and data storage expansions costing over $35 million; DoIT is responsible for the state's overarching information technology strategy and infrastructure oversight.
The bill enables land value taxation, which the fiscal note identifies as a tool for promoting 'smart growth' and sustainable development—core objectives of the Department of Planning's mission.

The OAG will provide necessary legal counsel to state agencies regarding the implementation of new tax subclasses and represent the state in litigation resulting from changes to the property tax system.

The Board of Public Works would be responsible for reviewing and approving the significant procurement contracts and capital expenditures required for the mandated IT system overhauls and software adjustments.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees general tax policy and revenue collection; changes to property tax structures and their fiscal impacts on the state budget are relevant to this agency's oversight.
The bill involves a significant shift in local taxation authority and requires high-level executive branch coordination and the proposal of substantial annual budget increases for implementation.
The Treasurer manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, which will likely review the large-scale IT contracts necessitated by the bill's technical requirements.

The transition to split-rate property taxes has a potentially meaningful impact on small businesses and the overall economic development climate, which the Department of Commerce is tasked with monitoring.

The bill's focus on taxing vacant land and improvements separately is a policy tool often used for community revitalization and discouraging urban blight, aligning with the department's housing and community objectives.
OLA will be responsible for conducting fiscal compliance and performance audits regarding the significant state expenditures and system transitions required to implement the bill.
This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable development; the bill supports planning visions related to smart growth and revitalizing urban centers through land value taxation incentives.

Synopsis: Specifying that certain requirements under the Climate Solutions Now Act of 2022 are to be carried out to the extent economically practicable, including requirements concerning achieving certain direct greenhouse gas emissions reductions from certain buildings, measuring and reporting direct emissions data to the Department of the Environment, achieving certain greenhouse gas emissions reduction goals, and achieving zero-emission vehicle goals relating to the State vehicle fleet and local school buses; etc.
Title: Climate Solutions Affordability Act of 2026
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
