The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. Since the bill concerns the legal status of trust settlors and mentions the reimbursement of taxes on trust income or principal, it may have implications for the administration and collection of state income or inheritance taxes.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel on the interpretation of state laws. This bill makes substantive changes to the Estates and Trusts Article regarding the definition of a trust settlor and creditor protection, requiring legal oversight.

The Register of Wills is the primary state agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes. Changes to the classification of trust settlors and spousal trusts directly impact estate administration and tax liability assessments under their jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow statewide a person to hunt deer on Sundays throughout the deer bow hunting season and to hunt turkey using a bow and arrow on Sundays throughout the turkey hunting season.
Title: Natural Resources - Bow Hunting - Sundays
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to allow bow hunting for deer and turkey on Sundays throughout their respective hunting seasons statewide in Maryland.
stakeholders: Bow hunters, small businesses (including outfitters and equipment retailers), farmers, and residents in areas with significant deer or turkey populations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. However, it may have a meaningful economic impact on small businesses due to increased hunter expenditures and potential reductions in agricultural crop damage and deer-vehicle collisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Natural Resources is authorized by this bill to establish Sunday hunting for deer and turkey using a bow and arrow. The agency manages hunting seasons, enforces conservation laws through its Natural Resources Police, and oversees the regulations amended by this legislation.

The expansion of hunting opportunities is intended, in part, to manage deer populations which cause significant crop damage. The Department of Agriculture represents the interests of the farming community that would benefit from reduced agricultural losses.

The fiscal note indicates that a reduction in the deer population may lead to a decrease in deer-vehicle collisions. MDOT, specifically through the State Highway Administration, is responsible for highway safety and infrastructure maintenance affected by such incidents.

The fiscal note highlights a potential meaningful economic impact on small businesses related to hunting, such as lodging, food, and equipment providers. The Department of Commerce is responsible for supporting economic growth and the state's competitive position in these sectors.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and would be responsible for ensuring the new regulations comply with existing state and federal law, as well as defending the agency in any related litigation.
The Council addresses challenges in Maryland's 18 rural counties, where hunting is a significant cultural and economic activity and where agricultural damage from deer populations is most prevalent.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Natural Resources. The Governor is responsible for policy initiatives regarding environmental conservation and rural affairs mentioned in the bill's scope.

Synopsis: Authorizing the expungement of a disposition under a certain provision of law if the disposition was included in a case that was disposed of by the court with a no finding designation or designated by the court as having been terminated without finding.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Expungement - No Finding and Case Terminated Without Finding
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the expungement of court and police records to include criminal charges that did not result in an unequivocal conviction but were instead disposed of by the court with a 'no finding' designation or marked as having been 'terminated without finding.'
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals with criminal cases resulting in 'no finding' or 'terminated without finding' dispositions, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $11,700 in fiscal 2027 for the Judiciary to update expungement-related brochures, forms, and instructional materials. Although the bill may increase the volume of expungement petitions, the Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services expect to handle the operational impact with existing resources. No material impact is anticipated for local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch as it requires the courts to process expungement petitions for new categories of dispositions ('no finding' and 'terminated without finding'). The Administrative Office of the Courts will need to update case management systems, forms, brochures, and instructional materials to accommodate these changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department's Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) is the central repository for criminal records in Maryland. This agency is responsible for executing expungement orders and ensuring that the designated records are removed from public inspection.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals who are the primary beneficiaries of expungement laws. Their staff will need to advise clients on eligibility and assist them in filing petitions under these newly authorized disposition categories.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police maintains police records that are subject to expungement orders. They must ensure compliance with court-ordered expungements by removing or shielding relevant investigative and arrest records.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides legal counsel to the agencies implementing this law (Judiciary and DPSCS). They also have a significant role in interpreting criminal procedure laws and advising on the legal standards for expungement.

The MVA maintains driving records that include criminal transportation-related offenses. Expungement orders for violations of the Transportation Article (which are included in the expanded scope of Section 10-110) require the MVA to remove those records from their systems.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the management of transportation-related records and coordinate the implementation of policies affecting motor vehicle and criminal law enforcement records across its modal administrations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy. It has a high interest in legislation that modifies the criminal justice process, record-keeping, and the long-term impacts of convictions on residents.

The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for permanent government and judicial records. When a court orders an expungement, the Archives must comply by identifying and removing or shielding any archived records that fall under the scope of the order.

The bill affects expungement eligibility for specific cannabis-related offenses listed under Section 10-110, which fall under the regulatory and policy oversight of the Maryland Cannabis Administration regarding the impact of past convictions on industry participation and public health.

Synopsis: Repealing and establishing the methodology used to calculate the weekly benefit amount; altering the taxable wage base used to determine employer contributions to the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund and the amount of earned wages subtracted from a weekly benefit amount; requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to determine and make available online the State annual average wage applicable to the rate of contribution; requiring, beginning in 2027, the maximum weekly benefit to be 40% of the state average weekly wage; etc.
Title: Unemployment Insurance Modernization Act of 2026
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The Unemployment Insurance Modernization Act of 2026 updates the Maryland unemployment insurance system by replacing fixed dollar amounts for benefits and employer contributions with formulas tied to the State's average wages. It establishes a new methodology for calculating weekly benefit amounts, phases in a maximum weekly benefit of 40% of the State average weekly wage by 2027, and increases the employer taxable wage base to 16% of the State average annual wage by 2029. Additionally, it modifies the treatment of earned wages and dependent allowances for claimants.
stakeholders: Unemployed individuals in Maryland, Maryland employers, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a significant increase in both revenues to the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund (via an increased taxable wage base) and expenditures from the Fund (via increased weekly benefit amounts). The taxable wage base is shifted from a fixed $8,500 to 16% of the State average annual wage by 2029, and the maximum weekly benefit is phased into 40% of the State average weekly wage by 2027. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the source text, specific total dollar estimates for these revenue and expenditure changes are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for administering the Unemployment Insurance program. The bill requires the Department and the Secretary of Labor to establish new methodologies for benefit amounts, taxable wage bases, and state average wage calculations.

The bill explicitly states that compensation for serving as an election judge for a local board of elections may not be included when computing wages subtracted from unemployment benefits. The State Board of Elections oversees these local boards.

The bill alters the taxable wage base used to determine employer contributions to the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund, which significantly impacts the cost of doing business and the economic climate in Maryland.

As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for monitoring the fiscal impact on the state budget, including the state's own costs as an employer contributing to the Unemployment Insurance system.
The OAH adjudicates contested cases involving the Department of Labor, including unemployment insurance benefit disputes which may arise from the new methodologies established by this bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and would be involved in the drafting and legal review of regulations required by the bill to carry out the modernization of unemployment insurance.

The Treasurer's Office manages and protects state funds. While the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund is separate, the Treasurer's role in state financial management and banking relates to the handling of large-scale state revenues and distributions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates major policy initiatives like unemployment insurance modernization, and the Governor proposes the annual state budget which is affected by these fiscal changes.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is concerned with the collection of state revenues and the overall fiscal health of Maryland funds, including those impacted by changes in employer contribution rates.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning in the 2028-2029 school year, each public middle school and each public high school to begin instruction not earlier than 8 a.m. and 8:30 a.m., respectively, unless granted a waiver by the State Board of Education under certain circumstances; and requiring each county board of education and each public charter school to implement a certain public service campaign to raise awareness of sleep deprivation and later school start times.
Title: Public Middle, High, and Charter Schools - Start Time for Instruction
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill mandates that beginning in the 2028-2029 school year, Maryland public middle schools must start instruction no earlier than 8:00 a.m. and public high schools no earlier than 8:30 a.m. The State Board of Education may grant waivers for compelling reasons, though a lack of funding is explicitly excluded as a valid reason. Additionally, local school boards and charter schools must conduct a public information campaign during the 2027-2028 school year to educate the community on the health and academic impacts of sleep deprivation and the benefits of later start times.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and local county boards of education
stakeholders: Middle and high school students, parents, teachers, school administrators, and local boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. At the local level, fiscal impacts vary significantly by jurisdiction; while some counties like Anne Arundel already comply and expect no impact, others face substantial costs primarily due to increased transportation needs. For example, Frederick County Public Schools estimates first-year costs exceeding $11,000,000 with annual recurring costs of $6,000,000 for additional buses, drivers, and maintenance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state agency overseeing public and charter schools, MSDE and the State Board of Education are responsible for granting waivers for school start times and assisting local boards with required public information campaigns regarding sleep deprivation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Education and MSDE, particularly concerning the statutory requirements for school hours and the legal framework for granting or denying start-time waivers.
The shifting of instruction start times for middle and high schools impacts the deployment and coordination of school safety personnel and protocols, which are overseen by this agency.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives; this bill involves a significant change in statewide education policy and student health initiatives.

Synopsis: Requiring each county to adopt a charter by December 31, 2032, using a certain procedure; altering the method by which a county shall adopt a charter under certain circumstances; requiring the charter to provide for the election of members of the county council by the voters of councilmanic districts; limiting the applicability of certain constitutional provisions governing code home rule counties; and requiring the amendment proposed by the Act be submitted to the qualified voters of the State for approval or rejection.
Title: Constitutional Amendment - Form of County Government - Requirement to Adopt Charter Home Rule

bill_summary: This constitutional amendment requires all Maryland counties to transition to a charter home rule form of government by December 31, 2032. It mandates that each county charter provide for a county executive and a county council with members elected from councilmanic districts. The bill establishes a specific procedure for adoption, requiring boards of county commissioners to appoint charter boards by 2029 and vote on the resulting charters by 2032, while phasing out code home rule provisions once charters are adopted.
responsible_party: Maryland County Boards of Commissioners, Charter Boards, and the State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Residents and local government officials in Maryland counties currently operating under commission or code home rule systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text. Financial implications include costs to counties for appointing charter boards, administrative support for drafting charters, and mandatory newspaper publications. Additionally, the State Board of Elections will incur costs to include the amendment on the 2026 general election ballot, and affected counties will incur expenses to restructure their local governments into executive and council-based branches.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor has a constitutional role in receiving election returns for constitutional amendments, as specified in the bill, and the office manages intergovernmental relations with county executives and local entities.
As the chief legal officer for the State, the OAG provides critical legal counsel on the constitutional amendment process and the legal framework for county home rule and legislative authority.

The agency provides technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments regarding administrative structures and land use planning, both of which are significantly affected by a transition to charter home rule.

The agency maintains the Maryland Manual On-Line, which is the official record of state and local government structures, and would be responsible for documenting these constitutional and structural changes.
The agency is responsible for supervising the statewide referendum for this constitutional amendment and overseeing the transition to councilmanic district-based voting required by the bill.
As the principal custodian of the state's official records, the Secretary of State manages the filing and certification of laws and constitutional amendments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a merchant, in a certain transaction, from prohibiting a person from making a cash payment to purchase a good or service; requiring a person to purchase a good or service by using a credit or debit card, or charging or collecting from a person a fee for making a cash payment for the purchase of a good or service; and establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to certain enforcement and penalty provisions under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
Title: Consumer Protection - Retail Transactions - Cash Payments
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds

bill_summary: This bill prohibits merchants from refusing cash payments for in-person retail transactions totaling between $5 and $300. It also bans merchants from requiring credit or debit cards for these transactions or charging fees for cash payments. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The bill requires the Office of the Attorney General to provide two warnings before a merchant is subject to civil penalties of up to $5,000 for a first violation and $10,000 for subsequent violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Retail merchants and consumers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's penalty provisions are not expected to have a material impact on State or local government finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can handle the bill's requirements using existing resources. Small businesses that do not currently accept cash may face meaningful operational impacts to comply with the new requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General with enforcement, including a specific mandate to provide merchants with two opportunities to comply before assessing civil penalties.

As the agency responsible for the licensing and regulation of various professions and industries, the Department of Labor oversees many of the merchants affected by these new requirements for retail cash transactions.

The bill mandates significant changes to business operations for merchants across the state, impacting the economic and competitive environment that the Department of Commerce is tasked with supporting.
The bill establishes civil penalties for violations that are recoverable through legal proceedings, potentially impacting the workload of the judicial branch.

Restricting cash payments in retail transactions is often identified as an equity issue impacting the unbanked and underbanked populations, which falls under the commission's interest in fair access to public accommodations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a 'meaningful' impact on small businesses, as those currently operating without cash will need to implement operational changes to comply with the mandate.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the various agencies, including the Office of the Attorney General and the Department of Labor, that will implement and enforce this legislation.

Synopsis: Exempting certain religious educational institutions accredited by accrediting bodies recognized by the U.S. Department of Education from the requirement to obtain a certificate of approval from the Maryland Higher Education Commission to operate in the State.
Title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Religious Educational Institutions - Certificate of Approval
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill exempts accredited religious educational institutions that were authorized and in continuous operation in Maryland before January 1, 2013, from the requirement to obtain a certificate of approval from the Maryland Higher Education Commission to operate in the State.
stakeholders: Accredited religious educational institutions authorized before 2013 and students enrolled in religious vocation programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no significant impact on the Maryland Higher Education Commission's administrative operations, special fund revenues, or expenditures. There is no fiscal impact on local governments or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state agency for postsecondary oversight, this commission is responsible for the Certificate of Approval process which the bill modifies for certain religious institutions.
As the primary state agency for postsecondary oversight, this commission is responsible for the Certificate of Approval process which the bill modifies for certain religious institutions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Higher Education Commission and would be responsible for advising on the interpretation and enforcement of the new exemption criteria.
DBM is responsible for state budget oversight; the bill affects regulatory processes and potential fee revenues for the Maryland Higher Education Commission, an executive agency within its purview.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies, including the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and coordinates policy initiatives related to educational standards and religious exemptions.

Synopsis: Requiring a unit of State government to provide a certain debriefing of a contract award to certain persons on request; adding an exemption to the prohibition on an individual who assists in the drafting of specifications, an invitation for bids, or a request for proposals from submitting a bid or proposal or assisting in the submission of a bid or proposal; requiring a procurement contract to include a certain clause pertaining to certain contract modifications related to changes in law; altering the required contents of a certain change order; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Transparency and Procedures
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's state procurement processes to increase transparency and adjust administrative procedures. It requires state units to provide debriefings to unsuccessful bidders upon request before a contract award is finalized, mandates that all procurement contracts include a clause for equitable adjustments due to changes in law, and extends the window for contractors to file a written notice of a claim from 30 to 60 days. Additionally, it applies standard contract claim procedures to all state procurements rather than just construction projects and requires contractors to certify the accuracy and good faith of their claims before receiving payment.
responsible_party: Office of State Procurement (within the Department of General Services)
stakeholders: State procurement officers, state government units, contractors, and subcontractors seeking or working on Maryland state contracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a potential significant increase in State procurement expenditures across all funds, although a reliable estimate of the total fiscal impact is not feasible. Cost increases may arise from the new requirement for equitable adjustments due to changes in law, which limits the State's ability to negotiate such modifications. Furthermore, project timelines and costs could be impacted by extended claim filing periods and the requirement that debriefings be completed before contract approval. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of State Procurement, which is located within the Department of General Services, with establishing guidelines for procurement debriefings. As the state's central procurement authority, DGS is the primary agency responsible for implementing these procedural changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MSBCA is the independent body responsible for adjudicating the bid protests and contract disputes that are fundamentally modified by this bill. The changes to timelines, procedures, and the definition of 'final action' directly impact their case processing and legal standards.

The bill explicitly requires procurement officers to seek advice from the Office of the Attorney General on legal issues raised in protests or contract claims. OAG serves as the legal counsel for the units implementing these new procedures.

The bill prohibits contract awards from being presented to the Board of Public Works until requested debriefings are completed. It also mandates that procurement contracts (which the BPW must often approve) include specific clauses regarding equitable adjustments for changes in law.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees the approval of significant state contracts. The bill affects the timing and documentation requirements for contracts brought before the Board.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the State Treasurer oversees state procurements. The bill’s requirements for debriefings and contract clauses directly affect the workflow and standards of the Board.

The bill amends Section 13-212.1 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, which deals with procurement ethics and conflicts of interest. It adds a new exemption for individuals providing certain information, falling under the Commission's broad interest in maintaining integrity in state government.

MDOT is a primary procurement unit that manages high-value infrastructure and service contracts. The new rules regarding change orders, equitable adjustments for changes in law, and expanded claim procedures will significantly affect their project management and expenditures.

The Department of Health manages a high volume of complex health and human service procurement contracts. The bill's changes to debriefings, protest procedures, and contract modification requirements will apply to their numerous procurements.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and procurement efficiency. The potential increase in state expenditures for equitable adjustments and the alterations to procurement timelines impact their long-term fiscal planning.

The USM is a major state procurement entity. The bill’s changes to contract claims, specifically extending construction-style claim rules to all procurement contracts, will impact how the system manages disputes with vendors.

DoIT is the primary agency for information technology procurement and strategy. The bill specifically references IT accessibility requirements (§ 3A-312) in the context of mandated contract clauses and governs the high-value IT contracts managed by this agency.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of state agencies. The new statutory requirements for contract certifications, payment authorizations, and claim procedures will become new criteria for their periodic audits of executive and judicial agencies.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to develop and offer an apprenticeship program in skilled trades for incarcerated individuals; establishing that the purpose of the program is to assist incarcerated individuals to develop marketable job skills and to earn money that can be used once the individual is released from incarceration; authorizing the Department to pay all or part of an incarcerated individual's wages to a spouse, child, or other dependent in need of financial support; etc.

Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to establish the Incarcerated Individual Apprenticeship Program to provide incarcerated individuals with opportunities to serve as paid apprentices in skilled trades. The program operates independently of Maryland Correctional Enterprises and allows participation by state and local government agencies as well as private entities, ensuring participants are paid at least the state minimum wage.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, state and local government agencies, and private entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund expenditures will increase by at least 297,300 dollars in FY 2027, rising to 395,000 dollars by FY 2031, primarily for hiring program staff and correctional officers. There is no impact on state revenues. Local governments may see a minimal increase in expenditures if they choose to participate as employers in the apprenticeship program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, DPSCS is responsible for establishing the Incarcerated Individual Apprenticeship Program, managing participant accounts, and providing for the care and security of apprentices.

The Department of Labor oversees the state's apprenticeship and training programs; it will likely coordinate with DPSCS to ensure the new program meets state standards for skilled trades and certifications.
DBM oversees the state budget and personnel policies; any state agency electing to participate as an employer would require DBM's coordination for funding and personnel position management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's focus on job training for incarcerated individuals to reduce recidivism and improve economic mobility aligns with GOCPP’s mission to develop public safety and criminal justice strategies.

The board sets the statewide vision for workforce development and coordinates partnerships to align talent pipelines with Maryland's economic goals, making this new apprenticeship pathway relevant to their strategy.
As the agency responsible for the maintenance and construction of state-owned facilities, DGS is a primary candidate for employing incarcerated apprentices in skilled trades.

The bill permits DPSCS to direct apprenticeship wages to an incarcerated individual’s dependents in need, which directly intersects with DHS's mission of providing child support and economic assistance to families.
Specifically identified in the fiscal note as a potential employer, MDOT could utilize apprentices for highway maintenance and other skilled trade roles within its various administrations.
Identified as an information source in the fiscal note, MDA could potentially employ apprentices within its regulatory or service programs that involve skilled labor.
Identified as an information source in the fiscal note, MDE could potentially serve as a participating state agency employer for apprentices in environmental infrastructure and technical trades.
Identified as an information source in the fiscal note, DHCD could potentially involve apprentices in community revitalization or infrastructure projects.
Identified as an information source in the fiscal note, DNR could employ apprentices in various skilled trade capacities related to public land and park maintenance.
As an independent state agency providing technical environmental services, MES is specifically identified in the fiscal note as a candidate for employing skilled trade apprentices in its operations.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to DPSCS and other participating state agencies regarding the contracts and agreements required for the apprenticeship program.
The Comptroller’s office manages state payroll and revenue collection; it would be involved in the fiscal administration of wages paid to incarcerated apprentices by state agencies.
The Treasurer's Office manages state funds and sits on the Board of Public Works, which would oversee the fiscal integrity and significant expenditures related to the new program.
The Board of Public Works would be responsible for approving significant state contracts or expenditures associated with the apprenticeship program and agreements with participating entities.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinate policy initiatives like this statewide job training and recidivism reduction program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's mission to develop workforce pathways and service opportunities aligns with the bill’s goal of creating a new talent pipeline through incarcerated individual apprenticeships.
MSDE oversees vocational training and rehabilitation; it may play a role in the educational components or certification coordination for apprentices in skilled trades.

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to conduct studies on emerging technologies and trends to ensure a safe and transparent gambling environment. These studies must specifically examine cybersecurity, artificial intelligence for monitoring behavior and promoting responsible gaming, and digital identity verification. If the Commission lacks internal expertise, it is required to collaborate or contract with Maryland institutions of higher education, foundations, or private entities to perform the analysis.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Maryland gambling customers, the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, Maryland institutions of higher education, and private gaming technology entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, general fund expenditures will increase by as much as $100,000 in fiscal 2027 for the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency to hire a consultant to conduct the required studies. There is no projected impact on revenues. The estimate assumes a one-time expenditure as the bill does not specify a timeline for repeated studies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission (the Agency's governing body) to conduct studies on emerging technologies and trends to enhance gambling safety and transparency. It also specifically requires the Agency Director to participate in these collaborations.

The bill requires the Commission to collaborate or contract with institutions of higher education in the State to conduct the mandated studies. The fiscal note explicitly mentions the University System of Maryland provided input regarding potential staffing needs if selected as a collaborator.

The bill requires the Commission to collaborate or contract with institutions of higher education in the State. Morgan State University is specifically mentioned in the fiscal note as a potential contractor that provided feedback on the resource requirements for such a collaboration.
The bill is estimated to increase general fund expenditures by $100,000 in fiscal 2027 to hire consultants for the mandated studies, which falls under the fiscal oversight of DBM.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies like the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency and would likely be involved in reviewing contracts for the studies mandated by the bill.

bill_summary: The Comprehensive Community Safety Funding Act establishes an 11% excise tax on the gross receipts of federally licensed firearms dealers derived from the retail sale of firearms, firearm accessories, and ammunition. The tax applies to sales made in Maryland and to sales made to Maryland residents by out-of-state dealers who meet certain revenue or transaction thresholds. Collected revenues are designated for distribution to several state funds focused on violence prevention, trauma services, and victim support.
stakeholders: Federally licensed firearms dealers, Maryland residents purchasing firearms or ammunition, victims of homicide and their survivors, and public health and safety organizations focused on trauma and violence prevention.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a new state revenue source via an 11% excise tax on the gross receipts from sales of firearms and ammunition. Revenue is distributed as follows: 26% to the Maryland Violence Intervention and Prevention Program Fund, 26% to the Center for Firearm Violence Prevention and Intervention, 20% to the Coordinated Community Supports Partnership Fund, 20% to the Survivors of Homicide Victims Grant Program, 4% to the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, and 4% to the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center. Implementation is phased, beginning with large retailers on July 1, 2027, and extending to all other dealers on July 1, 2028. bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Uniform Simultaneous Death Act to align with the national Uniform Simultaneous Death Act. It introduces a 120-hour survival requirement for individuals to be considered to have survived a decedent for inheritance, property distribution, and insurance purposes. Additionally, it establishes evidentiary procedures for determining death and provides liability protections for third-party payors who act in good faith when distributing assets.
stakeholders: Property co-owners, beneficiaries, estate executors, insurance companies, and trustees.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish new evidentiary procedures and rules for determining survival in legal disputes. The Judicial Branch will be responsible for adjudicating these matters and managing property deposited with the court during disputes.

The bill defines 'governing instrument' to include insurance and annuity policies and 'payor' to include insurers. It establishes new rules for how insurance proceeds must be distributed when beneficiaries and the insured die nearly simultaneously.

The bill's definition of 'governing instrument' includes pensions and retirement benefit plans. As the administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System, this agency is a 'payor' that must comply with the 120-hour survival requirement for beneficiary payouts.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives; as this bill updates a uniform act and impacts multiple executive agencies (MDH, DBM, etc.), it requires administrative oversight.

The Secretary of State may be involved if there are international implications or inter-state coordination regarding water quality standards, though their role is secondary.

Title: Violent Criminals - Parole Limitation and Legislative Testimony Removal (Sexual Offender Accountability and Victim Protection Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

bill_summary: This bill, the Sexual Offender Accountability and Victim Protection Act, limits individuals convicted of specific sexual crimes and sentenced to life plus additional years to a single parole consideration. It mandates that if a victim, their family, or an advocacy group objects to parole, it must be permanently denied. Furthermore, the bill requires the Maryland General Assembly to remove online records of legislative testimony provided by individuals convicted of violent crimes upon a victim's request and establishes a formal process for others to request access to those records.
responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission and the Maryland General Assembly
stakeholders: Victims of sexual and violent crimes, their families and representatives, victims' advocacy organizations, incarcerated individuals convicted of specified sexual or violent crimes, and Maryland General Assembly committee staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill creates administrative requirements for the Maryland Parole Commission regarding victim notification and permanent parole denial. It also imposes administrative duties on General Assembly committee managers to process and review requests for removed legislative testimony. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Parole Commission, an agency within this department, by restricting the number of times an individual can be considered for parole and mandating a permanent denial of parole if a victim or the Commission objects.

The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the General Assembly and executive agencies regarding the constitutionality and implementation of the parole restrictions and the removal of public records. They would also defend the state in potential legal challenges to the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates statewide public safety and victim services policies. The bill's focus on sexual offender accountability and enhanced victim rights in the parole process aligns directly with its mission.

Limiting parole opportunities for individuals serving life sentences will lead to an increase in the average length of incarceration, resulting in significant long-term fiscal impacts on the state budget and prison population management.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Maryland Parole Commission. This bill significantly alters executive branch policy regarding parole eligibility and the granting of parole.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent defendants, many of whom are serving sentences affected by this bill. The bill curtails the future parole rights and due process of their clients by allowing for a permanent veto of parole.

As the central depository for government and legislative records of permanent value, the mandate to remove legislative testimony records from public access affects the agency's mission to preserve and provide access to the state's historical records.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Senate and the House of Delegates beginning with the 2033 legislative session; altering the method and timing of the election of State Senators; and requiring a Delegate who seeks election for a certain Senate term to vacate the seat of Delegate on the first day of the next immediately following legislative session.
Title: General Assembly - Membership, Election Timing for State Senators, and Eligibility
Status: In the House - First Reading House Rules and Executive Nominations

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to increase the membership of the Maryland General Assembly to 48 Senators and 144 Delegates beginning with the 2033 legislative session. It alters the election schedule for State Senators to establish staggered four-year terms starting with the 2032 election and requires any serving Delegate who seeks election to the Senate for a term beginning before their House term expires to vacate their seat.
responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly and the State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, current and future members of the Maryland General Assembly, and candidates for legislative office.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase starting in 2033 to account for the salaries, benefits, and office expenses of four additional legislators (one Senator and three Delegates). The State Board of Elections will also incur costs to include the proposed constitutional amendment on the 2026 general election ballot. Since a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the timing and method of State Senator elections, including a complex ranking system based on vote totals to determine term lengths. The agency must also manage the statewide referendum required for this constitutional amendment.

The Governor is constitutionally required to receive election returns and proclaim the adoption or rejection of constitutional amendments. Additionally, the Governor oversees the filling of vacancies in the General Assembly, which is impacted by the new vacancy requirements for Delegates seeking Senate seats.

The agency provides the data analysis and technical assistance used in legislative redistricting. Increasing the number of Senate and House seats (from 47/141 to 48/144) necessitates significant changes to the state's legislative district mapping and demographic calculations.

The agency administers the pension system for legislators. Increasing the number of legislators and introducing staggered 2-year and 4-year terms requires adjustments to their tracking of service credits and retirement eligibility for members of the General Assembly.
The OAG provides legal counsel on constitutional amendments and election laws. They would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new term-length determination method based on vote rankings.
As the principal custodian of the state's official records and laws, the Secretary of State must record and maintain the updated Maryland Constitution following the referendum.

The addition of one Senator and three Delegates involves long-term fiscal impacts on the state budget regarding legislative salaries, benefits, and office staff expenditures managed within the state's personnel framework.

The Commission manages financial disclosures and ethics training for all state legislators. An increase in the number of members of the General Assembly directly increases the volume of the agency's compliance and oversight activities.
The Comptroller is responsible for paying state employees, including legislators. Adding new members to the General Assembly would require administrative updates to the state's payroll processing.
The agency is the central depository for government records of permanent value, including the results of constitutional referendums and updated versions of the Maryland Constitution.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to include the option on the certificate of candidacy form for candidates for congressional offices to indicate that, if elected, the candidate and the candidate's spouse will not engage in certain stock trading activities during the candidate's term of office; and requiring the State Board to publish on its website information concerning candidates for congressional offices who make that indication.
Title: Election Law - Certificate of Candidacy for Congressional Offices - Stock Trading Activities (Congressional Stock Trading Transparency Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/21 at 1:00 p.m.
