bill_summary: This bill establishes that the registered owner of a Class G (trailer) vehicle is liable for the payment of video tolls and associated civil penalties when using Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) facilities. It extends existing toll collection, liability transfer, and enforcement procedures—including registration suspension and referral to the Central Collection Unit—to include trailers, primarily to address instances where a trailer obscures the towing vehicle's license plate.
stakeholders: Registered owners of Class G (trailer) vehicles, commercial vehicle operators, the Maryland Transportation Authority, and the Motor Vehicle Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues for the Maryland Transportation Authority are estimated to increase by approximately 11,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Central Collection Unit (CCU) and general fund revenues are also expected to increase as additional delinquent accounts are referred to CCU for collection. Local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for toll collection on Maryland facilities, the MDTA will assess video tolls for Class G vehicles, issue notices and citations, and collect revenues and penalties established by the bill.

An agency within MDOT, the MVA is responsible for providing registered owner addresses to MDTA and enforcing penalties by refusing or suspending the registration of Class G vehicles for toll violations.
MDOT is the departmental sponsor of the bill and the parent agency of the MVA, which is tasked with critical enforcement and data-sharing roles under the proposed legislation.
DBM oversees the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which will receive delinquent toll accounts for collection, leading to a significant increase in special fund revenues and expenditures.

The Judicial Branch, via the District Court, manages contested toll citations; the fiscal note highlights that increased citation volume from automated enforcement requires system upgrades and operational adjustments.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the transportation agencies involved in implementing these new liability standards and represents the state in related litigation or appeals.

Synopsis: Altering certain standards and requirements for variances from land use requirements under the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program.
Title: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program - Variances - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Chesapeake Bay -see also- Chesapeake Bay Restoration
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the standards and requirements for obtaining a land use variance within the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area. It prohibits certain variance applications, such as those requesting unauthorized uses or adjustments to mitigation requirements. The bill establishes a rebuttable presumption that existing accessory structures provide reasonable use of a property, requires applicants to demonstrate a substantial need for a variance that is not based on convenience or financial advantage, and limits the comparison properties that can be used to justify a variance request. Additionally, local boards of appeals are required to hear appeals on the record and grant deference to administrative findings of fact.
responsible_party: Critical Area Commission and local jurisdictions
stakeholders: Property owners in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area, local government planning and appeals boards, and the Critical Area Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill modifies administrative and legal standards for critical area variances, which may impact local government application and appeal processes, but no specific revenue or expenditure mandates are explicitly stated in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Critical Area Commission, which requested this bill, is housed within the Department of Natural Resources. DNR is the primary agency responsible for the conservation and management of the state's natural resources, including the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays. This bill directly alters the regulatory standards for the program overseen by DNR and the Commission.

The OAG serves as the chief legal counsel for state agencies, including the Critical Area Commission. This bill changes legal standards, creates new rebuttable presumptions, and alters the requirements for appeals and evidence, which will require significant legal interpretation and enforcement support from the OAG.

MDE is responsible for environmental protection and the restoration of the Chesapeake Bay. This bill's focus on land use variances in critical areas directly impacts habitat protection and water quality goals, which are central to MDE's mission and its collaboration with other agencies on Bay restoration.

MDP promotes sustainable growth and provides land use planning technical assistance to local governments. Since the bill alters how local jurisdictions process variances and manage their local critical area programs, it impacts the land use planning and policy guidance MDP provides to municipalities.

MDOT manages significant infrastructure and highway projects that often cross or are adjacent to critical areas. The stricter standards for variances, particularly the requirement to demonstrate that development cannot be located outside a habitat protection area, may impact the planning and execution of state transportation projects.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council is responsible for advising the Governor on the management and restoration of the Chesapeake Bay and coordinates interagency collaboration. This bill directly involves the state's primary regulatory framework for protecting Bay-adjacent land, making it highly relevant to the Council's advisory scope.

The MDA protects environmental resources and manages soil conservation. Many agricultural parcels are located within the Critical Area, and changes to variance standards for accessory structures or land use may impact farm operations and building on agricultural land near the coast.

As a departmental bill requested by an executive commission, the Governor's Office oversees the policy direction and legislative implementation of these changes as part of the administration's environmental and land use priorities.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will be involved in any fiscal impacts related to the administrative workload or potential changes in state funding requirements resulting from the tightened variance standards and the implementation of this Act.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that the photograph included on an identification card, a driver's license, or a moped operator's permit issued by the Motor Vehicle Administration be in color.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is required to approve the grants and expenditures for the flood management programs and studies established or modified by this bill.
The State Treasurer's Office is a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve grant expenditures and the use of State debt for the programs mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Altering and updating the standards and procedures governing the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program related to the approval of regulations, local program comprehensive reviews, locational standards for growth allocation, correcting mapping mistakes, and tree replanting.
Title: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program - Standards and Procedures
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Chesapeake Bay -see also- Chesapeake Bay Restoration
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill updates and clarifies standards and procedures for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program. Key updates include extending the local program comprehensive review cycle from 6 to 10 years, clarifying mapping mistake criteria for the Atlantic Coastal Bays, and requiring that court-ordered damages for illegal tree cutting be paid to local jurisdictions rather than the Department of Natural Resources.
stakeholders: Local jurisdictions within the Critical Area, property owners, land developers, and forestry or landscape professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a direct financial impact on state or local government finances. Although the bill directs damages for illegal tree clearing to be paid to local jurisdictions instead of the Department of Natural Resources, the Fiscal Note indicates this change reflects current practices and that state and local fiscal impacts are expected to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Critical Area Commission, which manages the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program, is a unit within the Department of Natural Resources. The bill modifies the program's standards, review cycles, and procedures for which DNR/Commission is responsible.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Critical Area Commission is the primary body whose powers, voting procedures, and regulatory processes are being updated by this bill. It is the direct implementing entity for the legislative changes.

The bill explicitly mentions that the chair of the Commission may refer matters to the Attorney General to bring actions against individuals for illegal tree cutting or clearing within the Critical Area.

The Critical Area Program involves land use planning, remapping, and local program reviews. The Department of Planning provides data analysis and technical assistance to local governments on sustainable growth and land use, which must align with Critical Area standards.
The bill involves the judicial assessment of damages by circuit courts for program violations, impacting how the judiciary handles these specific environmental litigation matters.

The Critical Area Protection Program's primary goal is protecting water quality. MDE is the state's lead agency for environmental restoration and water quality, and it coordinates with the Commission on shared environmental objectives.
Significant portions of the Critical Area consist of agricultural lands (Resource Conservation Areas). Changes to growth allocation and land use standards impact agricultural resource management.

The bill updates the professional credentials required for individuals preparing tree replanting plans from 'registered' to 'licensed' foresters and landscape architects, professions regulated by MD Labor.

Synopsis: Repealing certain fees charged to certain banking institutions by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation; altering certain provisions relating to the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, including the purpose and administration of the Fund; altering the date by which the Commissioner may match certain investments in the Fund from June 30, 2028, to June 30, 2030; altering and providing for certain assessment offset credits for certain banking institutions and credit unions; etc.
Title: Financial Institutions - Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund and Regulation of Entities - Revisions
Status: In the House - Favorable Report by Economic Matters

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates regulations for Maryland-chartered financial institutions and the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund. It extends the authority of the Office of Financial Regulation to match private investments in the fund through June 30, 2030, and expands the fund's purpose to include providing financial assistance to consumers in low- to moderate-income tracts. The bill also introduces new assessment offset credits for banks and credit unions that offer 'Maryland Opportunity Accounts,' modifies the definitions of 'branch' and 'emergency' to include cybersecurity incidents for bank closures, and repeals certain obsolete certification and filing fees.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Maryland-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and consumers and businesses in low- to moderate-income census tracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund revenues are projected to decrease by approximately $25,000 in FY 2027, increasing to at least $52,000 by FY 2031 due to new assessment offset credits for institutions offering Maryland Opportunity Accounts. Special fund expenditures increase by $14,000 in FY 2029 and FY 2030 for state-matched contributions to the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund. Additionally, the bill authorizes an equity capital investment of up to $2,500,000 and up to $250,000 for administrative expenses from the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines the Governor's role in proclaiming emergencies that necessitate the closure of banking institutions or branches, specifically adding cybersecurity incidents to this authority.

The bill amends the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding how interest on State money in the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund is accounted for, which directly impacts the Comptroller's revenue accounting and fund management responsibilities.

The bill explicitly designates the State Treasurer as the custodian of the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund and mandates the Treasurer to invest the fund's money in the same manner as other State funds.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and the Department of Labor. The bill also includes criminal penalties (misdemeanors) for unauthorized representation as a financial institution, which falls under the OAG's broad enforcement and advisory scope.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the development and execution of the state budget and the management of special funds. The bill establishes the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund subject to the state budget process.

This is a departmental bill for the Department of Labor. Its Office of Financial Regulation is the primary entity responsible for overseeing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, regulating banking institutions and credit unions, collecting assessments, and managing the proposed fee repeals.

Synopsis: Altering, from January 1 of the year of the election to July 1 of the year before the election, the earliest date on which the State Board of Elections may begin making distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund.
Title: Public Financing Act – Fair Campaign Financing Fund – Distributions
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/21 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill moves the earliest date that the State Board of Elections can begin making distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund to candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor from January 1 of the year of the election to July 1 of the year before the election.
stakeholders: Candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor participating in the gubernatorial public campaign financing program
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances. It alters the timing for distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund, but does not change the amount of funding available or the appropriations mandated by current law. The fund had a balance of $10,400,000 in October 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the State Board of Elections (SBE), which is the primary agency responsible for certifying candidate qualifications and authorizing distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund.
The Comptroller administers the Fair Campaign Financing Fund and is explicitly responsible for making distributions from the fund promptly upon authorization by the State Board of Elections.
The bill directly affects the timing of public campaign funding available to candidates for the office of Governor, altering the campaign finance landscape for the state's chief executive.
The bill affects gubernatorial tickets, which include candidates for Lieutenant Governor, by allowing earlier access to public matching funds during the election cycle.

As the state's chief financial agency responsible for managing and distributing state funds, the Treasurer's Office has a general interest in the timing and management of distributions from state-held funds like the FCFF.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state and oversees budget execution and long-term fiscal planning; the timing of multimillion-dollar distributions from a state fund impacts cash flow and fiscal oversight.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and would be responsible for advising on the implementation of the new distribution timeline and any related regulatory changes.
OLA conducts fiscal compliance and performance audits of state agencies, including the SBE and the Comptroller, and would monitor the legality and accuracy of the earlier fund distributions.

Synopsis: Establishing competitive proof of concept procurements as an authorized procurement method; providing that a competitive proof of concept procurement may have multiple phases of evaluation; requiring a unit of State government to obtain the approval of the Chief Procurement Officer or a designee before conducting a certain competitive proof of concept procurement; altering the required contents of a competitive proof of concept procurement solicitation; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Competitive Proof of Concept Procurement
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer

bill_summary: This bill establishes competitive proof of concept procurements as a formal Maryland State procurement method. It allows State units to use this method to test and evaluate goods, services, or technologies in real-world environments and proceed through multiple evaluation phases, including full implementation or deployment. The bill mandates oversight by the Chief Procurement Officer and the Secretary of Information Technology and requires that solicitations and awards be posted on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage.
stakeholders: Maryland State government units and agencies, and private vendors including small, minority, and veteran-owned businesses seeking to provide innovative technology or services to the State.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no material impact on State or local government finances. While the new procurement method may create operational efficiencies for certain State agencies, it does not require additional allocations or change revenue structures. The Department of General Services and the Department of Legislative Services both characterize the fiscal impact as none or minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of General Services (DGS) is the primary implementing agency. The bill requires the Chief Procurement Officer (within DGS) to approve proof of concept procurements, requires solicitations and awards to be posted on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (managed by DGS), and tasks DGS with adopting regulations for the new procurement method.

The bill requires units to obtain approval from the Secretary of Information Technology for any proof of concept procurement involving IT. Additionally, DGS must consult with DoIT when adopting regulations and policies for these procurements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is responsible for establishing guidelines for Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) participation goals for these procurements. It also has the authority to exempt certain proof of concept procurements from the Small Business Reserve designation.

The Attorney General is consulted in establishing guidelines for MBE participation goals. Additionally, the OAG provides legal counsel on procurement law and, as noted in the fiscal note, has previously advised on the limitations of existing proof of concept laws.

The Secretary of Transportation is specifically named as a consultant in the establishment of guidelines for minority business enterprise participation percentage goals for procurement contracts under this bill.

As the state's highest administrative body for procurement oversight, the Board of Public Works approves significant contracts, including those that may result from the full implementation phases authorized by this new procurement method.
The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts that may be issued under the expanded scope of this bill.
The State Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works, which approves significant state contracts, and the agency is responsible for managing the state funds involved in these procurements.
The University System of Maryland is a major state procurement entity identified as a stakeholder and potential user of this new, streamlined procurement pathway for innovative products and services.

The Department of Commerce is identified as a stakeholder and potential user of the proof of concept procurement method, particularly for innovative technologies or services that support economic development.
The Department of Housing and Community Development is identified as a potential user of this procurement method to test and deploy new goods, services, or technologies relevant to its mission.
The Maryland Department of Labor is identified as a potential user of the competitive proof of concept procurement method for its operational needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is identified as a stakeholder and potential user that may benefit from the operational efficiencies provided by the streamlined proof of concept procurement process.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for adjudicating bid protests and contract disputes, the establishment of a new procurement method with multiple evaluation phases may result in new types of legal challenges or disputes for the Board to resolve.

Synopsis: Renaming the Council on Open Data to be the Council for Open Data; altering the membership and member terms of the Council; and altering the Council's responsibilities to include advising on data initiatives and priorities, and identifying and exploring ways in which partnerships may be developed and strengthened to connect Maryland data with communities and social service organizations.
Title: State Government – Council for Open Data – Membership and Responsibilities
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill renames the Council on Open Data to the Council for Open Data and reduces its membership from 37 to 11 members. It designates the State Chief Data Officer as the council chair, expands the definition of data to include non-final versions, and adds new responsibilities such as advising on data initiatives and developing partnerships to connect state data with community and social service organizations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Information Technology and the State Chief Data Officer
stakeholders: Maryland state agencies, local government entities, and representatives from the private, academic, and nonprofit sectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill's requirements can be managed with existing budgeted resources, with no impact on state revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental request from DoIT. It designates the State Chief Data Officer (a DoIT role) as the Chair of the Council and assigns primary staffing responsibilities to the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames, restructures, and alters the statutory responsibilities of the Council for Open Data, which is a state council composed of appointed officials and public servants.
The bill removes the Director of GOPI as the Vice Chair of the Council and removes the agency's shared staffing responsibilities for the Council.
The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Council, and the Council is required to report its activities and legislative recommendations to the Governor annually.

The bill removes the Secretary of Human Services from the Council's membership but adds a new responsibility for the Council to strengthen partnerships to connect Maryland data with social service organizations.
The bill removes the State Archivist from the Council's membership, though the Council remains responsible for advocating for sound records management and data preservation practices.
The bill removes the Secretary of Agriculture from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of the Environment from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Natural Resources from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Planning from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Transportation from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Housing and Community Development from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Commerce from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of General Services from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the State Superintendent of Schools from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Health from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of State Police from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Budget and Management from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Adjutant General of the Military Department from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Emergency Management from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Secretary of Labor from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill removes the Governor's Homeland Security Advisor from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the Executive Director of the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the Executive Director of MIEMSS from the formal membership of the Council for Open Data.
The bill directs the Council to invite and encourage the judicial branch to use state open data portals and adopt consistent open data policies.

Synopsis: Requiring buses operating on fixed local routes funded by a county or municipal corporation and operated by a county or municipal corporation or a contractor for a county or municipal corporation to allow passengers to embark and disembark at the entrance of early voting centers located within one-half mile of the route.
Title: Election Law - Early Voting Centers - Bus Stops
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: The bill requires local fixed-route bus systems funded or operated by counties or municipalities to allow passengers to get on or off at the entrance of early voting centers if the center is located within a half-mile of the route. This requirement applies during early voting periods and excludes express or commuter routes, as well as routes operated by the Maryland Transit Administration or the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority.
stakeholders: Registered voters in Maryland and local government transit agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local government expenditures are expected to increase starting in fiscal 2028 due to the costs of modifying bus routes, public communication, and temporary signage at early voting centers. While the total impact is indeterminate, Prince George's County estimates its specific costs will increase by at least 37300 in fiscal 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for this departmental bill. The bill mandates that the Board adopt regulations and guidelines for the conduct of early voting, and requires both the State and local boards to inform the public about early voting center locations and transit access.

While the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is explicitly excluded from the bill's requirements, the Department of Transportation provides technical assistance and funding to the locally operated transit systems that are subject to the bill's mandate to adjust routes for early voting centers.

The bill requires that bus route adjustments be consistent with accessibility requirements. As the principal agency for ensuring inclusive services and accessible transportation, the Department of Disabilities is relevant to the implementation of these accessibility mandates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and will likely be involved in reviewing the new regulations and guidelines the Board is required to adopt under the bill.

As a departmental bill requested by the State Board of Elections, the Governor's Office oversees the executive branch's policy initiatives and the administrative implementation of the bill's objectives.

Synopsis: Limiting the personal information that may be collected, maintained, processed, and retained by units of State government under certain circumstances; requiring certain personal information to be deleted or de-identified under certain circumstances; requiring each unit to post a certain privacy notice on its Internet website and establishing certain requirements for privacy notices and privacy policies; requiring each unit of State government to designate a Privacy Officer; etc.
Title: Maryland Data Privacy and Protection Act of 2026
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Biometrics -see also- Artificial Intelli; Identif; Fingerprt
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Data Privacy and Protection Act of 2026 establishes comprehensive data privacy standards for State government units. It limits the collection and retention of personal information to the minimum amount necessary for legitimate government purposes and requires the deletion or de-identification of data once those purposes are fulfilled. The bill mandates that each State unit designate a Privacy Officer, post privacy notices on their websites, and include specific security and privacy requirements in third-party IT contracts. It also expands the legal definition of 'personal information' to include sensitive categories such as biometric, genetic, health, and precise geolocation data.
stakeholders: Maryland State government agencies, third-party IT contractors, and Maryland residents whose personal data is managed by the State.
fiscal_impact_summary: Implementation of the bill will result in administrative costs for State government units to designate Privacy Officers and update data management protocols. The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) will also incur costs to develop regulations, model templates, and security standards for IT contracts. While the bill introduces new operational mandates, specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a unit of the State executive branch, the Governor's Office must comply with new data collection limits, designate a Privacy Officer, and update its public privacy notices.
As part of the executive branch, the Office of the Lieutenant Governor is subject to the Act's requirements for personal information management and the appointment of a Privacy Officer.
The Comptroller's office manages vast amounts of sensitive tax and financial data, making the bill's mandates on data minimization, retention, and deletion highly relevant to its operations.
As the state's chief financial agency, it handles sensitive financial records and must adhere to the new standards for data protection and transparency.
The bill explicitly requires each state unit's Privacy Officer to coordinate with the Office of the Attorney General to ensure compliance with privacy laws and standards.
As a state agency, it must comply with data collection limits and designate a Privacy Officer to oversee the protection of sensitive data regarding older adults.
The agency is required to designate a Privacy Officer and comply with new reporting and data retention standards for the personal information it collects.
The Secretary of Budget and Management is responsible for adopting regulations that exempt specific personal records from the Act's requirements.
The department must align its data collection practices with the bill's requirements and appoint a Privacy Officer to manage business and personal data privacy.
The bill's expanded definition of personal information includes disability status and health data, which are central to this department's records.
As a major state unit, MSDE must comply with data minimization and transparency requirements regarding student and educator data.
MDEM is subject to the Act's requirements for managing personal information collected during disaster response and hazard mitigation.
The agency must appoint a Privacy Officer and ensure that its environmental permitting and enforcement data follows the new retention and deletion protocols.
DGS is the designated repository for the annual reports state units must submit regarding their sets of personal records.
MDH handles extensive sensitive genetic, mental health, and disability data, all of which are subject to the bill's expanded definitions and heightened protection standards.
The agency must designate a Privacy Officer and follow the data minimization requirements for personal records collected through housing and community programs.
DHS collects significant personal information from vulnerable populations and is directly impacted by the mandates on data deletion and privacy notice requirements.
DoIT is the primary agency responsible for setting the standards, regulations, and contract requirements for data privacy and security across all state units.
The agency must appoint a Privacy Officer and manage sensitive data related to youth in the justice system according to the bill's standards.
The agency handles licensing and unemployment insurance data; while professional licensing materials are partially exempt from certain notices, other data handling must comply with the Act.
As a state agency, DNR must designate a Privacy Officer and comply with the Act's limitations on collecting and retaining personal information.
The agency must comply with the Act's data management requirements and designate a Privacy Officer to oversee its information systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: While some records concerning criminal law enforcement are exempt, the agency must still designate a Privacy Officer and follow the Act for non-exempt personal records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a state unit, it must appoint a Privacy Officer and ensure that the personal information of its program participants is managed according to the new standards.
MDOT and its sub-administrations collect substantial personal and geolocation data, which are explicitly addressed in the bill's privacy and transparency mandates.
The department must appoint a Privacy Officer and comply with the Act's requirements for protecting the sensitive data of veterans and their families.
The Military Department must designate a Privacy Officer and ensure that its personnel and readiness records comply with the Act's data protection standards.
The commission manages financial aid and student data, making it subject to the bill's requirements for a Privacy Officer and data minimization protocols.
Although criminal law enforcement information is exempt, the agency must still comply with the Act for other types of personal records it maintains.
As a state unit, it must appoint a Privacy Officer and ensure that its various registries (notaries, charities, etc.) comply with the new privacy notice and data retention rules.
As a state program under the Treasurer, it handles sensitive financial and personal information of participants and must comply with the Act's data protection mandates.
The administration handles sensitive health and personal data for medical cannabis patients and must adhere to the bill's updated privacy and retention standards.
The exchange manages extensive personal and financial data for health plan enrollment, making the bill's privacy and de-identification requirements highly pertinent.
The agency's primary function is to link and analyze student and workforce data, which is directly impacted by the bill's data minimization and transparency requirements.
The bill provides specific exemptions for records deposited with the State Archivist, and the agency is responsible for managing these long-term personal records.
The Board manages a large database of personal information and is required to designate a Privacy Officer and follow the Act's transparency and protection standards.
Managing data for hundreds of thousands of members, the agency must comply with new Privacy Officer mandates and data retention/deletion protocols.
As a state agency, the university must designate a Privacy Officer and ensure its student and employee records are handled according to the bill's standards.
The MVA manages vast amounts of personal and sensitive data for driver licensing and vehicle registration, making it a primary entity impacted by the Act.
The USM and its institutions are subject to the Act's requirements for designating a Privacy Officer and managing personal information responsibly.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person for the Address Confidentiality Program; and providing the contact person acts as the contact for inquiries about the Program from local boards of elections and Program participants on matters related to the implementation of the Address Confidentiality Program.
Title: State Board of Elections - Address Confidentiality Program - Designation of Contact Person
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/21 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person for the Address Confidentiality Program to manage inquiries from local boards of elections and program participants. It also clarifies that local boards must use a participant's actual address for absentee ballots and authorizes the State Board of Elections to adopt related regulations.
stakeholders: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, harassment, or human trafficking participating in the Address Confidentiality Program; local boards of elections; and the Maryland State Board of Elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Board of Elections can designate a contact person and establish regulations using existing resources, with no effect on state revenues. The bill is not expected to materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person for the Address Confidentiality Program, handle inquiries from local boards and program participants, and provides them with the authority to adopt related regulations.

The Secretary of State establishes and administers the Address Confidentiality Program. This bill was introduced as a departmental request by the Secretary of State to improve interagency coordination and ensure participants receive timely responses regarding election-related matters.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Information Technology Investment Fund, at the discretion of the Secretary of Information Technology, to be used to support State-owned communication sites, communication facilities, and telecommunications equipment used in connection with certain technology agreements.
Title: Department of Information Technology – Information Technology Investment Fund – Uses
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Secretary of Information Technology to use money from the Information Technology Investment Fund, specifically revenues derived from resource sharing agreements, to support State-owned communication sites, facilities, and telecommunications equipment used in connection with those agreements.
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies and private companies involved in telecommunications resource sharing agreements.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, expanding the authorized use of resource sharing agreement (RSA) revenues within the Information Technology Investment Fund does not affect overall State revenues or expenditures, though the distribution of funds may change. RSA revenues to the fund totaled $738,247 in fiscal 2024, whereas total fund spending reached 64300000 in fiscal 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for state IT strategy and the manager of the Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF), DoIT is the lead department for this bill. The legislation grants the Secretary of Information Technology discretionary authority to use fund revenues to support the infrastructure underlying Resource Sharing Agreements.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for approving the Resource Sharing Agreements (RSAs) that generate the revenue for the ITIF and oversees significant state expenditures and contracts related to state property and facilities.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for state budget development and execution. As the ITIF is a key state fund used for major IT projects, DBM oversees its fiscal planning and execution.

As a member of the Board of Public Works and the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees the collection of state revenues, including the payments from private companies under Resource Sharing Agreements that accrue to the ITIF.
As a member of the Board of Public Works and the chief custodian of state funds, the Treasurer is responsible for the management and protection of the funds within the ITIF.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Information Technology regarding the procurement, contracts, and information technology agreements (RSAs) affected by this change in fund utilization.

The Maryland State Police is a primary user of the Maryland First radio system, which is one of the two programs currently authorized to receive RSA revenues from the ITIF. Expanding the authorized uses of these funds may impact the distribution of resources available for system support.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS coordinates the state's emergency medical services network and relies on the Maryland First radio system for communications; changes to how the ITIF supports this infrastructure are relevant to their operations.
MDOT manages state rights-of-way and communications infrastructure that are frequently utilized in the Resource Sharing Agreements that generate the revenues for the ITIF.
The department manages state-owned real estate and assets that may be utilized in connection with the Resource Sharing Agreements described in the bill.

DGS is responsible for the maintenance and management of state-owned facilities and real estate. The bill's provision allowing ITIF funds to support state-owned communication sites and facilities may overlap with DGS's operational support and procurement roles.

Synopsis: Altering the manner in which the chair of a campaign finance entity is appointed; providing that the treasurer is the financial steward of a campaign finance entity; altering requirements for assets received by or on behalf of a campaign finance entity and disbursements made by or on behalf of a campaign finance entity; repealing the authority of the chair of a campaign finance entity to approve a disbursement on behalf of the campaign finance entity under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Election Law - Campaign Finance Entities - Oversight and Control of Campaign Funds
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill designates the treasurer as the financial steward of a campaign finance entity and authorizes them to appoint agents to handle disbursements. It prohibits candidates from accessing or making disbursements from campaign accounts, updates procedures for appointing campaign managers, and establishes civil penalties for unauthorized financial activities and failures to report compensation agreements.
stakeholders: Political candidates, campaign treasurers, campaign managers, campaign finance entities, and authorized agents of campaign committees.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund revenues for the Fair Campaign Financing Fund may increase starting in fiscal 2027 due to new civil penalties. Certain violations, such as making disbursements without proper written designation of an authorized agent, are subject to a penalty of $1,000 plus the amount of the disbursement. The total revenue increase cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of campaign finance in Maryland, SBE is responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including the oversight of campaign managers, the registration of authorized agents, and the collection of increased civil penalties. The bill was requested as departmental legislation by SBE.

The OSP is tasked with investigating and prosecuting offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process and election laws. The bill's changes to the fiduciary duties of campaign agents and restrictions on candidate access to funds provide new legal parameters for enforcement and investigation into financial misconduct.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and represents the state in civil and criminal matters. They would be involved in interpreting the new fiduciary duty requirements and defending the imposition of the new civil penalty structure.

OLA conducts fiscal and performance audits of state agencies, including the State Board of Elections. New financial stewardship roles and penalty mechanisms introduced by this bill would be subject to OLA's review during periodic audits of SBE's operations.

OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases. They would likely handle appeals regarding civil penalties imposed by the State Board of Elections for violations of the bill's campaign finance management requirements.

The State Treasurer's Office acts as the custodian of state funds. They are responsible for managing the Fair Campaign Financing Fund, which receives revenues from the civil penalties modified by this bill.
As the state's principal revenue collector, the Comptroller is involved in the overall accounting and receipt of state funds, including penalties collected for violations of campaign finance law.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the State Board of Elections. Additionally, the bill impacts the regulation of gubernatorial campaign finance entities used by the Governor and Lieutenant Governor.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Office of Enterprise Data and the position of State Chief Data Officer within the Maryland Department of Information Technology. The office is tasked with creating a statewide data strategy, establishing data governance and literacy programs, and maintaining a state data inventory. Additionally, the bill mandates that each principal State department appoint an Agency Data Officer to manage departmental data quality, privacy, and sharing in collaboration with the State Chief Data Officer.
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies and departments, State government employees, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates that the Department of Information Technology provide sufficient staff for the newly created Office of Enterprise Data and requires principal departments to appoint Agency Data Officers. These requirements will likely increase State expenditures for personnel and administration; however, specific dollar estimates are unavailable because no formal Fiscal Note was included in the provided text.

The bill is a departmental request from the executive branch and establishes high-level data governance policies that align with the Governor's role in overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives.

As a principal department, DBM is required to appoint an Agency Data Officer. Additionally, as the central personnel and fiscal agency, it will oversee the budgetary and staffing impacts of the new Office of Enterprise Data.

GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies to oversee state government operations. The establishment of statewide data standards and interoperability will directly support and impact their performance metrics and accountability goals.

As the state's central repository for linked education and workforce data, MLDS will be heavily impacted by the data governance, de-identification standards, and interoperability guidelines established by the new State Chief Data Officer.
The OAG will likely provide legal guidance on the development of data privacy, sharing agreements, and de-identification standards required by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Administrative Office of the Courts or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland to administer and implement certain provisions of law relating to financial disclosure statements for State officials of the Judicial Branch and candidates to be a State official of the Judicial Branch and maintain and make available to the public the records and statements of State officials of the Judicial Branch and candidates to be a State official of the Judicial Branch; etc.
Title: Maryland Public Ethics Law - Financial Disclosure Statements - State Officials of and Candidates to be a State Official of the Judicial Branch
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: This bill transfers the responsibility for administering and implementing financial disclosure requirements for Judicial Branch officials and candidates from the State Ethics Commission to the Administrative Office of the Courts or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland. It also clarifies that the Commission on Judicial Disabilities and the Judicial Ethics Committee retain responsibility for conflict of interest provisions while the Administrative Office of the Courts will now maintain and provide public access to judicial financial disclosure statements.
responsible_party: Administrative Office of the Courts or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland
stakeholders: State officials of the Judicial Branch (including judges, justices, and judicial appointees), candidates for judicial office, and the State Ethics Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates there is no state or local fiscal impact, as both the Judiciary and the State Ethics Commission can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. The change is intended to streamline administrative procedures and eliminate the burden of transmitting disclosure statements between agencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC), or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland, to administer and implement the financial disclosure provisions (Subtitle 6) of the Public Ethics Law for Judicial Branch officials and candidates. AOC is further required to maintain these records and ensure they are available for public inspection.

This is a departmental bill requested by the State Ethics Commission. It reduces the Commission's administrative burden by repealing the requirement that judicial financial disclosure statements be transmitted to them, and by transferring the implementation of those disclosures to the Judicial Branch.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly modifies the duties of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities and the Judicial Ethics Committee, which fall under this collective designation. It clarifies that these bodies are responsible for conflict of interest provisions (Subtitle 5) but are no longer responsible for financial disclosure administration (Subtitle 6).

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Trust Fund Board of Trustees, the Maryland Veterans Commission, the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, and the Maryland Youth Advisory Council.
Title: Military Family Inclusion Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Veterans and Military Families, Department of

bill_summary: The Military Family Inclusion Act alters the membership of several state entities, including the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees, the Maryland Veterans Commission, and the Maryland Youth Advisory Council. The bill introduces representation for military families and caregivers of service-disabled veterans, while also streamlining membership criteria and removal procedures for the Maryland Veterans Commission.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Veterans, military families, caregivers of service-disabled veterans, and youth with immediate family members who are service members.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, altering the composition of the specified boards and commissions does not materially affect State government operations or finances. There is no local fiscal impact, and the impact on small businesses is determined to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary proponent of this departmental bill, DVMF is directly impacted. The Secretary of DVMF chairs the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust, the department provides staff for the Maryland Veterans Commission, and the bill grants the department authority to appoint a new youth member to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council.

DHS staffs the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which is being expanded to include a family caregiver of a service-disabled veteran. Additionally, the Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary purpose is to alter the membership, quorum, and organizational removal procedures for four specific state bodies: the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees, the Maryland Veterans Commission, and the Maryland Youth Advisory Council.

The Governor's Office for Children oversees and nominates members for the Maryland Youth Advisory Council. The bill modifies the composition of this Council by adding a youth representative from a military family.

The Maryland Department of Health has three representatives on the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, and the Secretary of Health serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.

The Department of Aging has a representative on the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, and the Secretary of Aging serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.

The Department of Disabilities has a representative on the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, and the Secretary of Disabilities serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.
The Adjutant General (or their designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust, which is being modified by this bill.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the commissions and boards impacted by this bill, including the Maryland Commission on Caregiving and the Maryland Veterans Commission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of candidates for the state boards and commissions whose memberships are being altered by the bill.
The Secretary of Labor (or their designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.

The Student Advisory Council to the Maryland Higher Education Commission nominates members to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council, which is being modified by the addition of a military family youth seat.
The University System of Maryland Student Council nominates members to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council, which is being modified by the addition of a military family youth seat.

Synopsis: Authorizing the approval of certain contract modifications to State contracts if the modification does not materially change the scope of the work and does not increase the contract by more than a certain amount; altering the definition of "contract modification" for certain State procurements; and requiring a procurement officer to document certain contract modifications.
Title: State Procurement - Streamlining Contract Modifications
Status: In the House - First Reading Government, Labor, and Elections
bill_summary: The bill streamlines State procurement by authorizing procurement officers and department heads to approve contract modifications that do not materially alter the scope of work, provided the cost increase remains within specific thresholds related to small procurement limits. It also updates the legal definition of 'contract modification' and requires documentation of such changes in the official procurement file.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of General Services, the Chief Procurement Officer, and heads of primary procurement units
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, procurement officers, and private contractors holding State contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill modifies administrative approval thresholds for State contract modifications. A formal Fiscal Note with specific revenue or expenditure estimates is not included in the provided text. The financial impact is limited to the procedural streamlining of modifications within thresholds linked to small procurement limits, though specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a primary procurement unit and the agency that requested the bill, DGS is the principal implementer. The Secretary of DGS typically serves as the Chief Procurement Officer, who is granted specific authority under this bill to approve contract modifications up to five times the small procurement threshold.

The Board of Public Works oversees all significant state procurements and expenditures. This bill streamlines the approval process for contract modifications, impacting the volume and type of contract changes that require higher-level executive oversight or adherence to Board-established regulations.

MDOT is a primary procurement unit with significant independent contracting authority. The bill's provisions regarding the head of a primary procurement unit's ability to approve larger contract modifications directly impact MDOT's operational efficiency and internal procurement procedures.

DBM is a primary procurement unit responsible for state personnel and service contracts. The bill grants DBM's head authority to approve contract modifications without higher-level intervention if they meet specific fiscal and scope criteria.

DoIT is a primary procurement unit for the state's IT goods and services. The bill's streamlining of contract modifications directly applies to DoIT's procurement officers and leadership in managing technology contracts.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies on procurement law and contract interpretation. They would be responsible for advising agencies on the redefined 'contract modification' and ensuring that approvals comply with the new statutory limits.

The bill mandates that procurement officers document contract modifications in the procurement file. OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of these files to ensure state agencies are adhering to procurement laws and proper documentation standards.

The State Treasurer's Office is designated as a primary procurement unit under the State Finance and Procurement Article and is a member of the Board of Public Works, giving it both direct operational and oversight interest in procurement streamlining.

USM is a primary procurement unit with delegated authority. The changes to contract modification procedures and approval thresholds apply to the system's various institutions and procurement officers.
As a primary procurement unit, Morgan State University's procurement officers and leadership gain the modified approval authorities granted by the bill for their institutional contracts.
As a designated primary procurement unit, the college is directly impacted by changes to the approval process and documentation requirements for state contract modifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MSBCA adjudicates contract disputes. Changes to the definition of 'contract modification' and the authorized approval process may affect the resolution of legal disputes regarding contract performance and changes.

The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works and oversees state payments. While not a primary procurement unit, the agency monitors contract expenditures and the fiscal integrity of the state's procurement system.

Synopsis: Altering the type of toilet that certain food establishments may use to comply with the requirement to provide a convenient lavatory; requiring that the fee for an on-farm food service facility license be determined by the Maryland Department of Health based on certain factors and prohibiting the fee from exceeding $100; establishing the term of an on-farm service facility license; and requiring the Department, in consultation with certain other departments, to adopt regulations governing on-farm service facility licenses.
Title: Food Establishments - Lavatory Requirement and On-Farm Food Service Facility License
Status: In the House - Second Reading Passed with Amendments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates health and licensing requirements for on-farm food establishments. It replaces the previous short-term on-farm food service license with an annual license costing no more than $100. Additionally, it permits agritourism businesses, farm breweries, and limited wineries to use any portable toilet to meet lavatory requirements and directs the Maryland Department of Health to establish new regulations for water access, wastewater, and food preparation on farms.
stakeholders: Farm owners, agritourism operators, Class 4 limited wineries, Class 8 farm breweries, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase by an estimated $5,000 annually starting in fiscal 2027, based on approximately 50 licenses at the maximum $100 fee. While local health departments will handle inspections, the $100 fee cap may not fully cover administrative and enforcement costs, requiring the use of existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for implementing this bill. It is tasked with determining the license fee for on-farm food service facilities, issuing the licenses, and adopting the necessary regulations governing access to water, wastewater management, and food preparation.

The bill explicitly requires MDH to consult with the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) when adopting regulations for on-farm food service facility licenses. The bill also directly impacts the economic viability of farms, which falls under MDA's mission to support the agricultural community.

The bill explicitly requires MDH to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) regarding the management of wastewater and regulations for on-farm food service facilities. The bill also maintains requirements regarding toilet placement relative to wells to protect water quality.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is tasked with supporting the sustainability and profitability of Maryland's agricultural industry. The bill's creation of an on-farm food service facility license directly impacts the revenue-generating capabilities and operational flexibility of rural farm businesses.

The bill alters requirements for food establishments that hold Class 4 limited winery and Class 8 farm brewery licenses, which are regulated by the Comptroller's office in its role overseeing the alcohol industry and state revenues.

The bill affects agritourism, which is a key part of Maryland's tourism and economic development strategy. The Department of Commerce is responsible for promoting Maryland's assets and enhancing the state's competitive position, including rural tourism.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and will likely review the required regulations for legal sufficiency and consistency with state laws.

The bill references agritourism as defined in the Land Use Article and explicitly mentions local building and zoning codes. The Department of Planning provides policy guidance on land use and sustainable growth related to these designations.

Synopsis: Altering the effective dates of enrollment in a Small Business Health Options (SHOP) Exchange plan for individuals who enroll during certain special enrollment periods.
Title: Health Insurance – Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Enrollment – Effective Dates
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: This bill aligns Maryland law with federal regulations by updating the effective dates for health insurance coverage enrollment through the Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) during special enrollment periods. It ensures that for individuals enrolling during these periods, coverage typically begins on the first day of the month following their plan selection, removing previous delays for selections made late in a month.
stakeholders: Small employers with 1 to 50 employees and their eligible employees and dependents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, the bill codifies existing practices that already align with federal regulations. The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange currently operates the SHOP platform in accordance with these standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the requesting agency and the primary regulator of the state's insurance market, the Maryland Insurance Administration is directly responsible for enforcing the provisions of the bill and ensuring that health insurance laws regarding SHOP enrollment effective dates align with federal regulations.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange administers the Maryland Health Connection, which includes the Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) platform directly affected by this legislation's changes to enrollment effective dates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, assisting in the interpretation and implementation of these statutory changes to ensure compliance with federal law.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, and coordinates the policy initiatives and departmental legislation that includes this bill.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists, in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law), by extending to July 1, 2032, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists - Sunset Extension
Status: In the House - Second Reading Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists by five years, moving the sunset date from July 1, 2027, to July 1, 2032, to allow for the continued regulation and licensing of environmental health specialists in Maryland.
responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
stakeholders: Licensed environmental health specialists, applicants for licensure, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists are maintained through fiscal 2032. There is no fiscal impact on local governments, and the Maryland Department of Health identifies minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is an entity within the Maryland Department of Health. As the primary agency, MDH requested this departmental bill to ensure the continued regulation of environmental health specialists and the maintenance of the board's special fund revenues and expenditures.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel management. This bill extends the life of a state board, thereby maintaining its associated special fund budget and state-level personnel requirements through fiscal year 2032.

The OAG provides legal counsel and representation to all state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists. The extension of the board's statutory authority maintains the OAG's ongoing obligation to provide legal support.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state boards. The extension of the board ensures that OAH will continue to handle any disciplinary or licensing appeals stemming from the board's regulatory actions.

The Office of Appointments is responsible for recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards. This bill ensures the continued existence of the board's nine appointed member positions, which the office must manage when vacancies occur.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and MDH. The Governor is responsible for signing the sunset extension into law and overseeing the appointments to the board.

Synopsis: Requiring a carrier that issues Medicare supplement policies to issue a Medicare supplement policy to an individual who meets certain criteria during certain special enrollment periods.
Title: Medicare Supplement Policies - Issuance - Requirements
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: This bill requires insurance carriers that offer Medicare supplement policies in Maryland to issue those policies to eligible individuals during two new 63-day special enrollment periods. The first period applies to individuals who lose coverage under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) after having been enrolled in Medicare Part B for at least six months. The second applies to individuals who became eligible for Medicare before 2020 and qualify for a federal guaranteed issue right. During these periods, carriers are prohibited from denying coverage or discriminating in pricing based on an applicant's health status or medical history.
stakeholders: Medicare-eligible individuals, particularly those losing Medicaid coverage or those eligible for Medicare prior to 2020, and insurance carriers that issue Medicare supplement policies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's impact on the state is minimal, as any additional workload for the Maryland Insurance Administration can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances. The bill is also determined to have minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary agency responsible for regulating insurance carriers and enforcing the provisions of the Insurance Article. This is a departmental bill requested by the MIA, and the Insurance Commissioner is specifically tasked with adopting regulations to implement the bill.

The bill creates a special enrollment period for individuals transitioning out of the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health. The department will be responsible for providing the necessary documentation of termination or disenrollment required by applicants.

The Department of Aging supports older adults who are the primary users of Medicare and Medicare supplement policies. The bill directly affects the ability of this demographic to access supplemental insurance during specific life transitions.

The bill and existing law sections being amended address Medicare eligibility due to disability for individuals under age 65. The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for these residents and is impacted by changes to their health insurance access.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration regarding the interpretation, implementation, and enforcement of new insurance laws.

Synopsis: Altering the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program, including by establishing requirements regarding an automated external defibrillator (AED) coordinator, repealing certain provisions of law regarding regional council AED committees, and exempting certain law enforcement agencies from being required to obtain a certificate for an AED deployed in a patrol vehicle of the law enforcement agency; etc.
Title: State Emergency Medical Services Board - Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program - Revisions
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.
