bill_summary: This bill updates and streamlines the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator (AED) Program by codifying the role of an AED coordinator, clarifying registration requirements for participating entities, and exempting law enforcement patrol vehicles from requiring a specific AED certificate. It also repeals obsolete provisions related to regional committees and ensures that grocery stores and restaurants meet established program standards for AED maintenance and operation.
responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS) and the State Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Board
stakeholders: Organizations, businesses, law enforcement agencies, and owners or operators of grocery stores and restaurants that maintain automated external defibrillators (AEDs).
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact as the changes are technical in nature and do not affect governmental finances. Small businesses are also expected to experience minimal or no economic impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency that administers the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program and the primary requester of this departmental bill, MIEMSS (and the EMS Board it supports) is the lead entity responsible for implementing the alterations to AED coordinator requirements, entity certifications, and program oversight.

The bill explicitly exempts law enforcement agencies from the requirement to obtain a certificate for AEDs deployed in patrol vehicles, directly affecting the regulatory requirements for the State's primary law enforcement agency.

The bill updates requirements for grocery stores and restaurants (entities regulated by MDH) to comply with the Public Access AED Program and references health care facilities regulated by the department.

The bill amends Section 13-517 of the Education Article, which governs the Public Access AED Program. As the oversight body for public schools (which are common 'entities' possessing AEDs), MSDE is relevant to the implementation of these safety standards.

The fiscal note highlights that county library systems are required to place AEDs and comply with the program, making the clarified requirements for AED coordinators and maintenance procedures relevant to library administration.

DGS manages state-owned public buildings, which are specifically mentioned regarding the co-location of naloxone with AEDs. The bill's changes to the Public Access AED Program affect the management and compliance of equipment in these facilities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the EMS Board and MIEMSS, and would be responsible for advising the board on the drafting and enforcement of the new regulations and requirements for AED coordinators.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Insurance Commissioner's enforcement authority over third-party administrators (TPAs). It authorizes the Commissioner to deny, revoke, or suspend a TPA's registration and impose civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation for breaches of any Maryland insurance law or regulation, rather than limiting enforcement to the specific subtitle governing TPAs.
stakeholders: Third-party administrators (TPAs), insurance companies, plan sponsors, and plan beneficiaries.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State revenues or expenditures. The Maryland Insurance Administration can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. The bill was introduced as a departmental request from the MIA and directly expands the enforcement and regulatory authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who heads the agency.

Enforcement actions taken by the Insurance Commissioner, such as the denial, suspension, or revocation of a registration, are subject to the hearing provisions of the Insurance Article. The Office of Administrative Hearings is the central panel responsible for adjudicating such contested cases and regulatory disputes.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative and counsel for all state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration. It would provide legal support for the expanded enforcement actions authorized by the bill and represent the state in any subsequent appeals in court.

The Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (IWIF) specifically serves as the third-party administrator (TPA) for workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees. Because the bill alters the registration standards and enforcement penalties for all TPAs, IWIF is directly impacted as a regulated entity under this framework.

stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, family caregivers, Area Agencies on Aging, and state and local government agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact because it generally codifies existing policies, procedures, and initiatives already established by Executive Order 01.01.2024.01.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Aging is the primary agency responsible for implementing the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan and staffing the restructured Commission on Aging as established by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly alters the membership, duties, and operational requirements of the Commission on Aging, which functions as one of the permanent advisory bodies within the Maryland executive branch.

The bill codifies a multisector plan that originated from a Governor's Executive Order and requires the Secretary of Aging to coordinate with and advise various executive branch units under the Governor's supervision.

The bill expands and diversifies the membership of the Commission on Aging, requiring the Governor to appoint multiple new members from specific professional backgrounds and demographic categories, a process managed by this office.
Optimizing health and wellness is a primary goal of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, and the Secretary of Aging is tasked with advising health-related boards and units on the plan's implementation.
The bill amends the Human Services Article and targets older adults, many of whom are served by DHS programs for economic assistance and protection from abuse or neglect.

The Longevity Ready Maryland Plan includes goals related to promoting economic opportunity and a multigenerational workforce, aligning with the Department of Labor's mission regarding workforce development and adult learning.
Optimizing mobility is a core goal of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, requiring coordination with MDOT regarding infrastructure and transit services for an aging population.
The plan specifically focuses on helping older adults live independently in their own homes and communities, which relates to DHCD's programs for affordable housing and community revitalization.
The bill mandates that one member of the Commission on Aging be a veteran and addresses the needs of Maryland's older veteran population.
The bill emphasizes that commission membership and the plan itself must address the needs of older adults with disabilities and promote inclusive, integrated community living.

The OAG serves as the legal representative for the Department of Aging and the Commission on Aging and may be required to provide counsel on the new regulatory and advisory duties established by the bill.

The bill requires the use of data-driven strategies and performance monitoring for the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, which aligns with GOPI's mission to enhance the efficiency and accountability of multisector state initiatives.
The bill requires the Commission on Aging to reflect the state's diversity, including immigrant heritage and ethnic/faith-based communities, which are primary focus areas for GOCI.
As the plan aims to promote economic opportunity for seniors, the GWDB is a relevant stakeholder in developing workforce solutions for Maryland's aging residents.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to establish medication review committees to determine whether to involuntarily administer psychotropic medication to incarcerated individuals in state mental health infirmaries. The bill outlines specific clinical criteria for nonemergency administration, establishes the composition and procedures of the committees, and provides incarcerated individuals with rights to a lay advisor, administrative hearings through the Office of Administrative Hearings, and judicial appeals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in State correctional facilities with mental health disorders, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services staff, and the Office of Administrative Hearings.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) can implement the bill using existing resources. However, general fund expenditures for the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) may increase starting in FY 2027 by an indeterminate amount depending on the volume of hearings requested; for illustrative purposes, hiring one additional Administrative Law Judge to handle the caseload would cost approximately 175000. The bill is not expected to significantly impact the Judiciary or local finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary sponsor and implementing agency, DPSCS is responsible for establishing the medication review committees, appointing members, and overseeing the involuntary administration of psychotropic medications within its licensed mental health infirmaries.

The bill explicitly tasks OAH with conducting de novo administrative hearings for incarcerated individuals appealing the decisions of the medication review committees. The fiscal note also highlights a potential increase in workload and expenditures for this agency.

MDH is responsible for licensing the mental health infirmaries within State correctional facilities where these procedures occur. Additionally, the committee process involves mental health professionals and clinical assessments under standards related to public health.

The OAG serves as legal counsel for state agencies, including DPSCS and MDH, and would likely represent the state in administrative hearings and subsequent circuit court appeals resulting from the committee decisions.

The bill provides for judicial review of administrative decisions in the Circuit Court. The AOC provides operational and legal support for the Maryland Judicial Branch, which will process these appeals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent individuals in proceedings involving involuntary commitment and the safeguarding of constitutional rights, which are directly implicated by the involuntary administration of medication.
The fiscal note indicates potential increases in general fund expenditures for OAH to hire additional Administrative Law Judges to handle the new hearing requirements established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises on public safety and criminal justice strategies, including policies aimed at reducing recidivism and managing the treatment of justice-involved individuals with serious mental illnesses.

The bill concerns individuals with mental disorders, which falls under the purview of this department's mission to coordinate and improve services for Maryland residents with disabilities in various settings.

The involuntary administration of medication involves significant civil rights considerations. MCCR enforces anti-discrimination laws and ensures that state services are provided in compliance with protected class rights.

The OCSA regulates the prescribing and dispensing of controlled medications (including psychotropic drugs) and enforces the state's Controlled Dangerous Substance Act, ensuring these substances are used for legitimate medical purposes.

bill_summary: This bill codifies aspects of the federal 2024 Mental Health Parity Rule into Maryland law to strengthen enforcement of requirements for the treatment of mental health and substance use disorders. It requires health insurance carriers to identify and perform comparative analyses on nonquantitative treatment limitations, collect and evaluate outcomes data related to access, and provide meaningful benefits for mental health and substance use disorders including core treatments that are on par with medical and surgical services.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, the Maryland Insurance Administration, and Maryland residents receiving mental health or substance use disorder treatments through regulated health benefit plans.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill and promulgate required regulations using existing budgeted resources. The bill has no estimated fiscal impact on state or local revenues, the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, or local government expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of the state's insurance market, the Maryland Insurance Administration is the lead agency responsible for enforcing the Mental Health Parity Act, reviewing carrier reports, and adopting new regulations as mandated by the bill.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees behavioral health and substance use services and shares regulatory authority over health maintenance organizations, which are subject to the bill's parity requirements.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is tasked with improving access to health care and increasing accountability, directly aligning with the bill's goal of ensuring parity in access to mental health and substance use benefits.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange administers the state's health insurance marketplace, where participating carriers must comply with the codified mental health and substance use disorder parity requirements.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and tracks changes in insurance law that may affect state-administered health plans.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and would represent the state in enforcement actions or legal challenges related to the new parity regulations.
The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases and appeals of administrative orders issued by the Insurance Commissioner regarding noncompliance with state insurance laws.
The Governor's Office oversees executive agencies and policy coordination, and this departmental bill represents an executive initiative from the Maryland Insurance Administration.

bill_summary: This emergency bill modifies regulations for criminal background investigations for individuals who care for, supervise, or have access to children in various facilities. It aligns Maryland law with federal FBI requirements for the dissemination of national criminal history record information, ensuring that national background checks continue to be available to state licensing agencies. It also expands the requirement for background checks to include non-relative caregivers in emergency out-of-home placement situations, such as neighbors or friends.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, Maryland State Department of Education, and Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Employees, employers, and volunteers at child care centers and schools; nonpublic school staff; individuals seeking to adopt or become guardians; and emergency out-of-home caregivers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by at least 900,000 in FY 2027 for the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to develop a database required to process and review national criminal history records. MSDE also anticipates an annual cost of approximately 630,000 for six new positions to facilitate these reviews. The bill is intended to ensure compliance with federal law to maintain access to national background check data. Local governments may experience increased workloads for law enforcement agencies performing name-based checks, and the Department of Human Services may face additional foster care costs if potential emergency caregivers are disqualified by the background checks.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates criminal history records checks for individuals whom the juvenile court appoints as a guardian of a child, which directly impacts the operational procedures and oversight within the judicial branch.

The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in general fund expenditures (at least $900,000 in FY 2027) for database development and additional personnel, which falls under the budget development and personnel management duties of this department.

As the primary agency for licensing child care centers and family child care homes, and overseeing public and nonpublic schools, MSDE is a primary implementer. The fiscal note highlights a major fiscal and administrative impact for reviewing national background checks and developing a new database.

The bill explicitly includes home health agencies and residential service agencies licensed by the Maryland Department of Health that provide services for minors in the list of facilities requiring criminal background checks.

DHS is responsible for foster care family homes, emergency out-of-home placements, and certain child care licensing. The bill's changes to emergency placement background checks and substitute caregiver requirements directly affect its core social service and child protection operations.

The fiscal note mentions the need for a new $900,000 database to handle the processing and review of criminal history record information results, which falls under the strategic IT and infrastructure oversight of this department.

The bill requires employees of juvenile detention, correction, or treatment facilities to obtain criminal history records checks, directly impacting the personnel and regulatory compliance of this agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill by DPSCS. The agency operates the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which is the primary entity responsible for conducting the State and national criminal history records checks and managing the fingerprinting process described in the bill.
As this is a departmental bill, the Governor's Office oversaw its proposal and is responsible for coordinating the executive branch's enforcement of the safety and licensing laws altered by the bill.

The agency is dedicated to promoting the well-being of Maryland's children. This bill's focus on enhancing background checks for child care providers and emergency caretakers aligns with the office's mission to protect children.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency advises the Governor on public safety and manages funds for law enforcement and youth programs. The bill's emphasis on criminal background checks for child safety is central to their coordination of public safety strategies.

As an independent unit within MSDE that fosters safe learning environments and provides technical assistance to schools, the center is relevant due to the bill's expanded requirements for criminal background checks for school employees and volunteers.

The bill involves 'designated State or local law enforcement agencies' in the performance of national name-based checks for emergency out-of-home placements, a role typically fulfilled by the State Police.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MSDE, DHS, and DPSCS regarding compliance with state and federal laws, specifically the federal CJIS requirements cited by the agencies as the reason for the bill.

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's Adult Protective Services (APS) by expanding the definitions of abuse to include psychological harm and sexual abuse and specifying that abuse, neglect, and exploitation must be committed by an individual in a 'relationship of trust' with a vulnerable adult. The bill introduces an online reporting portal for suspected cases, mandates that local social services investigations assess whether a vulnerable adult is at risk of harm, and requires investigative findings to be categorized as 'indicated,' 'not indicated,' or 'undetermined.' These changes align Maryland's APS program with new federal minimum standards.
stakeholders: Vulnerable adults, health practitioners, police officers, human service workers, and local departments of social services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The bill aligns State definitions with federal APS rules, which may help protect federal funding by ensuring compliance by May 2028. No specific dollar estimates for expenditures or revenue changes were provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for Adult Protective Services (APS), DHS and its local departments of social services are responsible for receiving reports, conducting investigations, and making findings of abuse or neglect as modified by the bill.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Maryland Department of Aging and local offices on aging to assist in investigations of vulnerable adult abuse or neglect at the request of the local department.

Police officers are designated as mandated reporters under the bill, and law enforcement agencies are required to assist in the investigations of alleged abuse, neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults.
The Judiciary is involved in matters of adult guardianship and was a contributor to the fiscal note; the bill references the adult public guardianship review board and court-related definitions.

Health practitioners, who are regulated by the Department of Health, are mandated reporters under this bill; the department also oversees local health departments and programs for adults with disabilities.
The bill mandates the addition of an online reporting portal as a method for reporting suspected abuse, which falls under the purview of state IT infrastructure and strategy.
The bill's focus on vulnerable and disabled adults directly overlaps with the department's mission to coordinate and improve services for Marylanders with disabilities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Human Services and other state agencies involved in the enforcement of protective services and criminal investigations related to vulnerable adults.
The bill aligns state law with federal rules to ensure the state remains in compliance with federal requirements, thereby protecting federal funding managed by DBM.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a method for calculating actual cash value recovery in first-party property insurance claims, specifically prohibiting insurers from depreciating labor costs during claim settlement. It also requires insurers to provide homeowners and renters with a written notice at least 45 days before a policy renewal that identifies any differences in coverage limits, risks, or deductibles between the expiring and renewal policies.
stakeholders: Homeowners, renters, commercial property insurance policyholders, and insurance companies operating in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will increase minimally in FY 2027 due to rate and form filing fees. General fund revenues from the state's 2% premium tax may be affected if insurers adjust premiums to account for the bill's provisions, though any such impact is expected to be minimal. Enforcement of the bill's requirements can be managed with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary agency responsible for regulating insurance in the state and requested this departmental bill. The agency will be responsible for overseeing the new claim settlement standards, processing rate and form filings, and investigating the newly defined unfair claim settlement practices.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration. Enforcement actions against insurers for 'unfair claim settlement practices' defined in this bill would likely be heard by an Administrative Law Judge at this agency.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and would represent the state in civil litigation or appeals related to the interpretation and enforcement of the new insurance standards.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. The fiscal note indicates that general fund revenues from insurance premium taxes may be minimally affected if the bill leads insurers to adjust their premiums.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The bill's potential impact on premium tax revenue and the fiscal oversight of the Maryland Insurance Administration falls within its scope.

The bill establishes legal standards for calculating 'actual cash value' in property insurance settlements. While primary enforcement is administrative, these standards may also be applied or litigated in civil cases within the state court system.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Maryland Insurance Administration, and appoints the Insurance Commissioner. The bill is part of the administration's departmental legislative package.

The Office of Legislative Audits conducts periodic fiscal and performance audits of the Maryland Insurance Administration. OLA would evaluate the agency's compliance with and management of the new regulatory requirements during their audit process.

bill_summary: This bill requires licensed firearms dealers to notify the Secretary of State Police within 24 hours of discovering that their required security features—such as video surveillance, physical barriers, or monitored alarm systems—may have been compromised by a burglary, robbery, theft, or other event. fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the Maryland Department of State Police can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police is the primary agency responsible for the oversight and licensing of firearms dealers. The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including the Maryland State Police. Violations of the notification requirements in this bill can lead to civil penalties or the suspension and revocation of a dealer's license, which would be subject to administrative hearings.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Police. They would be responsible for providing legal advice on the implementation of these notification requirements and representing the state in any resulting litigation or appeals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The Maryland State Police enforce the motor vehicle laws affected by this bill. Changes to license modification requirements and the mandatory use of ignition interlock devices directly impact their traffic safety enforcement and roadside verification of restricted licenses.

The bill references court-ordered participation in the Ignition Interlock System Program under the Judiciary's authority, and changes to license suspension and modification protocols intersect with judicial sentencing and traffic case outcomes.

Title: Criminal Procedure - Lifetime Sexual Offender Supervision - Conditions, Violations, and Petitions for Discharge
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill modifies the regulations for lifetime sexual offender supervision by specifying mandatory conditions, requiring that violations be reported to State's Attorneys, and updating the process for discharge petitions. It mandates that discharge petitions include a risk assessment and polygraph, increases the waiting period for re-petitioning from one year to two years, and ensures victims are notified of such petitions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Sexual offenders subject to lifetime supervision, victims and their representatives, State's Attorneys, the Division of Parole and Probation, and the Maryland Judiciary.
fiscal_impact_summary: The formal Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances. It primarily clarifies and standardizes operational procedures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the court system regarding the management and discharge of individuals under lifetime sexual offender supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. Its units, the Division of Parole and Probation (DPP) and the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC), are tasked with overseeing lifetime sexual offender supervision, enforcing conditions, and reporting violations. The bill also requires the department to approve sexual offender treatment providers and polygraph examiners.

The bill directly modifies the responsibilities of sentencing and juvenile courts regarding the imposition of special conditions for sexual offender supervision and the adjudication of petitions for discharge. It establishes new requirements for court hearings and notifications to the State's Attorney.

The bill explicitly applies to individuals required to register as sexual offenders through the juvenile court system. It mandates that juvenile courts impose special conditions and adjudicate supervision terms, which impacts the youth and programs managed by DJS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Sexual Offender Advisory Board, which falls under this category, is responsible for reviewing Maryland's laws and practices concerning sexual offenders, developing risk assessment criteria, and making recommendations for offender management—all of which are directly impacted by the policy changes in this bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the primary implementing agencies (DPSCS and DJS) and represents the state in matters related to criminal procedure. This bill's changes to sentencing and discharge processes for sexual offenders may require legal guidance and representation in future court proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's coordinating body for public safety strategy and manages victim services funding. The bill's focus on enhancing public safety through offender supervision and mandatory victim notification for discharge petitions aligns with GOCPP's mission.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Superintendent of Schools to declare a prolonged state of emergency for an event that prevents regular, in-person attendance at a public school for at least 14 consecutive school days.
Title: State Superintendent of Schools - Prolonged State of Emergency - Authority to Declare
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland State Superintendent of Schools to declare a 'prolonged state of emergency' if an event prevents in-person attendance at a public school for at least 14 consecutive days. This declaration allows local school systems to transition to virtual education under their existing approved plans.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, teachers, staff, and local county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates no state or local fiscal impact. The State Superintendent of Schools and local school systems can implement the bill's provisions using existing resources and virtual education plans without requiring additional funding or staffing changes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, MSDE is directly impacted as the bill grants the State Superintendent of Schools the specific authority to declare a prolonged state of emergency for public schools and requires the State Board of Education to review and approve county-level virtual education plans.

The bill shifts the legal authority to declare a 'prolonged state of emergency' for school-related closures from the Governor to the State Superintendent, directly impacting the Governor's executive powers regarding emergency proclamations.

The bill explicitly states that the new authority granted to the State Superintendent does not limit or interfere with the Secretary of Health's statutory responsibilities during public health emergencies.

MDEM is the state's principal agency for coordinating emergency preparedness and response. Changes to how emergencies are declared and managed within the public school system affect statewide emergency coordination protocols.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Governor, the Department of Education, and the Secretary of Health regarding the implementation and boundaries of these revised emergency declaration powers.

GOHS advises the Governor on public safety and disaster prevention strategies. A shift in emergency declaration authority for schools is relevant to their mandate of assessing state readiness for various hazards.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education, the MCSS provides training and technical assistance for school safety, which likely includes the development and implementation of virtual education plans during emergencies.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Central Collection Unit and the Child Support Administration to certify certain information about restitution or child support obligors to a video lottery operator for purposes of enforcing a requirement to intercept certain prize payouts; requiring a video lottery operator to provide certain notice to a debtor that wins a prize to be paid by the licensee and withhold all or part of the prize; etc.
Title: Video Lottery Facility Payouts - Intercepts for Restitution Payments, Child Support Payments, and Debts Owed to the State
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery
Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: This bill expands the state's authority to intercept winnings from video lottery facilities (casinos) to cover debts and claims owed to the state, in addition to existing interceptions for child support and restitution payments. It requires video lottery operators to notify debtors of intercepted prizes, provides a process for appeals, and establishes the order of priority for various types of debt interceptions.
responsible_party: Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency and the Central Collection Unit
stakeholders: Individuals with overdue state debt, child support, or restitution who win prizes at Maryland casinos; video lottery facility operators; and state agencies seeking debt collection.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state revenues across all funds are estimated to increase by at least 3000000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Additionally, special fund revenues for the Central Collection Fund are expected to increase by at least 510000 annually due to administrative fees. Local community colleges may also see a revenue increase for debts referred to the Central Collection Unit.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced at the request of the Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency (SLGCA). The agency is responsible for overseeing the interception of prizes at video lottery facilities (casinos) and coordinating with video lottery operators to implement the bill's requirements.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is part of the Department of Budget and Management, is a primary entity authorized by the bill to certify debts to video lottery operators for intercept. Furthermore, the Secretary of Budget and Management is authorized to jointly adopt regulations to carry out the bill.

The Child Support Administration (CSA) within the Department of Human Services is authorized to certify child support arrears to video lottery operators for prize interception, which directly impacts their mission to collect support payments.

The Department of Juvenile Services refers overdue restitution accounts to the Central Collection Unit, which then uses the tools provided by this bill to intercept gaming prizes for those restitution payments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of Parole and Probation within this department refers overdue restitution for collection to the Central Collection Unit; the bill enhances the tools available for these collections through casino prize intercepts.

The bill establishes an appeal process for debtors whose prizes are intercepted. The Office of Administrative Hearings provides the impartial hearing process for contested cases involving state agencies, and the fiscal note explicitly mentions their role in handling potential increases in cases related to these intercepts.

The bill involves the collection of court-ordered restitution. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and legal support to the judiciary and is listed as a primary source of information in the fiscal note regarding the bill's impact on court operations.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to SLGCA, DBM, and other agencies during the development of regulations and the implementation of the new intercept procedures.

As the state's chief financial agency responsible for the management and protection of state funds, the Treasurer's Office is relevant because the bill is projected to significantly increase state revenues (all funds) from intercepted prizes.

The fiscal note identifies student tuition and fees as typical debts referred to the Central Collection Unit. As a state agency that uses CCU for collection, the University System will likely see a increase in recovered funds from casino prize intercepts.

Similar to the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University refers delinquent student accounts to the Central Collection Unit and would benefit from increased revenue collection under the bill.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland, as a state agency, refers delinquent debts to the Central Collection Unit and would likely see a positive fiscal impact from enhanced collection capabilities.

Synopsis: Establishing the Buy Maryland Cybersecurity Tax Credit; stating the purpose of the credit is to promote the cybersecurity industry in the State by helping Maryland businesses and nonprofits purchase cybersecurity technology services from Maryland companies; altering eligibility for the credit; increasing from $200,000 to $1,000,000 the aggregate amount of credits that may be issued for certain cybersecurity purchases; making the credit refundable; etc.
Title: Income Tax – Cybersecurity Technology and Service Tax Credit – Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill renames the Cybersecurity Technology and Service Tax Credit to the Buy Maryland Cybersecurity Tax Credit and establishes its purpose as promoting the cybersecurity industry in Maryland. Key changes include expanding eligibility by increasing the revenue cap for qualified sellers to $10,000,000 and removing the employee limit for qualified buyers, making the tax credit fully refundable, and increasing the aggregate credit limit for purchases from a single seller to $1,000,000 per year.
stakeholders: Maryland businesses and nonprofits (buyers), Maryland-based cybersecurity companies (sellers), and small businesses in the cybersecurity technology sector.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State and local revenues are estimated to decrease by $3,500,000 annually from fiscal 2027 through 2031. This includes an annual general fund revenue decrease of $2,800,000, a $200,000 decrease for the Higher Education Investment Fund, and a $600,000 decrease for the Transportation Trust Fund. Local highway user revenues are expected to decrease by approximately $100,000 per year. These estimates assume the program's existing $4,000,000 annual award cap will be fully utilized as a result of the bill's expanded eligibility and refundability provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency implementing the Buy Maryland Cybersecurity Tax Credit, Commerce is responsible for defining 'qualified buyers' and 'qualified sellers,' approving credit certificate applications, reporting on outcomes, and managing the overall program budget and utilization.

The Comptroller is responsible for processing the tax credits and refunds on income tax returns, and has the authority to make assessments against qualified buyers to recapture tax credits if certification is revoked.

The fiscal note indicates a significant revenue decrease for the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and a reduction in expenditures for local highway user revenue grants, both of which fall under the fiscal management of MDOT.

This is a departmental bill proposed by the Department of Commerce, an executive branch agency, and aligns with the Governor's role in overseeing policy initiatives related to economic development and the cybersecurity industry.
The fiscal note identifies the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) as a special fund that could potentially lose revenue if certain corporations claim the cybersecurity tax credit.
The bill repeals the authority for the Department of Commerce to establish an expert panel in consultation with TEDCO to assist in determining whether a company is a qualified seller.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Commerce and the Comptroller in developing the regulations required by the bill and ensuring the enforcement of tax credit revocation and recapture provisions.

The bill's changes are expected to decrease revenues for the Higher Education Investment Fund (HEIF), which supports state policies and funding for postsecondary institutions overseen by the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the definition of 'qualified seller' to include businesses owned by individuals from groups historically deprived of access to resources, including minority, women, and veteran-owned businesses, which aligns with this office's mission to monitor socioeconomic procurement and business programs.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to establish a certain limit, by regulation, on the amount of money given away as free promotional play by a sports wagering licensee that may be excluded from sports wagering proceeds.
Title: Sports Wagering Proceeds - Promotional Play Exclusion - Limitation
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: The bill authorizes the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to establish a limit on the amount of free promotional play that sports wagering licensees may exclude from their taxable proceeds after their first full fiscal year of operations.
responsible_party: Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Sports wagering facility licensees, mobile sports wagering licensees, and the Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact because it codifies existing procedures. While the document mentions that related regulatory changes could potentially increase General Fund revenues by $2,000,000 and Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund revenues by $6,000,000 annually by lowering promotional play caps, the bill itself is determined to have no direct fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill was requested by the agency and directly grants the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission the authority to establish limits, via regulation, on promotional play exclusions from sports wagering proceeds. The agency is the primary regulator and implementing body for the bill's provisions.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. Since sports wagering is subject to state taxes, the definition of 'proceeds'—and the limitations on promotional play exclusions—directly affects the calculation and collection of state revenue from licensees.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The fiscal note indicates that limiting promotional play exclusions may increase revenues for the General Fund and the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund, both of which are central to the state budget.

The bill impacts revenue for the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund, which is used to support the state's public education system. As the agency responsible for leading the public education system and managing related state and federal funding, this impact on a dedicated education fund is highly relevant.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal representative and counsel for all state agencies, including the Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency. They would be involved in the drafting and legal review of the regulations authorized by this bill.

Synopsis: Altering the schedule by which a county and Baltimore City must reimburse the State Department of Assessments and Taxation for the Department's administrative costs.
Title: State Department of Assessments and Taxation – Local Reimbursement for Administration Costs – Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill changes the schedule for when Maryland counties and Baltimore City must reimburse the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) for property assessment and information technology costs. It replaces the previous quarterly payment schedule with a new requirement to pay 50% of the costs by October 1, followed by 25% on January 1 and 25% on April 1.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland county governments and Baltimore City
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no net fiscal impact on State or local government finances. While it alters the timing of reimbursement payments for property tax assessment and information technology services, it does not change the total amount paid by local jurisdictions or received by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation within a fiscal year.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local jurisdictions to remit administrative reimbursement payments to the Comptroller and authorizes the Comptroller to withhold local income tax distributions from any jurisdiction that fails to make timely payments.

As the principal fiscal agency for the state, the Department of Budget and Management oversees budget execution and the receipt of state revenues, which includes the reimbursements for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation's administrative costs.

The bill specifies the reimbursement of costs for the Office of Information Technology within the assessments department, including funding for projects in the Major Information Technology Development Project Fund, which is overseen by DoIT.

The Governor's Office overseeing the executive branch departments, including the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and submitted this departmental bill to improve the efficiency of local reimbursement and state accounting processes.
The State Treasurer's Office is the chief financial agency responsible for receiving and depositing state funds, including the administrative reimbursements remitted by local governments.

The board provides administrative review of property tax assessments conducted by the state; this bill alters the funding and reimbursement schedule for the administration that performs the primary valuation work.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to provide certain student and workforce data to a third-party data center under certain circumstances; requiring each third-party data center to agree to comply with certain requirements relating to the data the center receives; requiring the Center to enter into a written data sharing agreement with certain third-party data centers; etc.
Title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center - External Data Sharing With Third-Party Data Centers for Multistate Reporting - Authorization
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center Governing Board to share individual-level student and workforce data with third-party data centers for the purpose of facilitating multistate research and reporting on student outcomes. It mandates strict security and privacy protocols, including FedRAMP certification and the use of privacy-enhancing techniques, and repeals existing authority to share student data with the U.S. Census Bureau.
responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center Governing Board
stakeholders: Maryland students and workforce participants whose data is contained in the system; Maryland State agencies (MSDE, MHEC, MD Labor); and third-party data research entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the MLDS Center and its Governing Board can implement the bill's provisions using existing resources. The Center has already been awarded a grant from the Coleridge Initiative’s Democratizing our Data Grant Challenge to facilitate multistate data sharing. There is no estimated impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns the MLDS Center and its Governing Board, granting them the authority to share student and workforce data with third-party data centers and establishing the protocols and security standards for such sharing.

MHEC is a primary data contributor to the MLDS. The bill and fiscal note also highlight MHEC's role in related projects, such as the Post-Secondary Employment Outcomes Explorer, which influenced the repeal of MLDS's Census Bureau sharing authority.
MSDE is a principal provider of student data to the MLDS Center. The bill facilitates the external sharing of data originally sourced from MSDE and local education agencies for multistate research.
The Maryland Department of Labor provides critical workforce data to the MLDS. This bill authorizes the external sharing of that individual-level workforce data with third-party research platforms.
The Department of Health provides data on social determinants that impact educational performance to the MLDS; this data is subject to the research and reporting frameworks addressed by the bill.
DHS, specifically the Social Services Administration, provides child welfare data to the MLDS Center, which is used to analyze educational and economic outcomes under the scope of this legislation.
DJS provides data to the MLDS regarding juvenile involvement in the justice system, which is part of the longitudinal data that may be shared for multistate research under the bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies. The bill requires the Center to enter into formal written data-sharing agreements that must comply with various state and federal privacy laws, necessitating legal review.

DoIT oversees state IT security policy. The bill requires third-party data centers to be FedRAMP-certified and meet specific security standards, which aligns with DoIT's role in managing statewide cybersecurity and infrastructure strategy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB), which directs MLDS data access and research related to the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future.
As a primary source of student data from its constituent institutions, USM's data will be part of the sets shared with third-party centers for multistate research on student outcomes.
As an independent state university, Morgan State provides student data to the MLDS that will be eligible for sharing under the new multistate reporting authorizations.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College provides data to the MLDS that is subject to the external data-sharing provisions of the bill.

Synopsis: Altering exemptions from the personal property tax for business personal property that has a total original cost below $20,000 by repealing provisions of law that prohibit the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from collecting information or requiring the submission of a personal property tax return from certain businesses that qualify for the exemptions; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Personal Property Tax - Exemptions for Low Assessment - Alteration
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the prohibition on the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) from collecting personal property information or requiring a personal property tax return from businesses that qualify for a tax exemption because their personal property has a total original cost of less than $20,000. By allowing the collection of this information, the bill enables SDAT to verify eligibility for the exemption and conduct audits for tax compliance.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Business owners with personal property valued under $20,000, local county and municipal governments, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no impact on State expenditures or revenues as SDAT can handle the requirements with existing resources. Local government revenues may see a minimal increase to the extent that improved verification and compliance efforts identify businesses that should be paying personal property taxes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The PTAAB is the administrative body responsible for hearing appeals regarding personal property tax valuations and assessments. This bill, which alters the reporting and exemption verification process for personal property, directly impacts the assessment data that form the basis for cases heard by these local boards.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates appeals from the final decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards. As the bill increases SDAT's authority to require returns and verify assessments for small businesses, it may lead to an increase in contested valuations and subsequent appeals to the Tax Court.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like SDAT and represents the state in tax-related litigation and appeals. This bill's implementation and any subsequent enforcement or disputes regarding the new reporting requirements would involve the OAG.

As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller has a general interest in tax compliance and the administration of personal property tax laws, even though the tax itself is collected locally.

The Department of Commerce is concerned with the regulatory burden and reporting requirements for Maryland businesses. This bill removes an exemption from filing tax returns for many small businesses, which directly affects the business climate the department monitors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's impact is specifically targeted at businesses with personal property valued under $20,000, which are primarily small businesses. Changes to their reporting requirements and tax compliance obligations fall within the office's scope of concern for the small business community.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency overseeing state personnel and budget execution. While the personal property tax is local, DBM manages the fiscal planning and resources for the agencies (like SDAT) tasked with implementing the new verification and data collection duties.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from operating, conducting, or promoting interactive games; requiring gaming license applicants and license holders to report to the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission annually any business relationship with certain persons known to support, operate, conduct, or promote certain interactive games; requiring the Commission to deny certain license applications and revoke certain licenses under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Gaming - Prohibition on Interactive Games and Revenue From Illegal Markets
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: The bill prohibits the operation and promotion of interactive games, such as online or mobile simulations of casino, lottery, or sports wagering involving currency exchange. It requires gaming licensees to disclose business relationships with illegal gaming entities and mandates that the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission deny or revoke licenses for persons who derive revenue from illegal markets, high-risk jurisdictions, or state sponsors of terrorism.
responsible_party: Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Gaming license applicants and licensees, including casino and sports wagering operators, and entities involved in interactive gaming markets.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the formal fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $110,800 in FY 2027 for the Office of the Attorney General to hire an assistant attorney general to support increased enforcement, with costs projected to reach $150,500 by FY 2031. General fund revenues may increase minimally through criminal fines ranging from $10,000 to $100,000 per violation. There is no anticipated material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill from the SLGCA. The agency is the primary regulator responsible for implementing the interactive gaming prohibition, managing the new reporting and disclosure requirements for licensees, and exercising authority to deny or revoke licenses.

The fiscal note explicitly states that OAG requires an additional Assistant Attorney General to handle the increased investigations and enforcement actions resulting from this bill, with a projected fiscal impact of over $110,000 annually.

The fiscal note identifies the Maryland State Police as a key agency responsible for interpreting and enforcing gambling laws. The agency will be involved in investigating the new criminal misdemeanor activities established by the bill.

The bill mandates that the Commission provide notice and an opportunity for a hearing before revoking a license. As the central panel for executive branch disputes, OAH would likely conduct these administrative hearings.
The bill creates a new misdemeanor with significant penalties (up to 3 years imprisonment and $100,000 in fines), which will be adjudicated within the state court system managed by the AOC.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a misdemeanor punishable by up to three years of imprisonment. DPSCS is responsible for the supervision and incarceration of individuals convicted of such offenses.

The Comptroller is listed as an information source for the bill's fiscal impact. As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors state revenues, including those derived from legal gaming which this bill seeks to protect from illegal competition.

DBM is the principal fiscal and personnel agency. It will be responsible for overseeing the budgetary adjustments and personnel requirements (such as the new OAG position) necessitated by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and manages public safety funds. This bill aligns with their mission to reduce illegal activity and coordinate public safety policy across agencies.

This is a departmental bill requested by an executive agency under the Governor's purview. The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch departments responsible for the bill's enforcement.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose, composition, and duties of the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee; repealing the CTE Skills Standards Advisory Committee; and requiring State agencies and certain workforce development and education programs to use a certain list of occupations as a guideline for curriculum alignment, credentialing, and career advancement.
Title: Education - Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee and CTE Skills Standards Advisory Committee - Revisions and Repeal
Status: In the House - Reassigned to Ways and Means and Economic Matters

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee's role to direct a globally competitive workforce system. It repeals the CTE Skills Standards Advisory Committee and requires the CTE Committee to create a list of priority jobs and career path standards that State agencies must follow for education and training programs.
stakeholders: Maryland students, employers, industry and trade associations, labor organizations, and community colleges.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. The bill explicitly allows the CTE Committee to employ additional staff as provided in the State budget, suggesting potential personnel and administrative expenditures, though committee members serve without compensation or reimbursement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill by the Department of Labor. The Secretary of Labor is a member of the CTE Committee, and the agency's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning oversees registered apprenticeship programs integrated into the CTE framework.

The State Superintendent is a core member of the CTE Committee. The bill directly impacts the administration of CTE programs in public schools, high school graduation requirements, and the deployment of CTE Expert Review Teams to review school performance.

The CTE Committee is established as a unit within the Governor's Workforce Development Board. The Board is responsible for approving the priority occupations list and overseeing the Committee's duties.

The Secretary of Higher Education is a member of the CTE Committee. The agency is responsible for coordinating postsecondary CTE programs and receives recommendations on system adjustments from the Committee.
The Secretary of Commerce is a member of the CTE Committee. The agency's mission to align workforce training with economic development and industry needs is central to the Committee's purpose.
The Governor is responsible for selecting and appointing members of the CTE Committee and its chair in collaboration with legislative leaders. The Committee also reports annually to the Governor.

The CTE Committee is required to review agency budget proposals involving CTE and make recommendations. Additionally, DBM oversees the personnel and staffing functions for the Committee as provided in the state budget.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting process for the various members and the chair of the CTE Committee.

The bill creates an integrated framework for CTE across secondary and postsecondary institutions. As the state's public higher education system, USM institutions are key stakeholders in providing aligned CTE pathways and credentials.
As a public institution of postsecondary education, Morgan State is part of the integrated system directed by the CTE Committee to align vocational training and credentialing.
As an independent state college, Saint Mary's is impacted by the CTE Committee's efforts to integrate postsecondary education into a unified career progression system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly alters the composition and duties of the CTE Committee and repeals the CTE Skills Standards Advisory Committee, both of which fall under this administrative category of executive bodies.
The CTE Committee uses state accountability data to identify schools for review. MLDS provides the infrastructure for linking student performance and workforce outcomes used in such evaluations.
The CTE Committee is required to include a representative of the agricultural community, and its occupational standards framework includes considerations for agricultural skills and career pathways.

Synopsis: Establishing the GED Option Pilot Program to expand the GED Option Program to students beyond English language learners to ensure a pathway for students to obtain a high school diploma and prepare for postsecondary education or the workforce; requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to establish criteria to select certain local school systems for participation in the Program; establishing the MDiplomaWorks pathway as an alternative method of earning a high school diploma in the State; etc.
Title: Adult Education – High School Diploma Pathways – GED Option Pilot Program and MDiplomaWorks Pathway
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the GED Option Pilot Program and the MDiplomaWorks Pathway to provide alternative methods for obtaining a high school diploma. The GED Option Pilot Program expands an existing program for English language learners to other students at significant risk of not completing high school in at least three selected local school systems. The MDiplomaWorks Pathway allows individuals who have withdrawn from school to earn a diploma by demonstrating academic and career competencies through industry credentials, assessments, coursework, and on-the-job learning.
stakeholders: Students at risk of not completing high school, adult learners without a high school diploma, local school systems, and Maryland small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the programs with existing resources. Participating local school systems will experience increased expenditures to expand GED options; for illustrative purposes, Montgomery County estimates costs of $550,000 annually for 130 additional students. No impact on State revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for establishing and overseeing the GED Option Pilot Program and the MDiplomaWorks pathway. It must consult with the Department of Education, develop selection criteria, and jointly report on program effectiveness.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is a required consultant for the pilot program's development and implementation. The bill directly impacts high school graduation requirements, which MSDE oversees, and may require the agency to update graduation, transcript, and data reporting systems.

The bill establishes the MDiplomaWorks pathway, which integrates industry-recognized credentials and on-the-job learning into high school diploma achievement. This aligns with the Board's mission to develop innovative workforce solutions and coordinate partnerships between business and education.

The bill requires the Department of Labor and the Department of Education to report jointly to the Governor on the effectiveness of the pilot program. The Governor's Office oversees these executive departments and coordinates the policy initiatives related to workforce and education.

The bill focuses on students at significant risk of not successfully completing high school, aiming to improve their access to economic opportunities and education. This aligns with the GOC's mission to improve access to health services, education, and economic opportunities for underinvested communities and youth.

The MLDSC links student performance and workforce data. This bill creates a new diploma pathway based on both academic and career competencies, and the required reporting on student outcomes will likely involve data managed or analyzed by this agency.

One stated goal of the GED Option Pilot Program is to ensure students are prepared to enter postsecondary programming. The Commission, which oversees policies for public and private colleges, has a vested interest in the standards and outcomes of alternative diploma pathways.

The bill is expected to have a meaningful positive impact on small businesses by increasing the pool of skilled workers with high school diplomas and industry credentials, which are necessary for Commerce's economic development and business attraction goals.

While the Department of Labor intends to use existing resources, the fiscal note indicates that the Department of Education may require additional staff and contractual support to implement the substantial regulatory and data system changes required by the bill.

The bill establishes a pilot program with specific reporting requirements and an evaluation component. GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to oversee state agency operations and ensure measurable results, which is relevant to the monitoring of this new initiative.

The bill's focus on enhancing economic mobility and addressing at-risk youth aligns with the Innovation Team's specific charge to pilot novel initiatives that reduce child poverty and improve outcomes for Maryland families.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that a county supervisor of real property assessments reside in the county for which the supervisor is appointed; and repealing the requirement that the county assessment office be located in the county seat.
Title: State Department of Assessments and Taxation – County Supervisor Residency Requirement and Location of County Assessment Offices – Alteration
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: This bill repeals the requirement that a county supervisor of real property assessments must reside in the county for which they are appointed and removes the requirement that county assessment offices be located specifically in the county seat.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: County Supervisors of Assessments, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and local county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the changes using its existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters residency requirements for County Supervisors of Assessments, who are members of the management service of the State Personnel Management System. As the state's central personnel agency, DBM manages employee policies and classifications relevant to these positions.

By repealing the requirement that county assessment offices be located in the county seat, the bill provides flexibility for office relocation. DGS is the primary agency responsible for managing state real estate, including the planning and leasing of facilities.

The relocation of county assessment offices away from county seats would involve new leases or property management decisions that require oversight and approval by the Board of Public Works to ensure fiscal responsibility.

The Comptroller is responsible for receiving quarterly payments from counties to reimburse the State for assessment costs and has the statutory authority to withhold tax distributions for non-payment, as detailed in the section of the Tax-Property Article being amended.

The PTAAB reviews assessment decisions made by the County Supervisors of Assessments. Changes to the residency requirements and office locations of these supervisors affect the administrative structure of the assessment process that the Board oversees.

This departmental bill was requested by an executive agency under the Governor's oversight. The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch departments involved in property tax administration.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Assessments and Taxation, regarding the implementation of legislative changes and the interpretation of personnel and facility regulations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly making or using, or causing to be made or used, a false record or statement resulting in underpayments of unemployment insurance contributions or payment of unemployment insurance benefits of more than $15,000; altering the enforcement mechanisms related to workplace fraud laws, living wage laws, and prevailing wage laws, including authorizing the Attorney General to investigate and bring suit in a certain manner; etc.
Title: Fraud Prevention, Prevailing Wage, and Living Wage - Prohibitions, Penalties, and Enforcement
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
