The Department of Education (MSDE) provides leadership and oversight to Maryland's 24 local school systems; this bill directly amends the Education Article of the Maryland Code to modify the governance and compensation structure of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education.

The bill increases scholarship awards for student board members to be applied toward higher education costs, which falls within the Commission's scope of coordinating postsecondary education and financial aid programs.

The bill increases scholarship awards for student board members to be applied toward higher education costs, which falls within the Commission's scope of coordinating postsecondary education and financial aid programs.

Changes in compensation for public officials can affect the calculation of retirement benefits, as well as employer and employee contributions, for those participating in the state's retirement and pension system.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly; the bill involves specific constitutional language regarding the timing of salary increases (Article III, Section 35) that may require legal review or interpretation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Transportation, as part of the planning and implementation of certain major highway expansion projects, to perform an impact assessment of the project and develop and implement a corresponding multimodal transportation program; requiring the Department, beginning with a certain Consolidated Transportation Program, to evaluate certain major capital projects for their impact on greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle miles traveled; etc.
Title: Transportation - Major Highway Capacity Expansion Projects and Impact Assessments (Transportation and Climate Alignment Act of 2026)

bill_summary: The Transportation and Climate Alignment Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to perform impact assessments for major highway expansion projects with costs exceeding $100,000,000. For these projects, MDOT must develop and fund multimodal transportation programs—such as transit, bike lanes, and pedestrian infrastructure—to offset any increases in greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle miles traveled, with the goal of achieving a net-zero or negative climate impact. The bill also requires MDOT to evaluate all major capital projects in the Consolidated Transportation Program for their environmental impacts and to set annual statewide and regional greenhouse gas reduction targets.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, commuters, individuals living in overburdened or underserved communities, and users of the state's transportation and transit systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates that the Maryland Department of Transportation fund multimodal transportation programs to offset greenhouse gas emissions for major highway expansion projects exceeding $100,000,000. It also requires funding for statewide and regional travel demand modeling starting in fiscal year 2028. While specific total dollar estimates are not provided in the bill text, the requirement to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas impacts for major projects suggests potentially significant redirected or additional state expenditures toward transit and alternative transportation infrastructure. Local transit systems may also see impacts as they are identified as potential offset investments. Formal fiscal note estimates are unavailable in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation, including conducting impact assessments, setting greenhouse gas emission targets, and developing multimodal transportation programs for major highway projects.

SHA is specifically tasked with issuing reports prior to final project planning phases for highway projects and is the primary administration overseeing the highway capacity expansion projects targeted by the bill.
MTA is a modal administration within MDOT that will be significantly impacted by the bill's requirement to implement transit improvements and expansions as offsetting activities for highway projects.
DBM oversees the state budget and the execution of the Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP), which the bill directly modifies by adding new evaluation and funding requirements.
The bill utilizes MDE's statutory definitions for overburdened and underserved communities and aligns transportation planning with the State's Climate Pollution Reduction Plan overseen by MDE.
The bill includes land use changes and transit-oriented development as key offsetting activities, areas where MDP provides technical assistance and policy guidance.
The BPW must approve the major capital projects and procurement contracts (exceeding $100 million) that are the subject of the bill's new assessment and mitigation requirements.
MDTA manages toll facilities and could potentially be subject to these requirements if they undertake major highway capacity expansion projects exceeding the $100 million threshold.
The bill explicitly lists 'accessible transportation and pedestrian improvements for people with disabilities' as prioritized offsetting activities.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and sets the policy priorities for climate reduction and the state budget, which are central to the 'Transportation and Climate Alignment Act.'
The bill mentions solar energy generation on state-controlled property as an offset, which aligns with MEA's mission to promote renewable energy.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Adult Prison School Board Model Development Committee to create a comprehensive plan for a school board system to oversee correctional education for individuals in the criminal and juvenile justice systems and to conduct a fiscal mapping project to determine funding requirements.
stakeholders: Individuals subject to the criminal and juvenile justice systems, Maryland State agencies including the Department of Labor and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and nonprofit correctional reform organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $111,518 in FY 2027 and $98,760 in FY 2028 to hire one contractual position to support the committee's research, planning, and reporting mandates. There is no impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Department of Education is mandated to provide staff for the Committee and the State Superintendent of Schools is a named member of the committee. Additionally, the Department is responsible for the fiscal mapping and research required by the bill, with the fiscal note identifying a direct expenditure impact for contractual staffing within the department.

The Secretary of Labor is an ex-officio member of the committee. The Department's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning currently oversees the Office of Correctional Education, which provides the services that would be governed by the proposed school board system.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services is a member of the committee, and the agency manages the adult correctional facilities where the proposed school board would operate. The bill also specifically includes representation for Maryland Correctional Enterprises, which is a unit within this department.

The Superintendent for the Juvenile Services Education Program (JSEP), which is overseen by DJS, is a named member of the committee. The committee is tasked with developing a plan that oversees correctional education for individuals within the juvenile justice system.

The bill explicitly requires the committee to develop an independent relationship with DBM to establish and manage capital and operating budgets for the new school board system. DBM is also central to the required fiscal mapping project.

The Secretary of Higher Education is a named member of the committee, and the commission is suggested as a permanent member of the future school board. The committee's plan will likely involve post-secondary education standards which MHEC regulates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes a new temporary development committee tasked with specific study, planning, and recommendation duties, which fits the category of an executive committee or task force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is Maryland's coordinating body for criminal justice policy and currently staffs the existing Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission, whose recommendations are reflected in this legislation.

The bill recommends that the Department of Information Technology be represented on the resulting school board system, reflecting the technical infrastructure needed for modern correctional education.
The Office of Appointments will be responsible for recruiting and vetting the individuals the Governor appoints to the new committee.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and commissions and would likely be involved in the legal formation and advisory work of the new committee and its comprehensive plan.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish an enhanced reimbursement structure for Medicaid providers who deliver medical services to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. The structure is designed to provide higher reimbursement rates that account for the specialized training, additional time, and communication supports often required to treat this population. The bill's implementation is contingent upon the availability of federal funding through the Health Equity for Adults with Disabilities (HEADs UP) Act or similar federal sources.
stakeholders: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and healthcare providers participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid).
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in an increase in State expenditures to provide enhanced reimbursement rates to Medicaid providers, as well as a corresponding increase in federal fund revenues. However, the bill is explicitly contingent on the availability of federal funding from the HEADs UP Act or other federal streams; if federal funds are not made available by December 31, 2036, the act will be null and void. Because a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the text provided, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). As the principal state agency for coordinating and improving services for residents with disabilities, this department is directly impacted by changes to healthcare reimbursement structures intended to improve service capacity and clinical quality for its primary constituency.

The bill specifically requires the Maryland Department of Health to consult with the Office of the Attorney General to determine if federal funds are available through the HEADs UP Act or other streams, which is the triggering condition for the Act to take effect.

As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM is heavily involved in any legislation that mandates changes to Medicaid reimbursement rates, which represent a significant portion of state expenditures.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including MDH. The bill's implementation depends on federal funding and executive branch coordination, aligning with the Governor's role in overseeing policy initiatives and the annual budget.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes and, under specific conditions involving multiple or high-value overdue citations, requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to suspend the registration of motor vehicles involved in speed monitoring system violations on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) in Prince George’s County. To reinstate a registration suspended under the bill, the vehicle owner must pay all overdue civil penalties, fees, and court costs, as well as a $30 administrative fee to Prince George’s County.
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners traveling on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County, the Prince George's County government, and the State Highway Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures from fiscal 2027 through 2029 by encouraging the payment of overdue speed camera fines on Maryland Route 210; as a baseline, $334,456 in net revenue was remitted to the State from these cameras in fiscal 2023. General fund revenues will increase to the extent more citations are contested in court. Prince George's County will collect a $30 administrative fee for each registration reinstatement. The authorization for the speed monitoring systems on this route is currently scheduled to terminate on September 30, 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes and requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to suspend motor vehicle registrations for unpaid or uncontested speed monitoring violations on Maryland Route 210. It also mandates that the MVA issue written notices to owners and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding these suspensions.

As noted in the fiscal note, fine revenues from speed cameras on Maryland Route 210 are remitted to the State Highway Administration (SHA). Because this bill increases enforcement mechanisms (suspensions), it is expected to increase fine collections, thereby increasing the revenue available to SHA for safety improvements on that specific highway.

The bill's enhanced enforcement measures for speed monitoring citations are expected to increase the number of contested cases in the District Court, which falls under the oversight of the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill provides that vehicle owners whose registrations are suspended may request a hearing under Title 12, Subtitle 2 of the Transportation Article, which involves the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) and its administrative law judges.

As the parent department for both the Motor Vehicle Administration and the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the modal administrations responsible for implementing the bill's registration suspension mandates and managing the resulting safety improvement funds.

The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for receiving net fine revenues from the county and distributing them to the State Highway Administration, a process that will see increased volume due to the bill's enforcement provisions.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Motor Vehicle Administration and would represent the agency in the event of legal challenges to the registration suspension process or administrative appeals.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for improving accountability and providing information regarding the quality and cost of health services to the public. stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies, county sheriffs, and individuals subject to civil immigration enforcement within Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While specific jurisdictions including Allegany, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, St. Mary’s, and Washington counties are required to terminate existing 287(g) agreements, no specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditure changes are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are directly prohibited by the bill from entering into or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements with the federal government.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities and parole/probation functions; the bill directly prohibits its agencies and employees from participating in civil immigration enforcement agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, directly advising the Governor on policy impacts like those mandated by this bill.

This office serves as the primary liaison to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which is the federal entity that enters into the immigration enforcement agreements (such as 287(g)) that this bill prohibits.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and has previously issued guidance to law enforcement regarding interactions with federal immigration authorities; it would likely oversee the legal termination of existing agreements.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing the state's mandate to terminate existing immigration enforcement agreements across all state agencies and units.
The MDTA maintains its own nationally accredited police force, which is subject to the bill's prohibition on state agencies entering or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements.
MDOT oversees several modal administrations with law enforcement functions (such as the Maryland Transit Administration police) that are subject to the bill's prohibitions.
The department oversees the Natural Resources Police, who are state officers prohibited by the bill from entering into immigration enforcement agreements.
As an agency that manages youth in detention and community supervision, DJS and its employees are prohibited from engaging in civil immigration enforcement under the bill.
As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM monitors the operational and budget execution impacts for agencies required to terminate existing federal agreements.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide certain coverage related to orthoses beginning January 1, 2027; clarifying that certain mandated benefits related to prostheses include all prostheses determined by a treating health care provider to be medically necessary for completing daily living activities, essential job-related activities or performing certain other physical activities; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Orthoses and Prostheses (So Every Body Can Move Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and certain health insurance carriers to provide coverage for orthoses (braces and similar devices), including components, repairs, and replacements. It also clarifies that mandated prosthetic coverage must include devices determined by a health care provider to be medically necessary for physical activities like running, biking, and swimming, as well as activities of daily living and job-related tasks. Additionally, the bill establishes reporting requirements for insurers and Medicaid regarding their compliance with these coverage mandates.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland residents requiring orthoses or prostheses, health insurance carriers, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, and health care providers of orthotic and prosthetic services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal special fund revenue increase of $125 in FY 2027 from filing fees. The bill is expected to have no fiscal impact on the Maryland Medical Assistance Program as it codifies existing coverage practices already implemented by the department. For the commercial insurance market, the expanded orthoses coverage is estimated to cost approximately $1,450,000 annually. Local government expenditures may increase if they purchase fully insured health plans for employees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is mandated by the bill to provide coverage for orthoses. MDH is also required to receive compliance reports from managed care organizations and submit a joint report to the General Assembly by 2032.

MIA is the primary regulator for private insurance carriers affected by the bill's mandates. It is responsible for reviewing rate and form filings, receiving compliance reports from carriers, and producing a joint report with MDH on utilization and costs.

The bill mandates coverage for orthoses and prostheses, which are essential assistive technologies for individuals with disabilities. The department is responsible for coordinating and improving service delivery and assistive technology access for this population.

MHCC is responsible for health system planning and has previously conducted the required cost-impact studies regarding the coverage mandates for orthoses and prostheses referenced in the bill's fiscal note.

DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Although the fiscal note indicates a negligible impact as coverage already exists, the agency is responsible for overseeing the benefits plans subject to state mandates.

Many older adults rely on orthoses and prostheses for mobility and activities of daily living. The department oversees programs and advocacy that support the independence and quality of life for this demographic.

As the administrator of the state’s health insurance marketplace, MHBE oversees private health plans that must comply with state-mandated benefits and ensures coordination with other state insurance regulations.
OAG provides legal counsel to MDH and MIA regarding the implementation of the mandate, the interpretation of medical necessity standards, and the drafting of required regulations.

The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch agencies (MDH, MIA) responsible for implementing the coverage requirements and reporting to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council to include an examination of the capacity of health care providers to deliver care to certain individuals and to identify methods by which the State can assist health care providers in delivering care to certain individuals; establishing the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program in the Maryland Department of Health to lead the State's public health efforts relating to brain health and dementia; etc.
Title: Health - Dementia Services and Brain Health Program and Clinical Toolkit
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health to lead public health efforts related to brain health and dementia. It requires the program to develop and maintain a clinical toolkit for dementia care for health care providers by January 1, 2027, and updates the responsibilities of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council to include examining provider readiness and capacity.
stakeholders: Individuals with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, their caregivers, health care providers, managed care programs, hospitals, health systems, and academic research institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $127,700 in FY 2027, reflecting the cost of hiring one program administrator and $50,000 for annual consultant services to develop the clinical toolkit. Costs are projected to increase annually, reaching an estimated $153,500 by FY 2031. The Maryland Department of Aging can participate using existing resources, and there is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, MDH is responsible for establishing the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program, hiring the Director, and developing the mandated clinical toolkit for dementia care.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency category covers the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council, whose duties and staffing are centrally altered and expanded by the bill.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of Aging to partner with MDH in establishing the clinical toolkit and providing staff support for the Council.
MHCC is responsible for health system planning and improving access to care; the bill's focus on dementia-capable care and provider tools aligns directly with their regulatory mission.
The bill requires coordination with academic institutions to promote dementia-specific education, training, and certification for health care professionals.
As a major public research university, Morgan State is a key 'academic institution' designated for coordination on dementia education and training initiatives.

The bill mandates collaboration with State-led care transformation initiatives to incorporate dementia-capable care practices into health care models, which falls under HSCRC's hospital quality and innovation remit.
DBM oversees the personnel and budget for the new Dementia Services and Brain Health Program, including the permanent Director position and contractual consultant costs identified in the fiscal note.
The Program and Council must advise the Governor and submit reports on their activities and recommendations regarding brain health policy.
The agency manages the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home; the clinical toolkit and dementia-capable care protocols are directly relevant to the health services provided to their residents.
The Commission coordinates policies for colleges and universities that will be involved in the bill's mandate for dementia-specific education and training.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: EMS providers are among the health care professionals expected to utilize the protocols and education resources developed under the new Program.
MIA regulates managed care programs and insurers that are specifically identified as targets for the promotion of the new clinical toolkit.
The department works with other agencies to ensure integrated services for those with disabilities, which includes cognitive impairments associated with dementia and Down Syndrome.
DHS provides services to vulnerable adults who may require protection and aid due to the cognitive decline and dementia addressed by the bill.
The bill explicitly tasks the new Program with applying for grants to enable the implementation of State Plan goals for dementia care.
The board coordinates workforce solutions that align with state needs, including the training and certification pathways for the healthcare professionals mentioned in the bill.
The MVA's Highway Safety Office and medical review processes are impacted by state efforts to manage cognitive impairment and brain health among the driving population.
The Council advocates for healthcare access in rural counties, where the dissemination of the dementia toolkit and provider training is a critical service need.
As a public academic institution, it is a potential partner for the professional education and training programs promoted by the new MDH program.
OCSA regulates the prescribing of controlled substances, which are often used in the treatment and management of patients with dementia in various medical settings.
The clinical toolkit includes information on reimbursement and billing codes, which overlaps with the Exchange's role in making health coverage accessible and understandable.

Synopsis: Establishing that every person has the right to hunt, fish, or harvest wildlife, including the right to use traditional methods to hunt, fish, or harvest wildlife, subject to certain regulations and restrictions; establishing that the right to hunt and fish is forever preserved for the public good; and establishing that fishing and hunting are preferred means of managing and controlling wildlife in the State.
Title: Natural Resources - Right to Hunt, Fish, and Harvest Wildlife
Status: In the House - First Reading House Rules and Executive Nominations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; FishNets&Dev
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Plants -see also- Invasive Species; Trees; Weeds

bill_summary: This bill proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution to establish a right for individuals to hunt, fish, and harvest wildlife using traditional methods, subject to regulations for wildlife conservation. It designates hunting and fishing as the preferred methods for managing and controlling wildlife in the state and requires that these rights be preserved for the public good.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, hunters, anglers, and state wildlife management officials
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill indicates that hunting and fishing activities contribute to tax revenues and employment and support conservation efforts through federal funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is the primary agency responsible for managing the state's wildlife and fisheries. This bill directly impacts their mandate by establishing hunting and fishing as the preferred means of wildlife management and creating a constitutional right that DNR must accommodate in its regulations and enforcement activities.

This bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be submitted to the qualified voters of the state for adoption or rejection. The State Board of Elections is responsible for administering the referendum process at the 2026 general election.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. Specifically, the Governor is required by the bill to receive the election returns and issue a proclamation if the constitutional amendment is adopted by the voters.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state. They would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the implementation of this new constitutional right and defending the state in any litigation challenging the scope of 'traditional methods' or the balance between the right and existing regulations.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records and the Great Seal. They are responsible for the formal record-keeping and processing of laws and amendments passed by the General Assembly and ratified by voters.

The bill's changes to wildlife management and the establishment of hunting/fishing as preferred management tools impact agricultural lands and the economic viability of resource-based industries supported by the Department of Agriculture.

The bill explicitly finds that hunting and fishing are valued parts of the state's cultural heritage and economy. The Department of Commerce, which handles economic development and tourism, would be impacted by the formal recognition of these activities as protected rights.

OTD is responsible for promoting Maryland's recreational and cultural assets. The establishment of a constitutional right to hunt and fish enhances the state's profile for outdoor recreation and tourism, which are key components of OTD's marketing mission.

As the support agency for the Judicial Branch, the AOC is relevant because courts will likely need to adjudicate cases where individuals cite the new constitutional right as a defense against existing natural resources regulations or trespass charges.

The OAH hears contested cases involving state agencies, including DNR. A constitutional right to hunt and fish would likely be raised in administrative hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of hunting and fishing licenses.

The Council addresses challenges in rural counties where hunting and fishing are significant economic and cultural activities. This bill directly supports the interests of the rural communities the agency represents.

The State Archives is the depository for government records of permanent value. A constitutional amendment represents a permanent change to the state's foundational documents, which the Archives must preserve and make accessible.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to conduct at least two on-site unannounced inspections of each certified recovery residence annually; authorizing the Department to direct the recovery residence credentialing entity to revoke the certification of a certified recovery residence that fails to correct a deficiency within 1 month after notice of the deficiency is provided; etc.
Title: Health Facilities - Certified Recovery Residences - Unannounced Inspections
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct at least two unannounced on-site inspections of each certified recovery residence annually. It establishes a one-month remediation period for residences found to be noncompliant and authorizes the Department to direct the credentialing entity to revoke the certification of residences that fail to correct deficiencies.
stakeholders: Certified recovery residences and individuals with substance-related or addictive disorders
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least $373,600 in FY 2027, which accounts for the bill's October 1, 2026 effective date. This funding is required for the Maryland Department of Health to hire five staff members to conduct inspections and manage compliance notifications. Expenditures are projected to grow to approximately $496,500 by FY 2031. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 448 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to perform at least two unannounced on-site inspections per year for every certified recovery residence in the state. The department is also responsible for managing the deficiency notice process and directing the revocation of certifications for non-compliant residences.

According to the fiscal note, the bill requires at least $373,600 in general fund expenditures in FY 2027 and the hiring of five additional full-time staff members (special program coordinators) to handle the inspection workload. DBM oversees the state budget and personnel management associated with these impacts.

If a certified recovery residence contests a deficiency finding or the revocation of its certification as authorized by this bill, the Office of Administrative Hearings would likely be the venue for the resulting administrative legal proceedings.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health. They would be involved in advising on the implementation of the new inspection regulations and representing the state in any litigation or appeals arising from certification revocations.

Synopsis: Altering a certain provision of law authorizing a law enforcement officer to conduct an otherwise lawful custodial interrogation of a child if the child's parent, guardian, or custodian consents to the custodial interrogation of the child without the child's consultation with an attorney.
Title: Juvenile Justice Restoration Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: The bill authorizes a law enforcement officer to conduct a custodial interrogation of a child without the child first consulting with an attorney if the child's parent, guardian, or custodian consents to the interrogation. It also preserves the existing exception for custodial interrogations conducted under the reasonable belief that the information sought is necessary to protect against a public safety threat.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Juveniles in Maryland, parents or guardians of juveniles, law enforcement officers, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text; therefore, specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The bill may result in a fiscal impact by reducing the number of mandatory legal consultations provided by the Office of the Public Defender if parents choose to consent to interrogations without counsel, potentially leading to decreased state expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, its officers must comply with the procedural requirements for custodial interrogations of children. This bill directly alters the protocols for when and how officers may interrogate juveniles, specifically by allowing an exception for parental consent.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the Office of the Public Defender's (OPD) role in providing mandatory legal consultations for juveniles. By allowing parental consent to bypass the attorney consultation requirement, this bill directly affects the workload and statutory responsibilities of the OPD in juvenile justice cases.

DJS is the principal agency for youth in the juvenile justice system. Changes to interrogation laws directly impact the delinquency proceedings and the processing of youth within the system that DJS manages.

The OAG represents the state in criminal and civil appeals, including delinquency proceedings where the admissibility of juvenile statements may be litigated. They also provide legal counsel to state law enforcement agencies regarding these procedural changes.

The bill explicitly includes School Resource Officers (SROs) in the definition of law enforcement officers subject to these interrogation rules. The Maryland Center for School Safety oversees SRO certification and training, making these procedural changes highly relevant to their guidance.

MSDE oversees school systems and coordinates with law enforcement on school safety issues. Since the bill specifically includes school resource officers (as defined in the Education Article), it affects personnel and safety protocols within the educational environment.
The judiciary is responsible for delinquency proceedings and criminal prosecutions where the admissibility of statements obtained under these rules will be evaluated and determined.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and juvenile delinquency reduction. This bill represents a significant shift in juvenile justice policy that falls within their oversight.
MDOT manages several law enforcement entities (such as the MDTA Police and Transit Police) whose officers conduct custodial interrogations and must follow these revised statutory procedures.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a court or a party in a criminal or juvenile delinquency case from disclosing or allowing inspection of a certain court filing or record to a nonparty unless the court or the party redacts certain identifying information relating to a certain victim of sexual assault or victim of stalking that appears in the filing or record, unless the Court finds clear and convincing evidence that there is good cause to order otherwise; etc.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Protection of Identity of Victim of Sexual Assault or Stalking
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a court or a party in a criminal or juvenile delinquency case from disclosing or allowing the inspection of court filings or records to a nonparty if they contain identifying information about a victim of sexual assault or stalking, unless the information is redacted. It also requires a court to redact such identifying information from existing records upon the written request of the victim, subject to a judicial finding of good cause for disclosure.
stakeholders: Victims of sexual assault and stalking, the Maryland Judiciary, parties in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, and members of the public seeking access to court records.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $13,500 in fiscal 2027 for one-time computer programming costs to update case management systems. There is no effect on State revenues. The bill may have an operational impact on local circuit courts due to the administrative requirements of redacting records, but specific local fiscal impacts are not quantified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch by requiring the court to redact identifying information from electronic and paper filings in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases. The fiscal note specifies $13,500 in programming costs for the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a primary party in most criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, the OPD is prohibited by this bill from disclosing or allowing inspection of case filings to nonparties without redacting identifying information.

The bill explicitly applies to juvenile delinquency cases. DJS is responsible for managing youth in the juvenile justice system and is often a party to these cases or manages the records and filings that would be subject to these redaction requirements.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP initiates charging documents which are specifically mentioned in the bill as records that must have identifying information redacted before disclosure to nonparties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages criminal records and reports (such as pre-sentence investigations) used in court filings. The agency would be a party or an entity providing records that fall under the bill's redaction mandate.

The OAG represents the State in criminal appeals and certain prosecutions. As a 'party' in these court cases, the office would be responsible for adhering to the redaction requirements for case filings and records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety strategies and manages funds for victim services. The bill’s focus on protecting the identities of sexual assault and stalking victims aligns with the office's policy and coordination mission.

Synopsis: Altering the deadlines for the interim and final reporting requirements for the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council; and extending the termination date for the Council from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2031.
Title: Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council – Reporting and Sunset Extension
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2031. It also updates the Council's reporting requirements, requiring annual interim reports to the Governor and General Assembly from 2027 through 2031, and a final report due by June 30, 2031.
responsible_party: Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council
stakeholders: Maryland electric vehicle owners, infrastructure developers, the Maryland Department of Transportation, and state legislators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill extends the operational life of the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council for five additional years. While this will likely result in continued administrative and staffing expenditures for the agencies supporting the Council, specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council is established under the Transportation Article, and the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) provides the primary administrative support and staffing for the Council's operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the reporting requirements and extends the duration of the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council, which is a permanent advisory body within this category.
The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is a key member of the Council and is responsible for implementing energy policies and grant programs related to electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
The Department of the Environment (MDE) coordinates with the Council on electric vehicle initiatives to meet state goals for greenhouse gas reduction and air quality improvement.
The Public Service Commission (PSC) regulates public utilities involved in the deployment of electric vehicle charging infrastructure and is a primary stakeholder in the Council's work.
The Council is required by the bill to submit its interim and final reports to the Governor, and the Governor's Office is responsible for appointing many of the Council's members.

The Department of General Services (DGS) manages state facilities and the state vehicle fleet, both of which are directly impacted by the Council's recommendations regarding zero-emission vehicle infrastructure.
The extension of the Council's sunset date has fiscal implications regarding the continued administrative support and potential staffing costs overseen by DBM.
The Department of Commerce is involved in the Council to represent economic development interests and the business community within Maryland's electric vehicle sector.
The Maryland Department of Planning participates in the Council's activities related to land use planning and local government coordination for EV charging deployment.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Council and ensures its reports and activities comply with state law and procedural requirements.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from suspending or revoking a license to practice veterinary medicine in the State, reprimanding or censuring a licensee, or placing a licensee on probation solely on the basis of the licensee discussing or recommending the use of cannabis or a product that contains cannabidiol on an animal for potential therapeutic effect or health supplementation purposes.
Title: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners - Grounds for Disciplinary Action - Restrictions
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from taking disciplinary action, such as license suspension, revocation, reprimand, or probation, against a veterinarian solely because the licensee discussed or recommended the use of cannabis or cannabidiol (CBD) products for an animal for therapeutic or health supplementation purposes.
responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed veterinarians, veterinary practitioners, and the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners has not taken formal actions to date that would be prohibited under the bill, and the impact on small veterinary businesses is expected to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is an entity within the Maryland Department of Agriculture. This bill directly limits the Board's authority to take disciplinary action against licensed veterinarians regarding the discussion or recommendation of cannabis products.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners. They would be responsible for advising the Board on the implementation of these new disciplinary restrictions and representing them in related legal matters.

The bill references the definition of cannabis provided in the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which is overseen by this administration. The legislation addresses the professional discussion and recommendation of products within the agency's regulatory subject matter.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies, including disciplinary disputes involving licensed professionals. Administrative Law Judges would be required to apply these new statutory restrictions in any contested cases involving the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners.

Synopsis: Establishing the Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund to provide grants to low-income unit owners of condominiums with insufficient reserve accounts to enable a low-income unit owner to pay increased assessments necessary for a condominium association to meet reserve account funding requirements; requiring that the Fund prioritize certain older adults; requiring the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish certain procedures, publicize the Fund and prioritize older owners; etc.
Title: Real Property - Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund - Establishment
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Department of Housing and Community Development. The fund's purpose is to provide grants to low-income unit owners (those with household incomes not exceeding 80% of the area median income) to help them pay increased assessments required for their condominium associations to meet statutory reserve account funding requirements. The bill requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to administer the fund and prioritize grants for owners who are at least 65 years old.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income condominium unit owners, especially those aged 65 and older, and Maryland condominium associations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a special fund that will receive money through State budget appropriations and interest earnings. It exempts the fund from the requirement that interest earnings accrue to the General Fund. However, because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific dollar estimates for the State appropriation, administrative costs, or interest revenue impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Department of Housing and Community Development to administer the Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund, establish application procedures, publicize the fund, and receive annual reports from grant recipients.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the new special fund separately and invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other state money.

The Secretary of State is responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums in Maryland. This bill creates a financial support mechanism for low-income unit owners to comply with reserve funding requirements related to those condominiums.
The bill requires that priority for grants be given to low-income unit owners who are at least 65 years old, which directly impacts the demographic served by the Department of Aging.

The bill amends the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding how interest on special funds is accounted for by the Comptroller and ensures interest from this new fund stays within the fund rather than accruing to the General Fund.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the budget execution and oversight of the new special, nonlapsing fund created by this bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget, which must include the appropriations and expenditures for this new grant fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Administrator of Elections to enroll the State in the federal Systematic Alien Verification of Entitlement (SAVE) Program for a certain purpose; requiring the State Board of Elections to establish a process to verify the U.S. citizenship of certain individuals applying to or who have registered to vote in the State; and requiring the State Board to establish a certain appeal process for certain individuals who dispute a certain report that the individual lacks U.S. citizenship.
Title: Election Law - Voter Registration Eligibility - U.S. Citizenship Verification (SAVE Our Elections Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: The SAVE Our Elections Act of 2026 requires the Maryland State Administrator of Elections to enroll the state in the federal Systematic Alien Verification of Entitlement (SAVE) Program. This program will be used to verify the U.S. citizenship status of individuals who are applying to register to vote or are already registered in Maryland. The bill also mandates that the State Board of Elections establish regulations for this verification process and create an appeal process for individuals whose citizenship status is disputed based on reports from the SAVE program.
stakeholders: Individuals applying for voter registration and currently registered voters in Maryland whose citizenship status may be subject to verification.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill's requirements for enrolling in the federal SAVE program and establishing verification and appeal procedures will result in administrative expenditures for the State Board of Elections and local boards of elections, potentially including federal program query fees and personnel costs for processing notices and hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the State Administrator and State Board of Elections to enroll in the federal SAVE program, verify U.S. citizenship for all voter registration applicants and current registrants, and establish a new appeals process for those flagged as non-citizens.

DNR is responsible for conserving state lands and managing natural resources. Restrictions on construction in preservation areas align with the department's conservation and land management interests.

stakeholders: Maryland voters, election judges, and state and local election officials
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for the supervision and administration of elections. The MVA is the primary issuer of government photo identification in Maryland. Because the bill requires voters to present valid photo ID (or specific secondary documentation), the MVA would likely see a notable increase in requests for state identification cards.

This office investigates and prosecutes offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process. The bill creates a new criminal offense for knowingly voting or attempting to vote under a false form of identification, which falls directly under the jurisdiction of the State Prosecutor.

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law relating to no-knock search warrants; providing that a search warrant may not authorize a law enforcement officer to enter a building, apartment, premises, place, or thing to be searched without first giving notice of the officer's authority and purpose; and providing that an officer executing a search warrant, under certain circumstances, may not enter the building, apartment, premises, place, or thing to be searched unless reasonable notice of the officer's authority and purpose is given to any individual inside.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the authority for judges to issue no-knock search warrants and prohibits law enforcement from entering a premises without first announcing their authority and purpose. It requires officers to wait at least 20 seconds for a response from occupants before entering, unless exigent circumstances exist, and removes specific reporting and training requirements related to no-knock warrants.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Maryland State and local law enforcement agencies, Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, and the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: Maryland residents, law enforcement officers, and the state's judicial system
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill's repeal of specific reporting and training requirements for no-knock warrants likely results in a minor reduction in administrative costs for state and local law enforcement agencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is the leading entity responsible for executing search warrants and performing high-risk entries; the repeal of no-knock warrants fundamentally alters their operational tactics and SWAT protocols.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly modifies the reporting requirements for search warrants and SWAT deployments that law enforcement agencies must submit to the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy annually.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The repeal of no-knock warrants significantly impacts criminal defense strategies, providing the Office of the Public Defender with new statutory grounds for filing motions to suppress evidence obtained through non-compliant warrant executions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and law enforcement on the implementation of new laws and represents the state in criminal appeals where the legality of a search or the execution of a warrant is at issue.
This independent agency investigates and prosecutes crimes related to public integrity and often utilizes search warrants; the new restrictions on no-knock entries will apply to their investigations.

MDOT oversees several modal administrations with law enforcement components, most notably the MDTA Police, who will be required to change their warrant execution procedures under this bill.

The MDTA maintains a nationally accredited police force that executes search warrants on state highways and bridges; they will be directly affected by the repeal of no-knock authority and the new 20-second notice rule.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, who are responsible for security and law enforcement on state property and must comply with the modified warrant execution standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards

The Comptroller's Office employs sworn agents who enforce tax, alcohol, and tobacco laws; these agents have the power to execute search warrants and will be subject to the bill's procedural changes.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the various law enforcement agencies impacted by this change and is responsible for broad public safety policy coordination.

Synopsis: Establishing an immunity from liability for a person who discloses information about allegations of sexually assaultive behavior if the person acts in good faith; establishing a presumption of good faith unless it is shown by a preponderance of the evidence that the person acted with actual malice or intentionally or recklessly disclosed false information; providing for the award of attorney's fees and costs in certain circumstances; etc.

bill_summary: The Stop Silencing Survivors Act establishes that a person who in good faith discloses information about allegations of sexually assaultive behavior is immune from civil liability for that disclosure. The bill creates a legal presumption that such disclosures are made in good faith unless a preponderance of evidence proves actual malice or the intentional/reckless disclosure of false information, and it requires courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to individuals who successfully defend against claims of bad faith.
stakeholders: Individuals reporting or disclosing sexual assault allegations, persons accused of sexually assaultive behavior, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. While it mandates the awarding of attorney's fees and costs in certain civil litigation, these represent transfers between private parties rather than State expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial proceedings by establishing a new immunity standard, a presumption of good faith in civil cases, and a requirement for courts to award attorney’s fees and costs in specific circumstances related to disclosures of sexually assaultive behavior.

The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund and handles liability claims against the state. The establishment of civil immunity for certain disclosures could impact the defense and outcome of liability claims involving state employees or agencies.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to all state agencies and would be responsible for interpreting this immunity and representing state entities or employees who may invoke this immunity in civil litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD was a contributor to the fiscal note and has a vested interest in the legal definitions of sexually assaultive behavior and the intersection between civil disclosures and criminal law proceedings.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a modified comparative negligence standard for civil lawsuits involving motor vehicle accidents where the plaintiff is a 'vulnerable individual' (such as a pedestrian, bicyclist, or person on a motorcycle). Under this standard, a plaintiff is not barred from recovering damages unless their own negligence was a proximate cause of the injury and was greater than the combined negligence of all defendants. Any damages awarded are reduced in proportion to the plaintiff's own degree of negligence.
stakeholders: Vulnerable individuals involved in motor vehicle accidents (pedestrians, cyclists, etc.), motor vehicle operators, the Maryland Transit Administration, and State and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may lead to a significant increase in State and local expenditures due to higher tort claim payments, settlements, and insurance premiums. Because the bill replaces the contributory negligence bar with a comparative negligence standard for vulnerable individuals, the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) may see increased payouts for claims previously barred. The Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is particularly impacted as it does not have a statutory limit on liability. Additionally, the State Treasurer’s Office and the Office of the Attorney General may require additional personnel to handle increased claim volumes and litigation, with one estimate for a claims employee starting at $86,100 in fiscal 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which pays out tort claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. The bill is expected to significantly increase SITF expenditures and requires additional staffing for the agency's Insurance Division to process increased claims.

The MTA is specifically identified as being significantly impacted because its tort liability is not capped under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. As a major operator of motor vehicles (buses and trains) that interact with vulnerable individuals, it faces a high risk of increased claim payouts and litigation costs.

The judicial branch is responsible for adjudicating the civil actions affected by this bill. The shift from contributory negligence to a comparative negligence standard for a specific class of plaintiffs represents a fundamental change in how motor vehicle negligence cases are handled in Maryland courts.

The OAG provides legal representation for the State and its agencies in civil litigation. The bill is expected to increase the volume and complexity of tort cases, requiring additional legal and administrative personnel to defend the State's interests.

As the parent agency for modal administrations like the MTA and SHA, MDOT oversees the state's transportation network and safety policies. The change in liability standards for accidents involving vulnerable road users directly impacts MDOT's operational and fiscal planning.

The MIA regulates the state's insurance industry. A change from contributory to comparative negligence for a significant portion of motor vehicle accidents will necessitate regulatory oversight of how insurance companies adjust their policies, rate-setting, and claims handling.

As the insurer of last resort for Maryland drivers, MAIF is directly impacted by changes in liability rules. The shift to comparative negligence will likely increase the number of claims for which the fund must pay damages and affect its overall fiscal stability.

MSP operates a large fleet of patrol vehicles and frequently interacts with vulnerable road users and emergency responders on highways. The agency is subject to tort claims that would now be evaluated under the new comparative negligence standard.

SHA is responsible for the design and maintenance of the state's non-toll highways where vulnerable individuals (including pedestrians and workers) are present. The agency's highway safety initiatives and its own vehicle operations are directly relevant to the bill's focus.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency. It oversees the budget execution and premium assessments for state agencies that pay into the SITF, which are expected to rise as a result of the bill's impact on tort payouts.

MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains a police force. Its operations involve significant interaction with motor vehicles and vulnerable individuals on bridges and tunnels, exposing the agency to potential tort claims under the revised negligence standard.

MVA houses the Highway Safety Office and regulates the operation of motor vehicles. The bill's specific focus on motor vehicle accidents and the definitions of vulnerable individuals is highly relevant to the agency's safety mission and regulatory scope.

DGS manages the state's vehicle fleet and provides security through the Capitol Police. The change in liability standards increases the potential fiscal impact of accidents involving state-owned vehicles operated by various departments.

The bill's definition of 'vulnerable individual' specifically includes individuals using wheelchairs and electric personal assistive mobility devices, groups for whom this department advocates and coordinates services.

The Department of Aging represents older adults, who are frequently pedestrians and thus categorized as 'vulnerable individuals' under the bill. The agency has an interest in policy changes that affect the legal recovery rights of this demographic.

The bill's definition of 'vulnerable individual' specifically includes individuals lawfully operating farm tractors or farm equipment on highways, which falls under the regulatory and support scope of the Department of Agriculture.

The definition of 'vulnerable individual' includes persons providing emergency services on a highway. MDEM coordinates such personnel, and the bill provides enhanced legal protections for these individuals in the event of a motor vehicle accident.

bill_summary: This bill implements reforms to the Maryland Parole Commission to enhance transparency and equity in the parole process. It requires the Commission to include race-disaggregated data in its annual reports and mandates that incarcerated individuals be provided with copies of the documents used in their parole suitability determinations. The bill also requires all parole hearings to be recorded and made available to the individual, prohibits the permanent denial of parole, establishes mandatory timeframes for subsequent hearings following a denial, and requires commissioners to provide specific reasoning and justifications for their decisions on the record.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, victims, the Maryland Parole Commission, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Parole Commission is an independent unit within this department. The bill directly mandates changes to the Commission's hearing procedures, reporting requirements, and record-keeping protocols.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Parole Commission and would be responsible for advising on the implementation of new transparency mandates, redaction requirements, and representing the Commission in any legal challenges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

The Maryland Parole Commission is an executive branch body that must submit its expanded annual report to the Governor. The Governor also oversees the departments responsible for implementing these reforms.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The bill requires parole data to be disaggregated by race to improve equity, which aligns with the Commission's mission to monitor and prevent discrimination in state-administered processes.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting the commissioners who serve on the Maryland Parole Commission, which is the subject of this legislation.
Parole decisions and recordings may be subject to judicial review or appeals in the state court system, making the availability and retention of hearing records relevant to judicial proceedings.

bill_summary: House Bill 468 establishes the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth and imposes a tiered gross revenues tax on digital social media services provided in Maryland. The proceeds, after administrative costs are deducted, are dedicated to the new fund to improve mental health care access for children and youth in the state.
responsible_party: Maryland Comptroller, Secretary of Health, and State Treasurer
stakeholders: Digital social media service providers with significant global and state revenue, and Maryland children and youth requiring mental health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a new revenue source by taxing digital social media services at tiered rates of 5%, 7.5%, or 10% of gross revenues derived from Maryland, depending on the provider's global gross income. Revenues are distributed to the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth after the Comptroller's administrative expenses are covered. Specific financial estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided bill text.

The Secretary of Health is specifically charged with administering the newly created Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth, which is dedicated to improving access to mental health services for youth in Maryland.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth separately and investing its money in the same manner as other State funds.

As the agency responsible for budget development and revenue estimation, DBM will oversee the inclusion of this new special fund and its tax revenues within the state's fiscal planning and budget execution.
The bill's focus on improving access to health services for children and youth aligns directly with the mission of this office to promote the well-being of Maryland's children.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the policy implementation of new taxes and special funds and is responsible for proposing the budget that will include the Fund's expenditures.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Comptroller and the Department of Health regarding the implementation of the new tax and fund, and would represent the State in potential legal challenges.
OAH may be required to adjudicate administrative disputes arising from the Department of Health's or Comptroller's decisions related to the new fund or tax regulations.
