The Maryland Aviation Administration, under MDOT, operates the BWI Fire & Rescue Department. As a state agency employing firefighters, it is directly subject to the bill's new overtime computation standards (168 hours over a 28-day period) and payroll disclosure requirements.

As the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration, MDOT oversees the personnel and budgetary operations of the airport's firefighting force, which would be directly impacted by the bill's wage and overtime changes.

The bill explicitly authorizes firefighters or their exclusive representatives to initiate grievances via collective bargaining agreements or established procedures if payroll information or wages are withheld. PERB is the central state agency responsible for overseeing public sector collective bargaining and labor disputes.

DBM is the central personnel and payroll agency for the State of Maryland. It would be responsible for updating state personnel policies and ensuring the state's payroll systems correctly calculate the specific overtime cycles for state-employed firefighters as mandated by the bill.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to state agencies employing firefighters regarding the interpretation of the new wage standards and would represent the state in any legal disputes or administrative grievances regarding 'bona fide disputes' over withheld wages.

The Comptroller's Office is responsible for paying state employees. It would be involved in the technical implementation of the bill's overtime pay requirements for state-employed firefighters and ensuring that payroll statements meet the new disclosure criteria.
The Treasurer's Office manages the distribution of state funds and coordinates with the Comptroller on the payment of state employees, including those in firefighting roles at the state level.

DNR employs personnel involved in fire protection and management on state lands. To the extent these employees are classified as firefighters under the bill, DNR would need to comply with the modified overtime and payroll reporting standards.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to include in an annual report to certain committees of the General Assembly the amount of proceeds from a certain agricultural land transfer tax that are attributable to the taxation of certain instruments of writing that transfer title to parcels of land that are entirely woodland that were distributed to the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund during the immediately preceding fiscal year; and requiring the Department to report any uncertainties regarding certain amounts.
Title: Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund - Reporting
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to provide more detailed information in its annual report concerning the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund. Specifically, the department must disclose the exact amount of agricultural land transfer tax proceeds distributed to the fund from woodland title transfers during the previous fiscal year and report any uncertainties or required actions regarding the distribution of those tax proceeds.
stakeholders: The Maryland Department of Natural Resources and the Maryland General Assembly.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the fiscal note, the Department of Natural Resources can handle the additional reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources administers the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund and is the primary agency responsible for the new reporting requirements mandated by the bill regarding tax proceeds and distribution uncertainties.

The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal tax collector and handles the remittance of agricultural land transfer tax revenues, which are the subject of the reporting requirements in the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Natural Resources as part of the executive branch and has a general interest in the administrative reporting and fiscal accountability of state agencies.

Synopsis: Prohibiting nonpublic schools that participate in State-funded education programs from refusing to provide a current or former student or the student's parent or guardian with a transcript or taking other punitive measures regarding a student's transcript request because the student owes a debt to the nonpublic school.
Title: Nonpublic Schools - Transcripts - Prohibition on Punitive Measures Related to Student Debt
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland nonpublic schools that participate in State-funded education programs from withholding a student's transcript, conditioning the issuance of a transcript on debt payment, or taking other punitive actions against a student or their parent or guardian because of outstanding debt owed to the school.
stakeholders: Current and former students of Maryland nonpublic schools, parents or guardians of those students, and nonpublic schools that participate in State-funded education programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. The bill prohibits certain debt collection practices by nonpublic schools, specifically the withholding of transcripts for unpaid debts, which may affect the debt collection efficacy of these private institutions but does not explicitly create State or local government mandates or revenue changes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing Maryland's education system and nonpublic schools that receive state funding (such as through the BOOST or textbook/technology grant programs), MSDE is responsible for ensuring that participating institutions comply with the prohibition on withholding transcripts due to student debt.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Department of Education and the General Assembly. They would be responsible for advising on the enforcement of this law and potentially investigating consumer protection issues related to schools that illegally withhold student records.

DBM is responsible for the state's fiscal planning and budget execution. It would review any fiscal impacts on the Department of Education-administered funding programs that define the scope of nonpublic schools subject to this regulation.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including those related to educational access and the administration of state-funded scholarship and grant programs for nonpublic school students.

The bill's focus on preventing punitive measures for student debt aligns with the mission of the Governor's Office for Children to reduce the impact of poverty and enhance access to educational and economic opportunities for Maryland youth.

Synopsis: Increasing from $50,000 to $100,000 the maximum amount of annual revenue a business may generate from the sale of cottage food products to be considered a cottage food business.
Title: Food Establishments - Cottage Food Businesses - Maximum Annual Revenue
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum annual revenue a business can earn from the sale of cottage food products from $50,000 to $100,000 while remaining classified as a cottage food business, which allows them to operate without a license from the Maryland Department of Health.
stakeholders: Cottage food business owners, small-scale food producers, and retail food stores.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $52,400 in FY 2027 to hire a part-time registered sanitarian to handle the projected increase in cottage food business registrations and oversight, with annual costs reaching $67,700 by FY 2031. There may be a minimal decrease in general fund revenues if businesses choose to operate as cottage food businesses instead of paying for food manufacturing licenses. Local health departments are expected to handle any increase in inspections or complaints with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary regulatory authority for cottage food businesses. The bill directly impacts MDH's workload for processing unique identification numbers, reviewing labels, and providing technical assistance, resulting in a documented need for additional staff and a potential loss of food manufacturing license fee revenue.

Cottage food products are specifically defined by their sale at farmers' markets and to retail food stores. The Department of Agriculture supports the agricultural community and promotes the marketing of local products often found in these venues.
The bill doubles the revenue ceiling for cottage food businesses, which has a meaningful impact on small business growth and economic development, a core mission of the Department of Commerce.

The fiscal note identifies a need for additional personnel (0.5 Registered Sanitarian) and general fund expenditures. As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for managing these budgetary and staffing changes.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and tax collector. The bill is expected to cause a minimal decrease in general fund revenues as businesses opt for cottage food status over licensed food manufacturing.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies implementing the bill and is responsible for proposing the state budget, which will need to incorporate the new staffing expenditures identified in the fiscal note.

The Rural Maryland Council advocates for rural interests and supports agricultural economic development. Cottage food businesses are frequently located in rural areas and contribute to local rural economies.

Synopsis: Expanding certain protections against employment discrimination to apply to temporary disabilities caused or contributed to by childbirth, menopause, or a related medical condition.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Reasonable Accommodations - Disabilities Due to Childbirth, Menopause, and Related Medical Conditions
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands employment discrimination protections by requiring employers to provide reasonable accommodations for temporary disabilities caused or contributed to by childbirth, menopause, or related medical conditions, such as lactation or vasomotor symptoms. It mandates that these conditions be treated as temporary disabilities for job-related purposes, including insurance and sick leave, and requires employers to explore various accommodation options like modified duties, altered work hours, or transfers.
stakeholders: Employees experiencing disabilities related to childbirth or menopause; Maryland private and public sector employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill requires all employers, including State and local government agencies, to provide reasonable accommodations and update employee handbooks and workplace postings, which may result in indeterminate administrative and operational expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary agency responsible for enforcing Title 20 of the State Government Article, which includes anti-discrimination laws in employment. This bill directly amends Section 20-609, expanding the definitions of temporary disabilities and reasonable accommodations that MCCR must oversee and investigate.

As the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies and benefits. This bill requires all employers, including state agencies, to provide reasonable accommodations for disabilities related to childbirth and menopause, which DBM would need to codify into state personnel regulations and training.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on the interpretation and implementation of new laws. They would likely assist the Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Budget and Management in drafting regulations and defending the state in litigation related to these expanded employment protections.

The Department of Labor enforces general workplace and labor laws. While the Commission on Civil Rights handles specific discrimination cases under Title 20, the Department of Labor manages broader workforce standards that may be impacted by new requirements for reasonable accommodations in the private sector.

The PERB oversees collective bargaining for public sector employees. Since the bill specifically mentions that reasonable accommodations, such as transfers to less strenuous positions, may be governed by collective bargaining agreements, the PERB may be involved in adjudicating disputes or unfair labor practice charges related to these new rights.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including the Commission on Civil Rights. If an employer is charged with a violation of these new accommodation requirements and the case is contested, an OAH Administrative Law Judge would likely preside over the hearing.

Synopsis: Establishing a bill of rights for unit owners of a condominium, members of a cooperative housing corporation, and lot owners of a homeowners association.
Title: Residential Owners in Common Ownership Communities - Bill of Rights
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Bill of Rights for residential owners in common ownership communities, including condominiums, cooperative housing corporations, and homeowners associations. It outlines specific rights for owners, such as the right to participate in and receive notice of meetings, vote by secret ballot, access community records, and receive due process during the enforcement of community rules. The bill also authorizes the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to investigate alleged violations and take enforcement actions.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Residential owners (condominium unit owners, cooperative members, and homeowners association lot owners) and the governing bodies of common ownership communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may result in an indeterminate increase in state expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General to handle the review and enforcement of alleged violations. There is also a potential for an increase in state revenue through the imposition of penalties. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General review alleged violations of laws governing common ownership communities and take direct enforcement actions, including court adjudication and the imposition of penalties.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of state records and specifically manages the registration and oversight of condominiums, which are one of the primary types of common ownership communities governed by this Bill of Rights.

The Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various professions; this includes the Board of Common Ownership Community Managers. The bill establishes rights regarding the conduct and training of community managers.

The bill provides for the adjudication of disputes and enforcement actions before a court, which would increase the volume of civil litigation related to common ownership communities managed by the judicial branch.

As the agency responsible for ensuring safe, secure housing and community revitalization, the establishment of a Bill of Rights for residents in common ownership communities directly aligns with their mission to improve the quality of life in Maryland neighborhoods.

The bill establishes a right to nondiscriminatory service from the staff and governing bodies of common ownership communities, which overlaps with the Commission's mandate to enforce anti-discrimination laws in housing.

While the bill mentions court adjudication, many enforcement actions by state agencies like the OAG are initially heard by Administrative Law Judges at the OAH, particularly regarding regulatory violations.

A significant portion of older adults live in common ownership communities (such as condominiums or co-ops with age restrictions). The Department advocates for the rights of older adults in these housing settings.
The bill's provisions regarding the use of community facilities and equal protection may impact residents with disabilities living within these communities.

Synopsis: Requiring each institution of higher education in the State that admits first-time undergraduate students to prominently display on its publicly accessible prospective student website a link to the U.S. Department of Education College Scorecard website and share related information in a certain manner.
Title: Institutions of Higher Education - Mandatory Disclosures for New and Prospective Students (Informed Enrollment Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland institutions of higher education that admit first-time undergraduate students to prominently display a link to the U.S. Department of Education College Scorecard on their websites and provide related information on cost, graduation rates, salary, and debt outcomes to prospective and current students.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission and Maryland institutions of higher education
stakeholders: New and prospective undergraduate students, parents and guardians, current students, academic advisors, campus career counselors, and Maryland institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Legislative Services indicates that public four-year institutions, Baltimore City Community College, and local community colleges can comply with the bill's requirements using existing resources. There is no projected impact on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Higher Education is responsible for determining if the federal College Scorecard is discontinued and notifying the legislature. The commission oversees all institutions required to provide the disclosures.
As the regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, the commission oversees the public and private institutions mandated to implement these new disclosure requirements.
The system's 12 institutions are directly required to implement the bill's provisions, including displaying the scorecard link and sharing outcome data with students.
As a state university, Morgan State is directly mandated to comply with the disclosure requirements on its website and in its recruitment materials.
As a public honors college, Saint Mary's is directly required to comply with the bill's mandates to share federal College Scorecard data with prospective and new students.
The Governor oversees the executive department and the Secretary of Higher Education, who is tasked with specific monitoring and reporting duties under the bill.
The MLDS Center collects and analyzes the student and workforce outcome data that is central to the disclosures mandated by the bill and was a source for the fiscal analysis.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the higher education institutions and the commission regarding their compliance with the new statutory disclosure requirements.
DBM serves as the principal fiscal agency overseeing the budgets of the universities and commission as they adjust operations to meet the bill's requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Education to provide a pathway for  individuals who are qualified to be child care teachers, but lack proof of necessary educational attainment, to attest to qualifying educational credentials to be a child care teacher teaching in a child care center.
Title: Child Care Centers - Teacher Qualifications - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Board of Education to establish a pathway for individuals to attest to their educational qualifications for child care teacher positions if they lack physical documentation of those credentials. It mandates that the Maryland State Department of Education develop a process for this attestation.
stakeholders: Individuals seeking employment as child care teachers, child care centers, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The Maryland State Department of Education will likely incur administrative costs to develop and implement the required attestation process for child care teacher credentials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Education to adopt regulations and the Department (MSDE) to establish a process for child care teachers to attest to their educational credentials. MSDE is the primary agency responsible for child care center licensing and oversight of early childhood education programs.

The bill identifies specific academic degrees (such as Early Childhood Education and Child Development) as qualifying credentials. The Commission is responsible for setting policies and standards for the colleges and universities that grant these degrees.

The Department of Labor oversees workforce development and the licensing of various professions. Altering the qualification pathway for child care teachers impacts the state's professional certification and labor supply strategies within the early childhood sector.

The MLDS Center tracks student and workforce data. The creation of a new attestation pathway for educational attainment will require the agency to adjust its data collection and analysis regarding teacher credentials and workforce outcomes.

The Governor's Office for Children coordinates policies to improve the well-being of children and families. Staffing standards and teacher qualifications in child care centers are critical factors in the quality and accessibility of services for Maryland children.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain electric, gas, and gas and electric companies from initiating a proceeding that may lead to a rate change unless the company provides customers with a certain notice; requiring certain electric, gas, and gas and electric companies to include a certain statement in each customer bill and automatic payment e-mail and distribute a certain annual rate report in a certain manner; requiring the Public Service Commission, in consultation with the Office of People's Counsel, to develop a certain report; etc.
Title: Investor-Owned Electric, Gas, and Gas and Electric Companies - Utility Rate Changes (Public Service Company Transparency Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill requires investor-owned electric and gas companies to provide customer notice and a 10-year rate trend report before initiating rate change proceedings. It also mandates that the Public Service Commission (PSC) and the Office of People's Counsel (OPC) develop annual rate reports and that utilities include transparency statements in customer bills.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel
stakeholders: Retail customers of investor-owned electric and gas companies and the companies themselves; municipal electric utilities and electric cooperatives are excluded.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Public Service Commission to develop, publish, and manage annual rate reports for investor-owned utilities, consult with the Office of the People’s Counsel, and oversee new transparency requirements for utility companies.

The bill explicitly requires the Office of the People's Counsel to consult with the Public Service Commission on annual rate reports and mandates that the office bring legal cases before the Commission if it determines that a report contains incorrect or misleading information.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and the Office of the People's Counsel regarding the implementation and enforcement of the bill's new regulatory requirements.

The bill's requirements for utility rate transparency and 10-year rate trend reporting provide critical data relevant to the Maryland Energy Administration's role in advising on state energy policy and coordinating long-term energy planning.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the fiscal resources of the implementing agencies; although the fiscal note indicates the bill can be implemented with existing resources, the department remains relevant as the state's principal fiscal agency.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Public Service Commission; this bill represents a significant change in transparency policy for regulated utilities under the Governor's administration.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education to ensure that each public school regularly restock dispensers in the women's restrooms at the school with menstrual hygiene products.
Title: Public Schools - Restocking Menstrual Hygiene Products - Requirement
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland county boards of education to ensure that every public school regularly restocks menstrual hygiene product dispensers in women's restrooms to ensure products are available to students at no charge.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students and local county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates that local county boards of education regularly restock menstrual hygiene products in all public school women's restrooms. While the bill text notes a previous state appropriation of $500,000 in fiscal 2023 for the initial purchase and installation of dispensers, it does not specify a new funding amount or state reimbursement for the ongoing restocking costs. Consequently, these costs will likely result in an increase in local school board expenditures. Specific dollar estimates for the restocking mandate are not provided in the bill text, and the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the source material.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of Maryland's 24 public school systems, MSDE is the primary entity tasked with implementing and enforcing education laws. The bill requires county boards to report to and potentially seek oversight from MSDE regarding the provision and restocking of menstrual hygiene products.

As a state-operated public school, the Maryland School for the Deaf is directly impacted by requirements concerning the provision of hygiene products in school restrooms and the mandate to ensure availability through regular restocking.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget, which includes mandated appropriations for school health initiatives and state reimbursements to county boards for health-related infrastructure like product dispensers.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and supervision of budget execution. This bill involves state mandates on county boards and has fiscal implications for the education budget, specifically regarding the ongoing state reimbursement mechanisms for school restroom equipment.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller's agency is responsible for paying state bills, which would include the reimbursements to county boards mandated under the Education Article for the installation of menstrual hygiene dispensers.

The Governor's Office for Children focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and the reduction of child poverty. Addressing 'period poverty'—the lack of access to menstrual products—is directly aligned with their mission to improve health services and economic opportunities for historically underinvested communities.

The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for protecting and improving public health. The provision of sanitary products in schools is a public health and hygiene matter that falls under the broader scope of health policies for residents.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the Governor's Office. They may be called upon to provide legal interpretations of the 'regular restocking' mandate to ensure compliance with state law.

The Innovation Team is tasked with piloting initiatives to address child poverty and enhance economic mobility. Improving access to essential hygiene products in schools is an evidence-based strategy to improve educational outcomes and health for students in need.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for the Maryland earned income tax credit for  individuals without qualifying children by altering the income thresholds at which the credit phases out; providing that, after the 2025 tax year, the income threshold and phase-out amounts are adjusted annually for inflation; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Earned Income Tax Credit - Individuals Without Qualifying Children - Eligibility
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the Maryland earned income tax credit for individuals without qualifying children by increasing the income threshold at which the credit begins to phase out and providing for annual cost-of-living adjustments starting after tax year 2025.
stakeholders: Low-to-moderate income Maryland residents without qualifying children and Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $101,300,000 in FY 2027, with projected annual decreases growing to $117,900,000 by FY 2031. While local revenues are not affected, Montgomery County may experience increased expenditures for its local earned income credit supplement program starting in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and the administration of tax laws. The bill directly requires the Comptroller to implement the expanded Earned Income Tax Credit formulas and calculate annual inflation-based adjustments for the income thresholds.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning. This bill is projected to decrease general fund revenues by more than $100 million annually, which has a significant impact on the state budget and revenue forecasts managed by this department.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. The significant revenue impact and the policy shift regarding poverty reduction and economic mobility are central to the Governor's executive and budgetary responsibilities.

As the chief financial agency responsible for the management and protection of state funds, the Treasurer's Office is impacted by major changes in state revenue streams and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees fiscal integrity.

The Department of Human Services assists Marylanders in economic need. The expansion of the Earned Income Tax Credit aligns with the agency's mission to provide financial support and aid to vulnerable and low-income populations.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes regarding income tax and tax credit determinations. Changes to eligibility and phase-out thresholds for the EITC may lead to new cases or appeals within its jurisdiction.

The Innovation Team is tasked with developing strategies for economic mobility. Expanding the EITC for individuals without qualifying children is a key policy mechanism for enhancing economic mobility for low-income workers.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of state tax laws and any potential litigation resulting from changes to the tax code.

Synopsis: Authorizing a landlord to impose an increased security deposit if a tenant operates or plans to operate a family child care home on the leased premises; prohibiting a landlord of certain residential rental property from prohibiting or unreasonably limiting the operation of a family child care home on the property; providing that landlords of certain residential rental property are immune from civil liability; authorizing a landlord to require a certain tenant to purchase a liability insurance policy; applying the Act prospectively; etc.
Title: Real Property - Landlord and Tenant - Family Child Care Homes
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: House Bill 543 prevents landlords of single-family rental properties from prohibiting or unreasonably restricting the operation of registered family child care homes, with specific exceptions for owner-occupied dwellings and age-restricted communities. The bill authorizes landlords to charge an increased security deposit of up to two months' rent for these tenants and requires tenants to provide 60-day notice, proof of registration, and liability insurance of up to 1000000 dollars naming the landlord as an additional insured. It also grants landlords immunity from civil liability for acts or omissions related to the tenant's operation of the child care home.
stakeholders: Landlords of single-family rental properties, tenants operating family child care homes, and families seeking home-based child care services
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill affects private financial transactions between landlords and tenants by allowing for increased security deposits (up to two months' rent) and requiring tenants to maintain liability insurance of up to 1000000 dollars. No specific state or local government revenue or expenditure mandates are identified in the bill text, though landlords who violate security deposit limits may be liable for three times the extra amount charged plus attorney's fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references Title 9.5, Subtitle 3 of the Education Article, which is administered by the Department of Education's Office of Child Care. MSDE is the primary agency responsible for registering the family child care homes discussed in the bill.

The bill establishes specific requirements for liability insurance policies relating to family child care homes, including coverage limits and additional insured status, which are regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

As the state's principal agency for housing policy and community development, the department is directly impacted by changes to landlord-tenant law and the regulation of residential rental properties.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on property and education law and handles consumer protection matters, which frequently include landlord-tenant disputes.
The bill modifies the conditions for security deposits and civil liability, which affects legal proceedings and court actions between landlords and tenants overseen by the Maryland Judicial Branch.
Expanding the availability of family child care homes on rental properties directly supports the office's mission to enhance child well-being and support family economic mobility.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy initiatives regarding child care and housing, both of which are central components of the Governor's legislative agenda addressed by this bill.
The bill amends a section of the Real Property Article that references utility assistance qualifications determined by the Department of Human Services as a condition for increased security deposits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Family child care homes are frequently small, minority-, or women-owned businesses that face unique operational barriers in residential rental markets.
The bill clarifies that it does not limit the local zoning authority of counties or municipalities, a key area of policy coordination for the Department of Planning.
The team is charged with piloting initiatives to address child poverty and enhance economic mobility, making the expansion of child care access a relevant policy area.
Increasing access to child care is a critical component of state workforce strategy, as it directly impacts the ability of parents to participate in the labor market.
The department oversees general fiscal planning and would be responsible for assessing the fiscal note or any budgetary impacts on the Department of Education related to registration oversight.

The bill creates new prohibitions against landlords refusing to lease or negotiate based on the operation of a registered child care home, which overlaps with the Commission's role in enforcing fair housing and anti-discrimination standards.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an individual from smoking, vaping, or consuming cannabis in the passenger area of a motor vehicle in which a minor is an occupant.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Cannabis Use in Motor Vehicle With Minor Occupant - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits individuals from smoking, vaping, or consuming cannabis in the passenger area of a motor vehicle if a minor is an occupant. Violators are guilty of a misdemeanor and face penalties of up to one year in prison, a fine of up to $1,000, or both.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Motor vehicle operators, passengers, and minors in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a misdemeanor penalty with a fine of up to $1,000 and possible imprisonment. While a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, the bill likely results in an indeterminate increase in State general fund revenues from fines and potentially increased expenditures related to law enforcement and court proceedings. bill_summary: This bill revises, restates, and recodifies the laws governing the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP). While primarily a technical and stylistic revision, the bill modifies eligibility requirements for certain professionals: it limits lawyer eligibility to graduates of Maryland law schools, removes certain degree requirements for specified licensed clinical counselors, and narrows teacher eligibility to those who qualify for the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance
stakeholders: Graduates of Maryland colleges and law schools, public school teachers, nurses, mental health professionals, licensed clinical counselors, and veterinary practitioners and technicians.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program are budgeted at 4,100,000 for fiscal 2027. Although the bill modifies eligibility criteria for certain professional categories, it is not expected to alter total program spending, as applicants may be placed on a waiting list if funds are exhausted. The Maryland Higher Education Commission may incur a minimal, one-time increase in general fund expenditures in fiscal 2027 for computer programming updates. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) through its Office of Student Financial Assistance. The bill recodifies the program's laws and alters eligibility criteria for various professional categories.
The bill mandates that the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) determines the 'high-need geographic areas' where clinical counselors must practice to qualify for the loan repayment program.

The bill outlines eligibility for education-related professionals, including public school teachers, nurses, and mental health professionals. It references teaching licenses issued by the Department and alternative preparation programs approved by the State Superintendent.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is impacted because the fiscal note indicates a likely increase in general fund expenditures for MHEC to update programming for eligibility changes.
The bill includes specific loan repayment provisions for veterinary practitioners and technicians; MDA is the primary state agency overseeing the agricultural and animal health community.
Graduates of Maryland's public universities are primary beneficiaries of the LARP. The bill specifically revises eligibility requirements for graduates of colleges and universities in the State.

As a state-funded institution, Morgan State's graduates are eligible participants in the loan assistance program, and the university has a vested interest in financial support for its alumni in high-need fields.
Graduates of St. Mary's College of Maryland who enter public service fields covered by the bill are eligible for the Janet L. Hoffman LARP.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MHEC and other state agencies, and would be responsible for ensuring that the code revisions and resulting regulations are legally sound.

The MLDS links student and workforce data; changes to loan repayment eligibility for graduates in specific workforce sectors relate to the system's role in analyzing student performance and workforce outcomes.

bill_summary: The Maryland Family Utility Tax Relief Act authorizes local governments, including Baltimore City, counties, and municipalities, to establish a property tax credit for homeowners who spend 25% or more of their net household income on utility services such as electricity, gas, water, and internet.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation
stakeholders: Homeowners paying significant portions of their income on utilities and local Maryland government taxing authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill permits local jurisdictions to grant property tax credits, which would lead to an indeterminate reduction in local property tax revenues if adopted. Because the implementation of the credit is optional for local governments and no formal Fiscal Note was provided in the text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new local property tax credit. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is the independent agency responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments, exemptions, and various property tax credits.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes in the state, including factual determinations and adjudications involving property tax credits and assessments.

The bill establishes a tax credit based on the percentage of income spent on utility services (electricity, gas, water, and internet). The Office of the People's Counsel is the primary advocate for the interests of residential utility consumers regarding the affordability and reliability of these services.

The bill defines eligibility based on 'household net income,' which refers to earnings after legally required withholdings. Verification of an applicant's income for this tax credit would likely require data or verification from the Comptroller, who serves as the state's chief tax collector and manager of income tax records.
The bill's tax credit is triggered by expenses for utility services, including electricity, gas, and water, all of which are industries regulated by the Public Service Commission.

The Department of Human Services administers energy assistance and aid to residents in economic need. The population targeted by this bill (households spending over 25% of income on utilities) overlaps significantly with the demographic served by the department's Office of Home Energy Programs.

bill_summary: This bill creates a predetermination review process for individuals with criminal records to determine if they would be disqualified from receiving an occupational license before they formally apply. It applies to several state departments and generally prohibits them from denying a license solely based on a conviction if seven years have passed since the sentence was completed, excluding crimes of violence or offenses requiring sex offender registration. The bill also allows agencies to charge a fee of up to $100 for the review, with a required waiver for low-income applicants.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture, Maryland Department of the Environment, Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Department of Human Services, and Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Individuals with criminal records seeking occupational licenses or certificates and the state agencies responsible for professional licensing
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has an indeterminate fiscal impact on state revenue and expenditures. Departments are authorized to charge a predetermination review fee of up to $100, which must be waived for individuals with income at or below 300% of the federal poverty level. While departments are directed to use existing resources for the reviews, the bill requires them to report on the actual costs and number of requests by October 1, 2028. No specific total fiscal estimate is provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the District Court of Maryland is responsible for determining whether an individual's income is at or below 300% of the federal poverty level for the purpose of waiving the criminal history review fee.

The Department of Agriculture is explicitly named as one of the departments required to establish a predetermination review process for occupational licenses and to submit a report on its implementation to the General Assembly by October 1, 2028.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will oversee the budgetary implications of the new predetermination review process, including the collection of review fees and the utilization of existing resources for implementation.

The Maryland Department of Labor is explicitly named as one of the primary departments required to implement the predetermination review process for occupational licenses and must report on its costs and implementation progress.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes DPSCS from the definition of 'department' subject to certain prohibitions regarding licensing based on criminal convictions, effectively exempting its units from these specific requirements.
The Department of the Environment is explicitly named as one of the departments mandated to implement the predetermination review process and report on its implementation to the legislature.

The Maryland Department of Health is explicitly named as one of the departments required to establish a predetermination review process and submit a report on its implementation to the Senate Finance and House Economic Matters committees.

The Department of Human Services is explicitly named as one of the departments required to implement the predetermination review process for occupational licenses and report on implementation metrics.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates state policy regarding criminal justice and the reintegration of ex-offenders; this bill directly impacts barriers to employment for individuals with criminal records.

The bill involves the review of criminal history records for licensing; as the central repository for such records in Maryland, MSP may experience changes in the volume of record requests for predetermination reviews.
The OAG will provide legal guidance to the affected departments regarding the interpretation of the new predetermination requirements and the legally binding nature of the departments' decisions.

Synopsis: Repealing the restriction on the number of wine festival licenses that the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County may issue annually.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the restriction that limits the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners to issuing only one wine festival license per year, thereby allowing the Board to issue multiple wine festival licenses and designate multiple weekends for wine festivals annually.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George’s County
stakeholders: Retail license holders, Class 3 and Class 4 winery license holders, the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners, and residents of Prince George’s County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in an indeterminate increase in local revenue for Prince George's County through the collection of additional wine festival license fees. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the bill does not set the fee amount (the Board of License Commissioners is empowered to do so) and the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and regulates the alcohol industry. This bill expands the number of wine festival licenses issued in Prince George's County, which impacts state revenue collection from alcohol taxes and the broader regulatory oversight of alcohol sales.

The bill explicitly states that the primary focus of the wine festivals must be the promotion of Maryland wine. This aligns with the Department of Agriculture's mission to promote the economic viability of farming and marketing local agricultural products.

The Department of Commerce oversees tourism and economic development. Repealing the cap on wine festival licenses allows for more events, which can stimulate local economies and enhance the state's competitive position as a destination for the wine industry.

As the agency responsible for driving Maryland's tourism economy, the Office of Tourism Development is impacted by legislation that facilitates cultural and recreational events like wine festivals, which serve as travel attractions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies. They may be required to interpret or defend the statutory changes to the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and implementation of state laws. Additionally, the Governor often appoints members to the local liquor boards that implement these licenses.

DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and fiscal planning. While the impact of this specific bill may be small, the increase in licenses and associated economic activity impacts state revenue projections.

bill_summary: This bill makes permanent the higher distribution levels of highway user revenues to Baltimore City, counties, and municipalities that were previously scheduled to decrease in fiscal year 2028. By altering the statutory formula, it ensures that local governments continue to receive capital transportation grants at the fiscal year 2026 and 2027 rates indefinitely.
stakeholders: Baltimore City, Maryland counties, and municipalities
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, while overall Transportation Trust Fund expenditures are not affected, the bill requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to redirect capital funding from its own programs to local governments. Between fiscal 2028 and 2031, an estimated $401.1 million in total will be redirected, with annual local revenue increases of $96.3 million in FY 2028, $98.8 million in FY 2029, $101.6 million in FY 2030, and $104.4 million in FY 2031.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works, which includes the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees significant state expenditures and fiscal integrity. This bill involves a substantial redirection of funds within the Transportation Trust Fund and Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, affecting state capital programs and fiscal planning.

The Comptroller is responsible for collecting the revenues that populate the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, including motor fuel taxes and vehicle titling taxes. The bill alters the distribution formula for these specific state revenues.

DBM is the principal agency for state budget development and long-term fiscal planning. The bill requires a significant, permanent shift in state funding priorities by redirecting over $400 million in capital grants to local governments over a four-year period.

MDOT is the primary agency impacted as it manages the Transportation Trust Fund and the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account. The bill directly alters the statutory formula MDOT uses to distribute highway user revenues to local governments and will require MDOT to redirect funds from state-level projects to local capital grants.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and MDOT, and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget. This bill dictates a permanent change in how a major portion of state transportation revenue is allocated.

The Treasurer's Office is the chief financial agency responsible for managing state funds, including the Transportation Trust Fund. It also manages state debt and serves on the Board of Public Works, which monitors the fiscal impact of such revenue shifts.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the sales and use tax exemption for certain personal property used in qualified data centers. It also repeals the authority of local governing bodies of counties or municipal corporations to reduce or eliminate the property tax assessment for personal property used in qualified data centers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Owners and operators of data centers in Maryland, the Maryland Department of Commerce, the Comptroller of Maryland, and Maryland county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The repeal of these tax exemptions will likely lead to an increase in State sales and use tax revenue and may increase local property tax revenues for jurisdictions that have previously utilized the authorized assessment reductions. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is Maryland's chief tax collector and is specifically responsible for issuing certificates of eligibility for the sales and use tax exemption and recapturing unpaid taxes if an exemption is revoked. Repealing this exemption directly impacts the agency's revenue collection and administrative operations.

The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for certifying data centers as 'qualified' and maintaining records of their eligibility. This bill repeals the program they currently administer, removing their certification and oversight responsibilities for this tax incentive.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. Repealing significant tax exemptions for sales and use tax and personal property tax will have a notable fiscal impact on state revenue projections and the annual budget.

As a quasi-governmental organization tasked with business attraction and retention, MEDCO is impacted by the removal of tax incentives designed to support the growth of data centers, an industry critical to Maryland's economic infrastructure.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller and the Department of Commerce. They would provide guidance on the statutory repeal and assist in legal matters related to tax recapture or disputes arising from the change in law.

The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from final decisions of state taxing authorities. The repeal of exemptions and potential recapture of taxes could lead to litigation and appeals within the court's jurisdiction.

This agency handles appeals regarding property tax assessments and exemptions. The bill repeals the authority of local governments to reduce assessments for qualified data centers, which may result in appeals to this board.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget. The repeal of these exemptions represents a shift in economic development policy and impacts the state's fiscal outlook.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to provide annual funding for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program starting in fiscal year 2028. responsible_party: Maryland Governor and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Child care providers, staff, and administrators seeking professional credentials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a permanent annual funding mandate for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program starting in fiscal year 2028. The mandated appropriation must be at least equal to the fiscal year 2024 level, which, based on prior statutory growth requirements from a 2021 base of $4,000,000, is calculated at $5,324,000.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Child Care Credential Program is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). This bill mandates specific annual funding levels for a program they oversee and implement.

As the agency responsible for developing and supervising the state's budget, DBM must ensure the mandated appropriations for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program are included in the annual budget proposals starting in FY 2028.

The bill explicitly requires the Governor to appropriate funds for the program. The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget including these mandated amounts.

This office focuses on child well-being and reducing child poverty. Extending funding for child care credentials improves the quality of early childhood services, which aligns with their mission of supporting underinvested communities and enhancing education access.

bill_summary: The Maintenance of Effort Modernization Act modifies the calculation for the minimum funding level that Maryland counties must provide to local school systems. It requires the per-pupil local appropriation for public schools to be increased annually by an inflation adjustment, which is defined as the lesser of the increase in the implicit price deflator for State and local government expenditures, the Consumer Price Index for the Washington Metropolitan Area, or 5%.
responsible_party: Maryland county governing bodies, including county councils, boards of county commissioners, and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore.
stakeholders: Maryland county governments, local boards of education, and public school students.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a local spending increase by requiring that the annual per-pupil maintenance of effort (MOE) appropriation be adjusted for inflation (capped at 5%). This results in a mandated increase in local expenditures for elementary and secondary education. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note were not provided in the bill text, but the mandate explicitly requires higher local funding levels based on inflationary indices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing public education funding and ensuring that the 24 local school systems comply with state mandates, including the Maintenance of Effort (MOE) requirements altered by this bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget; changes to school funding formulas significantly impact state education policy and fiscal priorities.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for long-term fiscal planning and estimating revenues; changes to local education funding mandates affect the overall fiscal landscape of the state.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly regarding the interpretation and enforcement of state laws, including changes to the Education Article.

The OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of state agencies and local school systems, ensuring that funding is appropriated and managed according to statutory requirements like the Maintenance of Effort.

The bill explicitly references the 'amount of the expenditure authorized for debt service and capital outlay' as an exception in the school funding calculation, which falls under the purview of the IAC.
The agency's mission to reduce child poverty and improve access to education is directly impacted by changes in the adequacy and calculation of local education funding.

bill_summary: This bill establishes specific criminal penalties for harassing, interfering with, injuring, or killing an emergency response animal, which includes law enforcement dogs and horses as well as search and rescue dogs. stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, search and rescue organizations, handlers of emergency response animals, and individuals subject to criminal prosecution for prohibited actions against such animals
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes new misdemeanor tiers with fines ranging from $5,000 to $15,000 and imprisonment terms from 1 to 5 years. This will likely result in an indeterminate increase in state and local revenue from criminal fines and an indeterminate increase in state and local expenditures related to incarceration costs. Specific aggregate dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police utilizes K9 units and other emergency response animals extensively. They are directly responsible for enforcing the criminal laws outlined in the bill and protecting their own service animals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department utilizes K9 units for drug and contraband detection and facility security. The bill's provisions regarding the harassment, injury, or killing of emergency response animals directly impact their operations and personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor classifications and penalty structures for offenses against emergency response animals. The Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged under these new criminal provisions.

MDOT oversees the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) and the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA), both of which employ police forces that use law enforcement animals (K9s) for security at toll facilities, airports, and on public transit systems.

The Natural Resources Police use K9 units for conservation law enforcement and search and rescue operations in state parks and waterways. These animals fall under the bill's expanded definition of emergency response animals.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state, providing legal counsel to state agencies on the implementation of new laws and representing the state in criminal appeals resulting from convictions under the revised statutes.

The bill alters criminal statutes and sentencing guidelines for offenses against emergency response animals, which directly impacts the workload and administrative processes of the Maryland Judicial Branch.

The bill's definition of 'emergency response animal' includes search and rescue dogs engaged in efforts directed by a state agency. MDEM is the principal agency for coordinating such emergency responses and disaster recovery operations.
The Maryland Capitol Police, which is housed within DGS, utilizes K9 units for security at state-owned facilities. The protections afforded by this bill would apply to their service animals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises the Governor on public safety and criminal justice strategies. This bill modifies criminal law and penalties, which falls under their policy development and coordination mandate.
DJS manages secure residential facilities where law enforcement units or specialized K9 services may be utilized for security, making the bill's protections relevant to their facility management.
Member institutions within USM maintain their own campus police departments, many of which use K9 units for explosives detection, narcotics enforcement, and general security.
As a state agency with its own police force, Morgan State University may utilize law enforcement animals that would be protected under the provisions of this bill.
As an independent state college with its own security and policing requirements, the bill is relevant to any law enforcement animals used to secure its campus.

bill_summary: The Pet Cremation and Burial Services Consumer Protection Act establishes regulations for businesses providing pet cremation and burial services. Section 5-7A-03(A)(3) of the bill explicitly requires registrants or permit holders to distribute written descriptions of their pet cremation services to the Department of Agriculture.

As the agency responsible for adjudicating contested cases for executive branch agencies, the OAH would handle appeals or hearings resulting from regulatory enforcement actions taken by the Department of Labor regarding pet cremation and burial services.

The bill establishes a misdemeanor penalty including a fine not exceeding $5,000, which could lead to an indeterminate increase in state revenue. There may also be an indeterminate increase in state and local expenditures associated with judicial and correctional resources for processing and punishing new criminal cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for supporting the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC would handle the administrative and operational impacts of processing new misdemeanor cases resulting from violations of this criminal statute.

MSDE oversees Maryland's public education system, including secondary schools (grades 6-12) mentioned in the bill. They would likely provide guidance to local school systems regarding the protection of students' personal identifying information and images.

DJS operates educational programs and facilities for youth in the juvenile justice system, many of whom fall within the grades 6-12 (secondary education) definition, making them responsible for ensuring compliance with student data protections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises on criminal justice strategies and manages funds for public safety; creating a new misdemeanor for distributing student information falls within its policy development and crime reduction purview.
The Commission is the regulatory and coordinating board for all postsecondary institutions in the state, which are explicitly covered under the bill's prohibitions and requirements.

As an independent unit within MSDE focused on safe and supportive learning environments, this agency would be concerned with the safety implications of 'doxing' or the malicious distribution of student identifying information.

The MLDSC is the state's central repository for student data; while it operates under statutory authority, changes to the criminal law regarding the distribution of student PII are directly relevant to its core data management functions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal misdemeanor, and the OPD would be responsible for providing legal representation to indigent individuals charged with violating this new section of the Criminal Law Article.

As a state-operated educational institution for students from birth through age 21 (including secondary and postsecondary students), the MSD must ensure its staff and students comply with and are protected by these new regulations.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the MSP would be responsible for investigating reports of intentional or reckless distribution of student information intended to cause harm.
As a state-governed postsecondary institution, Morgan State's students and employees are directly affected by the bill's prohibitions and exemptions regarding the distribution of student information.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to state-run secondary and postsecondary institutions regarding compliance with the new law and represent the state in any associated appeals.
As a state-governed public honors college (postsecondary institution), it is directly impacted by the regulations regarding the distribution of its students' personal identifying information.
The USM governs twelve institutions of postsecondary education, all of which must implement and adhere to the bill's restrictions and exemptions concerning student data distribution.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a single registration plate to all classes of vehicles; providing for the method of attachment of the registration plate to the rear of certain vehicles; and requiring the publisher of the Annotated Code of Maryland to make certain corrections.
Title: Motor Vehicle Laws - Registration Plates - Single Registration Plate
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a single registration plate for all classes of vehicles, rather than two plates for most vehicles. It specifies that the plate must be attached to the front of Class F (tractor) vehicles and to the rear of all other vehicles. Additionally, it requires the publisher of the Annotated Code of Maryland to correct obsolete references and mandates that any resulting savings in expenditures be retained in the Transportation Trust Fund.
stakeholders: Maryland vehicle owners, the Motor Vehicle Administration, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a reduction of expenditures for the Motor Vehicle Administration due to the manufacturing and issuance of one plate instead of two. The bill requires these savings to be retained in the Transportation Trust Fund. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT oversees vehicle registration and the Transportation Trust Fund, which is explicitly mentioned as the recipient of any expenditure savings generated by the transition to a single registration plate.

The MVA is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirement to issue a single registration plate instead of two, managing the registration process, and regulating plate dimensions and attachments.

The bill assigns a specific duty to police officers to report violations of the new registration plate requirements to the MVA and impacts the agency's highway patrol and motor vehicle law enforcement functions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This department oversees the state's correctional and rehabilitation programs; the reduction in the number of required registration plates from two to one has a notable fiscal and operational impact on Maryland Correctional Enterprises, which manufactures the state's license plates.

The MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains its own police force; the switch to single registration plates significantly impacts toll collection efficiency (License Plate Reader technology) and the enforcement of motor vehicle laws on toll roads and bridges.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning, which includes managing the expenditure reductions in the Transportation Trust Fund mandated by the bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the MVA and MDOT and would be responsible for reviewing the regulatory changes and legal implications of transitioning to a single registration plate system.

Synopsis: Adding candidates for State Senator and member of the House of Delegates to the candidates authorized to receive public contributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund; establishing qualifications that a candidate for State Senator or member of the House of Delegates must meet to qualify as an eligible candidate to receive public contributions from the Fund; etc.
Title: Public Financing Act - State Senate and House of Delegates Candidates
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Public Financing Act to include candidates running for the State Senate and House of Delegates. It allows these legislative candidates to receive public matching funds from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund if they meet specific requirements, such as collecting a minimum number of small-dollar private contributions. The bill also establishes matching ratios and sets maximum limits on the total public contributions a candidate can receive for both primary and general elections.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Candidates for the Maryland State Senate and House of Delegates, Maryland voters, and the State Board of Elections
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase significantly to provide public matching funds for legislative candidates and to cover administrative costs. The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation in the annual budget if the Fair Campaign Financing Fund balance is insufficient to provide full contributions for 47 State Senate and 141 House of Delegates candidates in both primary and general elections. While a formal fiscal note is absent, the bill text specifies maximum public contribution limits of $125,000 for Senate candidates and $75,000 for House candidates per election.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections (SBE) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Public Financing Act. This bill significantly expands its workload and regulatory oversight by adding candidates for the State Senate and House of Delegates to the public financing program. The SBE must certify candidates, determine fund sufficiency, authorize all distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund, and adopt comprehensive implementation regulations.

The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller as the administrator of the Fair Campaign Financing Fund. The Comptroller is responsible for managing the fund's assets, investing them, collecting various revenues (including tax checkoffs and fines), and executing prompt distributions to eligible legislative candidates upon authorization by the State Board of Elections.

The bill mandates that the Governor must include a specific appropriation in the annual budget bill if the State Board of Elections determines that the balance of the Fair Campaign Financing Fund is insufficient to provide full contributions to the mandated number of gubernatorial and legislative candidates.

As the principal agency for budget development and execution, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) would be responsible for facilitating the mandatory appropriations to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund required by the bill when the fund's balance is insufficient.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections. The OAG would be involved in advising on the implementation of these new statutory requirements and representing the State in any legal challenges related to the expanded public financing program.

Synopsis: Authorizing the County Commissioners of Queen Anne's County to use revenue from development impact fees to finance the capital costs related to the replacement of public school facilities.

Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.
