bill_summary: This bill establishes a licensing and regulatory system for anesthesiologist assistants under the Maryland State Board of Physicians, defining their scope of practice, supervision requirements, and qualifications for licensure.
stakeholders: Anesthesiologist assistants, licensed anesthesiologists, the State Board of Physicians, and Maryland healthcare patients.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Physicians will collect licensure and renewal fees to cover the direct and indirect costs of the new regulatory program, resulting in an increase in special fund revenues and expenditures. Fines collected from disciplinary actions will be deposited into the State's General Fund. Specific dollar estimates were not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new licensing and regulatory category for anesthesiologist assistants under the State Board of Physicians, which is a constituent unit of the Maryland Department of Health. The department will be responsible for overseeing the implementation and enforcement of the new subtitle.

The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Physicians to pay all license fees collected to the Comptroller, who is then responsible for distributing those fees back to the Board to fund the program.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Board of Physicians and has specific responsibilities under this bill to file certified docket entries with the Board and certify convictions for the purpose of mandatory license suspension or revocation.

The bill establishes disciplinary procedures and grounds for license denial, suspension, or revocation, which typically involve contested cases heard by Administrative Law Judges from the Office of Administrative Hearings.

As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM will be involved in the fiscal oversight of the new licensing program, including the potential creation of new state personnel positions within the Board of Physicians to manage the increased workload.
The bill requires applicants for licensure to undergo a criminal history records check, which is typically facilitated or processed through the Maryland State Police or its Central Repository.

The bill authorizes anesthesiologist assistants to order controlled substances under certain conditions. As the agency that enforces the state's Controlled Dangerous Substance Act and issues CDS permits, OCSA may need to adapt its registration and inspection protocols to include this new class of medical professionals.

The bill provides for direct judicial review and appeals of final decisions made by the Board of Physicians or disciplinary panels, which impacts the workload and procedures of the state court system managed by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the placement of children in unlicensed settings (such as hotels, motels, or office buildings) under Maryland's out-of-home placement program. It establishes a Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and a Rapid Response Placement Team within the Governor’s Office for Children to coordinate and expedite placements for children and pediatric hospital overstay patients. Additionally, it creates two councils to analyze system data, coordinate care between agencies, and recommend improvements to the state's system of care for children and families.
stakeholders: Children and youth under age 22 in out-of-home placements or hospitals, their families, foster parents, local departments of social services, hospitals, and behavioral health service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill authorizes the transfer of existing funds and positions from the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays to the Governor's Office for Children to support new oversight bodies and the Placement Manager role. Panel and council members are eligible for travel reimbursement, and the Placement Manager receives a salary. Specific dollar estimates for the total fiscal impact are unavailable as no formal fiscal note was provided with the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor has the authority to appoint the Placement Manager and various members of the newly created councils and panels, as well as the power to transfer positions and funds between entities as specified in the bill.

This agency is responsible for overseeing the state's budget and personnel. The bill authorizes the transfer of funds and positions and mandates that the Placement Manager's compensation be in accordance with the state budget.
The Secretary of Disabilities is a designated member of the Interagency Council on Children, Youth, and Families established by the bill.
The State Superintendent of Schools is a designated member of the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel and the Interagency Council on Children, Youth, and Families.

The Secretary of Health is a member of multiple councils established by the bill. Additionally, the department is responsible for established pediatric hospital overstay coordinators whose duties are altered by this legislation.

The bill directly impacts the Social Services Administration (part of DHS) by prohibiting unlicensed placements in its out-of-home program. The Secretary is also a member of the newly established Review Panel and Interagency Council.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services is a member of the Interagency Council, and the bill allows the Review Panel to refer children to DJS-operated or contracted residential programs.

The GOC is the primary implementing agency. It houses the new Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, the Placement Manager position, and the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care, and provides staff support for these entities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates several new bodies falling under this category, including the Child and Youth Placement Review Panel, the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care, and the Interagency Council on Children, Youth, and Families.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission is a mandated member of the Interagency Council on Children, Youth, and Families.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a designated member of the Interagency Council on Children, Youth, and Families.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender is a designated member of both the Advisory Council on Maryland's System of Care and the Interagency Council on Children, Youth, and Families.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to establish and implement a pilot program for ecosystem value-oriented forest management plans to provide additional incentives for enrolling in and extending commitments to forest conservation and management; establishing the Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to finance the pilot program; and requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $10,000,000 to the Fund in fiscal year 2028.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Natural Resources to establish a pilot program for ecosystem value-oriented forest management plans to provide financial incentives for private landowners to conserve and manage forest land. It establishes the Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to support the program, funded by a mandated $10 million appropriation in fiscal year 2028, potential impact fees from projects causing forest loss, and other sources.
stakeholders: Private forest landowners, Maryland Forestry Foundation, forest district conservancy boards, and Maryland residents benefiting from forest ecosystem services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a $10,000,000 State appropriation to the Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund in fiscal year 2028. It also authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to generate revenue through 'ecosystem value impact fees' assessed against projects resulting in the loss of forest ecological value, specifically mentioning new data centers and utility line construction. The fund will be used to compensate landowners for adopting 20-year management plans and for program administration, with $2,000,000 of the initial appropriation designated for program development and investment management.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Natural Resources as the primary agency responsible for establishing the ecosystem value-oriented forest management pilot program, developing the methodology for determining ecological value, and administering the Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund.
The bill requires the Governor to include a $10,000,000 appropriation in the fiscal year 2028 budget and aligns with broader state climate and conservation goals overseen by the Executive Department.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the mandated $10,000,000 budget appropriation in fiscal year 2028 and overseeing the execution of the new Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund.

The bill specifically references MDE's 2023 Maryland's Climate Pollution Reduction Plan and requires DNR to coordinate with relevant state agencies on policies to generate impact fee revenues related to carbon sequestration and climate mitigation.
The Treasurer is responsible for holding the Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund separately and investing its assets jointly with a conservation financing management entity.
The bill directs the pursuit of impact fees against new data centers and utility line construction, sectors regulated by the Public Service Commission.
The initiative coordinates sustainable development and environmental protection efforts across the various agencies (DNR, MDE, MDP) involved in the bill's forest conservation goals.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Forest Ecosystem Value Incentives Fund and managing the accrual of interest earnings to the Fund.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to DNR regarding the development of the new impact fee framework, regulatory adjustments, and any legal settlements directed to the Fund.
The bill proposes impact fees on data centers, which could affect the Department's efforts to attract and retain these businesses in Maryland.
The Department of Planning coordinates land use and sustainable growth policies that intersect with the bill's forest preservation and conservation agreement goals.
Maryland's forest lands are often owned by agricultural landholders, and the bill intersects with existing land conservation programs like the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation.
The bill proposes additional State property tax benefits for landowners adopting the new forest management plans, which may lead to appeals or disputes over tax credits handled by this board.
The Tax Court would have jurisdiction over disputes regarding the property tax benefits and impact fees established or enhanced by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the Maryland Climate Change Commission and the role of various task forces in historical and future forest policy development.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC) to mandate that electric companies develop resource adequacy plans if there is insufficient electricity supply or a 'price stability event' occurs. It authorizes investor-owned utilities to construct, own, or lease generating and transmission facilities and recover all prudently incurred costs, plus a reasonable return, from ratepayers via a nonbypassable surcharge. The bill also updates the selection criteria and pricing schedules for front-of-the-meter energy storage projects.
stakeholders: Investor-owned electric companies, Maryland electricity ratepayers, renewable energy resource developers, and PJM Interconnection.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. The bill establishes a cost-recovery mechanism allowing investor-owned electric companies to recoup costs for constructing, acquiring, and operating generating facilities through a nonbypassable surcharge on customer bills. This is expected to increase electricity costs for residential and business ratepayers. The Public Service Commission is responsible for overseeing these plans and approving the associated cost recovery and rates of return.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Public Service Commission to require electric companies to develop resource adequacy plans, oversee the construction and acquisition of generating facilities by investor-owned utilities, approve cost recovery surcharges, and propose new regulations for credit rating assessments.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission. This bill impacts utility rates, reliability, and cost recovery mechanisms, all of which fall under the office's advocacy mandate.

The Maryland Energy Administration advises on energy policy and manages clean energy initiatives. The bill's focus on resource adequacy, renewable energy generation, and front-of-the-meter energy storage aligns with the agency's planning and policy coordination roles.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal counsel for the Public Service Commission and other state agencies. It would be responsible for representing the state in appeals or litigation arising from the new regulatory mandates and cost recovery orders.

The bill, titled the Affordable Energy Act, represents a significant executive-level policy shift in energy regulation, utility ownership of generation, and grid reliability, requiring coordination across the executive branch.

The construction of new generating facilities and large capacity energy resources authorized by the bill would require environmental permits and compliance with state air, land, and water quality laws managed by this department.

Through its Power Plant Research Program, the Department of Natural Resources provides technical and environmental evaluations for the siting and operation of power plants and energy infrastructure in Maryland.

The bill explicitly refers to the PJM capacity market and regional transmission organizations. Maryland's participation and coordination with PJM Interconnection, LLC is a key component of its interstate energy policy.
Energy price stability and grid reliability are critical factors for business retention and economic competitiveness, which are the primary missions of the Department of Commerce.

The bill promotes the adoption of front-of-the-meter transmission energy storage and clean energy generation, which supports the center's mission as the state's green bank to advance clean energy technologies.

The Department of Planning oversees sustainable growth and land use. The development of new generating and transmission facilities requires coordination regarding land use and infrastructure planning.

As a multi-agency initiative focused on sustainable development and resource conservation, the bill's emphasis on renewable energy resources and utility-scale planning aligns with its core planning visions.

The agency ensures that state resources are managed effectively to deliver results aligned with the Governor's priorities, such as the energy affordability and reliability goals outlined in this bill.

bill_summary: This bill requires commercial telecommunications service providers to automatically issue a credit to customers who experience a 'material service outage,' which is defined as a disruption of wireless voice, text, or data service lasting at least three consecutive hours. The credit must be at least equivalent to one full day of the customer's monthly service charge and must be applied automatically within two billing cycles. Violations of these requirements are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Commercial telecommunications service providers and retail consumers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal and Policy Note is not included in the provided text, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The bill creates a mandate for private telecommunications providers to issue automatic credits for service outages, which results in indeterminate costs for those providers and potential bill reductions (savings) for customers, including state and local government agencies. Enforcement of the bill's provisions by the Office of the Attorney General may lead to indeterminate increases in state expenditures for oversight and indeterminate increases in state revenue from civil penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines violations of the Automatic Telecommunications Service Outage Credit Act as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The Office of the Attorney General is the primary agency responsible for enforcing consumer protection laws and investigating such violations.

The Public Service Commission is the state's regulatory body for public utilities, including telecommunications service providers. This bill imposes new operational and billing requirements on these providers regarding service outages and customer credits.

The Office of the People's Counsel is the independent state agency that advocates for residential utility consumers. This legislation directly impacts the rights and financial compensation of telecommunications consumers during service disruptions.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases and regulatory enforcement actions for state agencies. Any enforcement actions taken by the Attorney General or other state entities against telecommunications providers under this Act would likely be heard by Administrative Law Judges at this agency.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits health insurance carriers from denying coverage for emergency room services solely because the patient's condition did not ultimately meet the definition of an emergency medical condition, provided a prudent layperson would have sought emergency care. It also requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to report on adverse decisions regarding post-acute care and directs the Maryland Health Care Commission and the Health Services Cost Review Commission to conduct studies on hospital and post-acute bed capacity and options to facilitate clinically appropriate care transitions.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner, Maryland Health Care Commission, and Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, Maryland residents with health insurance, hospitals, and post-acute care facilities such as skilled nursing and rehabilitation centers.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not included in the provided text. However, the bill creates new administrative responsibilities for the Maryland Health Care Commission and the Health Services Cost Review Commission to conduct bed capacity and care transition studies. It also requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to include additional data in its annual summary report. The prohibition on denying certain emergency room claims may impact the expenditures and premiums of private health insurance carriers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct two major studies: one to quantify hospital and post-acute bed capacity and another to analyze options for facilitating clinically appropriate transitions from acute to post-acute care.

The bill explicitly requires the Health Services Cost Review Commission to work in conjunction with the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct the studies on bed capacity and care transitions and to make recommendations on auditing processes.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (who leads the MIA) is tasked with enforcing the new prohibitions on denying emergency room coverage and is required to include specific new data regarding adverse decisions and grievances for post-acute services in their annual summary report.

As the primary agency for health policy and regulation of healthcare facilities, MDH oversees the hospitals and post-acute settings targeted by the studies. Additionally, the insurance reporting requirements involve coordination with the Secretary of Health.

The bill mandates changes to coverage for emergency room services for all policies and contracts in the state, which includes those offered on the individual and small business marketplace managed by the Exchange.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the MDH, MIA, and the commissions in implementing the new statutory requirements and ensuring compliance with the 'prudent layperson' standard for emergency room coverage.
The Governor's Office receives the mandated reports and studies on bed capacity and transitions and oversees the agencies responsible for implementing these health care policy shifts.

Post-acute care settings, such as skilled nursing facilities, are central to the mission of the Department of Aging. The studies on bed capacity and transitions from hospitals to these settings directly impact the quality of life for Maryland's older adults.

The study on transitions to post-acute care settings, including inpatient rehabilitation facilities, is relevant to the department's focus on coordinating services and community living for residents with disabilities.
The Department of Budget and Management would be involved in the fiscal impact of the mandated studies and the reporting requirements imposed on the state's health and insurance agencies.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits any person or business operating in Maryland from knowingly manufacturing, selling, distributing, dispensing, or supplying drugs or medical devices, or compounding drugs, if they know or should reasonably know that the items are intended for use in carrying out a death sentence.
stakeholders: Pharmaceutical manufacturers, medical device suppliers, pharmacies, and wholesale distributors operating within the State of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates for state or local fiscal impact are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill creates a new prohibition on certain commercial activities, which may have an indeterminate impact on business tax revenue or regulatory enforcement costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Health - General Article, the body of law primarily administered by the Maryland Department of Health. The department oversees public health policy and the regulation of health care professionals and facilities.

A division of the Department of Health, OCSA is specifically responsible for regulating the prescribing and dispensing of drugs in Maryland. This bill directly prohibits specific pharmaceutical and dispensing activities related to drugs intended for death sentences.
The OAG is the state's chief legal officer and would be responsible for providing legal counsel to agencies on this new law and enforcing the prohibition against persons doing business in the state.

The bill regulates and restricts specific activities of persons doing business in the state, including manufacturers and distributors. As the state's economic development agency, Commerce is impacted by new restrictions on business operations.
The Department of Labor regulates various professions and business practices in the state; this prohibition establishes a new standard of conduct for businesses within its regulatory scope.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive agencies, such as the Department of Health, that will be tasked with monitoring compliance with this law.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Budget and Management to include a comprehensive obesity management and treatment program in the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. It also mandates that private health insurance carriers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations provide coverage for these programs to individuals diagnosed with obesity, diabetes, or related conditions. Covered services must include behavioral interventions, CDC-approved lifestyle change sessions, FDA-approved medications for weight management, and metabolic or bariatric surgery.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State employees and retirees, individuals diagnosed with obesity, diabetes, or obesity-related conditions, and Maryland health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The formal Fiscal and Policy Note is not included in the provided text; therefore, specific dollar estimates are unavailable. However, the bill establishes a new spending mandate for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and private health insurance carriers by requiring coverage for obesity-related medications and bariatric surgery. The bill notes that the program aims to achieve long-term savings that exceed costs, but short-term expenditures for the State and insurance premiums for individuals are likely to increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Budget and Management is explicitly mandated to implement the obesity treatment and management program within the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and oversee its requirements.
The bill creates new insurance mandates for obesity treatment coverage that the MIA must regulate and enforce for all insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs operating in the state.
The Secretary of Health is a mandated consultant for the development of the obesity program, which must also promote the goals of the Department's State Health Improvement Process.

As the administrator of the state's health insurance marketplace, the Exchange must ensure that private health plans sold to Maryland residents comply with the new mandated obesity treatment coverage.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies implementing this bill and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which will be impacted by the costs of the new state employee health benefits.
The Commission's mission to improve health care access and plan for the state's health system needs is directly relevant to mandated coverage for chronic conditions like obesity and diabetes.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the implementing departments and ensures that the new regulations for insurance coverage and state personnel benefits comply with state and federal law.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the holder of a promissory note, other instrument, or other obligation secured by a recorded deed of trust is entitled to the benefits of the deed of trust notwithstanding any person recorded in the land records as the holder.
Title: Real Property - Deeds of Trust - Recordation of Assignments
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/13 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill clarifies that the holder of a promissory note, instrument, or other obligation secured by a deed of trust is entitled to the benefits of that deed of trust, regardless of who is recorded as the holder in public land records. It also specifies that certain conclusive presumptions regarding the vesting of title in the record holder of a mortgage do not apply to deeds of trust.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and Clerks of the Circuit Courts
stakeholders: Lenders, property owners, and legal professionals involved in real estate transactions and deed of trust assignments.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not included in the provided text. No specific revenue or expenditure changes are explicitly stated in the bill text; therefore, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the legal interpretation of deeds of trust and land records, which are maintained by the Clerks of the Circuit Courts. As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is responsible for the operational and technological framework used to record these documents and the policies governing court proceedings involving mortgage disputes.

The Department of Labor regulates financial institutions, mortgage lenders, and servicers. This bill affects the legal framework regarding the transfer and holding of promissory notes and deeds of trust, which is a core component of the mortgage industry regulated by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation.

DHCD is responsible for state-funded mortgage programs and homeownership financing. Changes to the legal rights associated with recorded deeds of trust and assignments affect the administrative processes for these lending programs and the broader housing market in Maryland.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the state and provides counsel to agencies involved in land recordation and financial regulation. It also handles consumer protection issues that may arise from disputes over mortgage ownership and recorded assignments.

The Maryland State Archives is the permanent depository for land records. Legislative changes that clarify the legal effect of recordation or the status of instruments within the land records directly affect the agency's mission to preserve and make accessible these judicial and property records.

bill_summary: This bill, the Pass Pedestrians Safely Act, establishes safety requirements for operators of bicycles, motor scooters, and electric personal assistive mobility devices (EPAMDs). It requires these operators to exercise due care to avoid collisions, maintain a distance of at least three feet when passing vehicles or pedestrians if practicable, and provide an audible warning before overtaking a pedestrian. It also permits EPAMDs to be equipped with audible devices like bells or horns. Violations are classified as secondary offenses, meaning an officer may only enforce them when the operator has been detained for another suspected violation, and are subject to a $25 civil penalty.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation and State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Operators of bicycles, motor scooters, and electric personal assistive mobility devices (EPAMDs), pedestrians, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a $25 civil penalty for violations of passing and warning requirements. Because these are designated as secondary offenses, the fiscal impact on State revenue is expected to be minimal and indeterminate. A formal Fiscal Note with aggregate estimates was not included in the provided text, and specific total revenue figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for Maryland's multi-modal transportation network and the administration of the Transportation Article, MDOT is the primary entity overseeing the implementation and coordination of rules for bicycles, motor scooters, and EPAMDs.

The MVA, referred to as the Administration in the bill, is responsible for approving equipment such as reflectors and managing highway safety initiatives, including the updating of manuals and regulations to reflect new passing and equipment requirements.

As the primary law enforcement agency for state highways, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing traffic and motor vehicle laws, including the new secondary offenses established for safe passing and audible warnings.
The bill establishes a new civil penalty of $25 for violations of the passing and warning requirements, which will be adjudicated through the District Court system managed by the AOC.

EPAMDs (Electric Personal Assistive Mobility Devices) are frequently used as mobility aids by individuals with disabilities; new equipment requirements and operational rules for these devices directly impact the community this department serves.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MDOT and MSP regarding the interpretation and enforcement of new transportation laws and penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety strategies and policy development; the bill's focus on pedestrian safety and the establishment of new traffic offenses falls within its public safety policy mandate.
DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues; the creation of a new civil penalty will result in a minor impact on state revenue collection through the court system.

bill_summary: This bill requires all Maryland counties and municipalities to enact local laws or regulations that prohibit dogs from being at large. These local laws must also include procedures for the impoundment of dogs found at large and establish civil and criminal penalties for violations.
responsible_party: Maryland counties and municipalities, including their respective animal control units and enforcement entities.
stakeholders: Dog owners, local residents, and local government enforcement agencies in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided. The bill creates a mandate for local governments to adopt and enforce dog leash laws, which will likely result in administrative and enforcement costs. Local governments may also see a change in revenue due to the establishment and collection of civil and criminal penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires local governments to establish civil and criminal penalties for dogs found at large. These violations will be adjudicated within the state court system, impacting the workload and dockets of the District and Circuit Courts.

The Office of the Attorney General may be required to provide legal guidance to state and local entities regarding the interpretation of the mandate and the specific application of the appellate court definition of "running at large" mentioned in the bill.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees animal health and works closely with local animal control units. Mandating specific local animal control laws falls within the department's broader interest in animal welfare and regulation.

The Department of Health oversees local health departments, which often handle public health issues related to roaming animals, such as dog bites and rabies control coordination. Leash laws are a significant component of local public health and safety protocols.

The Natural Resources Police enforce regulations within state parks and public lands where dogs at large can impact wildlife and public safety; local mandates may interact with state park enforcement policies.
As the executive authority responsible for overseeing state laws and relations with local jurisdictions, the Governor's Office monitors mandates placed upon counties and municipalities.

bill_summary: This bill shifts liability for parking citations from a vehicle's registered owner to an auto repair or storage facility if the violation occurs while the vehicle is in the facility's custody. It allows owners to use this as an affirmative defense, requires courts to waive associated fines for owners, and permits enforcement agencies to reissue citations directly to the facility. Additionally, facilities are prohibited from requiring customers to waive these rights as a condition of service.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and local parking enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Registered motor vehicle owners, auto repair and storage facilities, and local parking enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. Explicit financial implications stated in the bill include the mandatory waiver of fines and fees for registered owners who successfully prove the vehicle was in a facility's custody, and potential administrative costs for enforcement agencies to reissue citations to those facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that if a registered owner demonstrates a vehicle was in the custody of a repair or storage facility, the court must immediately waive all fines and fees and dismiss the citation. This creates a new procedural requirement and affirmative defense for the state's judicial system.

As the primary department responsible for the Maryland Transportation Article, MDOT oversees the modal administrations that enforce parking and manage the vehicle systems impacted by this legislation.

The MVA maintains the vehicle registration and owner records that are the basis for issuing parking citations. The bill allows for citations to be reissued to business entities (repair facilities), which may require the MVA to facilitate linking citations to commercial entities rather than individual vehicle owners.

DGS, through the Maryland Capitol Police, provides security and parking enforcement for state-owned facilities. It would be considered a 'parking enforcement agency' tasked with following the new citation protocols and reissuance procedures defined in the bill.

MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains its own police force with parking enforcement authority. It would be impacted by the shift in liability and the requirement to potentially reissue citations to repair or storage facilities.

MTA operates parking facilities at transit hubs and enforces parking laws. The bill would change their enforcement protocols and potentially impact fine revenue if citations are dismissed or difficult to reissue to facilities.

MAA operates BWI and Martin State Airport, where it manages significant parking operations and enforcement. It would be required to adjust its citation procedures to accommodate the affirmative defense established by the bill.

The Maryland Stadium Authority manages sports complexes and parking facilities. As an entity with parking enforcement responsibilities, it would be subject to the bill's requirements regarding the liability of auto repair and storage facilities.

As the primary law enforcement agency for state highways, the Maryland State Police issue citations that fall under the Transportation Article. They would need to comply with the new liability standards when vehicles are in the custody of a service facility.

USM institutions operate independent parking enforcement systems on their campuses. They would be impacted as 'parking enforcement agencies' and would face administrative changes in how they process and collect fines.

As an independent state university with its own parking enforcement, Morgan State would be required to implement the bill's provisions regarding owner liability and the reissuance of citations to repair shops.
The college manages its own campus parking and enforcement; therefore, it would be subject to the bill's requirements for handling citations issued to vehicles in shop custody.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the various state agencies and the MVA on the implementation of these new parking enforcement standards and the interpretation of the affirmative defense.

SHA manages state roads where vehicles in shop custody might be parked. While they focus on maintenance and construction, they are a primary modal of MDOT and play a role in the regulation of highways where enforcement occurs.
MPA manages state-owned port terminals with parking areas. It would need to ensure its enforcement practices align with the new liability rules for repair and storage facilities.

bill_summary: This bill establishes requirements for units of Maryland State government when developing, adopting, and reviewing operational, technical, or procedural standards. It mandates that units rely on transparent and reproducible data, seek stakeholder consensus, utilize decision-support algorithms, and resolve disputes through independent third-party technical reviews. Additionally, the bill requires periodic reviews of standards based on technological best practices and independent peer input.
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, technical and multidisciplinary experts, and individuals or entities impacted by state-implemented operational and technical standards.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill creates new procedural mandates for state agencies, including the use of independent third-party reviews and decision-support algorithms, which would likely result in increased administrative and operational expenditures for State units.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that units of state government utilize a "decision-support algorithm" and follow "technological best practices" in their standards, which directly impacts the Department of Information Technology's role in statewide IT strategy, infrastructure, and digital service standards.

The agency utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to oversee implementation and align agency activities, which directly relates to the bill's focus on developing operational and technical standards (benchmarks) and the requirement for periodic reviews.

The Innovation Team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives and using multidisciplinary data analysis to improve state strategies; the bill's requirements for reproducible data, multidisciplinary experts, and the use of algorithms align with the team's core operational methodology.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees all state units and coordinates the policy initiatives that will be subject to these new procedural requirements for developing and reviewing standards.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM will be responsible for supervising the budget execution and personnel resources required for the mandated periodic reviews and the use of independent third-party technical experts.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and will be responsible for advising them on compliance with the new legal requirements for developing and reviewing procedural and technical standards.

The agency sets extensive scientific and technical standards for pollution control and resource management, all of which will now be subject to the bill's reproducibility, consensus-seeking, and independent review mandates.

The Department of Health manages complex technical and procedural benchmarks for public health and Medicaid; the bill significantly changes how these standards are developed and requires new algorithmic and technological reviews.

MDOT oversees the state's transportation network and develops technical engineering and operational standards that must now comply with the bill's requirements for periodic technological best-practice reviews and third-party dispute resolution.

The agency regulates various industries and professions through technical benchmarks and workplace safety standards, necessitating a transition to the data-driven and algorithmic development processes described in the bill.
MSDE sets statewide educational policies and leadership standards for public schools; these procedural benchmarks will require periodic independent peer input and technical reviews under the new law.
The Comptroller sets technical standards for tax collection and auditing; the bill's emphasis on feasible and transparent data directly impacts the agency's procedural and regulatory activities.

The agency serves as the central repository for state data analysis; its expertise in linking individual-level data is highly relevant to the bill's requirement that standards rely on transparent and reproducible data.

The bill explicitly requires that the development of standards take into account "transformative large-scale economic efficiency," which aligns with the mission of the state's primary economic development agency.

As the central procurement authority, DGS develops operational and technical standards for state contracts and facilities that will be subject to the new consensus-seeking and algorithmic requirements.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program to include mobile home park residents and updates laws governing mobile home park tenancies. It mandates initial one-year leases, limits security deposits to the greater of one month's rent or 500 dollars, and prohibits various charges such as pet, parking, and amenity fees. It also establishes new notice requirements for rent increases and evictions, regulates well water utility billing, and increases the potential damages residents can recover for retaliatory actions by park owners.
responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Mobile home park residents, subtenants, and mobile home park owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill is expected to increase state expenditures for the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to provide expanded legal representation to residents. The Maryland Judiciary will incur administrative costs to develop new forms and manage modified repossession proceedings. Additionally, the bill enables residents to recover damages and attorney fees in civil actions against park owners for various regulatory violations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Judiciary to develop and publish a specific 'Notice of Intent to File a Complaint for Repossession of the Premises' form and significantly alters judicial procedures for repossession, appeals, and escrow in the District Court.

The bill requires mobile home park owners to provide DHCD with notice of any contract of sale for a mobile home park at least 30 days before the sale. Additionally, the department's mission involves ensuring access to safe and affordable housing, which this bill directly regulates for mobile home residents.

The bill expands anti-discrimination protections in mobile home parks by adding several protected classes (including source of income, marital status, and military status) and explicitly authorizes civil actions for discriminatory housing practices under the State Government Article, which MCCR enforces.

The bill requires park owners to ensure water supplies comply with federal and state drinking water regulations and specifically references the definition of a supplier of water under the Environment Article, which MDE oversees.

The bill requires the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to submit an annual report to the Governor regarding the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program, which is expanded by this legislation to include mobile home residents.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to the executive branch and General Assembly on the enforcement of real property laws and consumer protection issues related to landlord-tenant relations.

The bill regulates the resale of utility services (electricity, gas, water) by park owners to residents, which often falls under the broader regulatory framework and oversight provided by the PSC for utility vendors and consumer billing practices.
The bill adds 'military status' as a protected class against discrimination in the accommodations, facilities, and privileges of a mobile home park.

bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of a Tier 1 renewable source under Maryland's Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS) to include energy derived from specific non-combustion waste-to-energy facilities. To qualify, a facility must use a carbon-recovery system, meet a minimum 80% waste-to-energy conversion ratio, avoid producing byproducts that require landfill disposal, and adhere to Environmental Protection Agency guidelines regarding the destruction of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).
stakeholders: Electric companies, renewable energy project developers, and electricity ratepayers in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates for state and local fiscal impacts are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill's expansion of Tier 1 renewable source eligibility to include specific waste-to-energy facilities could impact the supply and price of Renewable Energy Credits (RECs), which potentially affects utility compliance costs and electricity rates for consumers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory body responsible for overseeing the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS). This bill directly alters the definitions and eligibility of Tier 1 renewable sources within the RPS, which the PSC must implement and enforce.

The MEA is responsible for promoting renewable energy and coordinating state energy planning. Altering the RPS to include new waste-to-energy sources falls directly within their mission to manage energy policy and clean energy incentives.

The bill defines waste-to-energy based on environmental criteria, including carbon recovery, byproduct management, and adherence to EPA guidance on PFAS destruction. MDE oversees environmental protection, waste management, and pollution control standards relevant to these facilities.

The OPC represents the interests of residential utility consumers. Changes to the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard can impact utility rates and the types of energy costs passed through to consumers, which the OPC monitors in PSC proceedings.

MCEC functions as the state's green bank and advances clean energy technologies. Including a specific type of waste-to-energy as a Tier 1 renewable source could impact their financing, development, and support of new energy technologies in Maryland.

MES provides technical and operational services for waste and wastewater management. They may be involved in the design or operation of facilities that meet the bill's specific waste-to-energy criteria, particularly those that eliminate landfill byproducts.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the PSC, MEA, and MDE. They would be responsible for advising these agencies on the legal implementation of the new waste-to-energy standards and ensuring compliance with the specified EPA guidance and existing contracts.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a refundable State income tax credit for political contributions made to campaign finance entities. The credit is limited to a maximum of $50 for an individual or $100 for a married couple filing a joint return.
stakeholders: Maryland individual taxpayers, married couples filing joint returns, and campaign finance entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in an indeterminate decrease in State general fund revenue starting in fiscal 2027 as taxpayers claim the refundable credit. The credit is capped at $50 for individuals and $100 for joint filers. A formal Fiscal Note with specific aggregate dollar estimates was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for implementing and administering the new income tax credit, processing tax returns, issuing refunds for the credit, and submitting the mandated annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on the credit's fiscal impact.

The bill establishes a tax credit based on contributions to campaign finance entities as defined in the Election Law Article. The State Board of Elections regulates these entities and will likely need to coordinate with the Comptroller to verify the eligibility of organizations receiving contributions.

As the agency responsible for estimating state revenues and developing the budget, the Department of Budget and Management must account for the reduction in general fund revenue and the fiscal impact of the refundable nature of the credit.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is the recipient of the annual report from the Comptroller. The bill also affects the state budget, which the Governor is responsible for proposing and managing.

The Office of the Attorney General will provide legal counsel to the Comptroller regarding the implementation of the new tax laws and would represent the state in any legal challenges related to the credit's administration.
The Maryland Tax Court would have jurisdiction over appeals from taxpayers whose claims for the political contribution tax credit are denied or adjusted by the Comptroller.
As the state's chief financial agency responsible for managing funds and anticipating monetary needs, the Treasurer's Office is impacted by changes in tax revenue that affect state cash flow.
The State Prosecutor investigates offenses related to the electoral process. They could be involved if fraudulent campaign finance entities are established or used to improperly claim the tax credit.

The Office of Legislative Audits would be responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of the Comptroller’s administration of this new credit to ensure state funds are managed in accordance with the law.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the licensing, registration, and enforcement procedures for child care providers in Maryland. It requires the State Department of Education (MSDE) to establish a dedicated unit for processing criminal history record checks with specific notification timelines, mandates that MSDE issue warnings for first-time violations of newly adopted regulations, and establishes protections for child care quality ratings (Maryland EXCELS) during violation remediation. Additionally, the bill creates a "Workgroup to Study Illegally Provided Child Care" to evaluate the impact of unregulated care and maintains a list of individuals prohibited from employment due to supervision failures.
stakeholders: Child care center operators, family child care home providers, applicants for child care positions, parents and guardians, and state education officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text; therefore, specific dollar estimates are unavailable. However, the bill establishes financial implications including administrative costs for the Maryland State Department of Education to create and staff a dedicated unit for criminal history records checks and to provide staffing and travel expense reimbursement for the Workgroup to Study Illegally Provided Child Care.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is primarily focused on child care licensing and regulation, which is overseen by the State Department of Education (MSDE). It requires MSDE to establish a new unit for criminal history records checks, manage various child care provider lists (including prohibited individuals), update licensing regulations, and staff the Workgroup to Study Illegally Provided Child Care.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup to Study Illegally Provided Child Care, which is a temporary body tasked with studying the scale and impacts of unregulated child care and making legislative and regulatory recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that child care applicants submit to criminal history records checks through the Central Repository, which is managed by DPSCS. It also sets specific timelines for notification based on the receipt of records from this repository.

The Secretary of Human Services (or a designee) is a mandated member of the Workgroup to Study Illegally Provided Child Care. Additionally, the department's mission of aiding vulnerable children aligns with the bill's focus on child care safety and access.

As the agency responsible for adjudicating contested cases for state agencies, OAH would likely handle appeals regarding MSDE's licensing revocations, suspensions, or the placement of individuals on the 'failure to supervise' list.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and would be involved in drafting and reviewing the new rules, regulations, and enforcement mechanisms established by the bill, particularly regarding the due process rights of individuals on prohibited employment lists.
The Governor is responsible for appointing several members to the Workgroup to Study Illegally Provided Child Care, including parents, child care providers, and law enforcement representatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates public safety and criminal justice strategies. The bill's workgroup is specifically tasked with studying 'illegally provided' care and recommending legal changes to ease investigation and enforcement, which falls within GOCPP's policy domain.

The Governor's Office for Children focuses on child well-being and reducing poverty. The bill's mandate to study access to safe child care for children of different socioeconomic and ethnic backgrounds directly aligns with the office's mission.
The bill requires child care providers to send notices of drinking water contamination to parents in accordance with standards established under the Environment Article, which is overseen by MDE.

bill_summary: The Community Trust Act prohibits Maryland state and local law enforcement and correctional facilities from participating in federal immigration enforcement activities unless required by a valid judicial warrant or court order. The bill specifically bans inquiries into an individual's citizenship or immigration status, prohibits prolonging detention for the purpose of investigating immigration status, and restricts the sharing of non-public information or facility access with federal immigration authorities. Additionally, it requires agencies to establish internal policies with penalties for violations and grants individuals the right to bring legal action for actual damages, punitive damages, and injunctive relief.
responsible_party: State and local correctional facilities and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Immigrants, law enforcement agents, correctional facility employees, and state and local government entities
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the provided bill text. However, the bill is expected to have an indeterminate fiscal impact due to administrative costs associated with mandatory policy development and potential litigation expenditures for state and local governments resulting from the private right of action for actual and punitive damages.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines 'court order' and 'judicial warrant' in the context of immigration enforcement and creates a new civil cause of action allowing individuals to sue for actual damages, punitive damages, and injunctive relief, which will be processed through the state court system.

As the central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies; the bill requires state agencies to adopt policies that include specific penalties for employees who violate the prohibitions on immigration enforcement activities.

The Department of General Services operates the Maryland Capitol Police, whose officers are MPTC-certified law enforcement agents subject to the bill's prohibitions and the requirement to adopt a formal policy and penalties.

DJS operates residential facilities and employs personnel involved in youth supervision and transport; while primarily focused on juveniles, any of its MPTC-certified agents would be subject to the law enforcement prohibitions in the bill.

The DNR manages the Natural Resources Police; as MPTC-certified law enforcement agents, these officers are directly prohibited from taking certain immigration enforcement actions and the agency must adopt a corresponding policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is a primary implementing agency as the bill specifically restricts employees and agents of State correctional facilities from investigating immigration status, detaining individuals for federal authorities without a warrant, or providing non-public access to federal agents.

MDOT oversees the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) Police; these certified law enforcement agents are subject to the bill's restrictions on inquiring about citizenship or immigration status and the requirement to adopt an enforcement policy.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (DPSCS, State Police) and coordinates policy initiatives; this bill establishes significant new restrictions on how those agencies interact with federal authorities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the Governor's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, which are directly impacted by the changes in law enforcement and correctional procedures mandated by this bill.

GOHS serves as the liaison to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security; the bill specifically limits the ability of state agencies to cooperate with DHS entities like ICE and CBP regarding civil immigration violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent defendants; this bill impacts the rights and treatment of their clients during arrests, searches, and while in the custody of state and local correctional facilities.

The Maryland State Police is a primary implementing agency; its officers are 'law enforcement agents' who would be prohibited from inquiring about citizenship or immigration status during stops, searches, or arrests, and the agency must adopt a policy with penalties.

The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund; because the bill allows individuals to sue for actual and punitive damages, the office would be responsible for managing and paying out claims resulting from violations by state employees.

As an independent state agency with its own MPTC-certified campus police force, Morgan State University is required to comply with the bill's prohibitions for its law enforcement agents and adopt a formal policy.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases and personnel disputes; since the bill requires state agencies to implement disciplinary penalties for employees who violate the new regulations, the OAH may be involved in hearing appeals related to these penalties.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and will be responsible for interpreting the new requirements, assisting agencies in drafting policies, and defending the state against civil actions for damages authorized by the bill.
As an independent state college with MPTC-certified campus police, it is required to comply with the bill's law enforcement prohibitions and adopt a consistent policy and penalty structure.

The USM institutions employ MPTC-certified campus police officers who are 'law enforcement agents' under the bill, meaning the system and its institutions must adopt policies and penalties consistent with the Act's prohibitions.

bill_summary: This bill increases the sales and use tax on electronic smoking devices and certain vaping liquids. It redirects the additional revenue generated by these tax increases to the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund to support pediatric cancer research and related administrative costs.
responsible_party: The Comptroller of Maryland and the Maryland Secretary of Health
stakeholders: Consumers and retailers of electronic smoking devices and vaping liquid, and physicians, hospitals, and organizations conducting pediatric cancer research.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the sales and use tax rate for electronic smoking devices from 20% to 30% and for vaping liquid in containers of 5 milliliters or less from 60% to 90%. bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) to issue revenue bonds for the development of 'Maryland enhanced Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts,' subject to approval by the Board of Public Works. A Maryland enhanced TIF district is defined as a project exceeding $500,000,000 in total costs that includes a convention center or is located within a half-mile of a transit station. The bill allows the Board of Public Works, upon MEDCO's recommendation, to pledge State incremental sales and income tax revenues generated within the district to support the financing of these projects.
responsible_party: Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) and the Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Local jurisdictions, private developers of large-scale infrastructure projects, the Maryland Economic Development Corporation, and the State of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill allows for the diversion of State incremental sales and income tax revenues from the General Fund to special funds used to secure debt service for bonds issued for specific high-value development projects (exceeding $500,000,000). While specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are unavailable in the provided text, the bill creates a potential long-term reduction in State General Fund revenue in exchange for supporting major infrastructure and economic development. Local jurisdictions must also approve tax increment financing for these projects to qualify.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes MEDCO to issue bonds for the development of Maryland enhanced TIF districts and requires MEDCO to provide recommendations to the Board of Public Works regarding the pledge of State revenues.
The Board of Public Works must approve MEDCO's issuance of bonds for these districts and is authorized to pledge incremental State sales and income tax revenues to support the projects.

As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for the collection and administration of the sales and income taxes that the bill proposes to pledge as 'increments' for the financing districts.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve the bonds and revenue pledges, and the office manages state debt and the issuance of State bonds.
The Governor is a member of the Board of Public Works and oversees the executive branch's economic development and fiscal policy initiatives established by this bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Board of Public Works and state agencies, and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the bond issuances and tax increment pledge agreements.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning; pledging incremental sales and income tax revenues for TIF districts directly impacts the State's general fund and long-term fiscal execution.
The bill defines a 'Maryland enhanced TIF district' based on its proximity to transit stations, which are managed and planned by MDOT, and relates to transit-oriented development (TOD) strategies.
As the primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by new financing tools designed to attract large-scale ($500M+) projects and convention centers.

bill_summary: Known as the COMPASS Act, this bill modifies the educational accountability system for Maryland public schools. It alters the weighting of school quality and academic indicators in a school's composite score, increasing the maximum weight of academic indicators to 70% while capping any single proficiency indicator at 20%. The bill introduces new measures such as school staffing levels and well-rounded curriculum progress as quality indicators, while explicitly prohibiting the use of teacher evaluations within the accountability framework. It also mandates that composite scores be reported alongside their individual indicator components.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, educators, school administrators, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not include specific dollar estimates as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the legislation likely results in indeterminate administrative costs for the Maryland State Department of Education to update the school accountability system, recalculate composite scores based on new weighting rules, and implement the reporting requirements for indicators not included in the composite score through 2031.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing Maryland's public education system, MSDE is directly responsible for implementing the educational accountability program, establishing the composite scores, and managing the school quality indicators described in the bill.

The MLDS Center collects and links student and workforce data. Changes to the metrics for 'on-track progress' and 'well-rounded curriculum' directly affect the types of individual-level data collected and analyzed by the agency.

This is a departmental bill by the Department of Education, an executive agency. The Governor oversees the executive branch and coordinates the policy initiatives related to school accountability and performance.

The bill includes Career and Technology Education (CTE) Programs and dual enrollment as school quality indicators. The Department of Labor oversees workforce development and adult learning programs, which intersect with these indicators.

OLA conducts performance audits of local school systems and state programs. The alterations to the accountability system and composite scores provide new legal benchmarks and data points that OLA would evaluate for fiscal and program compliance.

The board coordinates partnerships between education and business. The bill's emphasis on CTE programs and 'well-rounded curriculum' progress points aligns with the board's mission to ensure students are on pathways to prosperity and meeting economic goals.

The bill explicitly prohibits the use of teacher evaluations within the state accountability system. As the agency overseeing collective bargaining and labor relations for public school personnel, this policy change regarding how educator performance data is utilized is relevant to their jurisdiction.

As the central personnel and fiscal agency, DBM has an interest in changes to educational indicators that impact state personnel policy (teacher certification/evaluations) and the long-term fiscal planning related to school performance reporting.

The bill includes dual enrollment and advanced coursework (AP/IB) as quality indicators. MHEC coordinates policies between secondary and postsecondary education, making these transition points relevant to their regulatory scope.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and the State Board of Education. They would be responsible for ensuring the new accountability framework complies with federal and state law, and defending the board in any legal challenges regarding school ratings.
USM institutions prepare many of the teachers who seek the Advanced Professional Certificates or National Board Certifications mentioned as staffing indicators in the bill.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a regulatory framework for delivery network companies and their operators (drivers) in Maryland. It requires companies to obtain permits and drivers to be licensed by the Public Service Commission, mandates criminal and driving background checks, and implements transparency requirements for driver pay, tips, and customer receipts. Additionally, companies must provide annual reports to the Commission detailing operator statistics and compensation data.

fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. However, the bill creates new regulatory, licensing, and permitting responsibilities for the Public Service Commission, which will result in increased administrative expenditures. The bill also likely generates revenue through permit and licensing fees associated with delivery network companies and operators.

The bill explicitly requires the Commission to adopt regulations to ensure that delivery network services are accessible to individuals with disabilities, including website and mobile application accessibility and reasonable accommodations.

The bill requires delivery network operators to use motor vehicles approved by the Commission and mandates driving record checks as part of the licensing process, functions directly related to the MVA's records and vehicle registration duties.

The bill establishes significant requirements regarding operator compensation, earnings transparency, itemization of tips, and weekly earnings summaries. These provisions intersect with the Department of Labor's mission to protect workers and regulate labor practices and industries.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the OAG would provide counsel to the Public Service Commission regarding the new regulations. Furthermore, the bill's focus on transparency and itemized receipts for customers relates to consumer protection, which the OAG enforces.

The bill requires delivery network companies to provide operators with information regarding state and federal antidiscrimination laws, which falls under the purview of the Commission on Civil Rights' enforcement and educational outreach.
The bill specifically references the Maryland Tax Court as an entity that may order the disclosure of otherwise confidential records or information provided to the Commission under this new title.

The regulation of a new industry involving millions of transactions and gig-economy workers has significant revenue and tax compliance implications. The Comptroller's office manages state revenue and tax enforcement for businesses and residents.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a regulatory framework for parametric insurance policies in Maryland, which pay a predetermined benefit when a specified, measurable trigger event occurs, such as a natural disaster, regardless of actual loss. Special fund revenues from rate and form filing fees are expected to be minimal.

bill_summary: The Fair Districts for Maryland Act proposes a constitutional amendment to establish an independent Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Commission. This commission would be responsible for drawing Maryland's legislative and congressional maps following each decennial census. The bill mandates that each legislative district be subdivided into three single-member delegate districts and establishes strict redistricting standards, including requirements for compactness and contiguity, and a prohibition on favoring political parties or incumbents. It also grants the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction to review maps or create them if the commission or legislature fails to act.
responsible_party: Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Commission
stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for the General Assembly and Congress, incumbent officeholders, and political parties.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase to fund the operations, staff, and consultants of the new independent commission, as well as potential litigation costs. While the bill mandates that the Governor include these funds in the state budget, the specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. There may also be minimal costs to local boards of elections to include the constitutional amendment on the November 2026 ballot.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's role in redistricting is significantly altered; while the Governor loses the power to draft the primary plan, they gain the authority to appoint members to the new Commission, must convene special sessions to consider the plans, and maintain the authority to sign or veto the final legislative and congressional maps.

The bill explicitly amends the Maryland Constitution to remove the Attorney General's authority to prosecute or defend the State in redistricting cases, transferring this legal representation and intervention authority to the newly created Commission.

The bill grants the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction to review redistricting plans and mandates the court to establish its own plans if the Commission or General Assembly fail to enact them within specified deadlines.

As the agency responsible for supervising and administering elections, the State Board of Elections must implement the boundaries established by the new redistricting plans. The bill also references definitions within the Election Law Article and places constraints on using voter registration data managed by the Board.

The Governor is tasked with appointing two members to the Redistricting Commission, a process that would be facilitated by the Office of Appointments to ensure candidates meet the strict registration and background requirements specified in the bill.

The bill mandates that the Governor include funds in the State budget specifically to carry out the provisions of the Act, including the operating costs of the new Commission and its associated litigation costs.
The bill explicitly states that findings of possible criminal violations by a member or employee of the Redistricting Commission may be referred to the State Prosecutor for criminal prosecution.
The Comptroller is specifically mentioned in the constitutional amendment as one of the officers entitled to receive written legal opinions from the Attorney General regarding districting matters.

The State Treasurer is specifically mentioned in the constitutional amendment as one of the officers entitled to receive written legal opinions from the Attorney General regarding districting matters.
