bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from knowingly and willfully causing another individual to ingest an abortion-inducing drug if they know or believe the person is pregnant and act without consent, or through fraud, coercion, force, or threat of force. A violation is a felony punishable by up to 25 years in prison.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Pregnant individuals and persons who attempt to induce an abortion in another without their consent.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a potential minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to incarceration costs. It is not expected to materially affect local finances or the operations of the Judiciary or the Office of the Public Defender.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary, through the Administrative Office of the Courts, is responsible for adjudicating criminal cases. This bill creates a new felony, directly impacting the court system's workload and processing of trials and sentencing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for defending indigent individuals charged with crimes. The creation of a new felony for causing the ingestion of abortion-inducing drugs will directly increase their caseload and litigation requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a felony with a prison sentence of up to 25 years. This has a direct fiscal impact on the department's correctional facilities and budget due to potential increases in the inmate population and duration of stay.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for investigating criminal violations of state law, including the felony offenses established by this bill.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the state in all criminal appeals. The creation of a new felony for drug-induced abortion coercion will require legal review and potential representation in the appellate courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates statewide public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy. A new felony regarding drug-induced coercion falls under their oversight of criminal justice and victim services strategy.

The Department of Health oversees public health and reproductive health services. While the bill is criminal in nature, the subject matter involves medicinal preparations and health policy related to abortion and reproductive rights.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is relevant due to the potential increase in general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services resulting from the bill's incarceration penalty.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an insurer, with respect to private passenger motor vehicle insurance, from increasing a premium, adding a surcharge, or removing, altering, or refusing to consider a discount based on accidents or losses caused by a collision with a free-roaming wild animal and for which the insured was not at fault for the loss.
Title: Collisions With Wild Animals - Prohibited Actions by Insurer
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits private passenger motor vehicle insurers from increasing premiums, adding surcharges, or altering discounts based on an accident or loss caused by a collision with a free-roaming wild animal, provided the insured was not at fault for the loss.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc

bill_summary: This bill increases the per-resident state funding levels for Maryland's regional resource centers and county public library systems starting in fiscal year 2028 and continuing through fiscal year 2032 and beyond. It also updates and streamlines the mandatory service categories that public libraries must offer, including programs for early childhood literacy, workforce development, digital equity, emergency community resource distribution, and mental health support.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, county public library systems, and regional resource centers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases state and local expenditures by raising the per-resident funding rates for the minimum library program and regional resource centers. For regional centers, the rate increases from $9.99 in FY 2027 to $11.58 by FY 2032. For county libraries, the rate increases from $19.10 in FY 2027 to $22.37 by FY 2032. As the State provides approximately 40 percent and counties provide approximately 60 percent of the minimum program costs, both state and local jurisdictions will experience increased fiscal obligations. Specific total dollar estimates are unavailable because no formal Fiscal Note was provided with the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for the coordination and leadership of the state's public library systems, the Maryland State Library will oversee the implementation of the revised funding formula and the new service mandates for regional and county libraries.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for state fiscal planning and budget development; the bill mandates specific, phased increases in per-resident funding for library systems that DBM must incorporate into the State's long-term budget projections.

The bill identifies the Comptroller as the authority responsible for withholding State funds from county library systems that fail to meet state standards, establishing a direct regulatory and fiscal enforcement role.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual budget; this bill requires the Governor to include significantly higher mandated funding levels for libraries in future budget cycles.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Library Board, which falls under this category, is specifically tasked with certifying whether library systems have met state standards, a prerequisite for the release of funding by the Comptroller.
The State Treasurer's Office manages and distributes state funds; this bill alters the mandated funding distributions for the regional and county library systems which the Treasurer must facilitate.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Library and the Comptroller regarding the statutory interpretation of the bill's new funding mandates and enforcement mechanisms.
The bill expands library service requirements to include economic, career, and workforce development programs, which directly align with and support the mission of the Department of Labor.
The revised service requirements for libraries focus on early childhood literacy and school readiness, which are core educational priorities overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education.

Synopsis: Extending through fiscal year 2030 the requirement that an appropriation of $500,000 be included in the annual budget bill for the Recovery Residence Grant Program.
Title: Recovery Residence Grant Program - Funding
Status: In the Senate - Third Reading Passed (41-0)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill extends the requirement for the annual budget to include a $500,000 appropriation for the Recovery Residence Grant Program through fiscal year 2030. The program provides competitive grants to certified nonprofit recovery residences that offer alcohol- and drug-free housing to individuals with substance-related or addictive disorders.
stakeholders: Nonprofit recovery residences and individuals with substance-related or addictive disorders seeking recovery housing.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from fiscal 2028 through 2030 due to the bill's extension of the mandated appropriation for the Recovery Residence Grant Program. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Recovery Residence Grant Program is housed within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH is responsible for administering the program, establishing application procedures, and awarding the competitive grants funded by the mandated appropriation extended by this bill.

As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM must incorporate the bill's mandated $500,000 annual appropriation for the Recovery Residence Grant Program into the state's fiscal planning through 2030.

The Governor's Office proposes the annual state budget, which must now include the extended mandated funding for this program. Additionally, the Department of Health is required to submit an annual report on the program's distribution and effectiveness to the Governor.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health and would be responsible for ensuring the grant program's procedures, criteria, and contract awards remain in compliance with state law.

As the state's chief financial officer responsible for paying state bills and distributing revenue, the Comptroller's office manages the actual disbursement of the grant funds authorized by the mandated budget appropriation.

The State Treasurer's Office manages and protects state funds and coordinates with the budget process. As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer may also oversee significant state expenditures related to the program's operations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County from issuing a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license for use at certain restaurants, subject to certain grandfather provisions; prohibiting the Board from issuing more than one Class A beer, wine, and liquor license for use in each county councilmanic district; repealing the authority of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license holder to purchase liquor for retail sale from an alcoholic beverages wholesaler; etc.
Title: Wicomico County - Class A Beer, Wine, and Liquor License - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/20 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill alters the regulations for Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Wicomico County by prohibiting the issuance of new licenses to restaurants (Class B license holders) after July 1, 2026, while grandfathering existing licenses for renewal. It restricts the number of Class A licenses to one per county councilmanic district and requires all Class A license holders to purchase liquor from a county dispensary instead of an alcoholic beverages wholesaler.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders and applicants in Wicomico County, restaurant owners, the Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners, and the county liquor dispensary.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes an annual license fee of $4,400. It changes the limit on the number of Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses from a total of three in the county to one per councilmanic district. Additionally, it requires license holders to purchase liquor through the county dispensary rather than wholesalers, which may impact county revenues. A formal Fiscal Note with aggregate dollar estimates was not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state official responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state revenues. This bill alters the licensing structure and purchasing requirements for liquor in Wicomico County (restricting purchases to county dispensaries), which directly impacts the Comptroller's regulatory oversight, auditing functions, and tax collection duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County is a regulatory body established by state law to manage local alcoholic beverages licenses. This agency category encompasses such ongoing boards with administrative and regulatory duties, and the bill directly modifies the Board's authority and licensing limitations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and local boards established by state law. The OAG would likely be responsible for interpreting the legal implications of the bill's changes, including the grandfather provisions and the exemptions from multiple-license prohibitions.

The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing members to various boards and commissions, including the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County. Changes to the board's duties and the regulatory environment of the county fall under the Governor's executive oversight of state-authorized entities.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in fulfilling the responsibility to appoint qualified individuals to state-created boards and commissions. Since the Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners is such a body, this office would be involved in managing the appointment process for the officials responsible for implementing the bill's provisions.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "eligible project"; requiring an appropriation of a certain amount to the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program if the Governor appropriates less than $80,000,000 to the Community College Construction Grant Program in each fiscal year; increasing the number of grants, from 8 to 16, the Maryland Higher Education Commission may make in each fiscal year; etc.
Title: Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Unfavorable Report by Budget and Taxation; Withdrawn
bill_summary: The bill expands the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program by removing project cost limits and increasing the number of grants that can be awarded each year from 8 to 16. It also sets a new funding requirement: if the state's main community college construction fund receives less than $80 million in a fiscal year, the state must provide enough funding to the renewal program to make up the difference. Additionally, it removes the rule that prevents colleges from receiving grants in consecutive years and requires funds to be distributed equally among eligible colleges.
stakeholders: Maryland community colleges and Baltimore City Community College
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a state funding mandate for the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program. If the annual appropriation for the Community College Construction Grant Program is less than $80,000,000, the Governor must appropriate the difference to the Facilities Renewal Grant Program. This ensures a baseline funding level when construction appropriations are below the $80,000,000 threshold. The bill also doubles the number of possible grants from 8 to 16 and removes the $1,000,000 project cost cap and the $500,000 individual grant limit. Specific state expenditure increases are indeterminate as they depend on future annual budget cycles, but the $80,000,000 figure serves as the primary fiscal benchmark.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering the Community College Facilities Renewal Grant Program, determining grant awards in consultation with colleges, and adopting necessary regulations.

The bill mandates the Governor to make specific annual appropriations for the Program within the state's operating or capital budget, contingent on funding levels for the Community College Construction Grant Program.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for developing the budget and ensuring the implementation of the bill's mandatory appropriation requirements for facility renewal grants.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures and capital projects, which include the facilities renewal grants and construction funding for community colleges addressed in this bill.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is involved in overseeing state expenditures and distributing the grant funds appropriated for the program.

The State Treasurer's Office manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, participating in the oversight of significant procurements and bond-funded projects related to community college facilities.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Higher Education Commission and would be responsible for reviewing the regulations required to implement the program's changes.

Synopsis: Establishing a consumption-only nonprofit swim club license in Anne Arundel County which authorizes the license holder to allow members of the swim club and their guests to bring beer, wine, and liquor onto the licensed premises for on-premises consumption during designated events; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County to issue the license to a nonprofit swim club in Anne Arundel County; and providing for an annual license fee of $100.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Alcoholic Beverages - Consumption-Only Nonprofit Swim Club License
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/20 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill creates a consumption-only nonprofit swim club license in Anne Arundel County, allowing members and guests to bring their own beer, wine, and liquor onto the premises for on-site consumption during designated events. The license is valid for up to five days per year, with the possibility of three additional days if authorized by the Board. The annual fee is $100 plus $50 for each additional day. Clubs must provide at least 10 days' notice before an event and consumption is limited to between 2 p.m. and 10 p.m.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Nonprofit swim clubs in Anne Arundel County and their members and guests
fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County will see a revenue increase from the $100 annual license fee and the $50 fee for each additional authorized day. The total fiscal impact is indeterminate as the number of swim clubs that will apply for the license is not specified in the bill text, and a formal Fiscal Note with aggregate estimates was not included.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry and chief revenue officer; this bill establishes a new class of alcoholic beverages license and specific fee structure within the state's regulatory and tax framework.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly empowers the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County—an ongoing regulatory body authorized by the General Assembly—to issue and administer the newly created consumption-only nonprofit swim club license.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel regarding the implementation and enforcement of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which this bill amends.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for appointing members to various boards and commissions, including local boards of license commissioners like the one in Anne Arundel County tasked with issuing this license.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county to establish, by law, a subclass of personal property consisting of all the personal property of certain qualified data centers and set a special personal property tax rate for the subclass; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Property Taxes - Authority of Counties to Establish a Subclass and Set a Special Rate for Personal Property of Data Centers
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county to establish a specific subclass of personal property for qualified data centers and set a unique personal property tax rate for that subclass. To be considered a qualified data center, the facility must meet specific investment thresholds ($2 million in Tier I areas or $5 million in other areas) and create at least five qualified positions.
responsible_party: The governing bodies of Maryland counties and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City.
stakeholders: Owners and operators of qualified data centers and Maryland local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill provides local governments with the authority to set special tax rates for data center personal property, which could result in an indeterminate change in local property tax revenues depending on whether jurisdictions choose to lower rates to attract such facilities. As a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text, specific dollar estimates for revenue changes are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines a 'qualified data center' based on criteria and applications for sales and use tax exemptions established under Section 11–239 of the Tax – General Article, which is administered by the Comptroller's office.
DBM is responsible for state fiscal planning and oversight; it would need to analyze the long-term impact of local property tax subclassing on local revenue capacity and state aid formulas.
As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce is directly involved in business attraction and industry-specific incentives, such as those targeting data center growth.
The growth and fiscal treatment of data centers are relevant to the state's broader IT infrastructure strategy and the technological competitiveness of the Maryland economy.
The bill represents a significant economic development policy shift regarding local tax authority that requires coordination with the Governor's executive branch priorities.
MEDCO assists with business attraction and expansion through real estate and financing services; data center projects are major industrial developments that frequently utilize MEDCO's support.
The Tax Court adjudicates appeals regarding personal property tax assessments and could be required to resolve disputes regarding the valuation or eligibility of data centers for this special rate.
The OAG provides legal counsel on the interpretation and implementation of state and local tax laws, including the creation of specific property tax subclasses.
This agency hears local appeals regarding the valuation and classification of personal property, making it the primary body for resolving initial disputes over data center tax rates.

Synopsis: Establishing a presumption that the sentencing of a minor convicted as an adult should be transferred to the juvenile court, under certain circumstances, and authorizing the court to do so; and requiring the juvenile court to make a juvenile determination under certain circumstances.
Title: Minors Convicted as Adults - Sentencing - Transfer to Juvenile Court
Status: In the Senate - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes that a court sentencing a minor convicted as an adult may transfer the case to juvenile court for sentencing if the minor was a victim of a sex crime or human trafficking by their victim within three months of the offense. It also prohibits life sentences without parole for minors and permits courts to impose sentences below statutory minimums.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: Minors convicted as adults who were victims of sex crimes or human trafficking, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Department of Juvenile Services
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided; however, the bill may result in a shift of costs from adult correctional facilities to juvenile services and potential reductions in long-term incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts court procedures by authorizing the transfer of sentencing for certain minors from adult criminal court to juvenile court and requiring the juvenile court to make a disposition.

DJS is responsible for managing youth in the juvenile justice system. This bill allows for more minors to be transferred to its jurisdiction for sentencing and disposition rather than remaining in the adult correctional system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent minors in criminal and juvenile proceedings. This bill provides a significant legal mechanism for their clients to seek transfer to the juvenile system for sentencing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages adult correctional facilities. Provisions that allow for the transfer of minors to juvenile court for sentencing would affect the population of justice-involved youth held in adult facilities under their jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates criminal justice strategies and policy development related to juvenile delinquency and public safety, making the changes to minor sentencing highly relevant to their mission.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel on matters of criminal procedure and state law, including the implementation of sentencing reforms.

The bill specifically references minors who were victims of sex crimes or human trafficking. DHS provides protective services and support to such vulnerable populations and may be involved in the history of the minor being considered for transfer.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including DJS and DPSCS, and sets policy initiatives regarding criminal justice and juvenile rehabilitation.

Synopsis: Establishing an exemption to the population ratio quota for certain Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) licenses in Anne Arundel County for an application filed on or after January 1, 2023, and approved by the Board of License Commissioners before July 1, 2025.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Population Ratio Quota for Class A (Off-Sale) and Class D (Off-Sale) Licenses - Exemption
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/20 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill creates an exemption to the population ratio quota for Class A and Class D (off-sale) alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County for license applications filed on or after January 1, 2023, and approved by the Board before July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Businesses applying for Class A and Class D (off-sale) alcoholic beverage licenses in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State effect is none. Local revenues for Anne Arundel County are estimated to increase by $5,160 annually beginning in fiscal 2027 because the bill allows for the issuance of three licenses that were previously approved but restricted by the population ratio quota. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly impacts the regulatory authority of the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners, which is a permanent administrative and regulatory body established by the General Assembly. The Board is the primary entity responsible for evaluating license applications and enforcing the population ratio quotas that this legislation modifies.

The Comptroller is tasked with the broad regulation of the alcohol industry in Maryland. While licensing is handled locally in this instance, the agency oversees the statewide regulatory framework and industry standards that encompass these Class A and Class D licenses.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions. They may be required to provide legal guidance to the local licensing board regarding the interpretation and implementation of this quota exemption within the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement to include taxes in the total price for a ticket on a ticket listing and at each step of a ticket purchase transaction; authorizing a consumer, an artist, or a venue to file a  private right of action against a ticket issuer, secondary ticket exchange, or reseller for a certain violation; authorizing a court to award economic and punitive damages; and establishing the circumstances under which damages may not exceed certain amounts.
Title: Consumer Protection - Sale and Resale of Tickets - Disclosure of Tax Information and Action for Damages
Status: In the Senate - Unfavorable Report by Finance; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill modifies ticket sale and resale disclosure requirements by removing the mandate that taxes be included in the total price of a ticket during listing and throughout the purchase transaction. It also establishes a private right of action, allowing consumers, artists, or venues aggrieved by violations of these regulations to sue ticket issuers, secondary ticket exchanges, or resellers for economic and punitive damages.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Ticket purchasers, musical artists, entertainment venues, ticket issuers, secondary ticket marketplaces, and ticket resellers.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is unavailable. The bill establishes civil liability for ticket sellers, authorizing courts to award punitive damages of up to $10,000 for a first violation and $25,000 for subsequent violations. While these private actions may increase the workload of the state court system, specific dollar estimates for state or local revenue and expenditures are not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Consumer Protection Act (Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article), which is primarily enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General. The agency would be responsible for oversight and enforcement of the new ticket price disclosure rules and the newly authorized private causes of action.

The Maryland Stadium Authority operates major sports and entertainment venues, such as the Camden Yards Sports Complex. As a venue operator and potential ticket issuer, the agency must comply with the modified price disclosure requirements and the mandatory refund provisions for counterfeit or canceled events.

The bill creates a specific private cause of action for consumers, artists, and venues to sue ticket issuers and resellers, and it establishes specific statutory limits for economic and punitive damages ($10,000 to $25,000). This may increase civil litigation and requires the judiciary to handle new categories of claims.

Member institutions within the University System of Maryland operate numerous stadiums, arenas, and theaters that host athletic and entertainment events. These institutions act as 'ticket issuers' and are directly subject to the bill's requirements for price transparency and refunds.

As a public university with its own athletic programs and entertainment venues, Morgan State University acts as a ticket issuer and venue operator, making the bill's disclosure and refund requirements relevant to its operations.
Saint Mary's College operates venues for performing arts and other events that require ticketing, making it subject to the bill's regulations on price disclosure and consumer protection.

The bill specifically repeals the requirement to include 'taxes' in the total disclosed price of a ticket at each step of a transaction (though they must still be itemized). As the state's chief tax officer, the Comptroller is relevant to any legislative changes affecting how tax information is communicated to consumers during sales.

The Department of Commerce oversees the state's economic development, including the film, arts, and tourism industries. Regulations affecting ticket sales and venues directly impact the businesses and cultural organizations within the department's portfolio.

The agency promotes Maryland as a destination for events and entertainment. Changes to consumer protection laws regarding event ticketing and pricing transparency can affect the state's reputation and the consumer experience for tourists attending Maryland events.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates casinos, many of which house entertainment venues and theaters. These venues act as ticket issuers and are subject to the bill's consumer protection and price disclosure requirements.

Maryland Public Television (MPT) occasionally hosts ticketed cultural and educational events. As an entity that may sell tickets to the public, it would be required to follow the revised disclosure and refund rules.

The Commission operates a museum and archaeological park that hosts ticketed events and entertainment. It would be classified as a venue operator under the bill and required to comply with its provisions.

The corporation manages the Reginald F. Lewis Museum, which hosts ticketed entertainment and cultural events. As a ticket issuer and venue operator, the agency is impacted by the bill's consumer protection standards.

The Governor's Office coordinates state policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch. This bill represents a shift in state consumer protection policy regarding the entertainment and secondary ticket industries.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved in assessing the fiscal impact of legislation on other state agencies, including the operational costs for state-run venues to comply with new ticketing laws.

Synopsis: Establishing that damages to be awarded for the taking of land in a condemnation proceeding include, in addition to the fair market value of the land taken, any legal, expert, or other fees or costs of the action incurred by a defendant.
Title: Eminent Domain - Just Compensation - Fees and Costs
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's eminent domain laws to require that damages awarded to a property owner in a condemnation proceeding include the property's fair market value as well as any legal, expert, or other fees and costs incurred by the defendant during the action.
responsible_party: Maryland State and local government entities with condemnation authority and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Property owners facing condemnation proceedings, state and local government agencies, and legal and expert service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in an indeterminate increase in expenditures for state and local government entities that exercise eminent domain, as they will be required to reimburse the defendant's legal and expert fees in addition to paying for the land taken. Because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary operational support agency, DGS is responsible for the acquisition of real estate for most executive branch agencies. This bill would significantly increase the costs associated with land acquisition by requiring the state to pay for a defendant's legal, expert, and other fees in condemnation proceedings.

MDOT is one of the primary users of eminent domain in Maryland for highway, transit, port, and aviation projects. Requiring the payment of defendants' legal and expert fees would significantly increase the capital costs of infrastructure projects throughout the state.

DNR frequently acquires land for state parks, forests, and conservation efforts. The bill would increase the fiscal burden on the department during land acquisition and specifically mentions damages for land designated as park land or open space.

MDTA is an independent agency that utilizes eminent domain to acquire property for toll facilities, bridges, and tunnels. The bill would directly increase their project expenditures which are funded by toll revenues.

The OAG represents state agencies in all civil litigation, including condemnation proceedings. This bill would change the scope of damages and likely increase the complexity and duration of litigation as legal and expert fees would now be a contested part of the award.
The bill explicitly references the Maryland Historical Trust, which is overseen by the Department of Planning, regarding the valuation of donated easements in condemnation proceedings.

The Board of Public Works must approve significant state expenditures and the acquisition of state property. This bill would increase the total cost of land acquisitions presented to the Board for approval.

The bill contains specific provisions relating to the taking of land or interests in land granted pursuant to the Agriculture Article (§ 2–504), impacting the department's agricultural land preservation programs.

DBM oversees state budget development and execution. The requirement to pay additional fees in condemnation proceedings would represent a notable increase in state capital expenditures across multiple departments.
Condemnation is a judicial proceeding handled in Maryland courts. This bill changes the statutory calculation of damages that must be applied in these court actions.

The Stadium Authority plans and builds various sports and public facilities, often requiring significant land acquisition and the use of eminent domain, which would become more expensive under this bill.
USM and its member institutions occasionally utilize eminent domain for campus expansion and research facility development, and would be subject to the increased costs for legal and expert fees.
The bill specifically mentions the Maryland Environmental Trust regarding the awarding of damages for land with donated easements.
DHCD is involved in community revitalization and infrastructure projects that may involve land acquisition or the coordination of condemnation actions in urban areas.
As a member of the Board of Public Works and the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees the fiscal impacts of increased state expenditures for property acquisition.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer is involved in the approval of state land acquisitions and the financing of capital projects that would be impacted by higher condemnation costs.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies primarily responsible for land acquisition and proposes the state budget which must account for these increased project costs.
MES provides technical services and manages infrastructure projects like landfills or treatment plants that sometimes require the acquisition of land.

Synopsis: Repealing a certain provision of law relating to a certain school police officer's authorization to carry a firearm under certain circumstances; and requiring a school resource officer to carry a firearm while present on the premises of the school to which the officer is assigned.
Title: Public Schools - School Resource Officers - Firearms Required
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires all school resource officers (SROs), including Baltimore City school police officers, to carry a firearm while on the premises of the public school to which they are assigned. It repeals existing legal provisions that restricted Baltimore City school police officers from carrying firearms during regular school hours.
responsible_party: Maryland local school systems and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: School resource officers, Baltimore City school police officers, public school students, and school staff
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state fiscal impact as it applies only to local school systems and law enforcement agencies. It is also estimated to have no material effect on local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety is the primary agency responsible for the statewide coordination of school safety. The bill directly amends section 7-1508, which governs the Center's duties regarding SRO training curricula, data collection on the use of force, and reporting on SRO coverage to the Governor and General Assembly.

As the oversight body for Maryland's public education system, MSDE is directly impacted by changes to the requirements for School Resource Officers (SROs) stationed in schools. Additionally, the Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within MSDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires SRO training programs to be approved by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is an entity housed within this department. MPTSC is responsible for certifying SROs and approving the specialized safety curriculum mentioned in the bill.

The Governor receives annual reports on SRO and law enforcement coverage in schools from the Center. Furthermore, the bill references the Governor's statutory mandate to include $10 million in the annual budget for SRO-related grants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary coordinating body for public safety and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, including those involving law enforcement officers and youth programs, making the policy shift regarding armed SROs relevant to their mission.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police is involved in general safety standards and coordinates with local agencies that provide the law enforcement officers defined as school resource officers in the bill.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE, the Center for School Safety, and other state entities regarding the implementation of statutory mandates and potential liability issues related to requiring firearms for school-based personnel.

Since developmental disability services must be accessible and inclusive, changes to the manual could impact their constituents' ability to direct their own care.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill mandates specific administrative actions for a Deputy Secretary within the Governor's executive cabinet.

Synopsis: Requiring, rather than authorizing, the Governor to include an appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2027 and each fiscal year thereafter.
Title: Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund - Funding
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to include a $1,000,000 annual appropriation in the state budget for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund starting in fiscal year 2027, making a previously optional funding provision mandatory.
stakeholders: Maryland health care providers, patients, and their families
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a mandated annual State general fund expenditure of $1,000,000 beginning in fiscal year 2027. This replaces a previous discretionary funding authorization for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund. No specific local fiscal impact is identified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific appropriation of $1,000,000 in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund, changing the current discretionary authority ('may') to a requirement ('shall').

The Maryland Health Care Commission (referred to as 'the Commission' in the bill) is responsible for designating the Patient Safety Center, administering the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund, providing annual grants, and reporting on the Center's activities to the General Assembly.
As the principal agency for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM is responsible for implementing the mandated $1,000,000 annual appropriation required by the bill.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund separately and to invest the money of the Fund in the same manner as other State money.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is a regulatory agency within the Department of Health, and the bill amends the Health - General Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland.

Synopsis: Altering certain requirements and authorizations for the issuance of certain complimentary fishing and hunting licenses; and requiring the Department of Natural Resources to compile certain statistics relating to complimentary hunting licenses after the close of the hunting season each year.
Title: Natural Resources - Complimentary Fishing and Hunting Licenses - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; FishNets&Dev
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the requirements for issuing complimentary hunting, fishing, and oyster licenses in Maryland. Key changes include extending eligibility for complimentary licenses to enforcement officers from states with reciprocal agreements, establishing lifetime complimentary recreational oyster licenses for former prisoners of war and disabled veterans (both residents and reciprocal non-residents), and requiring the Department of Natural Resources to track and report detailed annual statistics on the issuance of complimentary hunting licenses.
stakeholders: Former prisoners of war, disabled veterans, blind individuals, out-of-state fish and game officials and enforcement officers, and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenue is expected to decrease as the bill mandates that several categories of hunting, fishing, and oyster licenses be issued without a fee to eligible individuals. Furthermore, the bill repeals a provision requiring that proceeds from the sale of commemorative lifetime hunting licenses be used to fund conservation law enforcement. The Department of Natural Resources will also face indeterminate administrative costs to compile and report required annual statistics. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is the primary agency responsible for the administration and oversight of hunting and fishing licenses in Maryland. This bill directly alters the department's requirements for issuing complimentary licenses, mandates the compilation of annual license statistics, and modifies the funding allocation for its Natural Resources Police Force.

The bill significantly alters the eligibility requirements and reciprocity rules for complimentary hunting and fishing licenses for veterans, former prisoners of war (POWs), and service-connected disabled veterans, who are the primary constituents served and advocated for by this department.

The bill includes specific provisions for the issuance of complimentary recreational oyster licenses to individuals who are blind, which relates to the department's mission of ensuring inclusive access to state programs and services for residents with disabilities.

The bill explicitly lists the Governor of Maryland as an eligible recipient for complimentary angler, sport fishing, and hunting licenses, and the Governor oversees the Department of Natural Resources as a cabinet-level executive department.

As the state's fiscal oversight agency, DBM is responsible for assessing the financial impact of waiving license fees and the operational costs associated with the Department of Natural Resources' new annual statistical reporting requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Natural Resources and would be responsible for advising the agency on the implementation of reciprocal licensing agreements and the interpretation of the new statutory language.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Chapter of the National Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities in the Department of State Police; requiring the Department, in conjunction with the Department of Disabilities, to establish guidelines for the use of a certain interface and protocols and policy; establishing the National Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities Commission; requiring the Commission to study and make recommendations regarding the establishment of a secure interface; etc.
Title: National Public Safety Alliance for Individuals With Disabilities - Maryland Chapter - Establishment
Status: In the Senate - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crime Prevention and Policy, Governor's Office of
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Chapter of the National Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities within the Department of State Police. The Chapter is tasked with maintaining a secure, voluntary interface where individuals can provide personal and disability-related information for law enforcement to access during emergencies. The legislation also creates the Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities Commission to develop statewide protocols and training plans, and it establishes a grant program to assist law enforcement agencies with implementation and training costs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police and the Maryland Department of Disabilities
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities and their families, and Maryland law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a grant program for law enforcement agencies with discretionary funding authorized beginning in fiscal year 2028. Additionally, the Department of State Police and the Department of Disabilities will incur administrative costs to establish the secure data interface, manage the Maryland Chapter, and staff the study commission. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Chapter of the National Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities within this department. The State Police are tasked with establishing the secure interface, leading the Commission, developing training, and managing the grant program.

The department is mandated to work in conjunction with the State Police to develop guidelines and training for law enforcement and holds a designated seat on the Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Public Safety Alliance for Individuals with Disabilities Commission, a body of appointed officials and experts tasked with making recommendations and studying the implementation of the secure interface.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is required to coordinate with the newly established Commission to conduct public outreach and engagement campaigns regarding the resources provided by the Maryland Chapter.

The Attorney General is responsible for reviewing potential violations of state law by local law enforcement agencies that fail to comply with the protocols and training guidelines established by the bill.
The Maryland Transit Administration Police is designated a seat on the Commission, and the agency is required to provide staffing support for the Commission's work.
The Maryland Capitol Police, a unit of the Department of General Services, is designated a seat on the Commission, and the department is required to provide staffing support for the Commission.
As the parent agency of the Maryland Transit Administration, MDOT oversees the administration whose police force is mandated to participate in and staff the Commission.
The establishment and maintenance of a secure interface for public data submission falls under the state's IT strategy and cybersecurity infrastructure managed by DoIT.
The Governor is authorized to include appropriations in the annual budget to support the grant program and the chapter's operations established by the bill.
DBM oversees the state's budget development and execution, which is relevant to the bill's provisions for state funding and the creation of a new grant program.

Synopsis: Repealing certain criteria for a certain prohibition on cannabis advertising that targets minors; authorizing a standard dispensary to place certain exterior signage for certain limited purposes under certain circumstances; requiring the Maryland Cannabis Administration to accept certain advertising audience composition data and establish by regulation an alternative method for determining audience composition; etc.
Title: Cannabis - Advertising - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill alters regulations regarding cannabis advertising. It clarifies prohibitions on advertising targeting minors by removing terms like "indirectly" and "attractive to." It allows standard dispensaries to display limited exterior signage for business identification and safety information, provided the signs meet size requirements. The bill also mandates that the Maryland Cannabis Administration accept specific audience composition data and establish alternative verification methods. Furthermore, it exempts non-commercial editorial content from certain advertising restrictions.
stakeholders: Cannabis licensees, standard dispensaries, the Maryland Cannabis Administration, media organizations, and minors.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the text. The bill mandates that the Maryland Cannabis Administration adopt new regulations and enforcement procedures, which may result in administrative costs. No specific revenue changes or funding allocations are mentioned in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulatory body for the cannabis industry in Maryland, the Maryland Cannabis Administration is the chief agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements. The bill specifically mandates the Administration to adopt regulations regarding audience composition data and approve licensure designations for exterior signage.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Cannabis Administration and enforces state consumer protection laws. The changes to advertising standards and definitions of therapeutic or medical claims fall within the OAG's purview for legal review and enforcement of fair trade practices.

The bill establishes specific criteria for 'therapeutic or medical claims' in cannabis advertising, which directly intersects with the Department of Health's mission to manage public health policy and ensure accurate health information is provided to residents.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases involving state agencies. If the Maryland Cannabis Administration takes enforcement action against a licensee for violating the new advertising or signage regulations, the OAH would likely handle the subsequent hearing process.

The bill impacts the business operations and marketing capabilities of licensed dispensaries by altering signage and advertising restrictions. As the state's economic development agency, these changes affect the competitive and operational environment for businesses in the legal cannabis sector.

The Maryland Cannabis Administration is an independent agency within the Executive Branch, and the Governor's Office oversees the broader implementation of cannabis policy and the appointment of leadership within the regulatory framework.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership in the University System of Maryland to provide a single nexus for certain stakeholders in artificial intelligence initiatives to advance artificial intelligence in the State; establishing the Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab in the University System of Maryland to assist State agencies to accelerate the responsible use of artificial intelligence; altering the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program to include training students in artificial intelligence; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Artificial Intelligence (AI) Partnership and the Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab within the University System of Maryland to coordinate AI initiatives, support state agencies in adopting AI, and promote economic and workforce development. It expands the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program and renames and broadens the Cybersecurity Public Service Scholarship Program to include artificial intelligence, while also tasking Morgan State University with research on equitable AI use.
stakeholders: Higher education students, state agencies, small businesses, and institutions of higher education in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill creates new financial obligations including the establishment of three regional technology hubs, the creation of an AI Incubation Lab, and the expansion of the state's emerging technology scholarship and diversity training programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM will be responsible for managing the fiscal impact of the new AI programs and scholarships, as well as overseeing personnel policies for scholarship recipients fulfilling their service requirements within state government.

The bill's creation of the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership aims to drive economic growth and innovation, which directly aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission to stimulate the economy and support business development in emerging technology sectors.

The bill requires the Department to provide information on the scholarship program to high school students in career and technology programs and identifies public high schools as eligible work locations for scholarship recipients.

DoIT is specifically mandated to provide policy guidance, support, and potentially funding for the new Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab, making it a critical partner in implementing the state's AI strategy.
The Department of Labor is explicitly required to partner with the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership to establish Maryland Technology Extension Hubs across the state.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the authority of the Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet, which is a state body under this category, allowing it to request and receive specific AI-related research.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates the policy initiatives and subcabinets, such as the AI Subcabinet, that are central to this bill's implementation.

The Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership is required to collaborate with local workforce development boards, whose strategy and policy are guided by the Governor's Workforce Development Board.

MHEC is responsible for expanding the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program and administering the renamed Emerging Technology Public Service Scholarship Program, both of which are central components of the bill.
MLDS will likely be responsible for collecting and analyzing student performance and workforce outcomes for those participating in the new AI training and scholarship programs.
As a solution incubator for the Governor's priorities, the Innovation Team's work in prototyping policy solutions overlaps with the mission of the new Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab.

Morgan State University is explicitly named as a site for the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program and is mandated to host the Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems to support state agencies.
The bill establishes the Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership and the Artificial Intelligence Incubation Lab within the University System of Maryland, making it a primary implementing agency.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "retail sale" for purposes of provisions of law governing the sales and use tax to exclude certain sales of technology services under certain circumstances.
Title: Sales and Use Tax - Definition of Retail Sale - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's sales and use tax by excluding certain information technology and software publishing services from the definition of a 'retail sale' when those services are used as components for other taxable services or are transferred between affiliated business entities. This change effectively provides a tax exemption for these specific business-to-business technology transactions.
stakeholders: Data processing and hosting firms, computer systems design services, software publishers, and businesses within affiliated corporate groups.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will decrease due to the expansion of sales and use tax exclusions for specific technology services sold for resale or between affiliated companies. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided, specific dollar estimates are unavailable, though the nature of the impact is an indeterminate revenue decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief tax collector and administrator of the sales and use tax, the Comptroller's office is directly responsible for implementing the altered definition of 'retail sale' and managing the resulting tax exclusions for technology and software publishing services.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. This bill alters the tax base for IT services, which would result in a reduction in state general fund revenues that the department must account for in the annual budget.

The bill provides tax relief for companies in the data processing, software publishing, and computer systems design sectors (NAICS 518, 519, 5415, and 5132). This directly relates to Commerce's mission to stimulate the economy and support the growth of the technology industry in Maryland.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget. A change in sales tax policy impacting the technology sector aligns with the Governor's role in coordinating policy initiatives and fiscal management.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest administrative review body for tax disputes. It would likely hear appeals regarding the interpretation of 'affiliated groups' or 'incorporation of services' under the new exclusions created by this bill.

TEDCO supports early-stage technology-based businesses. The companies in their portfolio, particularly in software and IT systems design, would be primary beneficiaries of the sales and use tax exclusion for inter-company or resale transactions.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides legal counsel to the Comptroller regarding the enforcement and interpretation of tax laws, including changes to the Tax-General Article.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, on and after January 1, 2035, a person from disposing of a mattress in a landfill, subject to certain exceptions; prohibiting, on and after January 1, 2035, a person from disposing of a mattress in an incinerator, subject to a certain exception; requiring certain producers of mattresses sold at retail in the State or a certain representative organization to submit a plan for the establishment of a Mattress Stewardship Program in the Department of the Environment for approval on or before July 1, 2031; etc.
Title: Mattress Stewardship Program - Establishment

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Mattress Stewardship Program in Maryland, requiring mattress producers to develop and implement a plan for the collection, transportation, and recycling of postconsumer mattresses. Beginning July 1, 2031, producers must submit program plans to the Department of the Environment. The program is funded by a stewardship assessment fee added to the purchase price of mattresses sold in the state. The bill also prohibits the disposal of mattresses in landfills or incinerators beginning January 1, 2035, with limited exceptions, and creates a Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board to oversee implementation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (Office of Recycling)
stakeholders: Mattress producers, retailers, consumers, waste management and recycling entities, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a self-funding regulatory framework. It creates an indeterminate revenue increase for the State Recycling Trust Fund through plan review and annual report fees paid by producers to cover the Department of the Environment's administrative and oversight costs. A Mattress Stewardship Assessment fee will be added to the purchase price of mattresses to fund the program's collection and recycling operations. Local governments may experience reduced expenditures as the financial responsibility for mattress disposal shifts from the public sector to producers and consumers. Specific dollar estimates are not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for implementing and overseeing the Mattress Stewardship Program. Its Office of Recycling is tasked with reviewing plans, approving annual reports, setting assessments, and adopting enforcement regulations.
MES is explicitly required to coordinate with MDE's Office of Recycling to study and report on the progress of diverting mattresses from landfills and incinerators.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board to advise on the implementation and sustainability of the program.
The Comptroller (or designee) is a designated member of the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board. The agency is also responsible for accounting for the State Recycling Trust Fund.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is a designated member of the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is a designated member of the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board. The bill impacts mattress producers and retailers, which falls under economic development and business regulation.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the majority of members to the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board, including representatives from industry and advocacy groups.
OAG provides legal counsel to the implementing agencies. The bill also addresses immunity from antitrust and trade practice claims for activities undertaken in accordance with the approved program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program plan must specifically describe how Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), women-owned businesses, and veteran-owned businesses will be solicited and supported, which aligns with this office's mission.
The bill establishes civil penalties for violations by retailers and producers; contested enforcement actions or appeals of these penalties would be adjudicated by OAH.
The State Treasurer is the custodian of the State Recycling Trust Fund, which will receive new fees and penalties established by the bill.
DBM oversees the personnel and fiscal impacts on MDE and other agencies tasked with staffing the Advisory Board and administering the new program.
This office will manage the recruitment and vetting of the diverse stakeholders the Governor must appoint to the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board.
The bill requires the program to prioritize training and hiring individuals with disabilities and ensures that collection infrastructure is accessible to disabled residents.
The bill emphasizes creating jobs for homeless individuals and those experiencing housing insecurity, which are populations served by DHS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program plan must include strategies for hiring and training individuals reentering society after imprisonment, aligning with DPSCS's rehabilitation and re-entry goals.
