bill_summary: This bill prohibits child placement agencies, the Social Services Administration, and the Department of Human Services (DHS) from discriminating against prospective adoptive or foster parents, children in foster care, or employees based on characteristics such as race, sexual orientation, and gender identity. It sets criteria for the approval or denial of adoption applications and mandates that DHS and its funded contractors provide public services and maintain employment practices without discrimination, while allowing specific exceptions related to age, sex, and the religious heritage of minors.
stakeholders: Prospective adoptive and foster parents, children in foster care, employees of the Department of Human Services and its contractors, and the general public receiving services from those entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text. Financial implications explicitly mentioned include a prohibition on adoption agencies from denying applications due to an applicant's inability to pay fees, which could impact agency revenue. Additionally, there may be indeterminate administrative costs for the Department of Human Services to ensure compliance with the bill's non-discrimination mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the Social Services Administration, local departments, and the management of foster care and adoption services, DHS is the central body tasked with implementing the bill's non-discrimination mandates.
The Commission enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws in employment and state contracts, which are key areas regulated by the bill's prohibitions for DHS and its funded entities.
The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for DHS and will be responsible for providing legal counsel on the implementation and enforcement of the bill's new statutory requirements.
The bill's focus on non-discrimination in child welfare, foster care, and adoption directly aligns with the GOC's mission to promote the well-being of Maryland's children and families.

The bill explicitly prohibits discrimination based on physical or mental disability in the provision of services by DHS and its funded entities, directly involving this department's coordination role.
The OAH may be called upon to adjudicate administrative disputes and contested cases arising from alleged violations of the bill's non-discrimination mandates or adoption application denials.
As the central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and practices, which are affected by the bill's specific non-discrimination requirements for DHS and its funded partners.

The Board approves significant state procurement contracts; the bill's prohibition on purchasing services from entities that discriminate in public services or employment impacts DHS contract approvals.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Transportation Authority to submit a certain report on E-ZPass discount plans and unused commuter trips that contains certain data; requiring the Authority to provide recommendations for lowering the amount of unused commuter trips; requiring the Authority, under certain circumstances, to submit a certain corrective action plan or eliminate certain forfeitures; etc.
Title: Maryland E-ZPass Commuter Fairness and Transparency Act of 2026
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: The Maryland E-ZPass Commuter Fairness and Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Transportation Authority to report on E-ZPass discount plans and unused commuter trips for the years 2023 through 2025. The Authority must provide recommendations for reducing unused trips and a corrective action plan if more than 25% of plans result in unused trips, aimed at preventing the forfeiture of prepaid funds by commuters.
stakeholders: E-ZPass discount plan users, Maryland commuters, and the Maryland Transportation Authority
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Transportation Authority will incur costs to analyze tolling data and produce the required report. If the resulting recommendations or corrective action plan eliminate the forfeiture of prepaid toll funds, the Authority will experience an indeterminate revenue decrease. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because no Fiscal Note was provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Transportation Authority to analyze data on E-ZPass discount plans, submit a comprehensive report to the General Assembly, and implement corrective action plans to reduce the forfeiture of unused commuter trips.

As the parent agency overseeing all modal administrations, including the MDTA and MVA, the Department of Transportation is responsible for the overall state transportation network and revenue policies affected by the bill.

Toll penalties and administrative fees are frequently enforced through MVA registration holds and licensing actions, making the MVA central to the bill's goals of addressing transparency and consumer fairness in the tolling system.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives related to economic mobility and consumer protection, both of which are central themes in the bill's preamble and mandates.

This office utilizes data-driven strategies to improve government responsiveness and eliminate waste; it would likely oversee the MDTA's data analysis and the implementation of mandated corrective action plans.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller oversees state revenue collection and has a vested interest in the fiscal fairness and transparency of tolling systems.
The Treasurer manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, providing oversight on the fiscal integrity of revenue-producing agencies like the MDTA.
The Board oversees significant state expenditures and fiscal policies, acting as a check on decisions related to state-owned property and revenue-generating infrastructure.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the MDTA and enforces consumer protection laws, which the bill cites as a primary concern regarding current tolling and penalty practices.

The bill's preamble highlights inequitable barriers for unbanked and low-income residents, issues which fall under the Commission's mandate to ensure fairness and prevent discrimination in state programs.
DHS assists residents in economic need who are disproportionately impacted by the financial burdens and penalty structures described in the bill's focus on commuter fairness.
DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning, which includes monitoring the financial reporting and revenue impacts of MDTA's tolling policies.
OLA conducts performance evaluations and fiscal compliance audits of executive agencies, ensuring the accuracy and accountability of the data-driven reports required by this legislation.
The team is tasked with identifying initiatives to enhance economic mobility and reduce poverty, aligning with the bill's goal of mitigating consumer harm for low-income motorists.
The bill's preamble explicitly identifies older adults as a demographic disproportionately impacted by the shortened usage windows for prepaid toll trips.
Maryland's participation in the E-ZPass system is facilitated through interstate agreements, and changes to discount structures may involve coordination with the broader Interagency Group.
The OAH adjudicates administrative disputes, including those related to motor vehicle penalties and licensing actions that may stem from unpaid tolls and associated fees.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for single-gene and multigene pharmacogenomic testing. The coverage applies to individuals diagnosed with depression or anxiety when a healthcare provider is considering medication changes or dose adjustments for drugs with known gene-drug interactions. The bill also sets standards for prior authorization processes and establishes monetary penalties for noncompliance.
responsible_party: The Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Individuals diagnosed with depression or anxiety, healthcare providers, diagnostic laboratories, managed care organizations, and private health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates coverage for pharmacogenomic testing under Medicaid and private insurance plans starting July 1, 2027. This requirement is likely to increase state expenditures for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and may lead to increased premiums for private health insurance. Noncompliance by managed care organizations or insurers can result in penalties of up to $10,000 per instance plus $1,000 per day. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, specific total dollar estimates for the fiscal impact are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates coverage for pharmacogenomic testing under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and Managed Care Organizations (MCOs), granting the Department specific enforcement, auditing, and corrective action authority.

The Insurance Commissioner is responsible for enforcing the coverage mandate for private insurers and HMOs, including conducting periodic audits, managing a reporting process for noncompliance, and issuing penalties.
The bill explicitly provides that Managed Care Organizations and insurance carriers subject to penalties for noncompliance may request an administrative hearing, which is conducted by this agency.

As the agency responsible for state employee health benefits and the overall state budget, DBM will be impacted by the fiscal requirements of the coverage mandate for both the state employee plan and Medicaid appropriations.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration, providing counsel on the implementation and enforcement of the new testing requirements.
The commission is responsible for planning the state's health system needs and typically analyzes the social and economic impacts of new healthcare mandates on cost and access.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget, which will be affected by the fiscal impact of this mandate on Medicaid and state personnel costs.

The agency administers the state's health insurance marketplace; changes to mandated coverage for private health plans and HMOs directly affect the products offered and information provided on the exchange.

bill_summary: This bill requires owners of solid waste containers, excluding those for single-family homes, to contract with professional cleaning services for monthly cleaning and sanitization. It mandates specific cleaning protocols, including the use of approved disinfectants and high-pressure washing, and requires owners to maintain service documentation for 12 months. The Maryland Department of the Environment is authorized to impose administrative penalties of up to $250 for violations that remain uncorrected for three months.
stakeholders: Owners of commercial and multi-family residential solid waste containers, professional cleaning services, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates an indeterminate increase in state or local revenue from administrative penalties of up to $250 per violation. The Maryland Department of the Environment and local health departments will incur administrative costs to implement the new standards and provide oversight. A formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary implementing agency for this bill. It is responsible for approving disinfectant methods, testing protocols for professional cleaning services, providing guidance to local health departments, and exercising or delegating enforcement and administrative penalty authority.

As the state's primary operational support agency, DGS manages and maintains state-owned facilities. It would be responsible for procuring professional cleaning service contracts to meet the monthly sanitization requirements for solid waste containers at most state-operated buildings.

The bill allows MDE to delegate enforcement authority to local health departments. MDH oversees and coordinates with these local departments, and the mandate for cleaning waste containers is closely linked to public health and the control of harmful microorganisms.

MDOT operates diverse facilities including BWI Airport, the Port of Baltimore, transit stations, and highway rest areas, all of which utilize large numbers of solid waste containers that would require monthly professional cleaning under this bill.

The University System manages numerous campuses with extensive solid waste infrastructure. The requirement to contract professional cleaning services for every dumpster and waste container monthly represents a significant operational and fiscal impact on the member institutions.

MFCA manages wholesale food markets in Jessup and Rock Hall. Given the high volume of organic waste at these facilities, the sanitization requirements for their solid waste containers are directly relevant to their daily operations and food safety environment.

As an independent state university with a large urban campus, Morgan State University owns and manages numerous solid waste containers that would fall under the monthly sanitization mandate, incurring a fiscal and operational impact.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Department of the Environment in drafting regulations and would represent the state in matters related to the enforcement and collection of administrative penalties established by the bill.

MSDE provides leadership to local school systems. Public schools utilize numerous solid waste containers that would be subject to these requirements, and the agency may need to issue guidance or coordinate with local boards on compliance costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages correctional facilities statewide. These facilities generate substantial waste and utilize many containers that must be cleaned and sanitized monthly under the new mandate.
DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and state parks. Many of these parks utilize solid waste containers for public use which would require monthly professional cleaning and sanitization.

MES provides technical environmental services to state and local governments, including waste management. They may be tasked by other agencies to manage compliance with these cleaning requirements or could potentially offer such services as a provider.

The Judicial Branch manages numerous court facilities throughout the state. As the owner/operator of these facilities, they would be responsible for the fiscal cost of monthly sanitization contracts for their waste receptacles.

As an independent public college, St. Mary's College would be responsible for ensuring all solid waste containers on its campus are professionally cleaned and sanitized monthly in accordance with the bill.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund to provide loans and grants for building electrification and transportation electrification.
stakeholders: Maryland residents and businesses seeking electrification assistance, and the Maryland Energy Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates the use of the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund for building and transportation electrification loans and grants. Specific fiscal estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, but the bill establishes new required expenditures for an existing state fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is the primary agency responsible for managing the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF). This bill directly amends the required uses of the SEIF to include building and transportation electrification, placing the responsibility for administering these new loans and grants on the MEA.

The bill mandates the use of funds for 'transportation electrification,' which is a central component of MDOT's mission to operate and maintain the state's transportation network and improve its sustainability and environmental impact.

The bill explicitly mentions the fund's use to pay costs for the Air and Radiation Administration within the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). Furthermore, electrification is a key strategy for MDE's environmental protection and air quality goals.

The 'building electrification' aspect of the bill is highly relevant to DHCD, which oversees housing and community revitalization projects, energy efficiency programs, and municipal infrastructure projects.

DGS is responsible for the design, construction, and maintenance of state-owned facilities. The requirement for 'building electrification' funding would likely impact DGS's management of state facilities and its sustainability and energy conservation initiatives.

As the state's green bank, MCEC is dedicated to advancing clean energy and energy efficiency. The availability of new loans and grants from the SEIF for electrification aligns directly with MCEC's mission to leverage capital for such technologies.
Building and transportation electrification involve significant changes to the electric grid and utility planning, which are overseen and regulated by the Public Service Commission.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state. Any change in the mandated usage of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, a significant state funding source, has a direct fiscal impact and affects state budget execution and long-term planning.
The State Treasurer's Office is the chief financial agency responsible for receiving, investing, and distributing state funds, including the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is involved in the oversight of state funds and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which may oversee contracts related to the distribution of these funds.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the Secretary of Health is required to make a new certificate of birth due to the change of a sex designation of an individual; establishing requirements and a prohibition related to the making of new certificates of birth; and altering the options for indicating an individual's sex designation on a license, identification card, or moped operator's permit issued by the Motor Vehicle Administration.

bill_summary: The Birth Certificate Modernization Act alters the process for changing the sex designation on a Maryland birth certificate by allowing individuals to submit a written request under penalty of perjury, removing the previous requirement for a licensed health care practitioner's statement. The bill also introduces a third sex designation option, 'unspecified or another' (represented as 'X'), for both birth certificates and Motor Vehicle Administration documents, including driver's licenses and identification cards. Additionally, it provides a process for updating a birth certificate to reflect a parent's legal name change.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Individuals born in Maryland seeking to update their sex designation, residents applying for or renewing state-issued identification, and parents with legal name changes.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text; therefore, specific dollar estimates are unavailable. However, the bill creates administrative mandates for the Maryland Department of Health and the Motor Vehicle Administration to update electronic record systems, modify application forms, and process new or amended documents to accommodate 'X' designations and self-attestation requests.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Secretary of Health with creating and managing new birth certificates resulting from sex designation changes or parental name changes, as detailed in the amendments to Article – Health – General.

The bill directly mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration allow sex designation options of 'Male,' 'Female,' or 'Unspecified/Another' (marked as 'X') on licenses, identification cards, and moped permits.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT is responsible for the oversight and operational funding of the systems required to implement the bill's changes to state identification documents.

The bill relies on orders from courts of competent jurisdiction for name changes, parentage, and sex designations, and requires clerks of court to report specific decrees and adjudications to the Secretary of Health.
Changes to names and sex designations on MVA records and birth certificates directly impact the statewide voter registration system, which the Board of Elections manages and maintains.

The OAG will be required to provide legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Motor Vehicle Administration regarding the implementation of the 'penalty of perjury' request systems and the interpretation of court orders.

The department utilizes birth certificates and parentage information for child support enforcement and the administration of social service programs, all of which are impacted by changes to primary identity documents.
The bill relates to the legal recognition of gender identity and sex designation, which are protected classes under Maryland's anti-discrimination laws enforced by the Commission.

The State Archives is the central depository for permanent government records, including historical birth certificates, and would be responsible for the long-term preservation of both original and modified records.
Denials of requests for new birth certificates or identity documents are subject to administrative review, for which the Office of Administrative Hearings provides independent adjudication.

As a primary law enforcement agency, the State Police rely on MVA-issued licenses and identification cards for field verification and criminal records, making the inclusion of 'X' designations relevant to their operations.
DBM oversees the fiscal notes and potential budgetary requirements for state agencies like MDH and MVA to update information technology systems and forms to accommodate the new designations.
The Secretary of State is the custodian of official state records and manages programs like 'Safe at Home,' which may interact with residents seeking identity document changes for safety reasons.

The Register of Wills relies on birth and parentage records for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes, which are impacted by changes in legal parentage documentation.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Office of State Elected Officials Information Privacy within the Department of Legislative Services to manage a new Address Confidentiality Program for Maryland's current and former top elected officials and their resident families. It authorizes these protected individuals to request the removal of personal information, such as home addresses and phone numbers, from government websites and social media platforms. The bill also creates criminal penalties for the malicious publication of such information if it results in harm or threats.
stakeholders: Current and former Maryland Governors, Lieutenant Governors, Attorneys General, Comptrollers, and members of the Maryland General Assembly, as well as their resident spouses, children, and dependents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will increase state expenditures to staff and operate the new Office of State Elected Officials Information Privacy, including salaries for a director and additional management personnel. It also creates a criminal misdemeanor penalty with a fine of up to $5,000, which may result in a minimal increase in state revenue. A formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor and their household members are specifically defined as 'protected individuals' under the bill. The office would be responsible for ensuring that the Governor's personal information is not published on official platforms and for handling removal requests for such information.

The Lieutenant Governor and their household members are specifically defined as 'protected individuals' under the bill, granting them the right to request the shielding and removal of their personal information from public records and the internet.

The Comptroller and their household members are defined as 'protected individuals' under the bill. Additionally, the agency maintains tax records, which are identified as 'real property records' that may be subject to shielding requests.

The Attorney General and their household members are 'protected individuals.' Furthermore, as the chief legal representative for all state agencies, the OAG will be responsible for providing legal guidance on the implementation and enforcement of these new privacy and shielding requirements across state government.

The Secretary of State administers the existing Address Confidentiality Program (ACP). The bill explicitly amends statutes governing the ACP to integrate the new State Elected Officials program into the state's existing privacy framework.

The bill explicitly references the Judicial Address Confidentiality Program administered by the AOC and the Office of Information Privacy within the courts. It also impacts the shielding of real property records maintained by clerks of the circuit court, whom the AOC supports.

As the agency responsible for state IT strategy and web security, DoIT will likely be tasked with assisting other governmental entities in technically ensuring that the personal information of protected individuals is not published or is removed from state-managed websites and social networks.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel management. It would be involved in the fiscal implementation and staffing of the newly created Office of State Elected Officials Information Privacy within the Department of Legislative Services.

The bill establishes a new criminal misdemeanor for the unauthorized publication of a protected individual's information under certain threat-based conditions. The Maryland State Police would be responsible for investigating these crimes when they involve state-level officials.

As the central depository for government and judicial records, the Archives may possess records containing the personal information of protected individuals that would now be subject to shielding or redaction requests.

The bill creates a new Office of State Elected Officials Information Privacy within the Department of Legislative Services (DLS). OLA is a sub-unit of DLS and will likely be responsible for auditing the fiscal and regulatory compliance of the new office.

The Board is comprised of the Governor and the Comptroller, both of whom are 'protected individuals' under this bill. The Board's official records and proceedings may be impacted by requests to shield the personal information of its members.

The bill defines driver's license numbers and vehicle unique identifiers (license plates) as 'personal information.' The MVA is the primary agency managing this data and would be required to comply with non-publication and shielding requests from protected individuals.

The Commission manages financial disclosure programs that often involve home addresses and other personal information of the state officials defined as 'protected individuals' in this bill. The agency would need to modify how it publishes or shields these disclosure records.

The Board manages voter registration and election records which contain addresses and personal information of current and former elected officials. These records would be subject to the bill's shielding and non-publication mandates.

Synopsis: Authorizing a landlord to enter a leased premises without providing certain written notice on written request of a tenant to complete a repair or perform maintenance within 7 days after the tenant's request or if a repair is in progress and is being completed in a timely manner.
Title: Residential Real Property - Notice of Landlord Entry - Tenant Consent
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill allows landlords to enter a rental property without the standard written notice if the entry is made to perform maintenance or repairs requested in writing by the tenant. The exception applies if the landlord enters within seven days of the request or while the repair is already in progress, provided they are making a reasonable effort to complete the work in a timely manner.
stakeholders: Residential landlords and tenants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text. The legislation clarifies procedural rules for landlord entry into leased premises, which typically does not result in a direct impact on State or local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 8-221 of the Real Property Article regarding landlord entry notice. Disputes between landlords and tenants concerning entry rights and maintenance requests are adjudicated within the Maryland District Courts, making this highly relevant to the operational and legal support functions of the Judiciary.

As the primary state agency responsible for ensuring safe, secure, and affordable housing, DHCD is concerned with any legislation that impacts the rights and responsibilities of landlords and tenants in residential properties.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division provides guidance on landlord-tenant law and investigates complaints related to consumer housing rights. Additionally, the OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly regarding the implementation of real property laws.

The MCCR enforces anti-discrimination laws in housing. Modifications to the protocols for landlord entry can intersect with allegations of harassment or discriminatory treatment of tenants, making the bill relevant to their oversight of housing rights.

This bill affects the notice requirements for repairs and maintenance in residential leases. The Department of Aging is relevant as it advocates for the rights of older adults who are tenants and may be impacted by changes in landlord-tenant dynamics.

Changes to landlord entry notice for repairs can affect residents with disabilities who may require specific accommodations or advance notice for entry, making this relevant to the agency's mission to improve housing accessibility and inclusion.

Synopsis: Repealing the deadline by which a certain fee must be paid by the holder of a Class A beer and light wine license or a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license to exercise certain Sunday sales privileges; and altering the deadline by which a license holder must present to the Board certain proof that all of the license holder's personal property taxes due to Baltimore City and the State have been paid.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the September 30 deadline for Baltimore City Class A beer and light wine or beer, wine, and liquor license holders to pay a $120 supplementary fee for Sunday sales. It also moves the annual deadline for license holders to provide proof of paid personal property taxes to the Board of License Commissioners from October 30 to March 30.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverages license holders in Baltimore City and the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill adjusts administrative deadlines for license fee payments and tax compliance certification. While the bill text mentions a $120 fee for each Sunday sales privilege, it does not change the fee amount or provide aggregate revenue projections; therefore, specific dollar estimates for the total fiscal impact are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal tax collector and regulator of the alcohol industry. This bill is relevant because it concerns alcoholic beverages licensing and requires verification that state personal property taxes have been paid, which involves state revenue collection and regulatory oversight administered by the Comptroller's office.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state agencies, boards, and commissions. Because the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners is a state-appointed body, the OAG would be responsible for advising the Board on the implementation of these statutory changes, particularly the requirement for summary license suspension without a hearing.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for appointing the members of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners. This bill alters the statutory duties and administrative deadlines of that Board, which falls under the Governor's broader executive oversight.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions, including the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners. This board is the primary entity responsible for enforcing the licensing and tax compliance changes proposed in the bill.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland public school systems from including certain provisions in their contracts, such as binding arbitration, requirements to indemnify other parties without an appropriation, and naming out-of-state venues for legal disputes. Any such prohibited provisions are considered void, and the law applies to all contracts or renewals executed on or after July 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Local Boards of Education (Maryland Public School Systems)
stakeholders: Local school systems, legal counsel, administrative staff, and vendors or contractors providing goods or services to Maryland public schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, so specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The bill prohibits contracts from creating deficiencies or incurring liabilities in excess of appropriations, which may prevent unexpected expenditures, though administrative adjustments for contract compliance may be required.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of Maryland's 24 local school systems, the Department of Education will be responsible for ensuring that local school boards comply with the new restrictions on contract provisions and may need to provide guidance or regulatory oversight regarding these legal standards.

The IAC oversees public school construction and capital improvement projects. Because construction agreements are 'public school system contracts,' the prohibited provisions regarding indemnification, liability limits, and arbitration will directly impact the terms and risk management of projects funded and managed by this commission.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Department of Education and the IAC. They will be responsible for interpreting the bill's provisions, advising agencies on the enforceability of existing contracts, and reviewing future contract templates to ensure compliance with the new statutory prohibitions.

MCSS administers grants and provides training and technical assistance to schools. While not the primary focus, any contracts they facilitate or require local school systems to enter into regarding safety services or equipment would be subject to these new prohibited provisions.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a catastrophic line-of-duty disability retirement benefit for members of the State Police Retirement System and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System. Members who are found to be totally and permanently unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity due to a medically determinable physical impairment resulting from a work-related accident are eligible for a disability allowance consisting of a pension equal to 100% of their average final compensation plus an annuity based on their accumulated contributions. The bill requires retirees to provide annual federal tax returns to the State Retirement Agency and provides for the reduction of benefits back to standard levels if the retiree resumes employment with a participating employer or engages in substantial gainful activity.
stakeholders: Members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) and the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), including those in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP), and participating state and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the disability retirement allowance for eligible members of the State Police Retirement System and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System from approximately 66.7% to 100% of their average final compensation. This enhancement will increase the actuarial liabilities and required annual employer contributions for the State and participating local governments. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary agency responsible for administering the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). This bill directly tasks the agency with managing new catastrophic disability benefit applications, verifying annual federal tax returns of retirees to ensure they are not engaged in substantial gainful activity, and reporting data to the Joint Committee on Pensions.

The bill directly modifies the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), which applies specifically to Maryland State Police officers. It creates a new catastrophic line-of-duty disability allowance equal to 100% of average final compensation for officers who are totally and permanently unable to engage in substantial gainful activity.

The bill modifies the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS). The Department of Natural Resources employs a significant number of law enforcement officers (Natural Resources Police) who are members of LEOPS and would be eligible for the enhanced catastrophic disability benefits.

The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) oversees the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) Police, whose officers are members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS). These officers are directly impacted by the changes to catastrophic disability benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services employs various law enforcement personnel who are members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS), making this bill highly relevant to the retirement benefits and disability protections of its workforce.

The State Treasurer chairs the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System and manages the state's funds. This bill affects pension payouts and requires the Board to oversee new application processes for catastrophic disability.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for the state's budget and employee benefits. Changes to pension allowances have a fiscal impact on state contributions and affect personnel policies for law enforcement agencies.

The Department of General Services manages the Maryland Capitol Police, whose officers are members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) and thus impacted by changes to disability retirement benefits.

The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works and the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System. Additionally, the bill requires disability retirees to submit federal tax returns for verification of gainful employment, which relates to the Comptroller's role as the state's tax collector and financial officer.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees. It would be responsible for advising on the legal implementation of the new disability standards and the enforcement of gainful activity restrictions.

Law enforcement officers employed by University System of Maryland institutions are typically members of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS), making these institutions impacted as employers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on public safety strategies and supports law enforcement. Enhancing disability benefits for catastrophic injuries is a policy matter concerning the welfare and recruitment/retention of law enforcement officers.
Morgan State University employs a police force whose members are part of the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS), which is affected by this bill.
St. Mary's College of Maryland employs law enforcement personnel under the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS) who would be affected by the bill.
The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the state agencies affected, and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation affecting the state pension system.

bill_summary: This bill establishes requirements for the retail sale of electricity for electric vehicles, requiring that it be sold in kilowatt-hours and that charging station owners display contact information. It mandates the Maryland Comptroller to set an annual minimum retail price and allows station owners to charge additional service fees based on time or as a fixed amount.

stakeholders: Electric vehicle owners, charging station owners and operators, and retail electricity providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Comptroller to determine and publish a minimum retail price for electricity as vehicle fuel annually, likely resulting in administrative costs. The Maryland Department of Agriculture may also incur costs for enforcement of measurement and display requirements. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because no formal Fiscal Note was included in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to annually determine and publish the minimum price for the retail sale of electricity as a vehicle fuel on the agency's website.

The bill amends Title 11 of the Agriculture Article of the Maryland Code. The Department of Agriculture's Weights and Measures program is responsible for regulating the devices and units of measure for retail fuel sales, which this bill expands to include electric vehicle charging.

The PSC regulates electricity rates and public utilities. This bill establishes a minimum retail price for electricity sold as vehicle fuel and standardizes units of measure (kWh) for that sale, which directly interacts with the Commission's regulatory oversight of electric service and energy suppliers.

As the state's energy policy lead, the MEA manages programs and strategies related to renewable energy and electric vehicle infrastructure. The bill's requirements for units of measure and pricing standards for EV fuel are central to their policy goals.

MDOT is responsible for the state's transportation network and is a primary driver of electric vehicle infrastructure deployment. Changes to retail pricing and labeling requirements will affect MDOT's management of charging stations at transit hubs and along state highways.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Agriculture and the Comptroller. They would be responsible for providing guidance on the enforcement of the new weights and measures requirements and the legality of the minimum price determinations.

DGS manages state facilities and leads sustainability initiatives, including the installation and management of EV charging stations for state-owned vehicles and facilities. They will need to ensure compliance with the new labeling and measurement standards.

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland law enforcement agencies to dispatch at least one officer to observe and report on immigration enforcement actions occurring within their jurisdiction. The responding officer is tasked with recording the event using a body-worn camera, ensuring safe custody transfers, filing a detailed report on the incident, and preserving evidence. fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are unavailable. bill_summary: This bill updates several definitions within the Maryland Land Use Article and modifies the structure and authority of local boards of appeals. stakeholders: Minors under the age of 18, law enforcement agencies, the Maryland Attorney General, and individuals prosecuted for or convicted of possessing or viewing prohibited visual representations of children.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases maximum criminal fines from $2,500 to $25,000 for first offenses and from $10,000 to $50,000 for repeat offenses, which may increase state revenue. It also doubles maximum incarceration terms, potentially increasing state and local expenditures. A new civil cause of action allows for punitive damages up to $250,000. The Attorney General's office will face increased administrative costs to produce mandated annual reports. Specific aggregate dollar estimates of the fiscal impact were not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Attorney General to submit an annual report to the General Assembly providing guidance to law enforcement on detecting computer-generated images, discussing technological changes, and tracking data on charges and prosecutions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly increases criminal penalties for possession and viewing of prohibited images, including doubling maximum prison sentences for first and subsequent offenses. The bill establishes a new civil cause of action allowing depicted persons to sue for actual and punitive damages. Additionally, the increase in criminal penalties and the expanded scope of the law (raising the child's age from 16 to 18) will impact judicial caseloads and sentencing procedures.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police will be the recipient of the Attorney General's guidance on detecting computer-generated images and will be responsible for investigating crimes under the expanded criminal statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates state public safety strategies and manages funds for law enforcement and victim services. The agency is responsible for protecting children from abuse and neglect. The bill's aim to combat child exploitation by expanding the legal definition of prohibited visual representations relates to the agency's mission to aid and protect vulnerable children.

The bill requires the Attorney General to report on technological changes and best practices for detecting computer-generated images. As the lead IT agency, they may serve as a partner for the technical expertise needed to develop these detection protocols.

The office is dedicated to the well-being of Maryland's children. While not an enforcement agency, the bill's focus on protecting children from digital exploitation and abuse aligns with their overarching mission of promoting child safety.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Workgroup to Study State Laws on Electric Bicycles. The workgroup is charged with reviewing Maryland's rules of the road for electric bicycles, analyzing safety data and injury rates involving e-bikes and other micro-mobility devices, and making recommendations for legal revisions to improve public safety. stakeholders: Electric bicycle riders, pedestrians, vehicle operators, state and local law enforcement agencies, and municipal and county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to provide staff for the workgroup. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Secretary of Transportation is a named member of the workgroup, and the department is explicitly tasked with providing staff support for its operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary workgroup to conduct a special study and provide recommendations, which falls directly under this collective entity's functional definition.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Transportation and the General Assembly and may be consulted regarding existing State laws on electric bicycles and proposed statutory revisions.

The workgroup is tasked with reviewing safety concerns for pedestrians, which includes people with disabilities who may be uniquely impacted by the use of micro-mobility devices on sidewalks and in public spaces.
The workgroup's mandate to review information from academic studies and data on injury rates involves health data analysis, potentially requiring collaboration with public health agencies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency overseeing trauma systems and prehospital care, MIEMSS maintains data regarding injuries related to motor vehicle and bicycle accidents, which is a required area of study for the workgroup.

Any recommended changes to the State's rules of the road for electric bicycles would ultimately impact the adjudication of traffic violations within the Maryland Judicial Branch.

stakeholders: Police officers employed by municipal law enforcement agencies and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's fiscal impact is limited to municipal governments. agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The bill directly impacts the agricultural community by exempting certain farm vehicles from insurance requirements. The MDA supports the economic viability of farming and would be interested in the cost-saving implications for Maryland farmers.

The MIA regulates the insurance market and monitors compliance with state insurance laws. This bill changes the scope of mandatory insurance requirements in Maryland, which is within the MIA's regulatory purview.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and the MVA. It would likely be involved in interpreting the legal boundaries of the 25-mile radius and the registration requirements to ensure the state correctly implements the exemption.

MAIF acts as the insurer of last resort and also processes claims involving uninsured motorists. An increase in legally uninsured vehicles on the road could potentially impact the volume or nature of claims handled by the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay

The bill requires economic impact statements for fisheries regulations that have a major impact on stakeholders, which includes the businesses and industries that the Department of Commerce is tasked with supporting and retaining.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs

The University System, particularly through institutions like the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES), provides the scientific research and data analysis used by the state to inform fisheries management and the development of required economic impact statements.

The bill expands the definition of unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act to include the failure to disclose tariffs on consumer goods, a provision enforced by the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill specifically identifies the Department of Information Technology as a coordination partner for the Department of Commerce to leverage digital infrastructure in the creation of the Maryland Local Sourcing Portal.
The bill explicitly names the Office of the Comptroller as a coordinating entity to assist the Department of Commerce in identifying potential local sources for inclusion in the sourcing portal.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM will be responsible for overseeing the budgetary execution and potential personnel requirements associated with the Department of Commerce establishing the new portal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The portal's objective to connect local businesses with supply chain opportunities aligns with this office's mission to facilitate economic opportunities and implement socioeconomic procurement programs for small businesses.

The Governor's Office oversees the Department of Commerce and coordinates policy initiatives across the executive branch, including the development of the sourcing portal and its impact on the State's economy.

bill_summary: This bill allows Maryland horse racing licensees to receive capital improvement grants from the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account without providing matching funds, provided they agree to continue live racing for at least 10 years after the improvements are finished. It also mandates that the State Racing Commission recapture grant funds if the racing requirement is not met and requires specific racetracks to spend at least $300,000 annually on capital maintenance to remain eligible for funding.
stakeholders: Horse racing licensees (specifically Rosecroft Raceway and Ocean Downs Racetrack), standardbred owners and trainers, and the Maryland State Racing Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill allows racing licensees to access Racetrack Facility Renewal Account grants without a 50% match requirement, potentially increasing the rate of expenditures from the account. Licensees must still meet a $300,000 minimum annual capital maintenance spend. A recapture provision is included for licensees who fail to meet a 10-year racing commitment. Specific dollar estimates for the total fiscal impact are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Racing Commission, which is the primary entity charged with administering the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account, approving capital construction plans, and implementing the new pro rata recapture provisions. The Secretary of Labor is also specifically mentioned regarding applications for operating assistance.

The bill explicitly requires racing licensees to submit their capital improvement plans to the Department of General Services. Furthermore, the State Racing Commission must consult with DGS to monitor the implementation of any approved capital construction plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Racetrack Facility Renewal Account is funded by revenues from video lottery terminals (casinos), which are regulated by this agency. Any changes to the grant requirements or fund management within the State Government Article, Subtitle 1A, affect the broader gaming revenue allocation framework the agency oversees.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the state's budget and supervising the execution of funds within special accounts like the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account, ensuring the fiscal integrity of the grant process.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to the State Racing Commission and the Department of Labor. It will be responsible for advising on the drafting of new regulations and the legal enforcement of the grant recapture provisions if a licensee fails to meet live racing requirements.
The Comptroller, as the state's chief financial officer, is involved in the collection of revenues that fund the account and the ultimate distribution of grant payments to licensees.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the State Racing Commission, which is responsible for implementing this legislation and adopting the required regulations.
The State Treasurer's Office is responsible for the management and distribution of state funds, including those held in the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Growth Initiative in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to support the growth of start-up companies; requiring the Initiative to create a certain list of companies in the State that are between certain growth phases according to a certain priority; establishing the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund to be administered by the Corporation as a special, nonlapsing fund; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget an appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Initiative; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Growth Initiative and the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO). The program is designed to support start-up companies in the transition phase between early-stage development and scaling. It provides these companies with access to industry experts, infrastructure support (such as office space and equipment), and technical expertise. TEDCO is required to prioritize companies that are previous recipients of TEDCO funding or are certified minority business enterprises.
stakeholders: Maryland start-up companies transitioning to the scaling phase, minority business enterprises, and current or prior recipients of Maryland Innovation Initiative or TEDCO funding.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates an annual State appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Maryland Growth Initiative. It creates the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by TEDCO. Interest earnings from the fund will be credited to the fund itself rather than the General Fund. While a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, the bill explicitly mandates this $5,000,000 annual expenditure.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Maryland Growth Initiative and the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund within TEDCO, making it the primary agency responsible for administering the new program, managing the fund, and curating the list of eligible start-up companies.

The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other state funds, with interest earnings being credited back to the fund.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund and manage the accrual of net interest to the fund rather than the General Fund.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a $5,000,000 annual appropriation in the state budget for the Maryland Growth Initiative and oversees the executive branch departments involved in the program.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for executing the Governor's $5,000,000 annual budget mandate and supervising the execution of the new Maryland Growth Initiative Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the initiative to give priority to Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs) in its curated list of companies, aligning with this agency's mission to monitor socioeconomic procurement and business programs.

The initiative's mission to support the scaling of start-up companies in Maryland and prevent their relocation overlaps with the Department of Commerce's core mission of business retention and economic development.
The OAG provides legal counsel to TEDCO and would be involved in reviewing the new regulations authorized by the bill and ensuring the legal integrity of the Maryland Growth Initiative Fund.

bill_summary: This bill allows active members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) who are eligible for vested benefits in the Local Fire and Police System (LFPS) to transfer their creditable service to the SPRS, regardless of any break in employment that occurred between their LFPS and SPRS service. This transfer must be requested by December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Active members of the State Police Retirement System with prior vested service in the Local Fire and Police System who had a break in employment.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill creates a mechanism for pension service credit transfers which typically affects the actuarial liabilities of the involved retirement systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the primary administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System and is specifically tasked by the bill with providing forms and processing service credit transfers for eligible members.
The bill directly impacts active members of the State Police Retirement System, who are employees of this agency, by allowing them to transfer prior creditable service from a different system.
As the state's principal personnel and fiscal agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and the long-term fiscal impact and liabilities of the state's pension systems.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and would advise on the implementation of the statutory override and service transfer regulations.

Synopsis: Approving certain projects for the acquisition, development, and improvement of certain academic facilities for the University System of Maryland; authorizing the issuance of bonds by the University System of Maryland in a certain total principal amount for financing the projects; and providing that the bonds are not a debt or obligation of the State or any of its subdivisions.

bill_summary: The bill authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue $50,000,000 in bonds to finance the acquisition, development, and improvement of specific academic facilities and systemwide capital renewal projects. Key projects include electrical substation improvements at Towson University, a Health and Human Sciences Complex at the University of Maryland, College Park, and deferred maintenance at the Rita Colwell Center.
stakeholders: University System of Maryland constituent institutions, students, and faculty.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill authorizes $50,000,000 in bonding authority for the University System of Maryland, including $26,000,000 for specific capital projects and $24,000,000 for systemwide renewal projects. As stated in the bill, these bonds are obligations of the University System and do not constitute a debt or obligation of the State of Maryland or any of its political subdivisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The University System of Maryland (USM) is the primary agency authorized by this bill to issue, sell, and deliver bonds for the acquisition and improvement of its academic facilities. The bill explicitly names USM as the entity responsible for the projects and the resulting debt obligations.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is responsible for long-term fiscal planning and overseeing budget execution. Since this bill authorizes a significant amount of bonding ($50 million) for state-affiliated institutions, DBM must coordinate these authorizations within the state's capital budget and fiscal framework.

The State Treasurer's Office manages the state's bond sales and overall debt position. While these bonds are not a direct debt of the state, the Treasurer monitors all state-related bonding activity and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees such capital improvements.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures, capital projects, and the acquisition or transfer of state property. The facility improvements at USM institutions authorized by this bill typically require review or reporting to the Board.

The Comptroller, as a member of the Board of Public Works and the state's chief financial officer, is involved in the oversight of state-related financial transactions and the fiscal integrity of expenditures related to state university facilities.

The Governor proposes the state budget and serves on the Board of Public Works. This bill is a departmental request from the executive branch, and the Governor must approve the capital authorizations included in the legislative package.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) coordinates statewide policies for colleges and universities. Capital projects and facility renewals at USM institutions are relevant to MHEC's role in planning and overseeing the state's higher education infrastructure.

Synopsis: Requiring a federal firearms licensee or law enforcement agency  operating a gun buyback program to destroy each firearm and all its component parts that is traded in as part of a gun buyback program; authorizing a licensee or agency to contract with a law enforcement agency or a business to destroy certain firearms; requiring a law enforcement agency operating a program to determine if a firearm is a crime firearm or has been reported lost or stolen before destroying the weapon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires federal firearms licensees and law enforcement agencies operating gun buyback programs to destroy all surrendered firearms and their components, making them permanently inoperable and unrepairable. It also mandates that law enforcement agencies make reasonable efforts to check if a firearm was stolen or used in a crime before destruction. Violations of these requirements result in fines of up to $10,000 and the mandatory revocation of firearms dealer licenses by the Secretary of State Police.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State Police and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Federal firearms licensees, law enforcement agencies, and individuals participating in gun buyback programs
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, which may increase state revenue. Law enforcement agencies and federal firearms licensees may incur indeterminate costs related to the destruction of firearms or the procurement of destruction services. No formal Fiscal Note with specific total expenditure or revenue estimates was included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police (MSP) is the primary agency impacted by this bill. The Secretary of State Police is explicitly tasked with the mandatory revocation of firearms dealer licenses for violations of the gun buyback protocols. Furthermore, as the state's primary law enforcement agency, MSP would be required to follow the destruction and verification requirements for any gun buyback programs it operates.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Police and other state agencies. It would be responsible for interpreting the legal requirements of the bill, advising on enforcement, and representing the state in any legal challenges or appeals related to license revocations or civil penalties.

The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) would handle contested administrative cases, such as appeals by firearms dealers whose licenses are revoked by the Secretary of State Police for failing to comply with the gun buyback destruction requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and manages state and federal grant funding for law enforcement programs. Because gun buyback programs are often funded through grants or coordinated as public safety initiatives, GOCPP would be relevant to the implementation and funding oversight of programs meeting the bill's criteria.

The bill establishes new misdemeanor penalties and civil fines for violations. The Judicial Branch, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, would be responsible for adjudicating criminal cases and handling judicial reviews of administrative penalties or license revocations.

The Department of Natural Resources operates the Natural Resources Police. As a law enforcement agency, it would be subject to the bill's requirements to verify the status of firearms and ensure their complete destruction if it conducts or participates in gun buyback programs.

MDOT oversees several modal administrations with their own police forces (e.g., Maryland Transit Administration and Maryland Transportation Authority Police). These agencies would be required to comply with the bill's firearm destruction and reporting protocols if they operate buyback programs.

The Department of General Services oversees the Maryland Capitol Police. As a law enforcement agency, it must comply with the bill's standards for firearm verification and destruction if it engages in gun buyback activities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for broader public safety and rehabilitation policy and manages some law enforcement functions. While not the primary regulator for firearms, it is involved in general public safety coordination and information sharing regarding criminal justice.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children. The Commission is charged with investigating the history, operations, and resident deaths at a former state detention facility in Prince George's County. Its duties include identifying children buried in unmarked graves through forensic and archaeological research, providing a public accounting of deaths, establishing a DNA database for descendants, promoting community reconciliation, and making recommendations for a permanent memorial and systemic reforms.
stakeholders: Descendants of children buried at the site, former residents of the House of Reformation, former justice-involved youth, academic experts in forensic anthropology and African American history, civil rights organizations, and the community of Prince George's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase to support the operations of the Commission, including staffing provided by the Office of the Attorney General, reimbursement for member expenses, and potential stipends for community members. The Commission is authorized to enter into major contracts with universities and research institutions for archaeological surveys, forensic anthropology, and DNA testing. While the bill specifies that funding will be provided through the State Budget and potential federal grants, specific dollar estimates are not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The commission established by the bill is an executive-branch body that must submit its initial and final reports to the Governor.
The bill specifies that funding for the commission and member reimbursements are provided in the State budget, which is overseen by DBM.
The commission is tasked with recommending educational initiatives to incorporate the institution's history into the State's curriculum.
The Secretary of General Services (or a designee) is a mandated member of the commission.
The commission must consult with the Department of Health regarding methods and safety for archaeological surveys and the disinterment of human remains.

The Secretary of Juvenile Services is a member of the commission; the institution being investigated was a juvenile detention facility, and the commission is granted access to confidential juvenile records.
The Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is housed within the Department of Planning, is a member of the commission and must be consulted on archaeological methods.
The commission's membership includes the Chief Archaeologist from MDOT's State Highway Administration.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families (or a designee) is a mandated member of the commission.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration is a mandated member of the commission, providing expertise for archaeological surveys of the burial grounds.
The bill grants the commission and its contractors unrestricted access to sealed or confidential juvenile records, which are managed by the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children as a new executive body.
The State Archivist is a mandated member of the commission, reflecting the agency's role in historical research and records management.
The commission must include at least one representative from a historically black college or university (HBCU) in the state, and Morgan State University is a primary candidate.
The Attorney General chairs the commission, appoints public members, manages the commission's funding and procurement, and provides its primary staffing.
The commission includes the Executive Director of the Gibson-Banks Center for Race and Law at the University of Maryland (a USM institution), and potentially a representative from a USM HBCU.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to allocate money from the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund to local workforce development boards under certain circumstances; altering certain workforce development programs to require inclusion of local workforce boards; requiring the Department to provide funding to a local workforce  board as part of a certain quick response program; requiring local workforce boards to provide grants to employers under the Apprenticeship Career Training in Our Neighborhoods Program; etc.

bill_summary: The Local Workforce Solutions Investment Act requires the Maryland Department of Labor to allocate funds from the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund to local workforce development boards during hospital closures or downsizings. It further integrates these local boards into the state's quick response program for mass layoffs and transfers the administration of grants for the Apprenticeship Career Training in Our Neighborhoods (ACTION) Program from the state department to local workforce development boards.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and local workforce development boards
stakeholders: Hospital employees, construction industry employers and apprentices, direct care workers, and local workforce development boards
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are unavailable. The bill requires the redistribution of existing funds, such as the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund and the ACTION Program grants, to local workforce development boards. It also mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor provide funding to these local boards for quick response services when funding is available. The ACTION Program, whose grant administration is shifted to local boards, has an existing annual funding intent of at least 100000 dollars.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Labor and Employment Article, tasking the Maryland Department of Labor with administering the Hospital Employees Retraining Fund, the quick response program, the ACTION Program, and direct care worker grants in partnership with local boards.
The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Labor to cooperate with the Workforce Development Board to develop mandatory guidelines for employers facing a reduction in operations.

The Secretary of Health is required to adopt regulations jointly with the Secretary of Labor for the hospital employee retraining program. Additionally, the department is a named consultant for the recruitment and retention of direct care workers.

The bill mandates the allocation of specific funds (Hospital Employees Retraining Fund) and references State budget appropriations for the ACTION Program, impacting the fiscal planning and budget execution duties of DBM.

The bill encourages entities receiving grants for direct care worker strategies to consult with institutions of higher education, which fall under the oversight and policy coordination of this commission.
As a collective of institutions of higher education, USM institutions are potential consultants for entities developing direct care worker recruitment and retention strategies under the bill.
As an institution of higher education, Morgan State University is a potential consultant for grant-funded projects related to direct care worker recruitment and retention.
As a public honors college, it is among the 'institutions of higher education' that grant recipients are encouraged to consult regarding direct care worker strategies.
