responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Persons and entities acquiring or being assigned mortgages or installment loans, and the Maryland Department of Labor's Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation.
fiscal_impact_summary: By removing licensing exemptions, the bill is expected to increase the number of licensed entities in the state, leading to an indeterminate increase in licensing fee revenue and administrative oversight costs. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor, through the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, is the primary regulator responsible for licensing financial institutions and consumer credit providers. This bill directly impacts the department's operations by repealing an exemption, thereby expanding its licensing and regulatory jurisdiction over entities that acquire or are assigned mortgages and installment loans.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor's financial regulatory division. Additionally, the OAG enforces state consumer protection laws, which are directly related to the regulation of consumer credit and lending practices addressed in this bill.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and supervising budget execution. The repeal of licensing exemptions for certain consumer credit entities will likely result in a fiscal impact through increased licensing fee revenues and potential administrative costs.

OAH provides an impartial forum for contested administrative cases. An expansion of licensing requirements may lead to an increase in administrative hearings resulting from license denials or enforcement actions taken by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the implementation of state laws. As this bill is identified as a corrective measure for a provision enacted in a previous legislative session, the office provides high-level policy coordination and oversight of the regulatory changes.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person or form from representing that certification by an attorney or under the attorney's supervision is the only method of certification for recordation of a certain deed and prohibiting a clerk of the circuit court from refusing to record a deed that is certified as being prepared by a party to the deed as authorized by law.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits any person or form document from representing that certification by an attorney is the sole method for certifying the preparation of a deed for recordation. Additionally, it prohibits a clerk of the circuit court from refusing to record a deed solely because it does not contain an attorney's certification, provided the deed contains a certification by a party named in the instrument.
stakeholders: Property owners, parties named in real property instruments, and Clerks of the Circuit Court
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, and the bill itself does not specify any financial mandates, revenue changes, or spending requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the duties and conduct of the Clerks of the Circuit Court, who are part of the Judicial Branch. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and legal support to the clerks and would be responsible for implementing these changes and ensuring uniform compliance with deed recordation requirements across Maryland's 24 jurisdictions.

As the state's chief financial officer and primary collector of state revenues, the Comptroller oversees the collection of recordation and transfer taxes performed by the Clerks of the Circuit Court. Any change to the procedural requirements for recording deeds has a nexus to the agency's revenue collection and auditing oversight.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Judiciary and the Clerks of the Circuit Court. They may be required to provide guidance on the interpretation of the new statutory requirements or represent the state in matters where recordation is challenged based on these new prohibitions.

bill_summary: This bill requires persons who recalibrate Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) to be licensed by the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA). It establishes standards for automotive repair facilities, including adherence to manufacturer specifications and providing specific disclosures to consumers. Additionally, it prohibits insurance companies from denying coverage for required ADAS recalibrations and classifies violations as unfair or deceptive trade practices subject to the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
stakeholders: Automotive repair facilities, body shops, motor vehicle safety glass facilities, insurance companies, and motor vehicle owners in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided. The bill establishes a new licensing requirement and civil penalties ranging from $1,000 to $5,000 per violation, which will generate revenue for the State. The Motor Vehicle Administration and the Maryland Insurance Administration will experience increased administrative costs to develop regulations and manage the licensing and enforcement processes. Specific dollar estimates for revenue and expenditures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Motor Vehicle Administration (referred to as the Administration) as the primary regulatory body responsible for licensing individuals and facilities that perform ADAS recalibrations. It also tasks the agency with adopting regulations, conducting inspections, and enforcing penalties and license revocations.

The bill requires the MIA to consult on the development of licensing regulations and explicitly tasks it with disciplining insurance companies that violate the new standards regarding repair estimates and coverage for ADAS recalibrations.

As the parent department of the MVA, MDOT oversees the state's transportation laws and the modal administrations. The bill creates a significant new regulatory and licensing framework within the Transportation Article that MDOT's MVA will manage.

The bill classifies violations of the new ADAS recalibration standards as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the OAG. The OAG also provides legal representation for the MVA and MIA.

OAH would be responsible for presiding over contested cases and appeals resulting from the MVA's new authority to suspend or revoke licenses and impose civil penalties on automotive repair facilities.

As a state agency that functions as an automobile insurer of last resort, MAIF would be directly impacted by the bill's requirements governing mandatory coverage for OEM-recommended repairs and the specific line-item requirements for insurance estimates.

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC), in consultation with the Attorney General and the Maryland Hospital Association, to develop and publish a model policy for hospitals concerning their response to immigration enforcement actions. Most hospitals in the State are required to adopt a policy describing their protocols for such actions, post the policy on their websites, and provide annual training to all staff members to ensure the protocols are understood and followed.
responsible_party: State Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, hospital staff, patients, and guests
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the source text. However, the bill creates new administrative responsibilities for the State Health Services Cost Review Commission and mandates that hospitals implement policies and provide annual staff training, which will result in indeterminate administrative and operational costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) to develop and publish a model policy regarding hospital responses to immigration enforcement actions and to consult with other stakeholders to fulfill this requirement.

bill_summary: This bill allows individuals who enroll in health insurance during a special enrollment period due to pregnancy to choose the effective date of their coverage. Individuals can select either the first day of the month in which the pregnancy was confirmed or the first day of the month following their plan selection. bill_summary: This bill mandates that employers with workers exposed to temperatures of at least 80 degrees Fahrenheit, whether indoors or outdoors, develop and implement a heat-related illness prevention plan. Additionally, it requires acclimatization protocols for new or returning employees, emergency response planning, and annual heat stress training for all staff and supervisors.

stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees working in conditions of 80 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, excluding certain emergency services and incidental exposures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Parole Commission is a unit within this department. The bill removes the Secretary's direct appointment power over commissioners but designates the Secretary as a member of the newly created nominating panel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that this office provide staffing support for the newly created panel responsible for nominating candidates for the Maryland Parole Commission.
This office assists the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of candidates for boards and commissions and would manage the administrative process for the new nominating panel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender of Maryland is designated as a mandatory member of the panel responsible for selecting and submitting nominees for the Maryland Parole Commission to the Governor.
The State Superintendent of Schools is designated as a mandatory member of the newly created panel responsible for nominating candidates for the Maryland Parole Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new nominating panel, which functions as an advisory and recommendatory body to the Governor for filling vacancies on the Maryland Parole Commission.
As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG would provide legal guidance on the implementation of the new appointment process and the operations of the nominating panel.
DBM oversees state personnel and budget execution and would be involved if the staffing requirements for the new panel at GOCPP require additional resource allocation.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the requirements for vehicle manufacturers or distributors of battery-electric or nonfossil-fuel vehicles to be licensed as dealers in Maryland. It requires that manufacturers seeking a license are not affiliated with or controlled by any manufacturer that has franchised dealers in the State. Additionally, it limits the total number of these specific dealer licenses to four and requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to adopt implementing regulations.
stakeholders: Vehicle manufacturers and distributors of battery-electric or nonfossil-fuel vehicles, franchised vehicle dealers, and the Motor Vehicle Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. Financial implications may include administrative costs for the Motor Vehicle Administration to adopt new regulations and process license applications.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary agency responsible for licensing vehicle dealers. This bill directly tasks the MVA with verifying manufacturer compliance with the new battery-electric requirements and mandates that the agency adopt implementing regulations.
As the parent department for the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees state transportation policy, including the regulations governing how vehicles are sold and distributed within Maryland.

This bill impacts the business climate and economic development for electric vehicle manufacturers. Changes to dealer licensing laws are a significant factor for companies looking to establish a direct-to-consumer presence in the state.

The bill focuses specifically on battery-electric and non-fossil-fuel vehicles, aligning with the agency's mission to promote clean energy and reduce reliance on fossil fuels in the transportation sector.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the MVA regarding the drafting of new regulations and would represent the state in any legal challenges regarding franchise laws or licensing denials.
The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases, including disputes over regulatory enforcement and the denial or revocation of motor vehicle-related licenses.
The bill pertains to the distribution of zero-emission vehicles, which supports MDE's environmental protection goals regarding air quality and climate change mitigation.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a moratorium on the implementation and enforcement of State energy efficiency and conservation programs, services, and plans starting July 1, 2026. It requires the Public Service Commission to continue current rate-making policies until electric and gas companies recover all unpaid and unamortized costs incurred for these programs prior to the moratorium. After full cost recovery is achieved, the Commission must submit a report to the General Assembly recommending whether the moratorium should be rescinded.
stakeholders: Electric and gas companies, Maryland utility customers, and State government agencies involved in energy efficiency oversight.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a moratorium on energy efficiency programs, which will impact future State expenditures and utility customer surcharges. It specifically mandates the recovery of utility costs incurred before July 1, 2026. Specific dollar estimates for the fiscal impact are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary agency named in the bill, responsible for managing utility cost recovery, overseeing the moratorium on energy efficiency programs, and submitting a final report and recommendation to the General Assembly.

As the state's principal agency for maximizing energy efficiency and coordinating energy planning, the MEA's core mission is directly impacted by a moratorium on implementing or enforcing energy efficiency and conservation programs.

The OPC represents residential utility consumers in proceedings regarding rates and service quality; the bill's changes to the EmPOWER Maryland surcharges and energy efficiency programs are a central focus of their advocacy work.
The MCEC's mission to advance the adoption of energy efficiency technologies is directly challenged by a legislative moratorium on the implementation of state energy efficiency programs and services.

The bill explicitly references the greenhouse gas emissions reduction goals managed by MDE, and the moratorium on efficiency programs directly impacts the state's ability to meet those environmental targets.
The department administers various energy efficiency and weatherization programs that are typically funded or coordinated through the state energy efficiency framework targeted by this bill.

As the agency responsible for the maintenance of state-owned facilities and lead for sustainability initiatives, DGS is directly affected by a prohibition on state units implementing energy efficiency plans.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and other state agencies, and would be responsible for interpreting the legal scope of the moratorium on existing statutory duties.
The suspension of energy efficiency programs and the resulting changes to utility rate-making policies affect Maryland's economic competitiveness and the operational costs for businesses.
DHS manages energy assistance for vulnerable populations; the availability and funding of efficiency programs are key factors in reducing the long-term utility burden on their clients.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments affected by the moratorium and is responsible for the broader policy initiatives regarding the state's energy future and budget planning.

bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of cottage food products to include nonpotentially hazardous foods and establishes a new category for 'home bakeries.' It allows home-based businesses with annual revenues of up to $50,000 to produce and sell various baked goods, including potentially hazardous ones, without a state food license, provided they meet specific labeling, safety training, and inspection requirements.
stakeholders: Home-based bakers, cottage food business owners, Maryland consumers, retail food stores, and food cooperatives.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable. Financial implications include a potential decrease in licensing fee revenue for the State and local health departments due to the exemption for home bakeries with revenues under $50,000. The Maryland Department of Health will also incur costs associated with adopting new regulations and investigating complaints regarding home bakeries.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary regulatory agency for cottage food businesses and home bakeries. The bill tasks the Department with adopting regulations, defining nonpotentially hazardous foods, providing unique identification numbers for labeling, conducting inspections, investigating complaints, and reporting annually to the General Assembly.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health. The agency will be involved in reviewing the new regulations required by the bill and providing legal support for the investigation and enforcement provisions related to home bakeries and cottage food businesses.

The bill explicitly states that it does not exempt cottage food businesses or home bakeries from state tax laws. As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for ensuring these micro-businesses comply with income and sales tax requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office connects the small business community to economic opportunities and monitors socioeconomic programs. The bill supports the creation and expansion of home-based micro-businesses, which falls within the office's interest in small business development and advocacy.

The bill specifically mentions the sale of products at farmers' markets. The Department of Agriculture provides support to the agricultural community and promotes local agricultural products, often overseeing the markets where cottage food and home bakery products are primarily sold.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. If the Department of Health takes enforcement action against a home bakery or cottage food business for non-compliance or safety violations, the owner has the right to a hearing before an Administrative Law Judge at this agency.

The Rural Maryland Council addresses challenges in rural counties and supports economic development. Cottage food businesses and home bakeries are common micro-enterprises in rural areas that utilize local agricultural resources, fitting the Council's mission to improve quality of life and economic vitality.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services to support the sustainability of Maryland's agricultural and seafood industries. Home bakeries and cottage food businesses are part of the value-added agricultural sector, and this bill modifies the regulatory landscape for these small-scale food producers.

Synopsis: Requiring the Power Plant Research Program to make certain recommendations to the Governor's Energy Subcabinet on or before a certain date; requiring the Subcabinet to make a certain assessment and recommendations to the Maryland Stadium Authority; requiring the Subcabinet to report certain information on or before a certain date; and requiring the Authority to conduct certain feasibility studies and to submit certain information on or before a certain date.
Title: Maryland Stadium Authority - Electricity Generating Facilities - Site Planning

bill_summary: This bill requires the Power Plant Research Program to identify and recommend 5 to 10 sites in Maryland suitable for the rapid development of electricity generating facilities with a combined capacity of over 3,000 megawatts. These recommendations are reviewed by the Governor's Energy Subcabinet, which then directs the Maryland Stadium Authority to conduct feasibility studies on the selected sites. The studies must evaluate how the facilities will meet state electricity needs, provide competitive pricing, and adhere to environmental and emissions standards.
stakeholders: Maryland electricity consumers including residents, businesses, hospitals, and schools, as well as state energy and environment agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill establishes new research and reporting mandates for the Power Plant Research Program and requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to conduct feasibility studies for multiple sites, which will result in indeterminate administrative and operational expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill identifies the Authority as a primary implementing agency, requiring it to conduct feasibility studies for recommended electricity generating sites and submit findings to the Board of Public Works and the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly tasks the Power Plant Research Program, which is established under the Natural Resources Article and housed within this department, to lead the study and recommend potential sites for energy facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Energy Subcabinet, a collective executive body, is centrally responsible for assessing site recommendations, providing final site lists to the Stadium Authority, and reporting findings to the Governor.
The bill mandates that the Power Plant Research Program consult with the Maryland Energy Administration while conducting the study of suitable electricity generating sites.
The bill requires the Power Plant Research Program to consult with this department on site recommendations, particularly as the studies must address clean air, clean water, and environmental impacts.
The Department of Planning is a named consultant in the bill for the site selection study, reflecting its role in land use planning and sustainable growth.

The bill requires the Power Plant Research Program to consult with the Department of Commerce during the site selection study, likely due to the economic development implications of 3,000 megawatt facilities.
The Maryland Stadium Authority is required to submit its completed feasibility studies and descriptions of the planned facilities to the Board of Public Works for review.
The bill requires the Energy Subcabinet to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor, and it involves oversight of an executive subcabinet and the Maryland Stadium Authority.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller will review the feasibility studies and facility descriptions submitted by the Maryland Stadium Authority.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer will review the feasibility studies and facility descriptions submitted by the Maryland Stadium Authority.
The bill's focus on siting high-capacity electricity generation while maintaining clean water and air standards aligns with this multi-agency initiative's goals for sustainable development.

The bill concerns the siting of 'electricity generating facilities,' which fall under the primary regulatory and licensing jurisdiction of the Commission, although the agency is not specifically named in the study phase.
The bill includes solar, wind, and geothermal facilities in its scope, which directly relates to the Center's mission to advance clean energy technologies.
The agency has a fiscal interest in the funding of the site selection study and the subsequent feasibility studies conducted by the Stadium Authority.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the multiple executive agencies and the Stadium Authority tasked with implementation and reporting requirements under this bill.

Synopsis: Altering the uses of the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund and certain compliance fees; requiring the Maryland Energy Administration, in consultation with the Public Service Commission, to develop and conduct certain annual, competitive, low-bid alternative compliance fee auctions for the development of certain renewable energy generation projects; establishing the purpose and procedures for an auction and the eligibility requirements for certain bidders; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA), in consultation with the Public Service Commission (PSC), to establish an annual competitive bidding process known as the Alternative Compliance Fee Auction. This auction is designed to award contracts to developers for renewable energy generation projects, specifically solar, geothermal, and offshore wind. Funding for these contracts will come from Alternative Compliance Fees (ACFs) paid by electricity suppliers who fail to meet the state's Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard. The bill transitions the use of these fees from existing specialized programs and grants into this centralized, low-bid auction system to help Maryland reach its renewable energy capacity targets.
stakeholders: Renewable energy project developers, Maryland electricity suppliers, the Public Service Commission, and Maryland residents, including low-to-moderate income communities that previously received prioritized funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill redirects existing revenue streams within the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) derived from Alternative Compliance Fees (ACFs). It shifts the allocation of these fees from previous mandates—such as direct grants for customer-sited solar and geothermal systems for small or minority-owned businesses—to a new competitive auction for large-scale renewable projects. While the total revenue from fees is not modified by this bill, the text explicitly references the redirection of up to $100,000,000 in compliance fees for fiscal year 2026. Administrative costs for the MEA and PSC will likely increase to manage the annual auction and mandated reporting.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's requirements. MEA must administer the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), conduct the annual renewable energy auctions, set capacity targets and thresholds, award contracts, and adopt necessary regulations.

The bill requires the Public Service Commission (PSC) to consult with MEA on the development and conduct of auctions, the setting of capacity targets, the procurement methodology, and the adoption of regulations. The PSC also regulates the compliance fees that fund the auction program.

The SEIF is funded in part by proceeds from the sale of allowances under the Environment Article, and the fund is used to pay costs for the Air and Radiation Administration within MDE. The bill also references environmental justice definitions managed by MDE.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to MEA and PSC during the development of the auction process, the drafting of contracts for awarded bids, and the creation of new regulations under the added subtitle.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals existing provisions that specifically allocated compliance fee revenue to promote the growth of small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses in the geothermal sector.

DBM oversees the state's budget and personnel. As the bill alters the use and allocation of the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (a special fund), it has a direct fiscal impact on the state budget and agency resource management.

The Treasurer manages the state's funds and investments, including the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. The bill also involves bidders posting bonds or similar financial instruments, which falls under the Treasurer's expertise in protecting state funds.

The bill requires bidders to agree to be subject to all applicable taxes. As the state's principal tax collector and financial officer, the Comptroller's office would be involved in ensuring tax compliance for participating entities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a competitive, low-bid procurement-style auction process. The MSBCA is the independent unit responsible for adjudicating bid protests and contract disputes involving state agencies, which could arise from this new program.

The bill promotes large-scale renewable energy generation projects, which are significant economic development activities that attract business investment and impact Maryland's competitive energy landscape.
The bill repeals a specific provision that previously allowed compliance fees to be used for solar development on State government property, which is managed by DGS.

As the state's green bank, the Maryland Clean Energy Center's mission is to advance the adoption of clean energy and financing solutions, which aligns closely with the bill's goal of funding renewable energy generation projects.

The Governor's Office oversees MEA and the executive branch's policy initiatives. This bill represents a significant shift in the state's energy and environmental strategy, impacting the Governor's annual budget proposals.

Synopsis: Correcting certain errors or omissions in certain articles of the Annotated Code and the Public Local Laws of Maryland; clarifying language; correcting certain obsolete references; reorganizing certain sections of the Annotated Code; providing that the Act is not intended to affect any law other than to correct technical errors; and providing for the correction of certain errors and obsolete provisions by the publishers of the Annotated Code.

bill_summary: The Annual Corrective Bill is a technical measure designed to fix errors, omissions, and obsolete references within the Annotated Code of Maryland and the Public Local Laws. It corrects grammatical mistakes, misnomers, and cross-references, and reorganizes certain sections to improve clarity without intending to make substantive changes to the law.
stakeholders: Maryland state agencies, the legal community, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: As a technical and nonsubstantive corrective bill, this legislation has no direct fiscal impact on state or local expenditures or revenues. A formal fiscal note with specific dollar estimates was not provided in the text, but the bill's nature precludes financial mandates or revenue changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly renames the agency from the 'Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services' to the 'Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy' in several sections of the Annotated Code.

The bill contains extensive technical corrections to the Education Article, including provisions related to school funding formulas, special education service delivery models, and nutritional standards for the school breakfast program.

The bill makes numerous technical corrections across the Transportation Article, affecting reporting requirements for zero-emission buses, vehicle registration protocols, and equipment standards for emergency vehicles.

The bill updates various sections of the Health - General and Health Occupations articles, including correcting references to the AHEAD Model state agreement and updating terminology related to substance use disorders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects names of divisions within the department, updates procedures for inmate evaluations, and clarifies notification requirements for the reemployment of retired correctional officers.
The bill updates specific sections of the Transportation Article regarding vehicle titling between spouses and the registration of organ delivery vehicles as emergency vehicles.
The bill adds definitions for the Secretary and Department of Disabilities within the Human Services Article and confirms the department's oversight of the Ethan Saylor Alliance.
The bill makes technical corrections to the Labor and Employment Article, specifically regarding definitions of gross misconduct for unemployment insurance and eligibility for apprenticeship grants.
The bill updates the Land Use Article by renaming 'visions' to 'planning principles,' a core component of the state's comprehensive planning framework managed by the department.
The bill requires state agencies to notify the Retirement Agency regarding retirees who are reemployed on a contractual basis within the correctional system.
The bill clarifies language regarding safety grants and training programs, such as those for school resource officers and behavioral health services, which are administered by the Center.
The bill corrects language in the Public Utilities Article regarding community choice aggregation and maintenance requirements for investor-owned electric companies.
The bill corrects references to the 'Secretary' in the State Finance and Procurement Article and makes technical adjustments to the State Personnel and Pensions Article.
The bill updates the Environment Article, correcting language regarding groundwater recharge permits and the names of legislative committees to which the department must report.
The bill reorganizes and updates definitions within the Housing and Community Development Article, particularly concerning 'sustainable communities' and subcabinet coordination.
The bill corrects reporting requirements related to the implementation of zero-emission bus procurement and infrastructure projects.
The bill makes technical corrections to laws involving speed monitoring systems and work zone speed control, which are primary operational areas for the SHA.
As the state's chief tax collector, the Comptroller is impacted by technical corrections to the Tax - General Article and sections involving the Central Collection Unit.
The bill clarifies the Treasurer's authority to invest monies from the Safe Schools Fund and corrects references related to state financial management.
The bill modifies the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, specifically regarding the payment of penalties to the District Court for traffic-related monitoring citations.
The bill makes technical corrections to procurement contract clauses and processes for modifying minority business enterprise participation goals, which fall under the Board's oversight.
The bill corrects references to the Secretary of General Services regarding the approval of capital project designs and planning programs.
The bill updates references to nonvisual access standards for information technology procurement, which are managed and adopted by DoIT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects the terminology regarding the Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program participation goals in the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The bill formalizes the change of 'visions' to 'planning principles' and references the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, both central to this multi-agency initiative.
The bill corrects technical references to the AHEAD Model State Agreement with CMS, which is a major regulatory framework administered by the Commission.
The bill reorganizes definitions and makes technical corrections to sections of the Human Services Article, particularly regarding assistive technology programs.
The bill makes technical corrections to the Education Article regarding nonresident tuition exemptions for military families at public institutions of higher education.
The bill corrects the names of various executive sub-cabinets, councils, and offices that provide administrative support and policy coordination for the Governor.
The bill updates references to USDA standards for school meal programs, which aligns with the department's role in promoting food quality and agricultural standards.
Technical corrections to standard offer services and community choice aggregation in the Public Utilities Article impact the regulatory environment in which the OPC advocates for consumers.
The bill corrects sections of the Real Property Article regarding condominium newsletters and governing body vacancies, which are areas overseen by the Secretary of State.
The bill mentions that the Center for firearm violence reduction must work in consultation with the Maryland State Police to ensure a multidepartmental approach to safety.

bill_summary: This bill requires local election directors to immediately remove deceased individuals from the statewide voter registration list upon receiving reports from the Maryland Department of Health, the Social Security Administration, or vital statistics agencies in other states. It replaces the previous requirement to mail a notice and wait for a response before removal. The bill also establishes oversight procedures for the State Board of Elections to ensure local compliance, including the authority to mandate corrective action plans, require staff retraining, and withhold discretionary election funds from noncompliant local boards.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, local boards of elections, the State Board of Elections, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. Financial implications identified in the bill text include the potential withholding of discretionary election administration funds from local boards that fail to comply with registration list maintenance requirements and costs associated with mandatory staff retraining or audits by the Office of Legislative Audits for noncompliant jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for supervising elections and managing the statewide voter registration list. This bill directly mandates procedures for the State Administrator and local boards regarding the immediate removal of deceased voters and grants the State Board enforcement authority over non-compliant local boards.

The Maryland Department of Health is explicitly required by the bill to report names and addresses of individuals reported deceased in the State to the State Administrator, serving as a primary data source for updating the voter registration list.
The bill authorizes the State Board of Elections to refer local boards that are persistently non-compliant with voter registration list maintenance requirements to the Office of Legislative Audits.

The bill amends Section 3-504 of the Election Law Article, which defines reporting requirements for the clerks of the circuit courts and administrative clerks of the District Courts regarding felony convictions and name changes, both of which are managed under the AOC's operational oversight.

bill_summary: The Utility Affordability and Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026 requires that utility energy efficiency, conservation, and demand response programs provide demonstrable bill savings to residential customers. It extends the deadline for electric and gas companies to eliminate certain unamortized program costs from 2032 to 2040 and mandates that the Public Service Commission establish caps or limits on residential assessments for these programs by July 1, 2027.
stakeholders: Residential electric and gas customers, electric and gas utility companies, and midsize electric cooperatives.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill shifts the timeline for utilities to recover unamortized energy program costs by extending the recovery deadline from 2032 to 2040. It also requires the Public Service Commission to set caps on residential assessments to reduce customer costs. These changes will likely decrease immediate ratepayer charges but extend the duration of those charges over a longer period. Specific state or local fiscal estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulator for the electric and gas utilities affected by this bill. The bill specifically mandates the Commission to establish cost caps, limit residential assessments, review energy efficiency plans for demonstrable bill savings, and submit a progress report to the General Assembly.

The Office of the People's Counsel is the statutory advocate for residential utility consumers. Since the bill's primary purpose is 'Utility Affordability and Ratepayer Protection' for residential customers, the OPC will play a critical role in representing consumer interests during the Commission's implementation of these new requirements.

In the Public Utilities Article, 'the Department' referenced in Section 7-222 is the Department of Housing and Community Development. The agency is directly responsible for developing and implementing energy efficiency and conservation programs for low-income residential sectors that are part of the state's broader energy strategy modified by this bill.

The Maryland Energy Administration coordinates state energy policy and manages programs related to energy efficiency and demand response. Changes to utility-led conservation programs and their cost-recovery mechanisms directly impact the state energy strategies overseen by the MEA.

The bill explicitly links utility energy efficiency and demand response programs to the state's greenhouse gas emissions reduction goals. The Department of the Environment is the lead agency responsible for monitoring and implementing these environmental targets.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits state and local government officials, employees, and contractors from entering into nondisclosure agreements with entities involved in economic development activities, specifically including those establishing or operating data centers. It also expands the Maryland Public Information Act by defining public service companies as instrumentalities of the State, thereby making their records subject to public disclosure requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Economic Development, Maryland General Assembly, local governing bodies, and public service companies.
stakeholders: State and local government employees, contractors, and consultants; businesses involved in economic development projects; data center operators; public service companies; and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill may result in indeterminate administrative costs for state and local agencies and public service companies due to expanded Public Information Act compliance requirements. The bill significantly alters Maryland civil law by changing the evidentiary standard for punitive damages from 'actual malice' to 'gross negligence' and abrogating long-standing judicial precedent, which impacts civil litigation and state legal policy.

bill_summary: The Internet Poker Authorization and Regulation Act of 2026 authorizes the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to issue licenses for internet skill-based gaming, specifically including internet poker and other games like backgammon or chess. The bill establishes a licensing framework for video lottery operators, sports wagering licensees, and other qualified applicants, including specific provisions for minority-owned businesses. It sets a regulatory structure for taxation, revenue distribution, and consumer protections such as age verification and problem gambling resources. Additionally, it empowers the Governor to enter into multijurisdictional gaming agreements with other governments.

stakeholders: Potential internet skill-based gaming operators (including video lottery facility operators and sports wagering licensees), minority-owned business applicants, Maryland residents aged 21 and older, Maryland horse racing industry participants, small and minority-owned businesses, and public school students via the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates new state revenue through an initial internet skill-based gaming license fee of $1,000,000 ($500,000 for majority minority-owned applicants) and a 30% state share of gaming proceeds. Licensees are permitted to retain 70% of proceeds. While the bill specifies fee amounts and allocation percentages, a formal Fiscal Note with total projected revenue and expenditure estimates is not provided, making total annual dollar estimates unavailable.

OAH may be required to adjudicate contested cases related to license denials, revocations, or penalties imposed by the Commission.
As the custodian of state funds, the Treasurer's office will manage the deposit and protection of the new revenues generated by Internet gaming licenses and proceeds.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to license and regulate internet gaming and online bingo in Maryland, subject to approval by a statewide voter referendum in November 2026. It establishes a licensing framework for casino operators, sports wagering licensees, and social equity applicants, while creating a tax structure for gaming proceeds. The revenue generated is primarily directed to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund for public education, but also supports problem gambling programs, the horse racing industry, and a new fund for casino employees displaced by online gaming.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Potential online gamblers, video lottery facility operators, commercial bingo operators, social equity applicants for gaming licenses, displaced casino employees, and Maryland public school students and administrators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill generates state revenue through initial license fees (ranging from $250,000 to $1,000,000) and a share of internet gaming and online bingo proceeds (between 20% and 40% of gross receipts). The State distributes these funds to several accounts, including the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, the Purse Dedication Account, and the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account. A specific allocation of up to $10,000,000 is mandated for the Video Lottery Facility Employee Displacement Fund during the first year. Local jurisdictions receive 5% of all gaming proceeds for education, in addition to fixed annual distributions for local impact starting at $6,500,000 in fiscal year 2028 and increasing annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is authorized to enter into multijurisdictional Internet gaming agreements upon recommendation from the Commission. The bill also affects the Governor's policy priorities regarding revenue for education and small business support.
The Comptroller is responsible for the control and distribution of gaming and bingo proceeds as directed by the bill, including transfers to the State Lottery Fund and various dedicated accounts.
The State Treasurer is tasked with holding the new Video Lottery Facility Employee Displacement Fund and investing its money.
The OAG must be consulted by the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to establish a plan for minority business participation goals and procedures.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency and will oversee the budget execution of the new Video Lottery Facility Employee Displacement Fund and the distribution of revenues to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.
The bill requires certain licensees to commit to building live gaming or film production studios under the auspices of the Maryland Film Office, which is housed within the Department of Commerce.

The bill provides a significant new revenue stream for the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund and modifies how local jurisdictions meet education funding requirements using internet gaming proceeds.
The bill mandates coordination with the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling (typically overseen via MDH Behavioral Health) regarding voluntary exclusion lists and annual impact reports.
The Department of Labor is designated to administer the Video Lottery Facility Employee Displacement Fund, including job training and supplemental unemployment payments for displaced workers.
MHEC coordinates policy for higher education institutions; the bill specifically names Morgan State and Bowie State (part of the USM) as recipients of gaming data and metrics.

The bill authorizes multijurisdictional gaming agreements with other governments, which involves the diplomatic and intergovernmental coordination functions of this division within the Secretary of State.
The authorization for multijurisdictional Internet gaming agreements effectively creates or utilizes interstate compact-like structures for regulatory cooperation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is specifically required to establish a plan for setting minority business enterprise participation goals for the procurement of goods and services related to internet gaming.
The requirement for licensees to build studios under the Maryland Film Office (within the same division as Tourism) impacts the state's promotional and cultural infrastructure.
The bill is subject to a referendum of the qualified voters of the State in November 2026, and the Board of Elections is tasked with conducting this referendum.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission and Agency are the primary regulators for the new internet gaming and online bingo programs, responsible for licensing, oversight, and accounting of all proceeds.
The bill explicitly requires internet gaming licensees to provide annual transactional data and metrics to Morgan State University.
OLA will be responsible for fiscal compliance and performance audits of the new funds and distributions established by this bill.
The bill requires licensees to enter into labor peace agreements and maintain neutrality on unionization, areas falling under PERB's jurisdiction for labor relations and collective bargaining.
Bowie State University, a member of the USM, is specifically designated to receive transactional data and metrics related to internet gaming.

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to establish new congressional districts for Maryland to be used for elections held after the 2026 general election until the 2030 census redistricting. It clarifies that state constitutional requirements for compactness and population equality apply specifically to Maryland General Assembly districts and authorizes the General Assembly to grant the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction to review congressional redistricting plans.
responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly, Maryland State Board of Elections, and the Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for the U.S. House of Representatives, and state election officials
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text, and therefore specific dollar estimates for the state or local fiscal impact are unavailable. The implementation of the new congressional boundaries would likely result in administrative costs for the State Board of Elections and local election boards to update voting system maps and notify affected voters.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the districts for the election of Representatives in Congress and requires the State Board of Elections to administer a statewide constitutional amendment on the 2026 ballot. SBE is responsible for implementing these new boundaries in future election cycles and managing the voter registration system accordingly.

The bill explicitly references the Maryland Department of Planning as the entity responsible for reviewing and correcting the geographical boundaries of the precincts used to define the new congressional districts. MDP provides the GIS and census data critical to redistricting.

The bill proposes a constitutional amendment that would authorize the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review the congressional districting of the State, directly impacting the operations and jurisdiction of the judiciary.

As the chief legal officer for the State, the OAG will be responsible for providing counsel on the implementation of the new districts, defending the redistricting plan in court, and advising on the constitutional amendment process.

The Secretary of State is the custodian of the state's official records, including the laws passed by the General Assembly and constitutional amendments. The agency also handles the certification of ballot questions and election results as the custodian of the Great Seal.

The bill requires that election returns for the constitutional amendment be made to the Governor and that the Governor issue a proclamation if the amendment is adopted. The Governor's Office also oversees the executive branch's role in the legislative and redistricting processes.

DBM is responsible for the fiscal oversight of state agencies. Implementing new congressional districts and conducting a statewide referendum involves administrative and personnel costs that fall under DBM's fiscal management and budget execution oversight.

The Archives is the central depository for government records of permanent value, including executive orders, laws, and the official geographical descriptions and maps of election districts created by this bill.

bill_summary: The bill prohibits merchants from using 'surveillance-based price setting,' which involves adjusting prices for goods or services based on consumer data profiling or device information. It also bans food retailers with at least 15,000 square feet of space from using electronic shelving labels, requiring them to use traditional nondigital price displays. Furthermore, the bill prohibits employers from using 'surveillance-based wage setting' to determine employee pay through automated systems and surveillance data. Violations are subject to enforcement under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act or investigation by the Maryland Commissioner of Labor and Industry.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General and the Maryland Commissioner of Labor and Industry
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, employees, and food retailers with at least 15,000 square feet of business space.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text. Explicit financial implications include potential increases in State revenue from civil penalties for violations of the Maryland Consumer Protection Act and indeterminate enforcement costs for the Office of the Attorney General and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry. Affected food retailers will incur costs to transition from electronic to nondigital shelving labels. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates violations of the surveillance-based pricing and electronic shelving label sections as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the OAG's Division of Consumer Protection enforces. Additionally, the OAG is authorized to bring legal actions against employers for wage-setting violations.

The bill task the Commissioner of Labor with investigating complaints regarding surveillance-based wage setting and attempting to resolve violations through mediation, making them a primary regulatory authority for the labor provisions of the act.

The bill significantly impacts the operations and technology adoption of large food retailers and other merchants in Maryland by prohibiting electronic shelving labels and surveillance-based pricing strategies, which falls under the department's purview of monitoring the state's business environment.

As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM would need to ensure that the state government, as an employer, complies with the prohibition on surveillance-based wage setting and automated decision system disclosures if such technologies were utilized for state employees.

The bill's definition of a 'food retailer' relies on Section 11-206(c) of the Tax - General Article, which concerns food sales exempt from sales and use tax, an area administered by the Comptroller's office.

The bill regulates the use of 'automated decision systems' and 'artificial intelligence' in employment contexts, which intersects with DoIT's role in overseeing the state's IT strategy and data governance policies.

By creating new prohibitions under the Consumer Protection Act and the Labor and Employment Article, the bill may lead to increased civil litigation and enforcement actions within the state court system.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies tasked with implementing and enforcing this bill, specifically the Department of Labor and the Department of Commerce.

bill_summary: Senate Bill 896 reduces annual registration fees for most motor vehicle classes in Maryland, including passenger cars, trucks, motorcycles, buses, and trailers. The bill lowers weight-based fees for passenger and multipurpose vehicles and removes supplemental fee increases and surcharges for commercial vehicles and dump trucks.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA)
stakeholders: Maryland motor vehicle owners, including individual car owners, commercial trucking businesses, motorcycle riders, school bus operators, and historic vehicle collectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a significant reduction in state revenue for the Transportation Trust Fund due to the lowering of registration fees across multiple vehicle classes and the elimination of previously enacted fee surcharges. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text, a specific total dollar estimate for the revenue decrease is unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and the steward of the Transportation Trust Fund, MDOT is the primary agency impacted by changes to vehicle registration fees, which are a major source of revenue for the state's transportation network.
The MVA is the specific unit within MDOT responsible for registering vehicles and collecting the fees altered by this bill. It is the primary implementing agency for these statutory changes.

DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal planning. The bill's reduction in scheduled registration fee increases represents a significant impact on state revenue projections and the annual budget process.

As a modal administration within MDOT, the MTA relies on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) for its operating and capital budgets. Reductions in registration fee revenue directly affect the available resources for public transit services.

The SHA depends on the Transportation Trust Fund for the maintenance and construction of state highways. Changes to registration fees directly impact the funding available for road infrastructure projects.
As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for state revenues and managing the flow of funds from fee collections into state accounts.

The Treasurer manages state funds and oversees the issuance of state bonds, including those backed by Transportation Trust Fund revenues, which are impacted by changes in registration fee collections.
MAA is funded through the Transportation Trust Fund. A decrease in registration fee revenue reduces the total pool of funding available for MDOT's modal administrations, including aviation.
MPA is a modal administration of MDOT and relies on the Transportation Trust Fund for its operations and maritime business development initiatives.
The bill specifically alters registration fees for Class H (school) vehicles, which are used by local school systems and contractors under the leadership and policy oversight of MSDE.
DGS manages the state's vehicle fleet. Alterations to registration fees for passenger cars, trucks, and vans will impact the operational costs for the state government's vehicle inventory.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget; the fiscal impact of this bill on the Transportation Trust Fund is a major policy and budgetary matter for the administration.

MSP enforces motor vehicle laws, including registration requirements. While the bill focuses on fee amounts, changes to vehicle classifications and registration standards are relevant to highway patrol operations.
The MDTA operates state toll facilities and coordinates with MDOT on transportation finance and infrastructure projects, making it relevant to broad changes in transportation funding.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and the MVA and would be involved in interpreting the statutory revisions to ensures the administrative implementation of new fees is legally sound.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide reimbursement for applied behavior analysis services provided by registered behavior technicians to Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients with autism spectrum disorder. stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients with autism spectrum disorder, registered behavior technicians, licensed psychologists, and board-certified behavior analysts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State expenditures for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program by mandating reimbursement for services provided by registered behavior technicians. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to provide reimbursement for applied behavior analysis services provided by registered behavior technicians under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and requires the department to adopt new regulations.

As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM is impacted by changes to the Maryland Medical Assistance Program's reimbursement requirements, which likely have a significant fiscal impact on the state's Medicaid expenditures.

The bill concerns the provision of services for individuals with autism spectrum disorder, which aligns with the department's mission to coordinate and improve services for Maryland residents with disabilities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new regulations and ensuring the reimbursement changes comply with federal and state law.

Since autism spectrum disorder is a developmental disorder often requiring early intervention in children, this bill's impact on service accessibility is relevant to the office's mission of improving access to health services for children.

bill_summary: This bill provides civil immunity to federally licensed firearms dealers for personal injury or death resulting from the use of a firearm after it has been returned to its owner following a private 'firearm hold agreement.' The immunity does not apply if the dealer's conduct in the matter was unlawful.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Federally Licensed Firearms Dealers
stakeholders: Federally licensed firearms dealers and firearm owners in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the provided text. The bill establishes civil immunity for private firearms dealers, which may reduce litigation costs for those parties but does not appear to have a direct impact on State or local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police is the primary agency responsible for enforcing the Public Safety Article regarding firearms and overseeing the licensing and regulation of firearms dealers in the state.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel on state law and would be responsible for interpreting the civil immunity provisions and defending the statute in court if challenged.
This bill creates a statutory immunity from civil liability, which directly affects the adjudication of personal injury and wrongful death lawsuits in the Maryland court system.
Firearm hold agreements are a recognized 'lethal means safety' strategy in public health and suicide prevention efforts, which are managed and promoted by the Department of Health.
Suicide prevention and voluntary firearm storage are critical priorities for veterans' health and safety; this bill facilitates programs aimed at reducing veteran suicide rates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice and firearm-related policy developments.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to provide grants to companies specializing in regenerative medicine and advanced manufacturing. State expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount based on the level of funding provided in the state budget. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific dollar estimates for appropriations or administrative costs are unavailable.

The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund separately and to invest the money of the fund.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Advanced Manufacturing Grant Program Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that TEDCO consult with the Maryland Stem Cell Research Commission (which falls under this category of state-authorized bodies) to establish eligibility criteria, evaluation procedures, and regulations for the program.
The bill creates a new special, nonlapsing fund that will require state budget appropriations and fiscal oversight, functions managed by DBM.

The program's focus on advanced manufacturing and regenerative medicine aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission to stimulate economic development, attract businesses, and promote Maryland's competitive industrial assets.
The Governor oversees the executive agencies involved and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which would include the necessary appropriations for this new grant fund.
The program specifically targets regenerative medicine, which is a specialized field of healthcare and biotechnology regulated and overseen by the Department of Health.

Advanced manufacturing and regenerative medicine are significant research and commercialization priorities for the University System, and many companies eligible for these grants would likely be spin-offs or partners of USM institutions.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits weather engineering activities, defined as the intentional release of chemical compounds or substances into the atmosphere to affect temperature, weather, climate, or sunlight intensity. It requires the Maryland Department of the Environment, in consultation with the Maryland Department of Emergency Management, to establish a reporting system and investigation process for suspected weather engineering. Violations are classified as felonies and carry significant fines, which are to be deposited into the Bay Restoration Fund.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, aircraft operators and controllers, environmental regulators, and any entities engaged in atmospheric research or modification.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes felony penalties with fines up to 100000 dollars for general violations and 5000 dollars for aircraft operators, with all revenue directed to the Bay Restoration Fund. The Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management will incur costs to establish a reporting framework and conduct investigations, but specific dollar estimates for these expenditures are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of the Environment as the primary agency responsible for managing the prohibition of weather engineering. MDE must establish a reporting system, investigate reports of prohibited activities, and oversee the new Subtitle 15 in the Environment Article.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to consult with the Department of the Environment to establish a method for evaluating reports of weather engineering activity.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG will provide legal counsel to MDE regarding the implementation and enforcement of these new regulations and may be involved in the prosecution of the newly created felony offenses.

The bill establishes specific felony penalties for aircraft operators or controllers who participate in weather engineering activities, which directly impacts the aviation sector overseen by MDOT's Maryland Aviation Administration.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be involved in enforcing the prohibitions and assisting MDE with investigations into criminal weather engineering activities, particularly those involving aircraft.
The bill creates new felony offenses for weather engineering, which will impact the workload of the state's judicial system through new criminal proceedings and adjudications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new felony penalties that include potential imprisonment (up to 5 years for aircraft operators), which could impact state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a decrease in State revenue as certain vehicles will be exempt from the fees associated with biennial emissions inspections. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary agency responsible for administering the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP). This bill requires the MVA to provide forms and process certifications for a new class of exemptions for formerly historic vehicles.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT, MVA, and MDE regarding the drafting of new regulations and the legal sufficiency of the certification forms required by the bill.

DBM oversees the state's fiscal planning and revenue estimation. The bill will result in a decrease in fee revenue collected by the state, requiring DBM to account for this in the state's financial projections.

bill_summary: This bill expands and clarifies the definition of the 'practice of audiology' in Maryland. responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
stakeholders: Licensed audiologists and individuals seeking diagnosis or treatment for auditory or vestibular ear conditions.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note with specific revenue and expenditure estimates was not provided in the bill text. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable, though the bill primarily alters the scope of practice for licensed audiologists.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists. This bill directly amends the Health Occupations Article to redefine the scope of practice for audiologists, which is a primary regulatory and policy function of the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advocates for the welfare of Deaf and hard of hearing residents and provides expertise to other state agencies on related policies. The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and its various licensing boards. The OAG is responsible for advising the Board on the interpretation and enforcement of the expanded scope of practice defined in the bill.

Changes to the statutory definition of the 'practice of audiology' impact the insurance industry. The MIA regulates health insurance policies and reimbursement requirements, which are influenced by what is legally defined as a covered clinical practice.

Audiology and vestibular services are critical for the health and quality of life of older adults. Changes that clarify diagnostic and treatment procedures directly affect the care options and health promotion activities overseen by the Department for this demographic.

The Department of Education manages school-based health screenings and special education programs where audiologists play a key role. Changes to their scope of practice, particularly regarding screenings and imaging, affect the delivery of services in public schools.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for residents with hearing impairments. A bill refining the diagnostic and treatment protocols for auditory conditions is relevant to the department's mission of ensuring effective healthcare access for individuals with disabilities.

The school provides educational and clinical support to students who are deaf or hard of hearing. Clarifying the scope of audiological practice is relevant to the professional clinical services and screenings provided to their student population.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases and disciplinary actions involving health care professionals. It would handle administrative hearings if there are disputes regarding whether an audiologist is practicing within the newly defined scope.

The MHCC plans for health system needs and tracks the quality and cost of care. Modifications to the diagnostic authority of health professionals like audiologists are relevant to the commission's oversight of health service availability and quality standards.

The Exchange determines coverage eligibility and plan standards for the state's health insurance marketplace. Changes to the defined scope of professional medical practice can influence the benchmark services and benefits offered in these plans.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates health policy initiatives. The Governor will be responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the administration of the various health regulatory boards through the Executive Department.

Synopsis: Requiring that books and records kept by or on behalf of certain homeowners associations be posted online; clarifying that a governing body of a homeowners association may secure a line of credit or loan to fund reserves; requiring that certain homeowners associations provide notice of a meeting by electronic transmission; etc.
Title: Homeowners Associations - Reserve Funding, Meeting Notices, Voting, and Records
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
