bill_summary: This bill requires homeowners associations (HOAs) with at least 100 lots to maintain a website, online portal, or mobile application for posting governing documents, meeting minutes, and recordings of virtual meetings. It authorizes HOA governing bodies to secure lines of credit or loans for reserve funding with approval from 51% of lot owners in good standing. The bill also mandates electronic meeting notices for owners who provide authorization, requires specific details in such notices, and establishes a petition process for lot owners to enable electronic voting.
stakeholders: Homeowners association lot owners and HOA governing boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates for state or local government are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. The bill creates private sector fiscal impacts for homeowners associations with 100 or more lots, which must incur costs to develop and maintain a website, online portal, or mobile application for document storage by October 1, 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection laws and provides legal counsel to the General Assembly. This bill amends the Real Property Article regarding Homeowners Associations (HOAs), and the OAG's Consumer Protection Division frequently handles disputes and provides guidance to residents and associations concerning their rights and records.

While the Secretary of State's primary common-interest community oversight is for condominiums and time-shares, Homeowners Associations (HOAs) are under the same common ownership community policy umbrella. The agency's expertise in common-interest community registration and oversight makes this legislation relevant to their policy area.

The bill establishes new requirements for HOA records, voting procedures, and reserve funding. Disputes arising from these new statutory mandates would be adjudicated in the Maryland court system, which the Administrative Office of the Courts supports operationally and legally.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development is responsible for ensuring safe, secure, and thriving communities. Legislation governing the financial health (reserves) and administrative transparency of HOAs directly impacts the stability and quality of life in these residential communities.

The department focuses on improving access and inclusivity for residents with disabilities. The bill's provisions requiring HOAs to provide meeting notices via electronic transmission and to facilitate virtual meetings and electronic voting enhance the accessibility of community governance for people with disabilities.

The department is dedicated to improving the quality of life for older adults. The bill's shift toward electronic meetings, online records, and electronic voting impacts the accessibility of community engagement for seniors, many of whom reside in communities managed by HOAs.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides policy guidance and technical assistance to community organizations. The bill's requirements for HOAs to manage reserve funds and maintain digital repositories of governance documents relate to the department's mission of supporting effective resource management and community infrastructure.

This office promotes civic participation and coordinates with community organizations. The bill's changes to HOA voting and meeting procedures directly affect the civic engagement of Maryland residents within their local community associations.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Solar Photovoltaic Module Energy Security and Affordability Fund, the Maryland Energy Storage Energy Security and Affordability Fund, and the Maryland Zero-Emission Vehicle Energy Security and Affordability Fund; establishing advisory councils to administer the funds, support the marketing and promotion of certain technologies, and create certain checkoff programs; requiring certain surcharges on the sale of solar photovoltaic modules, energy storage systems, and zero-emission vehicles; etc.
Title: Solar Photovoltaic Modules, Energy Storage, and Zero-Emission Vehicles - Advisory Councils, Checkoff Programs, and Funds

bill_summary: Senate Bill 923 establishes three advisory councils and special funds—specifically for solar photovoltaic modules, energy storage systems, and zero-emission vehicles—under the Maryland Energy Administration. The councils are responsible for marketing, research, and educational campaigns to promote these technologies and combat misinformation. The initiatives are financed through new fees imposed on the sale and installation of solar modules, energy storage systems, and zero-emission vehicles in the state.
stakeholders: Manufacturers, retail sellers, and installers of solar modules, energy storage systems, and zero-emission vehicles; individual, business, and governmental purchasers of these technologies; and the Maryland Energy Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates three special funds supported by new fees: $0.02 per watt for solar modules, $5 per kilowatt-hour for energy storage capacity, and $200 per zero-emission vehicle sold in Maryland. These fees are capped at the lesser of 0.5% of the wholesale value or the amount necessary to cover council costs. The Maryland Energy Administration is entitled to 5% of the fees for administrative staffing. While the bill mandates these revenue streams, specific total dollar estimates for state revenue and expenditures are indeterminate as they depend on the volume of future technology sales. State and local agencies will also be subject to the fees when purchasing these technologies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the designated 'Administration' in the bill, MEA is the primary agency responsible for implementing this legislation. The Director of MEA chairs all three new advisory councils, and the agency is responsible for providing staff, imposing and collecting fees, and administering the new funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes three new permanent advisory councils: the Maryland Solar Photovoltaic Module, the Energy Storage, and the Zero-Emission Vehicle Energy Security and Affordability Fund Advisory Councils.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the three newly created special funds separately and to invest the money of the funds in accordance with state law.

The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the three new special funds. Additionally, the Comptroller may be involved if any proposed 'checkoff program' is administered through the state tax system.

The bill's fees apply to purchases of solar modules and energy storage by 'electric companies,' which are regulated by the PSC. The commission also has oversight over energy storage systems integrated into the grid.

MDOT is the lead agency for Maryland's zero-emission vehicle initiatives. The bill's creation of a ZEV Fund and Advisory Council directly overlaps with MDOT's strategic mission to promote electric vehicle adoption.

As part of MDOT, the MVA tracks vehicle sales and registration. The bill imposes a $200 fee on zero-emission vehicles sold in the state, which may require data sharing or coordination with MVA records.

The MCEC is tasked with advancing the adoption of clean energy and energy efficiency. The bill's focus on promoting solar, storage, and EVs via marketing and educational campaigns aligns closely with the Center's mission.

The OPC represents residential utility consumers in matters involving energy security and affordability. The new funds and fees on solar and storage technologies impact the costs and programs available to utility customers.

The Governor oversees the MEA and the executive branch agencies implementing the bill. The Governor is also responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which would include the initial appropriations for the new funds.
DBM oversees the state budget and the creation of new special funds. It would be responsible for managing the fiscal structure of the three new funds and the related fee-based revenue streams.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the MEA and would likely be involved in reviewing the legality of the new fees, the checkoff programs, and the structure of the advisory councils.

This multi-agency initiative focuses on sustainable development and clean energy. The bill's promotion of solar and zero-emission technologies is a core component of the state's sustainable growth strategy.
MDE implements clean energy and air quality laws. While MEA is the administrative lead for this bill, MDE is a primary stakeholder in the environmental benefits resulting from solar and ZEV adoption.

DGS is the state's central procurement authority. Since the bill's fees apply to purchases made by 'governmental agencies,' DGS would see a fiscal impact when purchasing solar modules or zero-emission vehicles for the state fleet.
The bill focuses on the 'marketing and promotion' of clean energy technologies, which intersects with Commerce's role in promoting Maryland's assets and supporting industry development.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "exempt material" for the purpose of provisions of law related to extended producer responsibility for packaging and paper products.

bill_summary: This bill expands the definition of 'exempt material' in the context of Maryland's producer responsibility laws for packaging and paper products. Specifically, it includes packaging for dietary supplements regulated by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a material exempt from these producer responsibility requirements.
stakeholders: Manufacturers and producers of dietary supplements, the packaging industry, and the Maryland Department of the Environment.
fiscal_impact_summary: By exempting dietary supplement packaging from producer responsibility laws, the bill may lead to an indeterminate reduction in potential fee revenues or compliance expenditures. However, because a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary agency for environmental protection and regulation, MDE is responsible for implementing and enforcing the producer responsibility laws for packaging and paper products found in Article – Environment. This bill directly alters the scope of materials under their regulatory authority by expanding the 'exempt material' definition to include dietary supplement packaging.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel to all state agencies, including the Department of the Environment. They would be responsible for advising MDE on the legal interpretation and enforcement of the expanded exemption for dietary supplements under environmental statutes.

The bill concerns the packaging of 'dietary supplements,' a category of health-related products. While the regulation is environmental in nature, MDH oversees health policy and the regulation of health care professionals and facilities, making them a secondary stakeholder in definitions concerning products regulated by the FDA for health purposes.

The Department of Commerce is responsible for the state's economic development and business retention. Altering the definition of exempt materials to include dietary supplements reduces the regulatory and financial burden on manufacturers within this sector operating in Maryland, which falls under Commerce's interest in the state's competitive business environment.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. As the primary entity responsible for enforcing state laws and overseeing the Department of the Environment, the Governor's Office has a general interest in the implementation of producer responsibility programs and environmental regulations.

bill_summary: This bill creates a temporary related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City for events associated with the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave. It requires promoters or participating license holders to apply for a permit for any event with at least 75 participants, sets specific application and permit fees based on venue capacity, and establishes penalties for conducting events without the necessary permit.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: Related event promoters, Baltimore City alcoholic beverages license holders, holders of State caterer's licenses, and participants of the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase local revenue for Baltimore City through a $50 application fee and permit fees of either $500 or $1,500 per event depending on venue capacity. Additionally, the Board and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission may collect fine revenue between $1,000 and $3,000 for violations. A formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, so specific aggregate dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's chief financial officer and regulator of the alcohol industry. This bill establishes a new alcoholic beverages permit in Baltimore City and mandates fines for state caterer's license holders who violate its provisions, directly involving the agency's regulatory and revenue-collection oversight.

The bill is specifically designed to facilitate the Kappa Alpha Psi 2027 Conclave, a major national convention. As the agency responsible for stimulating Maryland's tourism economy and promoting the state as a travel destination, the OTD has a significant interest in the successful execution and licensing of events for large-scale tourism activities.

The Department of Commerce is the state's primary economic development agency and oversees the Maryland Office of Tourism Development. The 2027 Conclave is a major economic driver for Baltimore City and the state, and this legislation provides the necessary regulatory framework for associated business and hospitality activity.

The bill references the 'Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article' and grants enforcement powers to the 'Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission.' Although the permit is for alcohol, the administrative structure and the laws being amended are part of a shared regulatory framework that includes the cannabis industry.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal representative for the state and its agencies. It provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, including those responsible for enforcing the alcoholic beverage laws and processing the penalties described in the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing state laws. This bill creates a specific, temporary regulatory mechanism for a major event that aligns with the office's oversight of state policy and economic initiatives.

bill_summary: This bill allows certain retired members of the State Police Retirement System who participated in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) between July 1, 2020, and July 1, 2026, to apply for a special disability retirement allowance if they were involved in a work-related accident before enrolling in DROP. It establishes a temporary window for application ending December 31, 2026, and requires the State to pay the difference between the special disability benefits and any retirement benefits previously received, including retroactive payments.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Retired members of the Maryland State Police Retirement System who participated in the DROP program and suffered work-related injuries prior to their enrollment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a spending mandate for the State Retirement and Pension System to provide special disability retirement benefits and retroactive payments (the difference between disability and regular retirement benefits) to a specific group of State Police retirees. Because a formal Fiscal Note with specific expenditure figures was not provided in the text, the exact financial impact is unavailable, though it will result in an increase in pension liabilities and state expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary body responsible for administering the State Retirement and Pension System, including the State Police Retirement System. The bill specifically directs the agency to provide forms and process applications for the special disability retirement allowance.

The bill directly impacts retirees of the Maryland State Police. It concerns the special disability retirement benefits for former members who participated in the agency's DROP program and were injured while in service for the department.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the state, DBM oversees state employee benefits and long-term fiscal planning. Changes to pension eligibility and the provision of retroactive benefits for state police retirees have a fiscal impact on the state's retirement liabilities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland State Retirement Agency and the Maryland State Police. They would likely be responsible for advising on the legal interpretation of the bill's eligibility requirements and retroactive benefit provisions.

bill_summary: This bill requires social media platforms to display the general geographical location, specifically the city and country derived from an IP address, of adult users to any user located within Maryland. It prohibits platforms from displaying the location of users known to be minors and classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the state's consumer protection laws.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Social media platform operators, Maryland social media users, and adult social media users whose account information is visible on these platforms.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to the enforcement and penalty provisions of the Consumer Protection Act. This implies potential state revenue from civil penalties and increased state expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General for enforcement. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that a violation of the new social media location display requirements is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is the primary agency responsible for enforcing these laws and investigating violations.

Civil enforcement actions and requests for injunctions brought by the Attorney General under the Consumer Protection Act are adjudicated within the State's court system, which is supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Office of Administrative Hearings may be required to adjudicate contested administrative enforcement actions brought by the Division of Consumer Protection regarding social media platform non-compliance.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for policy coordination and signing bills into law. This bill creates new regulations for technology companies and consumer privacy, which aligns with executive policy-making functions.

The bill contains specific provisions prohibiting the display of location data for users known to be minors, directly relating to the agency's mission to protect the well-being and safety of Maryland's children.

bill_summary: This bill proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution to allow the Chair of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities to recall former members to serve as temporary substitute members or to request that the Governor appoint a temporary substitute or extend a current member’s term in the event of a recusal, disqualification, or a term expiration without a replacement. It also repeals previously enacted chapters from 2025 related to the same subject.
responsible_party: Commission on Judicial Disabilities and the Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland State judges, members of the Maryland Bar, and the public.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is the primary authority responsible for appointing all 11 members of the Commission on Judicial Disabilities. The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. This bill directly impacts their workload regarding the vetting of temporary substitute members and the management of term extensions for the Commission on Judicial Disabilities.

The Commission on Judicial Disabilities is a key oversight body within the Judiciary Department. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and legal support to the judicial branch and is impacted by changes to the governance and continuity of the body responsible for investigating complaints against judges.

The bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be submitted to the qualified voters of the state for adoption or rejection during the November 2026 general election. The Board of Elections is responsible for administering this referendum.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Judicial Disabilities falls under the category of executive commissions and boards. The Secretary of State is the custodian of official records, including executive commissions and laws. They are involved in the official processing of constitutional amendments and the record-keeping of executive appointments and commissions.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the Governor, the General Assembly, and state commissions. They may be required to provide legal advice on the implementation of temporary appointments or the legal process of the constitutional amendment.

bill_summary: The Maryland Fair Chance Housing Act establishes regulations for the use of criminal history records during the residential leasing process. It generally prohibits landlords from inquiring about a prospective tenant's criminal record before extending a conditional offer of lease, although exceptions are provided for certain serious offenses such as murder, human trafficking, and specific sex crimes. After a conditional offer is made, landlords may only consider specific types of convictions and must allow the tenant to provide evidence of rehabilitation or mitigation. The bill also requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to create model notices and tasks the Attorney General with data collection and enforcement.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs) and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Prospective tenants with criminal records, residential landlords, and property management companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation, which may result in an indeterminate increase in state revenue. The Department of Housing and Community Development and the Office of the Attorney General will experience increased administrative workloads and costs to develop model documents, maintain complaint data, and conduct enforcement activities. Specific total dollar estimates for these fiscal impacts are not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Office of the Attorney General with collecting and maintaining data on complaints, publishing annual reports on substantiated violations, and adopting regulations to carry out the Maryland Fair Chance Housing Act. Additionally, a violation of the Act is classified as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Attorney General.

The bill specifically requires the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs within the Department of Housing and Community Development to develop and publish a model notice document for use by landlords to comply with the new criminal history disclosure requirements.

The bill addresses the 'Discriminatory Use of Criminal History in Residential Leasing' and aims to protect prospective tenants from unfair housing practices. This aligns with the Commission's mandate to enforce anti-discrimination laws in housing.

The bill creates new statutory requirements for residential leases and landlord conduct. Disputes arising from these new regulations, as well as the prohibition of certain information being used as a basis for claims against landlords, will likely impact the caseload and procedures of the state's judicial system.

The agency serves vulnerable populations, including those facing homelessness or in economic need. This bill directly impacts housing accessibility for individuals with criminal records, who are a demographic often served by DHS programs.

As the office responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives, the Governor's Office would be involved in the implementation of this significant shift in housing and consumer protection policy.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency. The bill mandates new duties for the Attorney General and DHCD, which may have fiscal impacts regarding staffing and resource allocation for data collection, regulation development, and enforcement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Affordable Multifamily Rental Housing Stabilization Program specifically within this department and tasks it with the administration, application processing, and awarding of funds for capital repairs.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include a specific appropriation of $5,000,000 in the annual budget bill for the program from fiscal years 2028 through 2031.
As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising its execution, DBM will be directly involved in managing the authorized $5,000,000 annual appropriation for the program.

The Office of the Attorney General will provide legal counsel to the Department of Housing and Community Development for the development of the program's regulations and the legal framework of its loan and grant agreements.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Reentry Readiness Program within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Reentry Readiness Program within this department and charges it with primary responsibility for staffing and administering the program to assist returning citizens.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates major policy initiatives, including inter-departmental efforts like the Reentry Readiness Program.

bill_summary: This bill imposes a 3% State admissions and amusement tax on gross receipts from athletic competitions at the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP). It also creates a 3% 'game day surcharge' on sales of food, alcoholic beverages, and accommodations within a 3-mile radius of the UMCP football stadium on game days and the preceding day. The revenue from these taxes is directed to the University of Maryland Athletic Department Support Fund to provide scholarships and financial compensation for UMCP student-athletes.
stakeholders: University of Maryland, College Park student-athletes and athletic department, businesses located within 3 miles of the UMCP football stadium, and attendees of UMCP athletic events.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a 3% tax on UMCP athletic event admissions and a 3% surcharge on food, drinks, and lodging near the stadium on football game days. All resulting revenue is distributed to the University of Maryland Athletic Department Support Fund, a special nonlapsing fund. While the bill specifies the tax rates, specific dollar estimates for total revenue and expenditures are unavailable in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for collecting and distributing the revenue from the State admissions and amusement tax and the newly established game day surcharge on food, alcohol, and accommodations. The bill specifically directs the Comptroller to account for the University of Maryland Athletic Department Support Fund.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the new University of Maryland Athletic Department Support Fund separately and overseeing the investment and reinvestment of its proceeds.

The bill directly impacts the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP), which is the flagship institution of the University System of Maryland. The revenue generated is dedicated to UMCP's Athletic Department for student-athlete scholarships and compensation.

The bill amends the distribution section for admissions and amusement tax revenue (Tax - General § 2-202), which is the section that governs funding for the Maryland Stadium Authority. The creation of a new state-level tax on athletic competitions held at UMCP intersects with the Authority's role in sports facility financing and revenue management.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. The creation of a new special, nonlapsing fund and new tax streams requires DBM's oversight regarding state revenue impacts and fiscal notes.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission coordinates policies for public universities and oversees financial aid. This bill establishes a new source of financial compensation and scholarships for student-athletes at a state university, which falls within the Commission's broad regulatory and coordinating scope.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Comptroller, the Treasurer, and the University System of Maryland regarding the implementation and enforcement of the new taxes and the management of the special fund.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. This bill establishes a significant new tax structure and special fund that supports a major state institution, requiring executive policy coordination.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "qualified rehabilitation expenditure", for purposes of the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit, to repeal the exclusion of expenditures for a certain rehabilitation that is otherwise funded, financed, or reimbursed by certain State or local expenditures; altering the definition of "substantial rehabilitation" to extend the period during which certain expenditures must occur; expanding certain competitive award criteria for commercial projects; etc.
Title: Historic Revitalization Tax Credit - Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/11 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- EthAff; Mus; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Smart Growth -see also- Zoning and Planning

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Historic Revitalization Tax Credit program by allowing projects that receive other state or local financial assistance to qualify for the credit and extending the required expenditure window for 'substantial rehabilitation' from 24 to 60 months. It authorizes the issuance of supplemental credit certificates to address construction cost inflation, establishes new high-impact economic development criteria for competitive awards in revitalization zones, and allows each structure within a multi-building campus project to be treated as a separate rehabilitation for the purpose of credit limits.
stakeholders: Owners and developers of historic properties, business entities, non-profit organizations, and local governments in designated revitalization zones.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates annual appropriations to the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Reserve Fund, requiring at least $16,500,000 for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 and $20,000,000 for fiscal years 2029 through 2031. It also mandates an annual $2,000,000 appropriation for the Small Commercial Project Trust Account through 2031. Additional fiscal impacts include potential revenue decreases due to expanded credit eligibility and the introduction of inflation-based supplemental credits, partially offset by administrative fees capped at 3% of the award amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Planning which houses the Maryland Historical Trust. The bill requires the Trust to report annually to the Governor on the status of the tax credit program and necessitates budget appropriations overseen by the office.

The Comptroller is responsible for tax administration, including processing the income tax credits and refunds created by the bill, auditing expenditures, and transferring funds into the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Reserve Fund.

The Treasurer is responsible for investing and reinvesting the money within the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Reserve Fund and is a member of the Board of Public Works which may interact with significant state contracts related to the projects.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is tasked with approving numeric sustainable development rating systems for high performance buildings under the credit. Additionally, the department oversees the budget process for mandatory appropriations to the Reserve Fund.

The bill expands competitive award criteria for commercial rehabilitations to include structures located in Enterprise Zones and Arts and Entertainment Districts, which are designated and managed by the Department of Commerce.

The Secretary of General Services must approve the numeric sustainable development rating systems used to define 'high performance buildings' for the purposes of qualifying for the additional tax credit.

The bill references 'affordable housing' as defined by the allocation of low-income housing tax credits by DHCD and includes 'Sustainable Communities' and 'Main Street Maryland' communities as high-impact criteria for awarding credits.

The definition of a 'certified historic structure' specifically includes properties owned by the Department of Natural Resources if they are occupied under an agreement requiring the occupant to pay for rehabilitation.

The Department of Planning oversees the Maryland Historical Trust. The Director of the Trust is the primary administrator of the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit, responsible for certifying structures, approving rehabilitation plans, and issuing credit certificates.

The bill includes transit-oriented developments (TODs) as a priority location for high-impact commercial rehabilitation projects. TODs are defined and managed under the authority of the Maryland Department of Transportation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, which is an executive body, must be consulted by the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust in the adoption of regulations for the program.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court would hear appeals regarding the Comptroller's or Director's final decisions on the eligibility or amount of the historic revitalization tax credits.

The Office of Legislative Audits is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive agencies, which would include the Maryland Historical Trust's management of the tax credit and the Reserve Fund.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates the state planning visions and the Sustainable Growth Subcabinet, both of which are central to the strategic implementation and regulatory oversight of the tax credit described in the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring that the accessible online absentee ballot application provided by the State Board of Elections include certain information for voters that choose to receive an absentee ballot provided by the Internet; prohibiting certain voters on permanent absentee ballot status from receiving a recurring absentee ballot provided by the Internet; and altering the contents of a certain communication sent to certain voters on permanent absentee voter status.
Title: Election Law - Internet-Delivered Absentee Ballots - Information and Receipt Limitation
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to update the online absentee ballot application to include a detailed modal box and a confirmation dialog for voters who choose internet delivery. It also limits most voters on permanent absentee status to receiving an internet-delivered ballot for only one election cycle, requiring them to select an alternative delivery method for subsequent cycles, with exceptions for military, overseas, and certain disabled voters.
stakeholders: Maryland voters, the State Board of Elections, and local boards of elections
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill creates administrative and IT requirements for the State Board of Elections to update the online absentee ballot application and manage ballot delivery method restrictions and notifications for permanent absentee voters.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for administering election laws and would be directly tasked with implementing the changes to the online absentee ballot application, managing the permanent absentee ballot list, and sending required communications to voters regarding their ballot delivery methods.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal counsel for the State Board of Elections and would be involved in ensuring that the proposed changes to the ballot delivery process comply with federal requirements such as the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act.

The Department of Information Technology oversees the state's IT strategy and cybersecurity; this bill requires specific technical changes to the State Board's online ballot application, including the implementation of modal boxes and dialog boxes for Internet-delivered ballots.

The bill contains specific provisions and exceptions regarding Internet-delivered ballots for voters with disabilities, making it relevant to the department's mission of ensuring accessible government services and inclusive policies.

The bill includes specific provisions and exceptions for absent uniformed services voters and overseas voters, aligning with the department's role in advocating for and supporting active-duty service members and their families.

As the principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management would oversee any budgetary increases or personnel adjustments needed for the State Board of Elections to update its systems and manage the new communication requirements mandated by the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor Authority in Charles County; requiring the Authority to support and develop a certain neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with certain residents; authorizing the Authority to modify certain boundaries, subject to a certain vote; requiring the Authority to take certain actions regarding the finances of the Authority; exempting the Authority from certain taxation or assessments under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Charles County Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor Authority - Established
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Corporations and Instrumentalities -see also- HBE
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor Authority in Charles County to oversee and support revitalization efforts in State Legislative Districts 27A and 28. The Authority is responsible for developing a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with residents, promoting economic development, and attracting new business activity. It is granted powers to acquire property through various means, manage funds, and enter into contracts, and it must become self-sustaining by fiscal year 2036.
responsible_party: Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor Authority (governed by a Board of Directors appointed by the Charles County Commissioners)
stakeholders: Residents, business owners, and property developers in Charles County Legislative Districts 27A and 28, as well as the Charles County local government.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a potential State and local expenditure impact through appropriations to the Authority and its dedicated Fund. It provides tax exemptions for the Authority regarding transfer, recordation, and sales taxes on construction materials, which will result in an indeterminate revenue decrease. However, property taxes will apply once the Authority sells or leases property to private entities. The Authority is mandated to be self-sustaining starting in fiscal year 2036. No specific dollar estimates were provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Authority's primary mission—neighborhood revitalization, housing development, and community modernization—directly aligns with this department's core responsibilities for supporting homeownership, rental housing, and community revitalization investments.
The Authority is tasked with economic development, attracting new businesses, and retaining existing enterprises in Charles County, which are the central functions of the Department of Commerce.

The bill mandates the development of a 20-year comprehensive plan for land use, housing, and transportation within the Waldorf corridor, overlapping with the department's role in promoting sustainable growth and providing technical planning assistance.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the newly established Waldorf Urban Redevelopment Corridor Authority Fund and is impacted by the Authority's broad exemptions from state sales, use, transfer, and recordation taxes.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the newly created special fund separately and manage the investment of its funds in the same manner as other state money.
The bill allows the Governor to include annual appropriations for the Authority in the state budget and establishes the Authority as a state instrumentality within the executive branch.
As the chief legal officer for state agencies and instrumentalities, the OAG would provide legal counsel and represent the new Authority in its corporate and governmental functions.

The department is the principal fiscal agency responsible for the state budget process, which the Authority will interact with for state appropriations, even though it is exempted from certain personnel and management titles.

The Authority’s revitalization plan must address transportation for motor vehicles and pedestrians along the corridor, which impacts the state's transportation network and highway systems managed by MDOT.
As a state instrumentality receiving public funds and required to establish financial accounting and reports, the Authority falls under the audit and fiscal compliance jurisdiction of the OLA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Authority is subject to state law regarding Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation, which this office implements and monitors across state agencies.
The Authority is granted the power of eminent domain and condemnation, which requires judicial proceedings managed by the state court system supported by the AOC.
The bill explicitly exempts the new Authority from certain Board of Public Works oversight and miscellaneous provisions in the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The Authority is explicitly exempted from Title 4 of the State Finance and Procurement Article, removing it from DGS's standard oversight of state facilities, real estate, and procurement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill exempts the Authority from most General Procurement Law, thereby reducing the volume of bid protests and contract disputes within the target area that would otherwise be adjudicated by the MSBCA.
The bill's complex tax exemptions for the Authority and specific conditions for when property becomes taxable create potential for tax-related disputes that fall under the Tax Court's jurisdiction.
The bill explicitly subjects the Authority’s board and employees to the Maryland Public Ethics Law, which is administered and enforced by this Commission.

The Authority's mission to create long-term comprehensive plans for green space and sustainable development aligns with this multi-agency initiative's goals for sustainable growth and resource management.
The Authority's charge to develop green space and neighborhood revitalization within the Waldorf corridor overlaps with DNR’s mission to manage and enhance state natural resources.
The Authority functions as a specialized, localized version of MEDCO, providing similar financing and real estate development services to stimulate economic prosperity.

Synopsis: Establishing a Class L beer, wine, and liquor license; authorizing a local licensing board to issue the license to a holder of a manufacturer's license; providing that the license authorizes the license holder to sell or provide samples of certain beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption under certain circumstances; establishing a license fee of $250; etc.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages – Class L Beer, Wine, and Liquor License – Established
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages Manufacturing -see also- Breweries; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Class L beer, wine, and liquor license, which local licensing boards may issue to holders of a manufacturer's license. The license authorizes the holder to sell or provide free samples of beer, wine, and liquor produced by themselves or other manufacturers for on-premises consumption.
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage manufacturers, local licensing boards, and consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes an annual license fee of $250 for each Class L license issued. Because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided, specific total revenue estimates are unavailable, but the bill indicates a revenue increase for local licensing boards based on the number of licenses granted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's primary regulator of the alcohol industry. The bill establishes a new class of liquor license (Class L) and a corresponding annual fee, directly impacting the Comptroller's responsibilities for industry oversight, tax collection, and revenue management.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for estimating state revenues and supervising budget execution. The creation of a new $250 license fee and the potential administrative costs of implementing the new Class L license will have a fiscal impact on the state budget.

The Department of Commerce is tasked with stimulating the economy and expanding existing companies. By allowing alcohol manufacturers to sell and provide samples on-premises, this bill provides a new revenue stream and business expansion opportunity for Maryland's craft beverage industry.

The Department of Agriculture promotes the economic viability of agribusiness. Many alcohol manufacturers, such as farm breweries and wineries, are considered agricultural businesses, and this bill supports their commercial viability by expanding their sales authority.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO supports the profitability of agricultural and rural businesses. This bill directly affects the business models of rural and agricultural alcohol producers (manufacturers) by allowing them to sell products produced by themselves or other manufacturers.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller and any boards involved in alcoholic beverages regulation. They will likely be involved in interpreting the legal requirements and drafting regulations for the newly established license.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases and regulatory enforcement actions for state agencies. The introduction of a new license type and associated regulations may lead to administrative disputes or appeals that fall under its jurisdiction.
